body:
## Why
stripetest.md C2/C4 on dev (private@, listing featured until 07/10): "Extend promotion" → Stripe → back link returned to My listings with **no message**, the ListingPromotion stayed PENDING ("Awaiting payment") indefinitely (the `checkout.session.expired` handler only knows PaymentOrders), and choosing again opened a second payable session. The dialog also promised "starts when your listing goes live" for a boat that is live and already featured.

## What
- `POST /api/v1/promotions/cancel/` `{target, listing_id?}`: expires the caller's pending sessions for that target at Stripe and marks them CANCELED. Foreign listing → 404.
- Opening a new checkout for the same listing/profile first closes the pending one ("replaced by a new checkout").
- Cancel URL carries `&listing=<id>`; My listings shows the cancelled / paid banner for promotions and calls the cancel endpoint.
- `PromotionDialog` gets `live` and `featuredUntil`: third bullet becomes "already featured until {date}; the new period continues from there" / "live, starts as soon as the payment is confirmed" (EN/IT/ES).

## Checks
- promotions: 15 passed. vitest listings + promotion: 164 passed. tsc clean.

author: mskazemi
body:
## Summary

Clean current-`main` replacement for conflicted #816. It preserves the exact branch-head identity reader/tests and reapplies the documentation onto the current Connector Control spec.

## Trust boundary

```text
authorized repository + branch
 -> untrusted GitHub ref object
 -> GitHubBranchHeadReader
 -> exact repository + branch + immutable commit object id
```

The reader fails closed unless the returned ref exactly matches `refs/heads/<requested-branch>`, targets a `commit`, and carries a valid immutable Git object id. Request repository/branch identity is validated before source I/O.

`GitHubBranchHeadBinding` remains identity evidence only: it has no `verified`, dispatch, candidate-ready, verification, acceptance, merge, or integration authority.

## Why replacement

#816 fell 41 commits behind while `CONNECTOR_CONTROL_API_V0_1.md` changed on main and became non-mergeable before any CI run. This PR is rebuilt directly on current main and contains only the intended reader, tests, and current-spec documentation delta.

## Related

Refs #575 #816 #819 #822.

## AI/tool provenance

Rebuilt with ChatGPT at the owner's request from #816 after verifying its divergence and preserving its code/tests exactly.

author: guilhermehenriquedasilva915-design
body:
Closes #15

## What this is

A transport, not a second pipeline. Upload a workshop recording to the VPS, get
`source_id`/`job_id`, close the laptop, ask later.

The audit found most of this already existed. The V1 Alpha worker is already a
persistent leased poll loop with crash recovery, and storage, validation, dedupe
and idempotency were already in place. Reused unchanged: `LocalStorage`,
`processing_jobs`/`processing_runs.checkpoint`, `claim_next_job`,
`transcribe_resumable`, the screen/OCR pass, `validate_and_hash`,
`find_source_by_hash`, `create_or_reuse_job`, `WatchService`, `safe_fields`.

**No new migration.** Source origin fits the existing `external_metadata` jsonb.

## Decisions (ADR 0009)

- **Loopback + SSH tunnel**, not a public port. No firewall change, no DNS, no
  certificate, no internet-facing listener. A bearer token is required anyway,
  because loopback is not authentication.
- **Native systemd**, not Docker. The runtime is already a native venv with pinned
  model caches, and the unit hardening provides the isolation containers would.

## Surface

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/health` | liveness; only unauthenticated route; returns a constant |
| `POST /v1/uploads` | stream in, register source, queue job |
| `GET /v1/sources/by-digest/{sha256}` | already held? lets the client skip a huge transfer |
| `GET /v1/jobs` / `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` | status |
| `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` | cancel |

CLI: `vorquel-watch remote configure|upload|status|list|cancel`.

## Security

- The API refuses to start without a token of >= 32 chars; comparison is
  `hmac.compare_digest`; every malformed header is indistinguishable from a wrong
  token.
- Auth runs **before the body is read**, so an unauthenticated caller cannot spend
  the host's disk. Test asserts nothing is written.
- Upload limits enforced in order: `Content-Length` required (411), oversized
  declaration refused before any transfer (413), free-space margin (507), then
  capped **again mid-stream** because Content-Length is a claim, then length and
  digest must match.
- The notebook holds only the API token, never the Supabase credential.
- Upload filenames are attacker-controlled: cleaned, stored as metadata, never
  used to build a path. Unverified bytes stage outside the content-addressed tree.
- Dedupe is decided on the digest **the server computed**, never one a client
  asserted.
- **Nothing added to the MCP surface** — still exactly 24 tools, `get_frame` still
  absent. Uploading and cancelling are operator actions, not model actions.
- No media in Supabase. Media/OCR/transcripts stay UNTRUSTED with
  `instruction_authority = NONE`.

## Tests

348 tests, 32 modules, all passing (was 271/28). New: `test_remote_auth` (11),
`test_remote_api` (34), `test_remote_client` (19), `test_remote_compatibility` (13).

E2E over a **real uvicorn server on real loopback sockets** with a real MP4 through
the real out-of-process probe: 27/27 checks green, including upload, queued-not-
processed, content-addressed storage, zero-byte re-upload, 415/404/400 rejections,
cancel, and state surviving a new connection. Persistence was stubbed so the run
wrote no rows to the live Supabase project — stated in
`docs/acceptance/remote-processing-v1-e2e.md` rather than implied.

## Dependencies

The `remote` extra adds **zero packages**: starlette, uvicorn and httpx were already
in the lock transitively via `mcp==2.2.0`. The extra only makes the imports explicit
at the already-pinned versions.

The lock diff also carries four unrelated upstream bumps (`filelock`, `httpcore2`,
`httpx2`, `pyjwt`) that the CI contract of comparing against a fresh resolution
forces. They are drift, not choices made here.

## CI

`--extra remote` added to the lock compile. The Linux job now proves the remote
modules import and the CLI exposes the commands on the platform the VPS runs.
New `scripts/ci/check_remote_api.py` gates three deployment invariants: refuses to
start without a token, defaults to loopback, adds nothing to the MCP surface.

## Not done, deliberately

- **No merge, no tag, no release, no branch deleted.**
- **No VPS deployment.** This work had no SSH access and invented no credentials.
  The runbook is exact copy-paste commands for you to run; the systemd units are
  untested on the real Oracle instance.
- **No long-workshop E2E.** A 10-test plan is written up in the acceptance doc.
- No firewall, DNS or production change of any kind.
- No RAG, embeddings, JEV or agent orchestration. Brain, Analyze, MCP and UI
  untouched; local mode still the default and still passing.

author: sarveshkd
body:
## Overview
This PR adds a complete automated installation and verification suite for ComfyUI + LTX-Video support. Users can now set up a fully configured LTX-Video environment with a single script.

## What's Included

### Installation Scripts
- **`install-ltx-video-windows.bat`** - Automated Windows NVIDIA GPU installer
- **`install-ltx-video-linux.sh`** - Automated Linux/macOS installer

Both scripts handle the complete setup pipeline:
1. Clone ComfyUI & ComfyUI-Manager
2. Create Python virtual environment
3. Install PyTorch with CUDA support
4. Install all dependencies
5. Configure low-VRAM mode
6. Create optimized launcher scripts
7. Generate setup guides

### Verification Script
- **`verify-ltx-video-setup.py`** - Post-installation validation
  - Checks Python version & dependencies
  - Validates CUDA/GPU availability
  - Detects LTX-Video models
  - Verifies installation completeness

### Documentation
- **`LTX-VIDEO-INSTALLER-README.md`** - Comprehensive 11KB guide
  - Quick start for Windows & Linux
  - RTX 5070 (8GB) specifications & presets
  - Troubleshooting common issues
  - Advanced VRAM configuration
  - Model download instructions
  - Performance optimization tips

## Key Features

✅ **Fully Automated** - Single command installation, no manual steps
✅ **RTX 5070 Optimized** - Pre-tuned for 8GB VRAM with low-VRAM mode
✅ **Cross-Platform** - Windows, Linux, and macOS support
✅ **Error Handling** - Clear error messages and recovery suggestions
✅ **Well-Documented** - 300+ lines of setup instructions
✅ **Post-Install Verification** - Python script validates complete setup

## Installation Usage

### Windows
```batch
mkdir C:\ComfyUI-LTX
cd C:\ComfyUI-LTX
REM Save install-ltx-video-windows.bat here
install-ltx-video-windows.bat
REM Download models from https://huggingface.co/Lightricks
run_gpu.bat
```

### Linux
```bash
mkdir ~/ComfyUI-LTX
cd ~/ComfyUI-LTX
chmod +x install-ltx-video-linux.sh
./install-ltx-video-linux.sh
# Download models from https://huggingface.co/Lightricks
./run_gpu.sh
```

## RTX 5070 (8GB) Presets

The installers configure these settings for optimal performance:
- Resolution: 512 × 512
- Frames: 25–40 (produces 3–5 second clips at 8 FPS)
- Steps: 20–25
- VRAM Mode: Low-VRAM with 1GB reserve
- Batch Size: 1

## Testing

The installation scripts have been validated for:
- ✅ Proper environment detection (Python 3.9+, Git)
- ✅ Repository cloning
- ✅ Virtual environment creation
- ✅ Dependency installation
- ✅ Launcher script generation
- ✅ Model directory setup

The verification script can be run post-install:
```bash
python scripts/verify-ltx-video-setup.py
```

## Related Issues
Addresses setup complexity for LTX-Video users on NVIDIA systems, particularly those with limited VRAM (6-8GB).

## Notes
- Scripts are idempotent - safe to run multiple times
- Virtual environment kept local to installation directory
- All configurations are user-editable after installation
- Model directories created but initially empty (users download separately)

author: hyang0129
body:
Part of #39. Resolves #29 (closes when the epic merges).

**Head SHA:** `cacc31edaa9b01c4d6aff1187715375760afdab3` (commits `02507bc` feature, `cacc31e` review fix) (based on `epic/39-dev-env-hardening` @ `9cb3a67`, which includes #30 / PR #45)

## What changed

- `scripts/dev-environment.mjs`
  - New exported `dependencyIdentity(dir)`: a deterministic, content-derived `sha256:<hex>` of an installed tree. It walks the tree in sorted order without following symlinks. Every entry adds its relative path and type. Files add their executable bit and a streamed SHA-256 of their contents, hashed up to 32 at a time. Symlinks add their target text only, so nothing outside the tree is read. FIFOs, sockets and devices add their type only and are never opened, because reading one could block. Each entry is hashed as one JSON array (`[path, type, …fields]`), so every path and symlink target is quoted and escaped and cannot forge or merge another entry. The records go in sorted path order, so the result does not depend on hashing concurrency.
  - `deploy`: the lockfile-equality precondition stays. After it, deploy computes `dependencies = { realpath, identity }`, where `realpath` is the resolved source `node_modules` that gets symlinked into the snapshot. It is recorded in `deployment.json`. The comment now says lockfile equality is a precondition, not proof of what is installed. Failed-deploy cleanup and previous-record preservation are unchanged, and the #25 tests pass unmodified.
  - New exported `verifyDependencies(snapshot, deployment)`. `start` calls it immediately after resolving the release, before the relay check, port check, auth preflights, the `daemon.json` intent record, and spawn. It refuses when:
    - `dependencies` is missing or malformed: "Dev deployment has no installed-dependency record (deployed by an older workflow); run npm run dev:deploy again"
    - the snapshot's `node_modules` link does not resolve to exactly the recorded realpath, including a missing link: "Snapshot node_modules resolves to X, not the deployed Y; reinstall matching dependencies and run npm run dev:deploy again"
    - the recomputed identity differs: "Installed dependencies changed since deploy (path: new != deployed old); reinstall matching dependencies and run npm run dev:deploy again"
  - The #30 start transaction is untouched.
- `docs/CLOUD_SETUP.md` (dev section): explains that the lockfile check is only a precondition, what the identity covers, the start-time refusal and how to recover, that pre-#29 deployments must be redeployed, and that the check runs at start only.
- `tests/dev-start-transaction.test.mjs`, `tests/dev-workflow.test.mjs`: **fixture setup only**. Their hand-written `deployment.json` records now carry a valid `dependencies` entry and a snapshot `node_modules` link, because `start` now refuses records without one. No assertion was changed, removed or loosened.

## Tests (new `tests/dev-dependencies.test.mjs`, 13 tests)

Each test uses a temporary git source with an ignored `node_modules` (nested files, an executable, an in-tree `.bin` symlink), a temporary dev home, and a real `deploy` with a mocked deployer (called 2 times). On `start`, the relay, port, auth and `saveRecord` are injected and observed.

- `deployment.json.dependencies.realpath === realpath(source/node_modules)`, the identity matches `sha256:[64 hex]` and equals a fresh recomputation, and the snapshot link resolves to it.
- **Positive control:** with the tree unchanged, `start` passes verification and reaches the injected relay stage (relay called once; `saveRecord` 0 times; no `daemon.json`).
- Editing, adding and removing a file, plus adding an empty directory, clearing an executable bit, and retargeting an in-tree symlink. Each makes `start` refuse with the actionable message **before spawning**: relay 0 calls, `saveRecord` (which writes the intent record right before spawn) 0 calls, and no `daemon.json`, `run.mjs` or `daemon.log`.
- The snapshot link is re-pointed at a copied directory whose identity is asserted to be **identical**, so only the realpath check can refuse it. `start` refuses on realpath before spawning. A missing link refuses too.
- A `deployment.json` without `dependencies` refuses with the redeploy instruction, before spawning.
- Unit test: the identity is deterministic across concurrency settings, is unaffected by changing a file outside the tree that a symlink points to, handles a FIFO without opening it, and changes when an entry is renamed.
- Framing test (review fix): these pairs must hash differently.
  - a symlink `x -> 't\n"y" d'` vs. `x -> 't'` plus an empty directory `y`;
  - a directory named `p d\n"q"` vs. directories `p` and `q`;
  - a symlink `x -> 't\n"z" l u'` vs. `x -> 't'` plus a symlink `z -> 'u'`.

## Sabotage

- With the identity comparison disabled (`if (false && identity !== …)`), **6 of 12 fail**: all six tree-mutation tests, including the file edit. The other 6 pass.
- With the realpath comparison disabled, **2 of 12 fail**: the re-pointed-link and missing-link tests.
- Both sabotages were reverted with `git checkout`, and the tree was clean before the runs below.
- Review fix: the new framing test **failed on `02507bc`** (A/B collision: both trees hashed to `sha256:2f9d7200…`; 12 pass, 1 fail). It passes after `cacc31e`. The path-with-newline pair already differed before the fix, because paths were JSON-quoted, so it is a regression guard only.

## Timing (read-only measurement)

`dependencyIdentity` over this worktree's freshly installed `node_modules` (`npm ci`): **576 MB, 11,090 entries, 16 symlinks, no special files**. It gave the same hash on 3 consecutive runs, taking **0.83 s, 0.70 s and 0.65 s**. After the framing fix, it took **0.80 s, 0.68 s and 0.65 s**. These times are with a warm file cache; the cache was not purged, so a cold start will be slower. That is well under the ~10 s limit.

## Verification on `cacc31e` (clean tree)

- Focused dev tests (`tests/dev-*.test.mjs`): **44 tests, 44 pass, 0 fail**
- `npm test`: **155 tests, 155 pass, 0 fail**, 0 skipped
- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0
- `npm run cloud:typecheck`: exit 0
- `npm run cloud:test`: 2 files, **36 tests passed**
- `npm run test:ui`: **not run**. Its web server binds the fixed port 4188, which the epic's test rules forbid outside an injected port. This story changes no UI code.

## Known limitations

- The check runs at `start` only. A dependency change made after the daemon starts is not detected until the next start. The window between verification and spawn is also not closed.
- Only the executable bit of each file's mode is part of the identity. Owner and timestamps are not.

body:
## Summary

ULYS-158.5 / ULYS-218 — FR-ORCA-009 + FR-ORCA-010 + FR-ORCA-011 bundle 实装 (per `docs/ecosystem-survey/orca-design-survey.md` v1.0 §3).

本 PR 是 3-ID bundle 的 **trait 抽象 + 默认实现 + 单元测试** 层, 与 sibling ULYS-194 (FR-ORCA-009 数据面) / ULYS-195 (FR-ORCA-011 数据面) 平行 ship:

- **ULYS-194 / FR-ORCA-009**: `worktree-service::StartFromPicker` 数据面 (PR #99 merged origin/dev) — 真实 git ls-remote / branch / log 抓取
- **ULYS-195 / FR-ORCA-011**: `worktree-service::ExternalWorktree` 数据面 (PR merged origin/dev) — 真实 `git worktree list --porcelain` v2 解析
- **ULYS-218 (本 PR) / FR-ORCA-009/010/011**: `worktree-shared-dir` trait 抽象 + Default impl + 跨 trait 桥接 stub

## What's in this PR

`crates/worktree-shared-dir/` (modified, 4 files, +536/-40 LOC):

| File | Change | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml` | +3 lines | `tokio` 从 dev-deps 升到 deps (RealStartFromPicker::fetch 用 spawn_blocking) |
| `src/start_from_picker.rs` | +10 lines | 修 2 bugfix (SharedDirError::new &str 参数 + map_err 闭包) |
| `src/branch_naming.rs` | +123/-? lines | 3 bugfix + FR-ORCA-010 完整 4 档优先级链 (linear > github > user > workspace) |
| `src/external_worktree_import.rs` | +440 lines (NEW) | FR-ORCA-011 trait 抽象层 (scan / import / cleanup_stale) + InMemory 实现 + 4 错误码 |

### FR-ORCA-009 Start-from Picker (`start_from_picker.rs`)

- `StartFrom` enum: `RepoBaseRef / LocalBranch(String) / CommitSha(String) / RemoteBranch(String)`
- `StartFromPicker` trait + `PickerCandidate` + `PickerCandidateKind`
- `RealStartFromPicker::fetch` (借用 git-adapter GitProvider, 本 PR 只修 2 个编译 bugfix, 数据面走 ULYS-194)
- 既有 865 行 (per `wc -l`) 全 cargo test 84/84 通过

### FR-ORCA-010 Branch 命名优先级链 (`branch_naming.rs`)

- `BranchNamer` trait + `BranchNamingInput` { linear_branch_name, github_pr_branch, user_input, workspace_name } + `BranchNamingResult` { branch_name, source }
- `DefaultBranchNamer::derive` 严格 4 段优先级 + 空字符串 guard + emoji shortcode 表 (`🚀` → `rocket`) + dedupe-leading-shortcode 后处理 + 64 字符限制 + `[a-z0-9-_/]` charset
- 27 条 unit test 全过 (含 `derive_priority_linear_github_user_workspace` 4 档全测 + `derive_falls_back_to_workspace_derived` + `derive_empty_user_input_falls_through`)

### FR-ORCA-011 External Worktree Import (`external_worktree_import.rs`)

- `ExternalWorktreeImport` trait (3 async 方法: scan / import / cleanup_stale, 对应 AC-1/2/3)
- `InMemoryExternalWorktreeImport` (in-process state-backed 实现)
- `ExternalWorktreeImportError` 4 变体 → `SharedDirError` 6-field 映射 (4 个 `WSD.EXT_*` 错误码)
- 13 条 `#[tokio::test]` UT 覆盖 scan / import / cleanup_stale 全部分支 + serde round-trip

### 3 个 bugfix (本期 self-review 修)

(a) `sanitize_branch_chars`: 旧 impl 用 `last_was_dash = c == '-'` 在循环里被持续重置, 连续 `-` 不合并. 改用 `out.ends_with('-')` + 末尾 trim loop. 通过 `feat---x---y` → `feat-x-y` 测试.

(b) `DefaultBranchNamer::derive`: 加 `!name.is_empty()` guard, `user_input = Some("")` fallback 不被误判为有效. 通过 `derive_empty_user_input_falls_through` + `derive_all_empty_inputs_truly_empty_errors` 测试.

(c) `normalize_branch`: 新增 `dedupe_leading_shortcode()` 后处理, 检测 `<shortcode>-<shortcode>-...` 冗余前缀去掉首段. 通过 `derive_falls_back_to_workspace_derived` (期望 `rocket-launch`) 测试.

## Rebase note

本分支基于 `cebba99c` (origin/main merge base), 已 **rebase onto origin/dev b235df86** (`da2729e7` 新 SHA), 0 conflict. force-with-lease 推送, origin 跟踪已建立.

## Verification (current worktree, on top of origin/dev)

```
cargo check -p worktree-shared-dir --lib --no-default-features -j 4  → 0 error
cargo test  -p worktree-shared-dir --lib -j 4                        → 84 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy -p worktree-shared-dir --lib --tests --no-deps -j 4    → 0 warning (本 crate)
cargo check --workspace --lib --tests --no-default-features -j 4    → 0 error (47 crate, 1 unrelated git-adapter deprecation + 1 star-saga dead_code pre-existing)
```

## Honest divergences from brief

- **bugfix-only on `start_from_picker.rs`**: 既有 871 行已 ship, 本 PR 仅修 2 个编译 error + 升 tokio dep. 数据面走 ULYS-194 `worktree-service::StartFromPicker`.
- **`InMemoryExternalWorktreeImport` 是 in-process 实现**: 真实 `RealExternalWorktreeImport` 桥接到 `worktree-service::scan_external_worktrees` (ULYS-195 数据面) 留 sibling followup (见 Out of scope).
- **branch_naming emoji 表只覆盖 ~30 个常用 shortcode**: 不维护全 GitHub 30k+ emoji list. caller 可扩展.

## Out of scope (per §剩余工作 / P1 followup)

留 sibling sub-issue, 不在本 PR 范围:

- ❌ 前端 `frontend/src/components/worktree/` Start-from Picker modal (4 选 1 radio) — ~1.5 周, 需 frontend agent worktree

author: dante01yoon
body:
## Summary

billing-web has only ever had one automatic path (none) and one manual path (production). Test should track `main` the way `billing-web-test` is meant to; staging and production stay deliberate, dispatched by a person. This PR splits that into three: test auto-deploys on every push to `main` that touches billing-web or its workspace deps, and staging/production stay behind a `workflow_dispatch` choice.

## Why

- `billing-web-test` (`testbilling.comfy.org`) existed as a Vercel project with no deploy path at all.
- `billing-web` (`billing.comfy.org`) had a manual production job but no staging path, even though the `staging` custom environment (`stagingbilling.comfy.org`) is already provisioned on that project.
- The preview workflow's path filter missed `packages/account-core/**`, `packages/account-ui/**` and `packages/billing-contract/**`, so an SDK-only PR never refreshed the preview even though billing-web imports all three at runtime.

## How

`.github/workflows/ci-vercel-billing-web-preview.yaml` keeps only the PR-preview job (label-gated, its path filter now includes the SDK packages billing-web actually imports, `packages/ingest-types/**` included since `account-core` imports it directly).

`.github/workflows/ci-vercel-billing-web-deploy.yaml` (new) owns the rest, both as prebuilt Vercel CLI deploys — the `billing-web` and `billing-web-test` Vercel projects keep `github.enabled: false` and Ignored Build Step `exit 0`, so a git-triggered build never deploys:

- `deploy-test`: `push` to `main` with the same workspace-dep path filter as the preview job, plus `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Deploys `--prod` into `billing-web-test` using a new `VERCEL_BILLING_WEB_TEST_PROJECT_ID` secret (same org id/token as the existing secrets). `concurrency` caps it at one test deploy at a time, newest wins. Its own `preflight` output skips it when that secret is unset.
- `deploy-manual`: `workflow_dispatch` with an `environment` choice input (`staging` | `production`, default `staging`), gated to `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`. `staging` runs `vercel pull --yes --environment=staging`, `vercel build --target=staging`, `vercel deploy --prebuilt --target=staging --archive=tgz` against the `staging` custom environment on the `billing-web` project. `production` keeps the existing `--prod` commands. No new GitHub Environment: no other prod Vercel deploy job in this repo uses `environment:` protection, so I didn't invent one for billing-web either.

`apps/billing-web/README.md`'s Deployment section now documents all four targets, the two workflows, and the required secrets including `VERCEL_BILLING_WEB_TEST_PROJECT_ID` = `prj_IMdXT8qFYty3Our9LfUwylIXYG79` (project ids aren't sensitive, matching the existing secret convention).

## AS IS / TO BE

This is a CI workflow change with no UI surface, so there is nothing to screenshot; the AS IS / TO BE is the deploy behavior itself.

**AS IS:** `billing-web-test` has no deploy path at all. `billing-web` production only deploys via manual dispatch of `ci-vercel-billing-web-preview.yaml`, and that same file mixes preview, and production concerns. There is no staging deploy path despite the `staging` custom environment already existing on the project. PRs that only touch `account-core`/`account-ui`/`billing-contract` never refresh the billing-web preview.

**TO BE:** `ci-vercel-billing-web-preview.yaml` only builds PR previews. `ci-vercel-billing-web-deploy.yaml` auto-deploys `billing-web-test` on every push to `main` touching billing-web or its workspace deps, and deploys `staging` or `production` on a `workflow_dispatch` with an `environment` choice input. Preview and test path filters both include the SDK packages billing-web imports.

## Environments

| Environment | Host | Vercel project | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR preview | `*.vercel.app` alias | `billing-web` | `billing-preview` label on a pull request |
| test | `testbilling.comfy.org` | `billing-web-test` | every push to `main` touching billing-web or its deps |
| staging | `stagingbilling.comfy.org` | `billing-web` (`staging` custom environment) | manual dispatch |
| production | `billing.comfy.org` | `billing-web` | manual dispatch |

## Test

- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci-vercel-billing-web-deploy.yaml .github/workflows/ci-vercel-billing-web-preview.yaml` — clean.
- `staging`'s exact CLI flags (`vercel pull --environment=<custom-env>`, `vercel build --target=<custom-env>`, `vercel deploy --prebuilt --target=<custom-env>`) are verified against the current Vercel CLI docs (`vercel build`, `vercel deploy`, `vercel pull` reference pages), not guessed.
- First real run happens after merge, on the next push to `main` touching billing-web (test) and on a manual dispatch (staging/production) — I don't have Vercel credentials to dry-run this locally.

## Required secret

Add `VERCEL_BILLING_WEB_TEST_PROJECT_ID` = `prj_IMdXT8qFYty3Our9LfUwylIXYG79` to the repo's Actions secrets before merge, or the test job skips with a notice instead of deploying.

**Do not merge** — flagging for review.

author: keelerm84
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of forward-porting concurrent multi-key support from v8 ([#817](https://github.com/launchdarkly/ld-relay/pull/817)) to v9.

**Stacked on [#893](https://github.com/launchdarkly/ld-relay/pull/893)** (phase 1), so this PR is based on `mk/SDK-3189/credential-model` and its diff shows only phase 2's changes. GitHub retargets it to `feat/concurrent-keys-v9` automatically once #893 merges.

`EnvironmentRep` gains `sdkKeys` and `mobileKeys` arrays of `{ key, value, expiry?, hasViews? }`, and `EnvironmentParams` gains the corresponding accepted-key slices. `ToParams` always leaves both non-nil, synthesizing them from the singular `sdkKey` and `mobKey` fields when a payload carries no arrays, so old-format and new-format payloads produce the same model. The parse path does not set `DisallowUnknownFields`, so a relay predating concurrent keys ignores the arrays and keeps using the singular fields.

`BuildAcceptedSet` converts those params into the `AcceptedSet` the credential rotator consumes. It is the single home for the anchor invariant, shared by auto-configuration and the offline archive, and it filters out view-scoped keys and names them so callers can log what they dropped. Credential identity is the value, not the wire identifier, so renaming a key produces an unchanged set.

Nothing calls `BuildAcceptedSet` yet, so no environment behavior changes.

### Why `ExpiringSDKKey` is still here

Its callers — `relay/autoconfig_actions.go` and `relay/filedata_actions.go` — belong to phase 3, so removing the field now would break the build. `ToParams` keeps it and the accepted set populated from the same wire fields, so they cannot diverge. It is removed along with `EnvContext.UpdateCredential`.

### Why the cache model version moves to 2

The shape of `EnvironmentRep` changed. Without the bump, a relay running the old model reads a new-format cache entry and silently strips the key arrays from it — the failure mode called out as a High finding in the review of #817. On a mismatch the read now rejects the entry and falls back to the stream.

### One validation gap fixed

A payload listing one credential value twice, once plain and once marked `hasViews`, admitted the value through the plain entry while reporting the marked entry as rejected — so relay accepted a credential *and* logged that it had rejected it, which is the worst outcome for anyone auditing the logs. The builder de-duplicates by value and keeps the first metadata it recorded, so filtering entry-by-entry was not enough; the view-scoped rule is now a property of the value. A marker on the anchor's own entry is still deliberately disregarded, since dropping the designated key would take the whole environment down.

Part of SDK-3191, under epic SDK-3188.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Overview**
> **Phase 2** extends the shared environment wire model with **`sdkKeys`** and **`mobileKeys`** arrays (`{ key, value, expiry?, hasViews? }`). **`EnvironmentParams`** now carries **`AcceptedSDKKeys`** / **`AcceptedMobileKeys`**; **`ToParams`** always fills them—from the arrays when present, or synthesized from legacy **`sdkKey`** / **`mobKey`** (including expiring SDK) so old and new payloads normalize the same way.
> 
> **`BuildAcceptedSet`** is added as the single place to turn those params into a credential **`AcceptedSet`**: anchor and primary-mobile invariants, expiring keys from the arrays (not **`sdkKey.expiring`**), rejection of structurally bad payloads, and dropping view-scoped keys (with names returned for logging). A duplicate-value **`hasViews`** bug is fixed so a value marked view-scoped anywhere is never admitted. **`ExpiringSDKKey`** remains for phase 3 callers; nothing invokes **`BuildAcceptedSet`** yet, so runtime credential behavior is unchanged.
> 
> **`CurrentModelVersion`** is bumped **1 → 2** so autoconfig cache entries with the new shape are not read as v1 and silently lose the key arrays.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e432fb83df2df3d2189355e000c8bd9ff3f5b438. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Makes the native `chqparse` stack overflow exploitable **directly from the iOS demo app**, end to end.

Two changes:

**1. Unclamped field encoding.** `ChqEncoder` previously clamped every field to 48 bytes; now it emits each field verbatim (real length as `field_len`). A memo longer than 256 bytes entered in the deposit flow overflows the parser's `char buf[256]` in `extract_field`.

**2. Raw hex memo payload.** A UTF-8 `String` can't carry the arbitrary bytes (nulls, code addresses) a full control-flow hijack needs, so the deposit setup screen gains a "Raw capture payload (security testing)" toggle + hex field. When enabled, the memo record's bytes come from the decoded hex instead of the text:

```swift
struct Fields { var micr, payee, memo: String; var rawMemo: Data? }   // rawMemo overrides memo bytes
// submit():
if rawPayloadEnabled { fields.rawMemo = Data(hexString: rawPayloadHex) }
```

So the app can submit `<256+ padding><saved rbp><&__audit_debug_hook>` and drive the overflow into a hijack to the parser's `__audit_debug_hook` "win" path (which `_exit(42)`s and writes the `PWNED_BY_QUICKDEPOSIT_UPLOAD` banner the endpoint returns as `parser_exit` / `parser_stderr`).

Adds a `Data(hexString:)` helper; updates `ios/README.md`.

## Validation
Being validated on a macOS child Devin: build the backend in Docker (Linux x86-64, `-no-pie -z execstack`, per `service/native/Makefile`), compute the offset + `__audit_debug_hook` address, run the app in the iOS Simulator, enter the payload in the raw-payload field, and confirm `parser_exit=42` + the PWNED banner. PR will be updated with the result. Not buildable on this Linux box (Swift/iOS needs macOS + Xcode).

Audit backlog, medium: *select_by_distance breaks equal-height ties by a fixed rightmost-wins rule; scipy's order is effectively arbitrary*.

**Problem.** Of two equal peaks closer than the distance, the rightmost always won, and the code comment claimed that matched scipy. It cannot match: scipy's tie order comes from an unstable sort.

**Fix.** A deliberate rule: the earlier peak (nearer the onset) wins, pinned by a test. A taller later peak still wins.

**Measured.** Tied pairs at distance 9: [25, 44] → [20, 40]. No corpus reading moves: golden 24/24.

**Gates.** cargo test 199/199. overtone-bench golden 24/24, nogrid 3/3.

author: jdegreef
body:
Follow-up to #3164.

## Change
A language that has every interface key but still holds declared English placeholders used to **PASS** the Interface check. It now **FAILs, but the failure can be forced**:

| Interface state | Status | Can force past it? |
|---|---|---|
| All keys, all translated | PASS | — |
| All keys, N English placeholders | FAIL: "N string(s) still in English as a placeholder, awaiting translation." | **yes** ("launch anyway") |
| Missing keys / no catalogue | FAIL | no: the reader build would fail |

**Why forceable:** some placeholders, like the feedback form, reach readers in English, so they shouldn't pass silently. But the build accepts declared debt, so launching past them is a judgement call, not a guaranteed red deploy. The admin page already handles forceable failures: it shows "launch anyway".

## What you'll see after deploy
- **ar, hi, lg, sw and uk (25 placeholders each)** show "not ready" with an **Interface** chip on `/admin/language-health`, and their readiness score drops until those keys are translated.
- Languages that are already live are not affected. This only gates the go-live action.
- Admins can still turn off `require_complete_ui` for a language to lower the bar. `test_editing_the_bar_changes_the_verdict` now does this too.

## Also
- Updated the `Check.forceable` and `require_complete_ui` comments, the module docstring, and the sermon-questions skill, which now warns that new placeholders turn those languages' Interface check into a forceable FAIL.

## Tests
- `library` + `accounts`: 1637 tests OK, run before the review edits.
- `tests_languages` + `tests_admin_dashboard` re-run after the review edits and the rebase: OK.
- No migration: the model change is a comment only.

Ran /simplify and /code-review high; findings folded in.

Asked after the 23 September drive: tapping a person in CarPlay should say what they said — all of it. Until now Siri read the one preview line the directory holds per conversation.

author: sajclarke
body:
Closes #2587

> **Stacked on #2803** — merge that first. Until it does, this PR's diff also shows its commit.

## Why

A reviewer opening a case sees `HANDLERS MALE`, `HAS FOOD LICENCE`, and a date exploded into an `EVENT TO → DAY / YEAR / MONTH` cascade, while the MDA email for the very same submission reads cleanly.

The CMS cannot fix this on its own: the payload carries no field labels, no step titles, no ordering, no visibility information — and no form identifier to look any of it up with. A repo-wide grep there for `formId` / `form_id` / `stepTitle` returns zero hits.

## What

`buildMappedCasePayload` now also emits, when the hydrated contract and the audit trail are both in hand:

```ts
sections: [{ stepId, title, fields: [{ fieldId, label, value }] }]
form_id: string
form_version: string
```

- `form_data` is **untouched** — it stays the machine-readable record for export and search. This is purely additive.
- `value` is pre-formatted for every type **except** `file`, which stays a raw node array so the CMS keeps `attachFileUrls` / `isFileNode` / `FileLink` — signed URLs and image thumbnails, which beat the email's flat filename list.
- `WebhookProcessor` already resolves the hydrated contract (`webhook.processor.ts:107`) and holds `payload.meta`, so this costs **zero extra I/O**.

## Safe to deploy before any CMS work

`CasePayloadSchema` is a plain `z.object`, so unknown keys are stripped rather than rejected — that is already happening to `higher_risk`. This can land and deploy alone, and case-management#288 can then be built against real payloads.

## Verification

- 8 new tests: labels from the contract, contract ordering, a date rendered as a string, a file still arriving as nodes, a branch-skipped question absent, `form_data` byte-identical with and without sections, no sections without an audit trail, and the audit trail threaded through the processor.
- `nx run api:test` — 1635 passing. `nx run-many -t build --exclude=landing` — green.

## Reviewer notes

- One fixture fix: `makeMappedPayload`'s `meta` was cast to `SubmissionAuditTrail` while carrying only `submittedAt`. It now carries the audit trail it claimed to.
- **`higher_risk` is still being dropped on the floor** by the CMS — we compute and send it as a deliberate reviewer signal (#2065) and zod strips it silently. Worth its own issue: surface it there, or stop sending it.

author: thxcode
body:
## Defect

On the published `vllm0.29.0` runners, a decode engine configured as `MultiConnector(MooncakeConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector)` (both `kv_consumer`) exits on the first request whose prompt the prefill side has already written to the store:

```
AssertionError: Missing current block table for store request ...
```

Call chain: `Scheduler.schedule` -> `_build_kv_connector_meta` -> `MultiConnector.build_connector_meta` -> `MooncakeStoreConnector.build_connector_meta` -> `MooncakeStoreScheduler._apply_current_save_block_ids`.

## Root cause

`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py` at v0.29.0:

1. The prompt is a hit for both children. `MultiConnector.get_num_new_matched_tokens` assigns the request to the first child with matched tokens (`MooncakeConnector`, async load) and `update_state_after_alloc` calls the store child with `num_external_tokens=0`, so the store's `LoadSpec` stays `can_load=False`.
2. The request waits for remote KV and is scheduled neither as new nor as cached, so it lands in the "pending load specs not yet scheduled" branch (lines 366-391), which builds its `ReqMeta` with `skip_save=None` (line 388). With `can_load=False`, `ReqMeta.from_request_tracker` turns that into `can_save=True`.
3. The core snapshots current block tables only for scheduled requests (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `KVConnectorBlockState`), so `_apply_current_save_block_ids` (line 424) finds no table and asserts.

The assertion was introduced by upstream vllm-project/vllm#51358 (`6b110badbb`), first released in v0.29.0. v0.27.1 has the same branch without the assertion.

**Upstream has already fixed this** in vllm-project/vllm#54643 (`34b1e9f7a6`), first released in v0.30.0 (also in v0.29.1rc0; no v0.29.x final carries it): the branch now skips a `LoadSpec` whose load this connector does not own (`if load_spec is None or not load_spec.can_load: continue`).

## Fix

Backport the #54643 hunk verbatim, with line numbers rebased onto v0.29.0, by the two paths the MooncakeConnector Prometheus fix used (766ef2f, ecab586):

- `pack/.post_operation/20260924_vllm_patch_mooncake_store_pending_load/`: patches the published `cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0`, `cuda12.9-vllm0.29.0` (amd64 and arm64) and `rocm7.2-vllm0.29.0` (amd64) images in place. It is idempotent, asserts the patch landed, imports the patched module, and ends with the dependency probe and `vllm-deps` export stage, as the post operation README requires.
- `pack/{cuda,rocm}/patches/vllm/003_mooncake_store_rejected_pending_load.patch`: carries the same hunk into new 0.29.0 builds, so that a rebuild does not ship the defect again and overwrite the in-place repair. Byte-identical between the two sides.

Why not `skip_save=is_consumer`, which the sibling branches use: it clears a consumer, but a `kv_both` engine still trips the same assertion. A request that has not computed anything has nothing to save under any role, and upstream's fix is what v0.30.0 ships.

Not affected: `cann` builds on vLLM 0.23.0, whose store scheduler has no such assertion, and vllm-ascend's kv pool runs its own scheduler instead of `MooncakeStoreConnector`'s.

## Interaction with #280

v0.30.0 still has `skip_save=None` in that branch (line 399), and the assertion is still there (line 444), but #54643's guard two lines above means the branch is only reached with `can_load=True`, where `ReqMeta.from_request_tracker` forces `skip_save=True`. It emits no save job, so the assertion cannot fire from this path; the reproduction below passes on an unpatched v0.30.0 tree. The patch is therefore meant for 0.29.0 only and does not apply to 0.30.0 (`git apply --check`: v0.29.0 forward passes; v0.30.0 forward fails, reverse passes).

#280 moves the pack path to 0.30.0, which already contains the fix. `003_*.patch` is refused there (GNU patch: "Reversed (or previously applied) patch detected", exit 1), and the `Dockerfile.vllm` patch loop stops the build. Whichever of the two merges second needs to delete `pack/{cuda,rocm}/patches/vllm/003_mooncake_store_rejected_pending_load.patch` as part of the 0.30.0 bump. The post operation is unaffected: it pins 0.29.0 and skips a tree that already carries the fix.

## Verification

- `git apply --check` of `003_*.patch` against v0.29.0 passes; against v0.30.0 the forward check fails and the reverse check passes, which shows the change is already upstream there.
- GNU patch 2.7.6 applies `001`, `002` and `003` in the build's order onto a v0.29.0 tree; the patched `scheduler.py` compiles.
- Reproduction in the style of `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py`: a request with a rejected `LoadSpec`, parked unscheduled, with the block state the core would build (no entry for it).

  | tree | upstream #54643 regression test | repro, `kv_consumer` | repro, `kv_both` |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | v0.29.0 | fails | `AssertionError: Missing current block table ...` | `AssertionError: Missing current block table ...` |
  | v0.29.0 + `003` | passes | passes | passes |
  | v0.29.0 + `skip_save=is_consumer` | fails | passes | fails |
  | v0.30.0 | passes | passes | passes |

  The existing `test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py` suite (39 tests) passes on v0.29.0 + `003`.
- The post operation's script run over a v0.29.0 tree: the first run patches it (result byte-identical to the tree `003` produces), the second is a no-op. A v0.30.0 tree is left untouched. A stub `scheduler.py` is refused at the patch step.
- `expand_matrix.sh` for the post operation yields exactly the five published platform tags listed in `runner.py.json` for vLLM 0.29.0.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files and `pytest` (228 passed).

Not verified here: building the post operation against the real published images. That runs in the Pack workflow with `post_operation` set, after this merges.

author: ithealthtech
body:
First half of milestone M3 (accounts and security). M3b (API, imports and exports, 0.2 migration, branding, client portal) follows.

## Sign-in and accounts
- **Passkeys (WebAuthn):** use one as the second step after the password, or sign in with it alone when it verifies the person (PIN or biometrics). Staff can enroll a passkey instead of an authenticator app.
- **Recovery codes:** 10 single-use codes, stored as hashes and shown once. They can be replaced from the account page.
- **Remember this browser:** skips the second step on that browser for 30 days. People can see and remove remembered browsers.
- **Sessions:** a list of where you're signed in, with remote sign-out. Admins can sign a user out everywhere.
- **Confirm your password:** changing people, groups, email settings, passkeys or recovery codes, and exporting logs, all need the password entered in the last 10 minutes. The app asks for it and then retries the action.
- **Forgot password by email:** the link works once, expires in 1 hour, and never reveals whether an account exists. Using it signs the person out everywhere, and two-step verification still applies at the next sign-in.

## Administration
- **Groups:** set per-client access for a team in one place. Restricted passwords can list groups as well as people.
- **Email settings:** a Microsoft 365 preset (`smtp.office365.com`, port 587, STARTTLS) or any SMTP server. The SMTP password is encrypted with the master key, and there's a test-send button.
- **Expirations page and dashboard card:** asset date fields marked as expiry dates, password rotations, and document reviews. Alert emails go out 30/14/7 days before (configurable) and on the day, plus a Monday digest, each sent once per person.
- **Tamper-evident security log:**
  - Database triggers hash-chain every event and refuse edits.
  - "Verify now" pinpoints an edited row.
  - A checkpoint signed with a key derived from the master key catches deleted recent events.
  - CSV export neutralises spreadsheet formulas, and retention is configurable.
- **Migration `0004`:** adds everything above.

## Bugs found and fixed
- **Sign-out:** signing out left the workspace on screen until a reload. This bug predates M3a.
- **Audit log, concurrent writes:** simultaneous security events could get IDs out of chain order. IDs are now assigned after the chain lock is taken.
- **Audit log, verification:** verification sorted event IDs as text, so logs with 10 or more events showed a false break.

## Verification
- **Server tests:** 45 of 45 pass. The 14 new ones include a software passkey authenticator, captured reset and alert emails, tamper detection, and 30 concurrent writers.
- **Browser tests:** 12 of 12 Playwright tests pass with axe WCAG 2.2 AA checks. They cover recovery-code sign-in, a virtual-authenticator passkey, Microsoft 365 settings, groups, expirations, and log verification. The e2e server now runs on `localhost` because passkeys need a host name.
- **Other checks:** lint, typecheck, and the legacy 0.2 tests pass. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 0 vulnerabilities.

author: quntao-z
body:
Closes #3187

## What broke

Node ships `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` as its own globals. Vitest's jsdom environment only
copies a window key onto `globalThis` when that key is absent there, so Node's pair wins: reading
`globalThis.localStorage` returns Node's `undefined` (no `--localstorage-file` was given) and
`globalThis.sessionStorage` returns Node's store rather than the document's.

## Reproduced

Measured on **Node 26.10.0**, `npx vitest run` in `client`:

| | test files | tests |
|---|---|---|
| before | 8 failed, 100 passed | **128 failed**, 1052 passed |
| after | 109 passed | **1179 passed** |

Node 20.20.2 with the same change: 109 files, 1179 tests, all passing. No behaviour moves on the
version CI pins.

## Two corrections to the issue body

- The title says Node 22+. Web Storage is behind `--experimental-webstorage` through Node 24, so
  the suite is green on 24.19.0 as well. The globals are unflagged from **Node 26**, which is where
  this bites.
- The body says there is no second place to read the real store from. There is: the jsdom
  environment leaves the JSDOM instance on `globalThis.jsdom`, and `globalThis.jsdom.window` is the
  real jsdom window rather than the global, so the document's own stores are reachable through it.
  That is what the repair uses, so the suite keeps jsdom's real `Storage` (quota, `key()`, `length`,
  string coercion) instead of a hand-rolled stand-in.

## The change

Harness only, per the issue's constraint. `client/src/setupTests.ts` adopts the document's two
stores onto the global when the global is not already holding them. No product code moves.

`client/src/__tests__/jsdomStorageHarness.test.ts` pins it. Mutation-checked: with the adoption call
neutered, 5 of 5 assertions go red on Node 26.

## Why CI still cannot see this, and why that is not fixed here

The issue notes every workflow pins `node-version: 20`. Bumping it is not a one-line change:
**Node 25 removed Corepack from the distribution**, and this repo declares
`"packageManager": "yarn@4.15.0"` with no bundled release under `.yarn/releases`. On Node 26,
`corepack enable` fails and the install step dies before any test runs. Making CI exercise a current
Node therefore needs a Yarn provisioning change of its own, and folding a second full client-suite
run into the one required check would also double its flake exposure.

`client/package.json` declares `"node": ">=20.19.0"`, so Node 26 is inside the supported range and
this gap is worth its own issue. Filing that is left to the issue owner rather than assumed here.

author: nathanvale
body:
## Summary

Nathan can connect the Connectors Figma route to the hosted MCP server through an attended MCPorter login. Later route reads reuse its isolated grant and expose only `whoami`, leaving principal verification and design reads for later work.

This local interoperability route uses the borrowed `clientName: "Claude Code"` after MCPorter's own name was refused. It does not establish Figma approval of an independently named Connectors client.

## Boundaries

- The endpoint is fixed at `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, imports are disabled, and only `whoami` is admitted. Ad-hoc route and transport overrides are refused.
- Attended `auth` is confined to the declared Figma OAuth route. Ordinary `list` and `call` use cached credentials with `--no-oauth`, so reads do not open consent.
- The scoped `auth --reset` clears only the local `figma-connectors` grant before reauthorization. It does not prove remote revocation. A live reset was not run because it would clear Nathan's working grant.
- Attended `--no-browser` auth may print authorization or redirect URLs into an agent-captured terminal transcript. The skill instructs agents to keep that output out of chat and additional logs.
- Canva and Atlassian authentication remain unchanged. No Figma design-content tool is admitted, and no private design content was read.

## Validation

- On the isolated `figma-connectors` route at `2dacadc8`, a cached listing first returned HTTP 401. Nathan completed attended Chrome consent; `auth` exited 0. A later cached `list --schema --json --timeout 15000` exited 0 with status `ok` and exposed only `whoami`. No Figma tool was called, so the authenticated principal is still unverified.
- On current head `9eaaf583`, `auth --no-browser --json` exited 0 using the existing isolated grant, and a later cached schema listing exited 0 with status `ok` and exposed only `whoami`. Fresh attended consent was observed on its ancestor; no new consent or live reset was needed on this head. MCPorter 0.14.0 was used for the live route.
- Process tests cover exact route selection, other-route refusals, ambient `figma` grant isolation, and synthetic scoped reset. The 325-test Connectors suite, plugin and repository typechecks, Biome, changed-code Fallow, strict Claude plugin validation, and an independent read-only review passed locally. The repository CI check passed on `9eaaf583`. Its prior run failed in an unchanged Playground timing test, whose focused local rerun passed.

## Related

Related: [Spec #67](https://github.com/nathanvale/dotfiles-private/issues/67) and [ticket #68](https://github.com/nathanvale/dotfiles-private/issues/68) now track Nathan's accepted local route. #68 remains open until this PR is merged and the merged result is verified. Principal verification, design reads, and fresh Harness activation remain later work.

author: phancao
body:
## Vì sao

#8 chuyển `build` và `release` sang runner `galaxy` vì trần chi tiêu Actions chặn job hosted, và đã kiểm tra kỹ rằng kho không có bước deploy. Điều nó bỏ sót là **kho này công khai**:

- Với trigger `pull_request`, PR từ fork chạy **workflow do người mở PR viết**. Chỉ cần kho có một runner đã đăng ký là họ đổi `runs-on` và chạy mã trên máy của runner đó.
- Runner `galaxy` nằm trên máy staging và chạy bằng user đang giữ **token GitHub cá nhân** (`~/.git-credentials`, `gh auth`).
- Chính sách duyệt PR fork hiện chỉ áp cho `first_time_contributors`.

## Đã làm (24/09/2026)

- **Gỡ runner**: dừng service, gỡ unit systemd, huỷ đăng ký. Kho giờ có 0 runner, và không còn tiến trình nào trên máy.
- Tới lúc gỡ, **chưa có PR fork hay lượt chạy nào từ kho khác**.
- PR này đưa `build.yml` và `release.yml` về `ubuntu-latest`, kèm chú thích ngay tại `runs-on`. Nếu không sửa, mọi job sẽ treo ở trạng thái queued mãi mãi vì không còn runner nào mang nhãn `galaxy`.

## Lưu ý

Job hosted sẽ **đỏ với 0 bước** cho tới 1/10, khi trần 5 USD tự hết chặn. Điều này có chủ ý: một job đỏ vẫn hơn một cửa mở vào máy.

Galaxy-Paca cũng đã gỡ runner, và không cần sửa workflow vì main của nó vốn toàn dùng `ubuntu-latest`.

author: fdcastel
body:
Part of #618 (item 2), following the outage in #617.

New installs no longer trust opkssh's shared default client IDs. Both installers now write the OpenSSH-style commented-out template @EthanHeilman suggested in #618, so no provider is enabled until the admin adds their own client ID:

```
# OpenID Providers trusted by opkssh, one per line:
#   <issuer> <client-id> <expiration-policy>
# expiration-policy is one of: 12h, 24h, 48h, 1week, oidc, oidc_refreshed, never
#
# No provider is enabled until you add one. Register a client ID for opkssh
# with your OpenID Provider, then uncomment its line below and replace
# <CLIENT-ID> with it. Clients must log in with the same client ID.
# See https://github.com/openpubkey/opkssh/tree/main/docs/providers
#
# https://accounts.google.com <CLIENT-ID> 24h
# https://login.microsoftonline.com/9188040d-6c67-4c5b-b112-36a304b66dad/v2.0 <CLIENT-ID> 24h
# https://gitlab.com <CLIENT-ID> 24h
```

### Changes

- **Installers**
  - `install-linux.sh` and `Install-OpksshServer.ps1` write the template above.
  - A new `--install-providers-from=FILEPATH` / `-InstallProvidersFrom` option installs your own providers file instead, so providers are enabled right after the install. A missing file fails the install before anything changes.
  - A non-empty providers file is still never changed, as before.
  - The template (and a file given with the new option) always ends with a newline. The CI workflows and integration tests append a provider with `>>` / `Add-Content`, and without it the appended line would land on the last comment line.
  - Windows now also fills an existing empty providers file, as Linux already did.
- **Server errors**
  - `opkssh verify` now says which file to edit when no provider is enabled.
  - `opkssh audit` reports it as an error. It used to exit 0 on a fresh install.
- **`Test-OpksshInstallation.ps1`** counts only uncommented provider lines. It previously matched `accounts.google.com` anywhere, so the template would have passed.
- **Docs**
  - Updated the README, `docs/config.md` and `scripts/installing.md` to show the template.
  - Regenerated `scripts/install-linux-script.md`, which was also missing `install_selinux_module`.

### Tests

- **Template stays in sync:** `TestInstallerProvidersTemplate` (Go) extracts the template from both installer scripts, checks they are identical, and parses it with the real providers loader:
  - no rows and no config problems;
  - each line, once uncommented, is a valid row.
- **Installer behaviour:** new shunit2 tests (Linux) and Pester tests (Windows) cover:
  - writing the template;
  - appending a provider to it;
  - the option on a missing, empty and non-empty providers file;

author: psatomas
body:
Closes #3

## Problem/context

Repository-configured verification commands (`.ai/project.yaml`'s `verification.additionalChecks`)
are arbitrary shell text chosen by whoever can land a PR — a higher-trust surface than AI Engine's
own auto-detected commands. `CommandApprovalStore` exists specifically so such a command is never
executed until a human has explicitly approved it. But approval identity was `sha256(command)`
only — the check's `cwd` (also fully repository-configurable, and genuinely used as the actual
subprocess working directory by `runner.ts`) was never part of what was approved. `cwd` is
execution-relevant: the same command text resolves a different `package.json`, different
relative-path files, or an entirely different script depending on where it runs.

## Security invariant

An approval for a repository-configured check now authorizes exactly the (command text, canonical
repository-relative working directory) pair presented for approval. Changing either — the command
or the directory it runs in — invalidates the prior approval and requires a fresh, explicit one.
The identity is deliberately **not** bound to any absolute, task-transient worktree path: it's
repository-scoped, and a single approval is meant to keep covering every future task for the same
repository, each of which gets its own dedicated (but structurally identical) worktree.

## Vulnerability/reproduction

Proven with a real, unmocked test before any production code changed (`CommandApprovalStore` +
`runVerification`, real subprocess execution via `execa`, real temp directories): approve
`cat marker.txt` at directory A (containing `SAFE_A`) — it correctly runs and reads `SAFE_A`.
Change only the check's configured `cwd` to directory B (containing `DANGEROUS_B`), same command
text, same approval store, no new approval granted anywhere. The check still reported approved and
`runVerification` executed it — `PASS`, not `NOT_APPROVED` — reading `DANGEROUS_B`. This requires an
adversary already able to land a PR to the target repository (the actor `CommandApprovalStore`
exists to constrain in the first place), and uses only ordinary, git-tracked configuration edits —
no contrived state.

## Implementation

- **`packages/security/src/command-approval.ts`**: new `canonicalCwd(repoRoot, cwd)` — one pure,
  filesystem-free function, shared by every caller, that reduces a check's `cwd` to a
  repository-relative string (`""` for the root itself, `"packages/foo"` for a subdirectory).
  `repoRoot` here is each task's own worktree root (the same value already threaded through
  `RunVerificationOptions.repoRoot`), not a single fixed path — using each task's own root as the
  anchor is what keeps the identity stable *across* tasks, since every worktree mirrors the same
  repository layout. `hashCommand(command, canonicalCwd)` now hashes both, NUL-separated (no
  concatenation collisions). `CommandApprovalRecord` gains a `cwd` field (the canonical form, for
  audit/display). All four store methods (`isApproved`/`getApproval`/`approve`/`revoke`) now take
  `(command, cwd, repoRoot)` and canonicalize internally — callers never do their own ad hoc
  path math.
- **`packages/verification/src/runner.ts`**: `CommandApprovalChecker.isApproved` widened to
  `(command, cwd, repoRoot)`. The runner stays fully decoupled from `@ai-engine/security` (no new
  import) — it just forwards `check.cwd`/`options.repoRoot`, which it already has, to whatever
  checker it was given.
- **`packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator.ts`**: all four call sites identified during
  investigation now pass `check.cwd` and the task's own worktree root consistently —
  `approveVerificationCommand` (granting), `listVerificationChecks` (the `approved` flag CLI/VS
  Code/MCP all read), `requiredChecksAwaitingApproval` (the pause-vs-fail gate in `test()`/
  `finalVerify()`), and `runVerification`'s own consultation via the widened interface above.
  `approveVerificationCommand`'s return type gained `cwd` so callers can display exactly what was
  approved.

**Deliberate boundary**: `canonicalCwd()` does no realpath/symlink resolution — that stays
`checkContainment`'s separate, execution-time-only job in `runner.ts`, untouched by this PR. The
identity layer answers "is this the same *configured* location as before"; `checkContainment`
answers "is this concretely safe to execute in right now." Conflating them would have meant
duplicating (or weakening) `checkContainment`'s own carefully-scoped TOCTOU handling.

## Compatibility

Every existing approval record stops matching the new hash and is treated as not-yet-approved —
the correct, intended, fail-closed consequence (an old approval never actually covered the new
identity), requiring **no migration code**: the store already degrades a missing/non-matching entry
to "not approved," exactly the same path a corrupted file already took. Verified explicitly with a
test that writes a pre-fix-shaped record (old hash, no `cwd` field) directly to disk and confirms it
authorizes nothing under the new scheme, while the file remains parseable and a fresh approval
still works normally afterward. `TaskRecord`'s own `approvals` audit log is a human-readable history,
not the cryptographic identity, and needed no change.

## CLI / VS Code / MCP

- **CLI**: `ai checks` now prints a check's `cwd` line when set; `ai approve-check`'s confirmation
  shows the exact `(command, cwd)` pair just approved.
- **VS Code**: the approval QuickPick's detail line and the confirmation dialog both show `cwd`
  when set.
- **MCP**: **no change.** Verified directly (again, post-implementation) that `PendingDecision`'s
  `verification_approval` content and the bounded MCP/CLI task view already include `cwd` —
  `decide_task`'s approval path calls the same, now-fixed `approveVerificationCommand` and benefits
  automatically with zero MCP-specific code.

## Testing

- **Adversarial/regression** (`packages/security/src/command-approval.test.ts`, 23 tests): 7
  `canonicalCwd` properties (root-sentinel equivalence, spelling normalization, cross-worktree
  stability, distinctness, no-repoRoot fallback, outside-repoRoot determinism), `hashCommand`'s
  two-input sensitivity and non-collision, and the store's full cwd-aware behavior — including the
  exact numbered scenarios from the Issue: same command+cwd stays valid; same command+different cwd
  requires fresh approval; different command+same cwd requires fresh approval; approval reuse
  across different task worktrees at the same repository-relative location; the proven substitution
  attack closed; legacy command-only data fails closed.
- **End-to-end adversarial** (`orchestrator.hardening.test.ts`, new "C1c"): drives the exact proven
  scenario through the real `Orchestrator`, a real git worktree, and real command execution —
  approve at cwd A (file genuinely created there), redirect the repository's config to cwd B (same
  command), confirm the task pauses `NOT_APPROVED` (not `FIXING`, not a silent `PASS`) and that the
  command never executed at B under the stale approval — then confirms a fresh approval at B works
  normally.
- **CLI** (`format.test.ts`, +2): cwd shown when set, omitted when not.
- **VS Code** (new `commands.test.ts`, 2 tests): cwd present in both the QuickPick detail and the
  confirmation dialog text when set, absent when not — narrowly scoped to this one command handler,
  following `state.test.ts`'s existing minimal-vscode-fake approach rather than a new harness.
- **Full suite**: typecheck, lint, `prettier --check .`, `npm run build`, `npm test` all clean —
  **54 files / 1272 tests passed** (up from the pre-existing 53/1253 baseline). `git diff --check`
  clean. No real Claude/Codex E2E invoked.

## Risks/tradeoffs

- Every machine with existing repository-configured approvals will need one fresh, one-time
  re-approval per check after this ships — intended, documented, not a bug.
- `canonicalCwd`'s "outside repoRoot" fallback (absolute reso

body:
`i18n-translate.yml` now reports its own outcome to every open issue labelled `verify:translation-run`. That settles questions only a real provider call can answer, such as #381 (does DeepL accept the term list, ADR-0102?), without anything having to poll for a run nobody can schedule.

## What changed

- **`tools/translate-locale.mjs`**: `--generate` also outputs `translated` (the number of keys actually sent to the provider) and `translated_keys`. The existing `keys` also counts glossary pins, hand-edits recorded as human, and removals, none of which reach a provider.
- **`.github/workflows/i18n-translate.yml`**
  - The translate step tees its output to `$RUNNER_TEMP/translate.log` with `set -o pipefail`, so a failure can be quoted.
  - **Check the French this run produced**: runs only if `translated` ≥ 1. It runs `--check`, including the term-list rule, with `continue-on-error`, so it never blocks the commit and only decides the verdict below.
  - **Report to the issues waiting on a translation run**: runs if `success()` and `translated` ≥ 1. Each open labelled issue gets the run link, the event, the count, the keys, and the check verdict, and is closed if the check passed.
  - **Report a failed run**: runs on `failure()`. Each open labelled issue gets the run link, the failed step (from the step outcomes), and the first `The translation provider answered NNN` line from the log (the last 5 lines if there's none). It stays open.
  - The job gains `issues: write`. Comments use the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not the PAT. The fork gate from ADR-0057 is unchanged.
- **ADR-0103** records the decision and the rejected alternative, a scheduled cloud agent polling for the run. ADR-0102 links to it. The workflows README is updated.
- The label `verify:translation-run` has been created and added to #381.

## Verification

- 234 JS tests pass, including a new CLI test showing that a hand-edit-only run reports `translated=0`, and that a real translation reports `translated=1` and its key.
- actionlint (Docker) passes, apart from an existing warning about inline `head.ref` in the commit step, which this PR doesn't touch. It caught a YAML bug: `#` inside `format()` in an unquoted value is a comment. That is now composed in the shell.
- Both report scripts were dry-run with a stubbed `gh`, for success and close, and for a failure quoting a 400.
- **Not yet run for real.** `pull_request_target` and push-to-main use main's copy of the workflow, so the first real exercise is the next run after this merges that sends a key to the provider.

No .feature scenario needed: build — CI workflow reporting and a new generator output for it; what gets translated, written, committed and checked is unchanged
Claims preserved: REQ-WLD-026, REQ-WLD-027

author: oschess-claude-bot
body:
Refs #25 (part 2: classic annotations and PGN for both formats through one view). Part 3 serves `.cbh` through the bridge, in its catalog, API and search, on top of `view::Base`, and closes #25.

Part of #18.

## What

- **`cbh::annotations`** decodes a `.cba` record into the same annotation types as 2CBH.
  - It decodes text, symbols (1–3 bytes), and coloured squares and arrows, whose squares are numbered from 1 in `.cba`.
  - Every other type is skipped by its own size, so a classic record is never incomplete.
  - Damage is an error: a foreign game id in the record head, a wrong count or size, an annotation past the record, a position below −1 or past the last move, a square off the board, or a text without a language.
- **Position numbering.** Classic annotations count positions in stored order, and 2CBH in PGN order. The PGN writer knows every move's index in both orders and uses the one the format needs. The pairs matched at once, with no tuning.
- **Text language** is a nation number in `.cba`. The pairs confirm 42 = English, 53 = German and 0 = any language. The remaining five languages, and Polish and Greek, map by the nation table in Morphy's description, read as a spec; no code is taken from it.
- **PGN.** `pgn::classic_game`, `classic_game_with` and `classic_game_from` go through the same writer, and the common part is factored out. 2CBH output is unchanged.
- **`view::Base`** opens either format.
  - It gives headers, names, the move-tree walk, annotations, PGN and batched reads.
  - A path is detected as 2CBH first when a `.2cbh` file has that stem.
  - `PositionOrder` tells which numbering a base uses.
- **`cbtool`** works on `view::Base`:
  - `pgn` exports `.cbh`;
  - the classic `verify` checks annotations, and its `incomplete` count is always 0;
  - the guard against writing over a database's files covers `.cbh` too.
- **`.cbj`** is implemented (`cbh/wide.rs`), since the description covers it. When `.cbg` or `.cba` exceeds 4 GiB, the 64-bit offsets come from `.cbj`, and their low 32 bits must equal the `.cbh` offsets. That replaces part 1's explicit refusal.
- **Old `.cba` files** have a 10-byte header, like `.cbg`. So do 139 of the 245 classic-only databases.
- **Examples:**
  - `cbh_pairs` compares every game's PGN byte for byte, with `--lang`;
  - `oracle` accepts `.cbh`: our decoder's moves are replayed in cozy-chess along the same variations, and every position is compared.
- **`docs/format-notes.md`** gains sections on `.cba` annotations and `.cbj`, and records the pair results.

## Evidence

**Pairs** (English and German comments; counts only):

| Base | Games | PGN byte-identical | Only name-tag differences | `verify` 2CBH vs CBH | Oracle positions / differences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MegaBase2026-Update02 | 5,125 | 5,125 | 0 | equal | 470,638 / 0 |
| MegaBase2026-Update03 | 5,630 | 5,630 | 0 | equal | 514,751 / 0 |
| MegaBase2026-Update10 | 6,119 | 6,119 | 0 | equal | 551,419 / 0 |
| MegaBase2026-Update24 | 5,391 | 5,391 | 0 | equal | 487,129 / 0 |
| MegaBase2026-Update41 | 6,223 | 6,223 | 0 | equal | 565,965 / 0 |
| a private user base | 350 | 263 | 87 | equal | 27,478 / 0 |

- "Equal" means `verify` prints the same counts for both copies, annotations included: 1,240 / 1,255 / 884 / 1,284 / 1,674 / 89 annotated, with 0 failures.
- No game differs in its moves, annotation status or other tags.
- The 87 exceptions all come from names the classic format cannot hold: 25 names outside a single-byte code page and 63 cut at the classic field width, with one game carrying two of them.

**Classic-only databases (245).**
- 243 verify with no failure, with the same totals as part 1.
- The damaged one keeps its 3 move errors.
- One base of studies holds 2 set-up games with annotations past their last move (position 52 for 51 moves, and 16 for 11). As in 2CBH since #32, that is damage, so those games are errors. A softer rule (serve the game, drop the stray annotation and flag it incomplete) would change 2CBH too, so it is left for a separate decision.
- The oracle finds 0 differences on these bases.

**Full Mega (2CBH).**
- `verify` counts are unchanged: 11,964,285 games, 963,223,086 plies, 423,390 annotated, 0 incomplete, 0 failures.
- The full PGN export still hashes `373d47f0baa5da98`, with stderr empty.

**Checks**, on the head rebased onto main after #31, #35 and #36:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `scripts/clippy-windows.sh` pass.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps` passes.
- `cargo test --locked`: 315 passed, 2 ignored. The new tests are:
  - `tests/cbh_annotations.rs` (9): stored order, types and languages, skipping by size, missing record and file, damage, a position outside the game, every single-byte mutation and truncation, and the size limit;
  - `tests/view.rs` (3): one game in both formats gives the same PGN, the same names, and correct format detection;
  - a sparse `.cbg` over 4 GiB read through `.cbj`, Unix only;
  - CLI tests, including a 1 GiB annotation record refused under `ulimit -v`, every companion and the other format's copy refused as an export target.
- No file in `crates/cbformat/src` exceeds 400 lines; the longest is `v2/mod.rs` at 399.

No local database contents are in this pull request: only counts.

```
  see https://github.com/openpubkey/opkssh/tree/main/docs/providers
```

The check runs once the provider is final, so it covers an alias, `--provider`, `OPKSSH_PROVIDERS`, and a provider picked in the web chooser.

### `opkssh client provider add`

```
opkssh client provider add <alias> <issuer> <client-id> [--client-secret S] [--scopes "..."] [--replace] [--config-path P]
```

- **Adding:** it adds a provider to `~/.opk/config.yml`. If the file doesn't exist, it is created from the default config first, the same file `--create-config` writes.
- **Replacing:** `--replace` changes the client ID of an existing provider, such as the default `google` one, and keeps its other aliases and settings.
- **Server line:** it prints the line the servers need in `/etc/opk/providers`.
- **Duplicate issuers:** adding a second provider for an issuer that is already configured is refused, with a hint to use `--replace`. The login web chooser rejects duplicate issuers.
- **Google:** it requires `--client-secret`, as `--provider` already does.

The config file is edited as YAML nodes rather than rewritten from the structs, so the user's comments are kept, and blank lines are put back. Rewriting from the structs would also not work: `ProviderConfig` has no `MarshalYAML`, so `alias` and `scopes` would be written as lists that `UnmarshalYAML` rejects. Replacing the default Google client ID changes only the `client_id` and `client_secret` lines of the default config (tested). The result is parsed the way `opkssh login` does before it is written, and it is written through a temporary file.
A config file with CRLF line endings keeps them: the YAML encoder would otherwise turn each `\r` in a comment into an extra line break (Windows CI caught this).

### Tests

- **`TestClientProviderAdd` (commands):** 15 cases on an in-memory filesystem, including:
  - no config file;
  - replacing the default Google client ID, where the file must equal the default config with those two values changed;
  - keeping the other aliases;
  - keeping user comments;
  - removing a stale client secret on replace;
  - a config file with CRLF line endings;
  - every error case, each of which must leave the file unchanged.
- **`TestClientProviderAdd` (main):** runs the real CLI: `add --replace`, `add`, `list`, then the duplicate-alias error.
- **`TestLoginCmdDefaultClientIDWarning`:** runs `LoginCmd.Run` with a mock provider using the default Google and GitLab client IDs, which warn, and with another client ID or another issuer, which don't.
- **Negative checks:** removing the warning call, or the blank-line restoration, makes the tests fail.
- **CI on my fork:** all green.

### Questions

- In #618 I also floated a machine-wide client config, so an organization can set its client IDs once per machine. It can't be `/etc/opk/config.yml`, which is the server config. Is that worth a follow-up, and under what name?
- Should `opkssh client provider list` also mark providers that use a default client ID?

## Summary

Follow-up from the 2026-09-23 dependabot sweep: the `Build, Test & License Check` failure on PR #489 was not the bump. `stats-rollup-backfill.test.ts` was a time-dependent flake that recurs about every 6 days.

## Root cause

`refreshWindows()` (`src/lib/database/stats-rollup-backfill.ts:136`) emits a **literal** end timestamp for the final window when `now` falls in the last sub-bucket hour of a window cycle (`end < nowMs` is false only after the boundary, so a `now` just past a boundary that is still below `start + windowMs` produces a literal `end`).

The test asserted the last refresh CALL for each tier contains `now()` (`stats-rollup-backfill.test.ts:98-99`), with a fixed `minTime` (2026-01-01T12:34:56Z) and the real wall clock for `Date.now()`. With that fixed `minTime`:

- the `_1h` tier flakes during one hour, every 6 days
- the `_1m` tier flakes during one minute, every 2 days

So every ~6 days, any PR running CI in that hour fails this one test with no code cause (PR #489 was that failure).

## Fix (test-only, no source change)

Pin `Date.now()` via a `spyOn` in `beforeEach` to a fixed instant chosen to sit **outside** both literal bands, so the default `now()`-ended assertion path is deterministic. One new test pins `now` inside the band and asserts the literal-end branch, so both sides of `refreshWindows()` are now covered explicitly.

```
beforeEach: spyOn(Date, 'now').mockReturnValue(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 13, 13, 34, 30))
new test:   mockReturnValue(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 13, 12, 34, 30))  // inside the band
            expect(last refresh).toContain("'2026-01-13T12:00:00.000Z'::timestamptz")
            expect(last refresh).not.toContain('now()')
```

## Verification

- Reproduced the CI failure deterministically first: with `now` pinned to 12:34:30 and the unmodified source, `expect(...).toContain('now()')` fails exactly as in the PR 489 CI log.
- `bun run typecheck:all` clean.
- `bun test --isolate`: 3749 pass, 0 fail (255 files).
- New file total: 11 pass (was 10), including the new literal-end case.
