author: sglvladi
body:
This PR extends the existing weak-reference handling for historical `Prediction.prior` references.

Previously, the handling covered the case where a new prediction followed an update whose hypothesis exposed a single `.prediction`. It did not cover consecutive predictions, where the prior is itself another `Prediction`, or updates containing a `MultipleHypothesis`, where predictions are stored within the individual hypotheses.

Additions:
- The existing behaviour for single hypotheses is largely preserved, along with the current `prior` getter and serialisation behaviour. The existing test has been renamed to reflect its purpose.
- The updated implementation collects the relevant historical predictions from these cases and weakens their prior references through a new `_weaken_historical_references()` helper. Predictions are deduplicated before processing so that a shared prediction referenced by multiple hypotheses is only handled once.
- The immediate prior of a newly created prediction remains strongly referenced. Only the prior held by an older historical prediction is weakened, preserving access to the most recent history while allowing older states to be released when no longer referenced elsewhere.
- Tests have been added for consecutive `Prediction -> Prediction` histories, `MultipleHypothesis` containing distinct predictions, and `MultipleHypothesis` entries sharing the same prediction. The tests verify that the historical prior remains available while the referenced object exists and resolves to `None` once that object is deleted.

Fixes #1355

author: heffnt
body:
## Your rulings

2026-09-22: "we should also setup agents via openrouter and/or lambda because I am constantly hitting my subscription limits so I want to build things with the cheapest agent that can do the job. a couple frontier models orchestrate either as the orchestrator agent itself or in session with me (ie. this session)."

2026-09-24: "I have the open router key. how can i share it?"

The 2026-09-23 handoff records the agreed design: "Cheap agents run through Codex's OpenAI-compatible provider config (OpenRouter), spend-capped; waits on Tom's key."

## How to put the key on the box

The key goes from your own shell on the box into `/etc/tts/worker.env`, the box's secrets file, so it never passes through a chat. Before you do this, set a credit limit on the key at openrouter.ai (Settings, API Keys, the key's limit). That limit is the spend cap, and OpenRouter enforces it. After this pull request merges, ssh to the box and run the first command below. `read -s` takes the key without echoing it or writing it to shell history, and the line is appended to the file:

```sh
read -rsp 'OpenRouter key: ' K && printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=%s\n' "$K" >> /etc/tts/worker.env && unset K; echo
```

Then roll out, which also restarts `tts-session-host` so the daemon drops the key from every session shell:

```sh
cd /root/tom.quest && git pull && bash worker/setup.sh
```

This line in its output confirms the provider entry was written: `codex now has the openrouter provider`. To prove a cheap model answers, run the first command below; it should print `pong`. The second sends the same test through `tts-run`, which is how a session spawns:

```sh
echo "Reply with exactly: pong" | tts-codex --model openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b --effort low
```

```sh
echo "Reply with exactly: pong" | tts-run --cli codex --model openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b --effort low
```

`openai/gpt-oss-120b` is one OpenRouter model id. Any id from openrouter.ai/models works in its place. The id has to support tool calls, because Codex hands the model its shell and file tools.

## The state this leaves

A Codex run now takes a model spelled `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>`, for example `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b`. That run still runs in Codex, with the same sandbox, tools, operate instructions and registration. Only the **model provider** changes. The model provider is Codex's own configuration term for the server that answers its model calls: by default that is OpenAI, signed in with your ChatGPT login, and for these runs it is OpenRouter, billed to the key. So an OpenRouter run draws nothing from your ChatGPT or Claude subscription windows.

Every Codex door on the box goes through `scripts/codex-run.mjs` (installed as `tts-codex`). That includes `tts-run --cli codex`, the cron jobs and a session's Codex subagent, so each of them can now name a cheap model on a single spawn. The rule that every spawn names its model still holds: the name now says the provider as well.

The key reaches only the Codex process of a run that names an OpenRouter model:

| Where | What holds the key |
|---|---|
| `/etc/tts/worker.env` | the key, as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (the variable's name) |
| `/root/.codex/config.toml` | a `[model_providers.openrouter]` entry naming the variable (`env_key`), never the value; `worker/setup.sh` writes it only while the key is set |
| the daemon, every session shell, every `tts-run` child | nothing: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is on the scrub list in `worker/session-host/env-scrub.mjs`, beside `GH_TOKEN` |
| the Codex process of an `openrouter/` run | the key, read from the env file by `codex-run.mjs` for that run alone |
| the shell commands that run's model executes | nothing: Codex passes its whole environment to them by default, so `codex-run.mjs` excludes this variable (`shell_environment_policy.exclude`) |

The model can still read `/etc/tts/worker.env` from disk, as it can for every other key there. The scrub keeps the key out of process environments, as it does for the others.

A run with no key, or with a spelling that lacks the vendor part, is refused before anything is recorded. `tts-run` with an `openrouter/` model and without `--cli codex` is refused before it takes a slot, because Claude Code has no way to reach OpenRouter.

**Verified against the installed Codex (codex-cli 0.153.3), without a model call.** `codex debug prompt-input` builds a run's prompt without contacting a model, and it accepted the provider entry and selected it. It type-checks `name`, `base_url`, `env_key`, `env_key_instructions` and `shell_environment_policy.exclude`: a wrong type for each is an error naming that key. It refuses `wire_api = "chat"` and asks for `"responses"`, the only value this Codex accepts. OpenRouter serves that protocol, the OpenAI Responses API, at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses`. No model has run through OpenRouter yet, since the key is not on the box. The smoke test above is the first proof.

## Cost

The digest cannot total OpenRouter cost from the run record yet. OpenRouter returns each call's cost in its response (`usage.cost`), but Codex does not keep that field: its rollout (the transcript file Codex writes under `/root/.codex/sessions/`, which the run sweep ingests) records only token counts. So each OpenRouter run's row holds three things. The first is the model requested, `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>`, from the launcher's registration. The second is the model Codex sent, `<vendor>/<model>`. The third is its input, cached and output tokens. It holds no dollar figure. `worker/runs/prices.mjs` prices a run from its model and tokens with dated per-model rates, so a dated entry keyed by `<vendor>/<model>` for each cheap model you settle on gives those rows a cost with no other change. Until then, OpenRouter's activity page shows the true spend against the key's limit.

## Where this meets the models branch

Another worker is gathering the model names into one place on the branch `models-sonnet-opus-ceiling`. Today the names are resolved in more than one place. The session model table (`SESSION_MODELS` in `convex/ttsShared.ts`, mirrored in `worker/session-host/session.mjs`) decides what a whole session or a todo's model tag may run on. This change does not touch that table, so a session or a todo cannot yet be tagged with an OpenRouter model; a spawn can. The two branches meet at that table and at `worker/runs/prices.mjs`. When the one home lands, OpenRouter entries go there, spelled `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>` as here.

## Not verified

- Codex sends `model_reasoning_effort`, which defaults to `xhigh` in `codex-run.mjs`. Whether OpenRouter passes `xhigh` through for a model other than OpenAI's is unverified, which is why the smoke test passes `--effort low`.
- Codex has no built-in metadata for a model outside OpenAI's list. It warns and uses a fallback, so its context-window figure and the point at which it compacts history may be wrong for that model.

## Checks

- `vitest run worker/runs/__tests__ worker/session-host/__tests__ scripts/codex-run.test.mjs worker/jobs/worker-env.test.mjs`: 39 files, 583 tests passed. New tests cover four cases. An OpenRouter run selects the provider, sends OpenRouter's id, and hands the key from the env file to Codex and not to its argv. A run with no key is refused before anything is spooled. A spelling without a vendor is refused. A default-provider run never receives the key. For `tts-run`, the name reaches Codex whole without the key, and the Claude CLI refuses it and starts nothing. The scrub list also drops the new name.
- `scripts/laptop-setup.test.mjs` and `scripts/session-start-hook.test.mjs` fail 7 tests. They fail the same 7 on unmodified main.
- `pnpm check:guardrails`: passed (exit 0). It reports that one entry in the removal baseline, a dead export in `convex/ttsCompose.ts`, is no longer live; that entry comes from main, not this change.
- `bash -n worker/setup.sh`: passed. shellcheck is not installed on the

author: keppy
body:
Fixes #1911

## What changed

The queue worker treated every extraction failure as terminal: it logged, called
`task_done()`, and moved on. An episode whose extraction failed was left in the graph
with no edges and 0 facts, with no retry, no backoff, and no counter — the failure was
only discoverable later by inspecting the graph.

### Failure handling — `mcp_server/src/services/queue_service.py`

| failure | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| empty LLM response, query timeout, driver error (transient) | logged and dropped | retried in place, up to `max_attempts` (default 3), 1s doubling backoff |
| `ExtractedEntities` / schema validation error (deterministic, roots in #912) | logged and dropped | dropped immediately, no retry |
| outcome visibility | one `ERROR` log line, no counters | `processed` / `retried` / `dropped` counters per `group_id`, plus a distinct drop line with the episode id and the counters |

Retries happen **in place** rather than by re-queueing, so a group's episodes stay
sequential and a retrying episode cannot be overtaken by the ones behind it.
`QueueService(max_attempts=..., retry_base_delay=...)` sets the policy; the defaults are
`3` and `1.0`.

Validation failures are the one thing worth *not* retrying: the same episode produces the
same malformed extraction every time, so retrying only delays the episodes queued behind
it. That is the whole content of `is_retryable_failure()`.

### One bug found while testing this

`add_episode_task()` only started a worker `if not self._queue_workers.get(group_id)`, but
the flag was set *inside* the worker coroutine — which does not run until the task is
scheduled. Calls arriving back to back therefore each spawned their own worker for the
same queue, and one group's episodes were processed concurrently and out of order (measured:
3 items queued back to back → 3 workers). The "sequential per `group_id`" guarantee this
service exists for was not actually holding. The flag is now set before the task is
scheduled, and `test_items_queued_back_to_back_run_one_at_a_time` pins it.

### Tests — `mcp_server/tests/test_queue_service.py` (new, 21 tests)

No database, LLM, or network: the worker is driven with fake process functions.

- transient failure retried, then succeeds (attempts, counters)
- backoff schedule doubles (1.0s, 2.0s) and the worker awaits it
- retries do not reorder the queue
- attempts exhausted → episode dropped, and the next episode still runs
- validation failure → not retried, does not block the queue
- `max_attempts < 1` and negative `retry_base_delay` are clamped
- back-to-back items start exactly one worker

74 tests pass locally with the exact command added to CI below (`test_queue_service.py`,
`test_factories.py`, `test_core_parity.py`).

### CI — `.github/workflows/mcp-server-tests.yml`

The separate commit adds a step running the MCP unit tests. Right now they run *nowhere*:
the root suite sets `collect_ignore_glob = ['mcp_server/*']` and this workflow only runs
`tests/test_live_falkordb_int.py`. `tests/` cannot be collected wholesale
(`test_cross_encoder_factory.py` needs the `providers` extra, `test_stress_load.py` imports
`test_fixtures` by module name), so the database-free modules are listed explicitly. Happy
to drop that commit if you would rather wire the MCP unit tests up differently.

## Evidence

Same probe against `main` and against this branch — three items queued back to back, and an
episode that always raises `asyncio.TimeoutError`:

```
# before (main)
in-flight items queued back to back: ['a', 'b', 'c']
attempts for a transiently failing episode: 1

# after
in-flight items queued back to back: ['a']
attempts for a transiently failing episode: 3
counters: QueueStats(processed=0, retried=2, dropped=1)
```

## Open question

After a failed `add_episode`, the episode node can persist with 0 edges (the third failure
shape in the issue). Is retrying with the same `uuid` safe, given `add_episode` does
`EpisodicNode.get_by_uuid(driver, uuid)` and re-runs extraction for an existing episode — or
would you rather the retry land on a new uuid or go through a dead-letter path? If same-uuid
retry is not safe, the retry commit is separable: the counters, the drop logging, and the
worker-start fix stand on their own without it.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked issue (`Fixes #1911`)
- [x] Tests for the behavior change
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean
- [x] pyright clean on `mcp_server/src/services/queue_service.py` (0 errors)
- [x] CLA signed

Part of #618 (item 5).

Adds `docs/providers/google.md`, following `azure.md` and `keycloak.md`:

- Configure the Google Auth Platform: app information, and Internal or External audience.
- Create a **Web application** client with opkssh's three `http://localhost:{3000,10001,11110}/login-callback` redirect URIs. Google documents localhost redirect URIs with a path for this client type. For "Desktop app" clients, it doesn't document whether a path like `/login-callback` works.
- Put the client ID in `/etc/opk/providers` and in `~/.opk/config.yml`.
- **Troubleshooting** covers:
  - `disabled_client` / `deleted_client` (Google deletes OAuth clients unused for six months);
  - `redirect_uri_mismatch`;
  - `org_internal`.

Because opkssh only requests `openid email profile`, an External app works in the Testing publishing status, with no test-user list and no app verification ([Google's publishing status docs](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)). The guide says so, so users don't go through verification needlessly.

The guide is also linked from the README provider table and from the client ID security note, which now says to register your own client ID for production.

**Validated end to end.** A new client was registered by following the guide exactly, with no step differing from the Google Cloud console. Then:
- Google's token endpoint accepts the client on all three redirect URIs, and rejects an unregistered one with `redirect_uri_mismatch`;
- `opkssh login --provider="https://accounts.google.com,<CLIENT-ID>,<CLIENT-SECRET>"` (step 3) completed a real Google sign-in and wrote the SSH certificate;
- that certificate, run through the server path `opkssh verify` uses (providers file parsing, `CreateVerifier` with Google's live keys, `auth_id` policy, `AuthorizedKeysCommand`), is accepted with the new client ID in the providers file, and rejected when the providers file only has the default Google client ID (`audience does not contain clientID`) or when the user is not in `auth_id`.

body:
## Scope

Child of #86 at `5998b24de8c8bc520adcee3e9df52a2ef2f49223`: **single-asset, deterministic-rate BS / 1F / 2F Bergomi with Buehler stochastic cash dividends**. No parent PR or main branch is modified or merged; #85's separate legacy 5 bp requirement change is not included.

- Add explicit Rust/Python `evaluate_aad()` and immutable Python `StochasticDividendAadRisk`. Constructors still require price-only request flags.
- Reuse contractual payoff adjoints and analytically reverse the actual positive split. Active inputs: Spot, initial residual-equity volatility, dividend mean reversion/linkage/volatility, every cash mean including post-expiry cash, and original discount/repo-spread log-DF pillars. Include pre/post dividend observations, full future-reserve reconstruction, initial funding, curve extrapolation and payment discounting. There are no finite differences in production risk.
- Precompute coefficient Jacobians once per evaluation. Reuse unchanged primal paths and OU innovations; handle sigma0=0 without division. Existing price-only formulas, random coordinates, scheme labels, fingerprints and replay fixtures are unchanged.
- Return raw derivatives and sampling errors, per-vol-point scales and zero-rate node DV01. MC uses independent antithetic units; RQMC uses scramble means. This is not market-IV Vega/VegaKT or recalibrated risk.
- Reject unsmoothed discontinuous payoff risk before sampling. Explicit compact-C2 smoothing gives derivatives of the smoothed payoff at fixed width. Existing American/continuous-barrier restrictions remain.
- Add full-recompile FD tests, continuous-time BS moment validation, common-noise Brownian/OU price refinement, bindings/stubs/example/source contracts, and a dedicated read-only Linux/macOS/Windows release job.

**Held fixed/out of scope:** all correlations, Bergomi vol-of-vol/mean-reversions/mixing, dates/grid, smoothing width; HW, rough, LSV, multi-asset, Gamma, market-IV VegaKT and dividend-option calibration. First-order results differentiate the finite simulation algorithm. Sampling SE excludes timestep/model uncertainty.

## Source and observed validation

PR commit `30ce1f2cae0974b075e5099415735b7a927df797`, tree `24367b169470d25a4574bf5ff9492d0ca7ddbcf2`. The temporary validation workflow/history is excluded.

The read-only [native run 35940370431](https://github.com/msfmfjt/rust-pricing-library/actions/runs/35940370431), Ubuntu 24.04 / Rust 1.98.1 / Python 3.12, verifies patch SHA256 `28a4d6cbe56be13c816d800eec9c26d4e03c2d96f8038529566681b6fe3b90de` and input tree `4ce82033ed4bc1e8b22aa9ebb7418c686f481802`, then formats with the pinned toolchain.

### Passed

- Workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy with warnings denied.
- **4 new Rust AAD tests:** all active risks against full-recompile central FD at both h=1e-5 and h=1e-6; BS/1F/2F, MC/RQMC, two seeds, Asian delayed payment, smoothed pre/post-cash barriers, one/three-worker exact replay, zero-parameter inward differences. Price and price SE exactly equal `evaluate()` in these tests.
- **2 new Rust refinement tests**, including the ignored release panel: continuous-time BS moment ODE and 24 paired finite-grid price comparisons across BS/1F/2F, two seeds, and 16/32/64/128 versus 256 steps.
- **12 existing stochastic-dividend/Bergomi-dividend Rust tests**.
- Release Python wheel build/install; **4 new Python risk tests plus 8 existing BS/Bergomi-dividend Python tests**, and the new runnable risk example.
- **242 existing equation/reference checks**, schemas, Markdown links, complete source archive, explicit Python stub shape, Rust API docs and dependency direction.

The exact PR commit's [normal CI run 35940620182](https://github.com/msfmfjt/rust-pricing-library/actions/runs/35940620182) also passed formatting and Clippy on **Linux, macOS and Windows**. Its dedicated first-order/refinement jobs and other jobs are tracked separately.

Local input-source checks also passed references/schemas/Markdown/new Python syntax/static stub/source archive/whitespace. No local Rust toolchain was used to claim native passes.

### Pending at the last observation

The native run's **full normal Rust suites were running; full Python suite was pending**. Normal PR platform, wheel/replay and full legacy release gates were incomplete. Its final source artifact/hash remains to be collected; do not infer full platform acceptance from focused success. Keep draft pending these checks and parent-stack acceptance.

## Prespecified budgets and interpretation

- At both central-difference scales, `abs(AAD-FD) <= 3e-5 + 2e-5*max(abs(AAD),abs(FD))`; sampling SE never widens it. Zero-parameter inward FD uses h=1e-7 and 3e-4 absolute budget.
- The BS split's second moments are compared with an independent continuous-time Ito ODE integrated by RK4 with 32768 steps: final 128-step max error <1e-5; successive error ratios >3.5. This is moment validation, not a continuous-time SV option oracle.
- Coarse Brownian increments sum fine increments; coarse OU integrals use exponential aggregation, rather than unrelated same-seed paths. Each model/seed's 128-versus-256-step call difference satisfies `abs(mean gap) + 4*paired SE < 0.02` **in price units**. The finest grid is not exact. Selected finite-grid price gaps do not establish absolute continuous-time option accuracy, risk convergence or broad stress/exotic acceptance.
- All new-test budgets were fixed before native observation. No existing tolerance, seed, fixture, dependency or request schema changed.

The initial [run 35940154354](https://github.com/msfmfjt/rust-pricing-library/actions/runs/35940154354) stopped before numerical tests because its Actions token could not publish workflow changes. Validation is now read-only with artifacts; publication uses connected GitHub tools. No token scope or repository protection changed.

See `design/adr/0015-stochastic-dividend-risk.md`, `design/validation/stochastic-dividend-risk.md`, `docs/models/stochastic-dividends.md` and `examples/python/stochastic_dividend_risk.py`.

author: aikins01
body:
Dokploy cannot reach Postgres through Docker Swarm's default VIP networking on kernels without IPVS, leaving installation waiting for an unreachable control plane. The installer now accepts `ENDPOINT_MODE=dnsrr` for its three control-plane services and rejects default VIP mode before installation when readable kernel configuration explicitly disables IPVS. Unavailable configuration leaves the default unchanged.

Existing services with a conflicting endpoint mode are refused rather than modified. Host-mode port publication is preserved, and migrated Docker Compose workloads are unaffected; this does not make arbitrary Swarm applications or ingress publication work without IPVS.

On a Linux kernel without IPVS or module support, the original installer failed to connect to Postgres. With DNSRR selected, Dokploy v0.30.7 bootstrapped successfully and a real Coolify 4.3.23 Compose application migrated and rolled back, including database and volume data checks.

author: eminyous
body:
Depends on #2137. Part 2 of 8 for #2129.

## What changed

- Village and age group each hold a list. The url carries it joined in one parameter, `village=a,b`, the way the expenses screen carries tags. A link from before reads as a list of one.
- A member matches when their village is any of the villages chosen, and the same for age group. The two still combine with each other and with every other filter.
- Every village and every age group chosen gets its own chip, removable on its own. Village had no chip at all before, so a village filter could not be seen or cleared from the chip row.
- The badge counts one per village and one per age group, like expense tags.
- The members filter badge and the sheet now read one count, `activeFilterCount`. The badge had its own list that left out the origin and its three narrowings, while the sheet's count included the status tab and the search, which clearing keeps.
- Chip removal moves into `withoutMemberChip` in `src/lib/memberFilters.ts`, next to `withoutExpensesChip` on the expenses side, with its tests.
- New shared control `MultiSelect` under `src/components/admin/filters/`. It takes options and the chosen values and hands back the new list. With nothing chosen it shows the all label it is given and narrows nothing. With several it shows the first and a count of the rest.
- The origin block of the sheet moves to `OriginFilter.tsx`.
- `page.tsx` is split. Member loading, the village and age group lists, the review drawer, the row selection, the stats panel and the four management dialogs each move to their own hook or component. Behaviour is unchanged, except that closing a dialog now always forgets the bare account it was filling.
- Every new file joins `KEPT_CLEAN`.

## Why

The screen could only ask for one village or one age group at a time. The list follows the convention the expenses screen already uses rather than a new one. P5 takes the same control for expense tags.

A village or age group name holding an ASCII comma would split in the url. None of the existing names do, and Arabic names use the Arabic comma.

## How it was tested

- Reading and writing several villages and age groups through the url, including an old single value link and a hand edited list with empty entries.
- A member from any chosen village or age group is kept, one from neither is dropped.
- The count leaves out the tab and the search and counts one per value.
- Removing one village chip or one age group chip keeps the rest, and removing the origin chip lets go of its narrowings.
- The sheet adds an age group to those already chosen and offers every village and the other option.
- The multi select reads as all with nothing chosen, ticks what is chosen, adds and removes values, and closes when tapped outside.
- The unit and ui tiers pass locally with coverage.

Closes #2129

author: chenlaicai
body:
## 背景

9/23 台账（healing_events `a9260c50`，《issue处理》对话 12:43–15:23 约 20 条连环拦）实证：bash 守卫三天三修（F20260923qbsw 引号盲 / F20260923glay 分层 / F20260923gr1f r1 处置）仍误拦正当命令，**直接阻塞了守卫修复 PR 自身的 commit**。

根因：历史三次修复只覆盖「该拦的拦住」一侧，**放行侧系统性缺失**——误拦/漏拦是同一硬币两面，只测一面必然翻车。

## 修复的 5 处根因

| # | 根因 | 修法 |
|---|------|------|
| ① | git 写族正则 `merge\b` 吞只读 `git merge-base`（实测 dist 当前 main BLOCKED） | `merge(?!-)` 负向断言；同型审计 `commit(?!-tree)`（commit-tree 是 plumbing 只读） |
| ② | 缺 git 只读白名单快通道（黑名单思维，只读面全靠「恰好不在写族正则」兜底） | `GIT_READONLY_WHITELIST`（22 词精确全称）+ `gitSubcommandOf`（剥赋值前缀）+ `allSegmentsGitReadonly`（全段只读才命中，链式绕过防线） |
| ③ | cd 检测漏识别变量赋值前缀段（`W=/path; cd $W/...` 首段是赋值不是 cd） | `hasRealCdSegment` 跳过纯赋值前缀段后再取真 cd 段 |
| ④ | python/node heredoc 载荷体字符串（测试文本 kill 字样）被当真实终止命令 | `stripHeredocPayloads` 整体剥离（fail-closed：未闭合/裸定界符+展开特征不剥） |
| ⑤ | 「进程名模式吞路径」——排查期误判，实测证伪（无独立第五缺陷） | 拦截回执里的「进程名模式」仅是诊断回显层（locateTriggerContext，不参与拦截判定）；真正拦截的还是①-④的判定层在旧 dist（未 build + 主进程未重启）上的表现。修复合入 + 重启后消失，**无需改代码** |

## 安全红线自检（每处放宽的变形绕过评估）

- 白名单**精确匹配子命令全称**（首词元全等），`git log-f` 变形不命中
- 白名单**只管跳过 git 写族判定**——重定向/data 破坏/kill 族判定照常跑
- **写族字面判定先于白名单**（`git stash push` 的 push 在写族正则内，先于白名单命中，杜绝 stash 白名单词被显式写子命令借壳）
- 链式绕过防线：`git log && git commit` / `git log; rm -rf data` 任一段不在白名单 → 不命中快通道，回落既有判定仍拦
- heredoc 剥离 fail-closed：未闭合/裸定界符+`$()`/反引号/`${}` → 不剥，保守拦

## 测试

**新增 `tests/frameworks/agent/bash-guard-false-positive-fix.test.ts`（81 例）**——历史三次修复都缺的**放行侧回归**（PASS 断言）+ 拦截侧保持（BLOCKED 断言）：

- git merge-base 各形态（5 例）→ 全部 PASS
- git 只读白名单（20 例）→ 全部 PASS
- cd worktree + git 写族正道（6 例，台账连环拦现场形态）→ 全部 PASS
- 变量赋值前缀（5 例）→ PASS；赋值后无 cd → 仍拦
- python heredoc 载荷剥离（8 例）→ cd worktree 后载荷含 kill/pkill/eval/项目路径 PASS；未闭合 fail-closed / 真 patch 未 cd 仍拦
- node -e 载荷（4 例）→ kill+数字保守拦（glay 语义不回退）/ 纯项目路径或 kill 无数字 PASS
- gh issue create --body 含项目路径（3 例）→ #858 脱敏管道保持
- **拦截侧总回归（10 例）** → kill 主 PID / git commit 未 cd / eval kill / pkill -f / bash -c kill / kill $(lsof) / rm -rf data / 重定向未 cd / git merge 真合并 / FOO=1 git commit 未 cd → 全部仍拦

**既有测试基线保持绿**：`bash-safety-guard.test.ts` / `quoted-text-sanitizer.test.ts` / `bash-guard-layered-detect.test.ts` 全绿；全仓 `npx vitest run` **3937 例全绿**。

**bugfix Verification（修复前失败 + 修复后通过）**：
- 修复前：`git merge-base main feature/x` → BLOCKED（dist 当前 main 实测，guard-test3.mjs）；新测试 77 例中 18 例失败
- 修复后：全部台账命令形态 PASS（单测 81 例全绿）

## 影响范围

- `src/frameworks/agent/bash-safety-guard.ts`：写族正则（merge/commit-tree 负向断言 + 赋值前缀锚）、GIT_READONLY_WHITELIST + gitSubcommandOf + allSegmentsGitReadonly、hasRealCdSegment 跳过赋值前缀、checkMainCheckoutWrite 判定顺序（cd 豁免 → 写族字面 → 白名单快通道）
- `src/frameworks/agent/quoted-text-sanitizer.ts`：stripHeredocPayloads（heredoc 载荷剥离，fail-closed）
- `tests/frameworks/agent/bash-guard-false-positive-fix.test.ts`：新增 81 例放行侧 + 拦截侧回归

## 合入后生效验证 checklist（本次最大教训）

**核心教训**：守卫修复改的是 `src/`，但主进程运行时加载的是 `dist/`（build 产物）。**只改 src 不 build + 不重启主进程，修复不生效**——排查期误以为存在「第五个独立 bug」，实为旧 dist 上①-④缺陷的持续表现。

1. `npm run build`——重新编译 dist（含①-④ + r1 全部修复）
2. 重启主进程——让运行时代码重载新 dist（遵循受控脚本，勿直接 kill 主进程）
3. 台账观察 24–48h——复跑 9/23 台账（healing_events a9260c50）里被拦的命令形态，确认误拦面收敛
4. 抽验拦截侧仍拦——`kill <主PID>` / `git commit -m x`（未 cd）/ `git log > /repo/x.txt` 等仍 BLOCKED

**⑤ 结论（实测证伪，无独立第五缺陷）**：经真实主进程 PID（95447）实测，「进程名模式」仅是 `locateTriggerContext` 诊断回显层（代码注释明确不参与拦截判定），真正拦截的还是①-④的判定层。该症状是①-④缺陷在旧 dist 上的表现，修复合入 + 重启后自然消失，不存在未修的第五个 bug。

## 已知取舍（非遗留 bug）

- **node -e / python heredoc 的 kill 字样保守拦**：glay 既定「kill 检测看原文」语义在 node -e 字符串含 kill+数字时保守拦，分析脚本须写成 .mjs 文件绕开。既定取舍（防误放行），本 PR 固化该语义，后续如需放宽须独立评估。

author: memohnsen
body:
## Summary

### Request limits (API)
- The default body limit is now an explicit 1 MiB. Before, it was axum's implicit 2 MB.
- Name-list routes are capped at 256 KiB (`NAME_LIST_BODY_LIMIT`) and user-write routes at 160 KiB (`USER_WRITE_BODY_LIMIT`).
  - Compile-time asserts check that a maximal valid body fits even with every character JSON-escaped.
  - That covers `\u00XX` escapes (6 bytes per byte) and surrogate pairs (12 bytes per character).
- A new `AppError::PayloadTooLarge` makes over-limit requests return JSON: 413 `{"error":"request body too large"}`.
- `MAX_NAME_LEN` is 400 bytes and always strict.

### Ingest limits (scrapers)
- `postgres_ingest.py` caps stdin at 16 MiB and 20,000 rows, and exits with code 3 when either is exceeded.

### Batched callers
- The last scrapers that wrote one row per connection now send each run as one batch:
  - sport80 BWL sync and USAMW event scrape use `actions_skipping_errors`.
  - USAW standards and USAMW QT use `actions`.
- `test_ingest_callers.py` fails if a new per-row loop is added. It stubs scraping-only dependencies such as `requests`, because CI installs only `requirements.txt`.

### Athlete matching
- The federated `upsert_athlete` lookup matches on `NORMALIZED_NAME_SQL` and prefers an exact `convex_id`. A change in name casing or spacing no longer creates a duplicate athlete.

### Placeholder parity
- `placeholder_member_id.js` extracts the JS rule for `noid:` placeholder IDs.
- A shared fixture checks the JS rule against the Python one. It found one difference: JS turned a numeric `0` into an empty placeholder. That is fixed.

### Docs
- `AGENTS.md`, `docs/testing.md` and `docs/entry-scraper-idless-athletes.md` are updated.

## Risk
- **Slack endpoints:** the global limit drops from 2 MB to 1 MiB. Slack payloads should be far below this, but real traffic hasn't been measured.
- **Migrations:** this PR adds none.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test`: 193 tests, including new tests for:
  - 413 responses
  - the per-name length cap
  - maximal bodies sent fully escaped
- [x] Python `compileall`
- [x] Python suites:
  - `common/tests`: 56 tests, run on an empty DB as in CI
  - meet-automation: 40 tests
  - writer: 23 tests

author: tylervsd
body:
## Summary

Phase 26: BigQuery product analytics, built around trustworthy metrics.

- **Transactional outbox:** migration `2026092601` adds `analytics_events`. `record_event` writes an event in the same transaction as the business change, for four events: `user_signed_up`, `workflow_started`, `workflow_completed`, and `suggestion_finished` (`ready` / `failed` / `expired`). Replays, rollbacks and superseded suggestions record nothing. The table has no free-text columns; `user_key` is the pseudonymous `users.public_id`.
- **At-least-once export:** the worker route `POST /internal/analytics/export` is called by Cloud Scheduler every 15 minutes. It runs a BigQuery load job and marks rows exported only after the load succeeds. Exported rows are pruned after 30 days. It returns 503 when unconfigured and 500 on a load failure (rows stay for retry). Adds `google-cloud-bigquery==3.45.2`.
- **Metrics:** BigQuery views `events_deduped`, `activation_funnel` and `suggestion_success`, with PostgreSQL reconciliation SQL implementing the same written definitions.
- **Terraform (opt-in, default off):** `analytics_raw` / `analytics` datasets, a partitioned and clustered raw table, the authorized view, dataset-scoped grants, worker `bigquery.jobUser`, the Scheduler job, and the worker's `ANALYTICS_EVENTS_TABLE`.
- **Walkthrough:** [`docs/guides/26-bigquery-analytics.md`](docs/guides/26-bigquery-analytics.md), plus the spec (with amendments), the plan, and roadmap/README status.

## Rollout order (important)

Apply Terraform **before merging**, using Guide 20's worker revision workaround (guide §1 step 4). Then merge this PR so the release promotes a worker revision that already carries `ANALYTICS_EVENTS_TABLE`. Merging first is safe but leaves the export returning 503 until a later release.

## Verification

- `pnpm test:api`: 747 passed. `pnpm lint:api` clean.
- `terraform test` (sandbox): 53 passed. `pnpm lint:markdown` and `pnpm lint:links` clean.
- A whole-branch review found 4 Important issues, all in the guide or its claims (rollout order, byte-cap demo, raw-dataset default access, reconciliation window). All are fixed. Minor findings are deferred and listed in the session notes.
- BigQuery view SQL and all cloud behavior are verified only during live acceptance, which is pending.

author: kunal3
body:
## Summary

Fixes the class of triggered abilities reading `[trigger], each opponent / each
player [effect] unless that player / they [cost]`, which never offered the
affected player the choice.

`extract_unless_pay_modifier` hoisted the unless-payment out of the effect chain
onto `TriggerDefinition.unless_pay`, which the runtime copies onto the resolved
trigger root — decoupling the payment from the clause whose `player_scope` binds
the payer. Two measured harms:

1. **The root is not the scoped clause** (Rottenmouth Viper: root `PutCounter`,
   scoped `LoseLife` two links down). The root's `scoped_player` is whatever
   unrelated event-context machinery stamped — the attack route taxed the
   *controller* and offered them their own permanents; the ETB route prompted
   *nobody* and the opponent simply lost 4 life.
2. **The payer inference never produced a scope-bound filter.**
   `infer_pronoun_unless_payer` scanned only `"each opponent "`, so
   `"each player "` fell through to `TriggeringPlayer`, which resolves to the
   same seat every fan-out iteration — one seat answered for the table
   (Bellowing Mauler: P0 asked twice, P1 never asked, both lost 4).

The guard is keyed on the payer's kind, not on the hoist: any trigger whose payer
inference yields `TargetFilter::ScopedPlayer` declines, so the per-clause path
attaches the modifier to the scoped node where the fan-out binds `scoped_player`.
It is the fourth decline-to-hoist guard in that function and sits at the exit
because it is a property of the computed payer rather than of the text.

Closes #7198. Related: #8261 (the maintainer's unless-clause payer-subject
consolidation note, which explicitly sanctions narrow one-site fixes like this
and is **not** attempted here).

## Files changed

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_trigger.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/game/effects/mod.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_trigger_tests.rs`
- `crates/engine/tests/integration/scoped_unless_payer_per_iteration.rs` (new)
- `crates/engine/tests/integration/main.rs`
- `crates/engine/tests/fixtures/integration_cards.json.gz` (regenerated)

## Track

Developer

## LLM

Model: claude-opus-5
Tier: Frontier
Thinking: high

## Implementation method (required)

Method: /engine-implementer

Plan → 6 plan-review rounds (clean at round 6) → implement → checkpoint → verify
→ 3 implementation-review rounds (both gates passed at round 2; clean at round 3)
→ accept.

## CR references

- `CR 608.2f` — the **authorizing** rule: a multi-player action is processed
  considering each affected player individually, in APNAP order. This is why the
  payer must be bound per iteration rather than living on a shared trigger root.
- `CR 118.12a` — "[Do something] unless [a player does something else]" names who
  may pay (the *layering* rule; cited alongside 608.2f, never instead of it).
- `CR 101.4` — APNAP, on the multi-player test assertions.
- `CR 603.2b` — the phase-actor binding asserted by the Mogis arm-ordering test.
- `CR 608.2c`, `CR 118.12` — retained/relocated pre-existing annotations.

Every `CR` citation in the diff was grep-verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`:
101.4, 118.12, 118.12a, 603.2b, 608.2c, 608.2f — all resolve.

## Verification

- [x] Required checks ran clean, or the exact CI-owned alternative is stated below.
- [x] Gate A output below is for the current committed head.
- [x] Final review-impl below is clean for the current committed head.
- [x] Both anchors cite existing analogous code at the same seam.

All run at `5c65093e8`, in a tree verified byte-identical to the commit
(`git diff HEAD --stat` empty):

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0, clean
- `./scripts/check-parser-combinators.sh` — exit 0, `Gate G PASS` + Gate A below
- `cargo clippy -p phase-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **exit 0, clean**
- `cargo test -p phase-engine` — lib **21847 passed / 0 failed**; six bin suites 22/7/15/7/19/20 passed, 0 failed; integration **7545 passed / 0 failed**
- new `scoped_unless_payer_per_iteration` — **7 / 7 pass**
- `no_top_level_test_binaries::every_integration_file_is_registered_in_main_rs` — ok
- regression suites — `court_of_ambition` 8/0, `issue_2916_torment_repeat_unless` 3/0, `ashling_delayed_sacrifice_unless_pay` 2/0, `scoped_unless_sacrifice_token` 8/0
- `cargo coverage` — 36079 total, 32231 supported, 89.3345%, tokens 2917/2917
- `cargo semantic-audit` — 33081 audited, 254 findings; **zero of the 254 is in this change's corpus**
- `python3 scripts/gen-test-fixture.py --check` — `ok: fixture covers all 4439 referenced cards with canonical gzip bytes`

Discrimination was **measured by revert**: reverting the guard fails 5 integration
+ 5 parser tests with Mauler and Hag green; reverting the `each player` arm fails
exactly the Mauler pair with all Viper tests green.

## Gate A

```
Gate A PASS head=5c65093e85ec68c1ac84197e00fc8cbb4af28ddc base=6669d088210a9deeae37a6672e6e970278816a9e
```

## Anchored on

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_trigger.rs:3753` — the delayed-trigger
  decline-to-hoist guard (issue #4369, Ashling). Its comment states the doctrine:
  *"Decline to hoist; the per-clause path … attaches the cost to the delayed
  trigger's inner def."* Runtime regression on record at
  `crates/engine/tests/integration/ashling_delayed_sacrifice_unless_pay.rs`.
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_trigger.rs:3769` — the `primary_is_discard`
  decline-to-hoist guard, same shape, same `(text.to_string(), None)` return.

## Final review-impl

```
Review Head: 5c65093e85ec68c1ac84197e00fc8cbb4af28ddc
Completion Gate: PASS
Maintainer-Simulation Gate: PASS
```

Three rounds. Round 1 (`4b26474`) returned `Maintainer-Simulation Gate: FAIL`,
1 MED + 3 LOW. Rounds 2 (`92820af`) and 3 (`5c65093e8`) both passed both gates.
Every round re-ran the completion checks at its own candidate rather than taking
them on report; round 3 re-ran the full suite (1904s) and Gate A itself. No
finding in any round required a production-logic change.

## Claimed parse impact

Measured over all 36,079 export entries, then reproduced by the reviewer:

- **Repaired at runtime, measured:** Rottenmouth Viper, Bellowing Mauler.
- **Parse repaired, runtime unmeasured:** sAnS mERcY (a Plane; `chAoS EnSUeS`
  reachability unestablished).
- **Parse repaired, runtime still blocked:** Possessed Portal, Rishadan Brigand /
  Cutpurse / Footpad, and **The Long Reach of Night** (both Saga chapters) —
  blocked by the out-of-scope `Effect::Sacrifice` player-scope diversion
  (`should_collect_player_scope_sacrifice_choices`, consulted before the unless
  intercept), **not** by this change.
- **Modifier relocates, no runtime change:** Bandit's Talent, Hag of Ceaseless
  Torment, Perforating Artist, and the three Rishadans above.
- **Known residual — same defect, not reached:** **Lim-Dûl's Hex.** Its chain
  carries `player_scope: All` and its modifier is hoisted with
  `payer = TriggeringPlayer`, which a beginning-of-upkeep trigger cannot resolve,
  so the poll list is empty and the damage applies unasked — the identical
  fail-open this PR fixes for Bellowing Mauler. The guard never sees it because
  the **`effect_references_that_player` arm** (`oracle_trigger.rs:4020-4025`,
  returning at `:4051-4052`) claims the text first: Hex reads "…deals 1 damage
  **to that player** unless they pay {B} or {3}", and that anaphor matches one arm
  *before* the scope-subject scan at `:4062-4066`, whereas Mauler's "each player
  loses 4 life unless they…" carries no such anaphor and so reaches the scan. No
  follow-up issue is filed yet. Deliberately not widened here, since widening
  that arm would change the payer for every card it currently claims.
- **Untouched:** Court of Ambition (already correct), Acererak the Archlich,
  Blood Clock, Mogis God of Slaughter, Antagonism, Crimson Honor Guard, Furnace
  Punisher, Ood Sphere, Skullcage.

Partition: `A1=2 A2=6 B=2 C=1 N=5 X=4` → `A1=0 A2=0 B=0 C=11 N=5 X=4`, 20 cards /
20 triggers.

## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes. -->
<!--- Mention related issues, pull requests, or discussions with #<issue/PR/discussion ID>. -->
<!--- Tag people for whom this PR may be of interest using @<username>. -->

The diff-coverage tests added in #2731 can fail on Windows after another test clears and restores `os.environ`. An empty `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*` remains in Python's environment mapping but can disappear from the environment implicitly inherited by child processes. Git then fails with `missing config value GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2` and `unable to parse command-line config`.

Pass `env=dict(os.environ)` explicitly at all three Git/diff-cover subprocess boundaries. This preserves the original settings, including empty values, rather than dropping Git configuration to make the tests pass. The change is confined to the test harness.

author: firejune
body:
## What was wrong, measured on the branch point

`A02_NO_BONE_TRANSFORM_KEY` refuses a bone carrying the key `transform`. On the branch
point (`5296b7d`) its detail, as `M02_bone_transform_key` prints it:

```
caught by A02_NO_BONE_TRANSFORM_KEY: bone "stage" uses 4.2's "transform"; 4.3 wants "inherit"
```

The parsers disagree with "4.2's". Each `SkeletonJson.js` reads the bone key as follows
(grepped in the exam tooling's runtimes, `node_modules/@esotericsoftware/spine-core/dist/`):

| `spine-core` | line | reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4.0.31 | `:89` | `getValue(boneMap, "transform", "Normal")` |
| 4.1.56 | `:91` | `getValue(boneMap, "transform", "Normal")` |
| 4.2.120 | `:94` | `getValue(boneMap, "inherit", "Normal")` |
| 4.3.13 (the pinned one) | `:97` | `getValue(boneMap, "inherit", "Normal")` |

So the rename is **4.1 → 4.2**, and 4.2 never spelled `transform`. The card is
confirmed as written. `docs/SPEC_COVERAGE.md`'s timeline already records the rename that
way ("4.2 added `physics` + `referenceScale` and renamed bone `transform`→`inherit`").

**The card named two sites and there were six.** A sweep for the attribution
(`4\.2's .?transform`, `4\.3 renamed.{0,20}inherit`, `renamed.{0,30}inherit`) found it
in the message, the comment above it in `src/validate.ts` ("4.3 renamed it to
`inherit`"), the `LEGACY_BONE_INHERIT_KEY` comment, `docs/AUTHORING.md` §5.2's row and
§0.3's `GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED` paragraph, `docs/INGEST.md`'s
`GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED` row, `docs/BENCHMARK.md`'s assertion table, and a doc comment
in `selftest.ts` (the forged pre-4.3 file's "spelled 4.2's `transform`"). All are
corrected. `src/ingest.ts:1025` and `:1088` were checked as the brief asked. They say
"where 4.3 spells" and name no older generation, so they are true and unchanged.

## What now happens

The check is unchanged. A 4.3 file carrying the key is refused whichever generation
last wrote it. Only the sentence moves:

```
bone "…" uses "transform", the key 4.0 and 4.1 spelled; 4.2 and 4.3 spell it "inherit"
```

`LEGACY_BONE_INHERIT_KEY`'s comment now reads "The bone key 4.0 and 4.1 spelled
`transform`, renamed `inherit` in 4.2 and spelled that way by 4.3."

## The control — `CUR106`, one new case

Nothing held the guide's `A02` row to the message. `M02_bone_transform_key` asserts
the verdict and does not read the detail, and no control in the tree contained the
old sentence. So the old row ("a bone uses 4.2's `transform`") and the message could
drift apart silently. The highest existing `CUR` was `CUR105` (both casings
scanned). `CUR106` is appended as one hunk at the end of the currency suite, and it
copies `CUR104`'s shape:

- The sentence is **read off the validator** and not typed. `CUR104`'s pack is used,
  with its last bone given `LEGACY_BONE_INHERIT_KEY` through `editJson`, then gated,
  and the bone's name in the detail is put back to the row's `…`.
- A floor: exactly one `A02` sentence for one forged bone, and the guide must have an
  `A02` row.
- Held both ways: cutting the sentence from the row must raise exactly one fault.

`CUR107` was not needed and is not taken.

### Red-first

**Mutation window — two plants, both source edits, run one at a time.**

- **Plant 1 — the guide's row back to the branch point's sentence** (`docs/AUTHORING.md`).
  `bun run selftest` exit **1**, `PASS 1279 FAIL 1 SKIP 4`, and the one FAIL:
  ```
  FAIL  CUR106_THE_GUIDES_A02_ROW_QUOTES_THE_SENTENCE_THE_GATE_PRINTS: the A02 row does not quote "bone "…" uses "transform", the key 4.0 and 4.1 spelled; 4.2 and 4.3 spell it "inherit""
  ```
- **Plant 2 — guide kept, the message back to the branch point's** (`src/validate.ts`).
  Exit **1**, `PASS 1279 FAIL 1 SKIP 4`:
  ```
  FAIL  CUR106_THE_GUIDES_A02_ROW_QUOTES_THE_SENTENCE_THE_GATE_PRINTS: the A02 row does not quote "bone "…" uses 4.2's "transform"; 4.3 wants "inherit""
  ```
  The second plant shows the sentence really is read off the gate. A typed copy would
  have stayed green here.

In both runs the detail's second line, "cut from the row raised 0 fault(s)", follows
from the first. Cutting a sentence from a row that already lacks it changes nothing,
and `CUR104` behaves the same way.

Sweep complete, working tree restored, `docs/AUTHORING.md` md5
`09918a324378c7c23931fb3696a48d2f`, `src/validate.ts` md5
`e706ab813b8a167cf0f8ad6c7fa22b5d`. Both are equal to the sweep's branch point (this
branch's edited files before the first plant).

## The doc rows

- `docs/AUTHORING.md` §5.2 `A02` row: now quotes the gate's sentence, followed by the
  remedy. §0.3: "the bones carrying 4.0/4.1's `transform` where 4.3 spells `inherit`".
- `docs/GENERATIONS.md`: row 6 was already right. The "⚠️ Row 6 corrects its source"
  paragraph below it described where the misattribution lived (#706, the detail, the
  comment). Those places now say row 6's fact, so the paragraph is cut down to that
  fact. It keeps the rename (4.1 → 4.2), what the check refuses, and the sentence it
  prints. It adds no history, because a user of 1.0 never saw the old sentence.
- `docs/INGEST.md` `GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED` row, `docs/BENCHMARK.md` `A02` row: the
  attribution only.

## Rejected

- **A generation-aware message ("uses 4.1's `transform`").** The file declares
  `spine: 4.3.x` and carries the key. Which generation last wrote it cannot be known
  from the file, so the message states what both older generations spelled instead of
  guessing.
- **A `CUR107` banning the retired phrase across the tree** (the way `CUR101` bans the
  retired physics-bound sentences). It would catch one spelling of the misattribution
  and miss the rest. "4.2 spelled `transform`" and "4.3 renamed it" are the same claim
  in different words, and both were in the tree. The drift that can actually be
  measured is between the message and the row an agent is sent to, and `CUR106` checks
  that from the gate's own output.
- **Leaving `src/ingest.ts:1025`/`:1088` alone was a measured choice.** Their "where
  4.3 spells" names only 4.3, and that is true.

## Verification — every figure measured on this branch

`examples/` is absent from the worktree. It is a read-only symlink to the main
checkout's corpus (`/Users/firejune/Workspace/Firejune/rigc/examples`), and it is
gitignored (`.gitignore:27`).

| Command | Branch point | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bun run typecheck` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| `bun run lint` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| `bun run selftest` | exit 0 · PASS 1279 FAIL 0 SKIP 4 | exit 0 · PASS 1280 FAIL 0 SKIP 4 |
| `TMPDIR=/tmp/rigc-ci-sim bun run selftest` | — | exit 0 · PASS 1280 FAIL 0 SKIP 4 |
| `bun cli.ts bench 3 --candidate <rung3-2 build>` | — | exit 0, summary lines equal to `docs/LADDER.md`'s quoted window |
| `bun cli.ts check --candidate <same> --frames bench/reference/3-timing-and-spacing` | — | exit 0, MAE mean 10.67, worst 17.08 at f0002 |

Case lines are counted with `grep -cE '^  (PASS|FAIL|SKIP)\b'`. The verdict and name
pairs are identical to the branch point's, except for the one added line `PASS
CUR106_THE_GUIDES_A02_ROW_QUOTES_THE_SENTENCE_THE_GATE_PRINTS`. One detail line moves
on purpose: `M02_bone_transform_key`'s "caught by" line now shows the new sentence.
The summary's currency figure moves from 78 to 79, and the tally derives it.

**No emitted byte of a green build moves.** `gallery/look` and the rung-3 candidate
(`bench/runs/2026-08-23-rung3-2`) were each built with `--copy-images` into the same
out path, once from a `git archive` of the branch point under `/tmp` and once from this
branch. `diff -r` reported nothing for either: 26 files for `gallery/look`, where
`skeleton.json` md5 is `f2479ce97b7cd4ba3639eb6935f2d3a6`, and the rung-3 pair as well.
Before `--copy-images` was added, the only difference was the `images` path, which
names the source tree's location. The change alters a failure detail on a path that no
green build reaches.

No corpus export or gallery example is newly refused. The rule is unchanged.

Refs #814.

author: quntao-z
body:
## What

The grant-shell retype repair re-gates only the rows it changed.

## Why

It called `runStudentVisibilityGate({ collection: 'research', mode: 'apply' })` with no `recordIds`, so a run that corrects a handful of rows re-decides **all 4,756 live research rows**.

That buys nothing — a row the run did not touch cannot have changed tier because of it — and it has a practical cost: it makes a two-row repair unsafe to run beside any other Development write pass. I hit exactly that while trying to land #3145's remaining data operation, with a peer session mid-apply on a 6,000-row profile-link verification. Waiting on an unrelated pass to finish before correcting two rows is the wrong shape.

`retireSurnameClashLeadGrafts` already passes `recordIds: entityIds` for this reason, so this is bringing one repair in line with the other rather than introducing a pattern.

## Tests

No behaviour change to assert beyond scope, and the existing script suites cover the report shape. Full server suite green (10,567 tests, 646 files, 0 worker failures), `format:check` clean, lint 0 errors.

Refs #3145

author: fledgewing
body:
## Summary
Part of #264. Stacked on #268 (CI green). **Merge after #267, #269 and #270.** Until those are in, this check will (correctly) fail on OpenCode, Claude and Codex, and in `enforce` mode it refuses tool-bearing requests on those sidecars.

Every way the tool path has broken was a property of a specific CLI release, and none of them was visible to the offline suite:

- #195 and #256: Claude grew tools past a denylist.
- #255: Codex's catalog moved every model into a code-mode host.
- #267: OpenCode was hiding built-ins without denying them.

`sidecars/mcp_bridge/selfcheck.py` answers the question on the sidecar itself, at startup:

- **How it runs:** it spawns **this sidecar's CLI binary** with **this bridge's own argv** against a loopback fake model that speaks the Anthropic messages, OpenAI responses and OpenAI chat protocols. The CLI is redirected with its own base-URL mechanism and isolated config dirs, so there is no credential, no quota and no network.
- **What it forces:** the fake makes the model call the CLI's **native shell**, using a relative `touch`.
- **Pass condition:** every tool offered is a bridged caller tool (plus Codex's three read-only MCP-resource helpers), the bridged tool is visible, and the native call did not run.
- **`MCP_HOST_MIRROR_CHECK=enforce`** (the default): tool-bearing requests get **503 `host_mirror_unverified`** until the check has passed. The gateway reads a 5xx as transient and places the request on another plan, so tool work never runs on a CLI that isn't locked down. `report` only records the verdict; `off` skips the check.
- **Reporting:** the verdict appears on `/health` as `host_mirror`, and `python3 /app/mcp_bridge/selfcheck.py` reruns it inside a sidecar.

## Verification
Real pinned CLIs, run inside the sidecar image as `node`:

| provider | today's code | with #267–#274 |
|---|---|---|
| claude 2.1.278 | ❌ 13 native tools offered (Agent, Skill, Workflow, Cron*, …) | ✅ only `mcp__switchyard__…probe` |
| codex 0.155.1 | ❌ **`exec_command` ran in the sidecar**; `exec`, `spawn_agent`, `request_user_input`, … offered | ✅ probe + the 3 read-only resource helpers |
| opencode 1.18.31 | ❌ `skill` offered | ✅ only `switchyard_…probe` |

- A local integration branch merging all eight PRs merges cleanly, passes the full suite (695), and passes every pinned-CLI lockdown test inside the image.
- The unit tests drive the real `run()` with a fake CLI that is obedient, leaky or hides the bridged tool. They also cover the verdict logic, the fake model, and the gate (`enforce` 503s, `report` doesn't).
- `ruff check .` clean; pytest green.

## Deploy
The change is baked into the sidecar image. Run `scripts/apply.sh --build` from the main checkout.

author: ken8203
body:
## Motivation

想讓 local 的 Claude Code／Codex 只擔任 coordinator，research 與 implement 都委派到 outpost 執行。之前在 `~/bg-handoff/` 手動做過一輪（共用 context、brief、REPORT、bundle），這個 PR 把那套做法整理成固定流程。

兩個要解決的問題：

- outpost 與 local stow 同一份 `AGENTS.md`，若只寫「一律派到 outpost」，remote 的 agent 也會照做，變成往外委派。
- Claude Code 不會保存 `$HOME` 的 folder trust，worker 在 home 啟動每次都會卡在 trust 提示。

## 改動

- `agents/.codex/AGENTS.md`：新增「Outpost 分工」，工作目錄在 `/home/outpost/` 底下即為 worker，否則為 coordinator，並列出留在 local 的任務類型。
- `agents/.agents/skills/outpost-delegate/`：
  - `SKILL.md`：新任務走 preflight → worker 預設沿用 coordinator 的 harness／model／effort → 寫 brief → 推送 → `herdr --machine` 建 worktree／workspace 並啟動 agent → 等待 → 收回並驗證；另有「後續修正」與「清理」兩個入口。
  - `brief-template.md`：brief 範本與 `REPORT.md` 格式。
- `README.md`：補上 `outpost-delegate` 屬於非 skills CLI 管理的 skill。

## 設計決策

- **控制走 Herdr，內容走檔案**：每個任務一個 mailbox `~/code/delegate/<task>/`，prompt 只送一行指向 brief；報告從檔案讀回，不依賴 TUI scrollback。
- **程式碼走 git over ssh**：`outpost:code/<repo>` 直接當 remote 用，local 未 push 的 base 用 `git push` 送過去，結果用 `git fetch` 取回，不需要 bundle。
- **Worker 在 repo 內執行**：implement 用 `<clone>.<task>` worktree，repo 相關的 research 直接在主 clone 執行，才能讀到該 repo 的 instructions、skills 與 Hindsight bank；只有與任何 repo 無關的 research 才在 mailbox 執行。outpost 上沒有該 repo 時先 clone 到 `~/code/<repo>`。
- **`~/code` 為 trust 根目錄**：實測 Claude Code 的 trust 會由上層目錄繼承，新 clone 放 `~/code` 底下即可免去 trust 提示。
- **選用的 `delegate/<project>/common.md`**：同一 initiative 的多個任務共用 context 與已拍板的決策。

## 驗證

- 在 outpost 實測 `herdr --machine` 的 `workspace create`、`worktree create`、`worktree remove`、`workspace close` 與其 JSON 結構，測試資源已清除。
- 確認 `git ls-remote outpost:code/outpost` 可用。
- 過程中發現並寫進 skill 的陷阱：machine label 是 `Remote`、本機會先展開 `~`、`worktree create` 會自動開啟主 repo 的 workspace、`worktree remove` 不刪 branch。
- 實際跑完一輪 research 委派（查 `herdr agent prompt --wait --until` 語意，Claude worker），從送出 brief 到收回 REPORT 全程照 skill 執行。試跑修正了三個問題：`rsync` 不會建立多層目錄、cwd 不存在時 Herdr 會默默退回 home、`agent prompt` 的參數順序。
- Worker 的報告確認 `--until working --until blocked` 會回傳先觀察到的 state，但只有在 worker 原本 idle 時才能證明新 prompt 已開始，已寫進 skill。

## Merge 後

- local 與 outpost 都要 pull，並跑 `./scripts/skills-restore.sh` 把 skill link 進 `~/.claude/skills/`。
- 在 outpost 上執行一次 `cd ~/code && claude`，接受 folder trust。

author: mtmattei
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces FieldCheck, a complete cross-platform field inspection application built with Uno Platform. The application demonstrates a full-featured mobile and desktop app with asset management, inspection workflows, and data persistence.

## Key Changes

### Application Structure
- **Multi-platform support**: Android and Windows implementations using Uno Platform (Uno.Sdk 6.7.30, .NET 10)
- **MVVM architecture**: Comprehensive ViewModels for Dashboard, Assets, Inspections, and History views
- **Data persistence**: JSON-based repository with local file storage for assets and inspection records

### Core Features
- **Dashboard**: Overview of inspection statistics and quick actions
- **Asset Management**: Browse, search, and filter field assets with status indicators
- **Inspection Workflow**: Create new inspections with photo capture and form validation
- **History**: Track completed inspections with persistent storage
- **Responsive Design**: Adaptive layouts for mobile (Android) and desktop (Windows) platforms

### UI/UX Components
- **XAML Views**: ShellPage, DashboardPage, AssetsPage, AssetDetailPage, NewInspectionPage, HistoryPage, InspectionSuccessPage
- **Custom Controls**: StatusChip, StatePanel, and AssetDetailView for specialized UI patterns
- **Theme System**: Centralized resource dictionary for consistent styling across platforms
- **Navigation**: Frame-based navigation service for page transitions

### Services & Infrastructure

author: indigo423
body:
Closes #872.

A Grafana that reads no provisioning files, hosted or owned by someone else, could only get the riptide dashboards by hand-importing nine JSON files per release, or through a one-off script. Step 3 of the dashboards plan, after the tarball (#866) and the Helm values (#869).

## What changes

- **`deployment/clickhouse/dashboards-import.py`**, stdlib only. Given a Grafana URL, a token in `GRAFANA_TOKEN` and the release tarball or a directory, it:
  - creates `Riptide` with `Flow Analytics` inside, or moves an existing `Flow Analytics` there;
  - imports every dashboard there with overwrite, under its own uid;
  - deletes nothing.
- **One line per dashboard:** `created`, `updated 1.0.0 -> 1.0.2`, `unchanged (1.0.2)`, or `refused: <Grafana's reason>`. A run exits 1 on any refusal, and `--dry-run` writes nothing.
- **Shipped with every release** as `riptide-dashboards-import.py`, signed and attested (`make dashboards-import-asset`). `RELEASING.md` gets the row.
- **The guide** gains an API section, a table of what the script prints, and a symptom table for its errors.

## Measured on Grafana 13.2.2 with an Editor token, then encoded in the fake the tests use

- **An absent folder reads as 403, not 404.** So the script creates folders first and treats a 412 as "already there".
- **An identical re-import keeps the revision.** The first cut printed `updated 1.0.2 -> 1.0.2` for nine dashboards Grafana had not touched. It now prints `unchanged`.
- **Search is not a safe test for "empty".** It showed a folder as empty while the folder still held a library panel, and deleting that folder would have deleted the panel. "Empty" now comes from `GET /api/folders/<uid>/counts`, which covers dashboards, folders, alert rules and library elements. The script says what is left rather than suggesting a delete.
- **A file-provisioned uid** is refused with "Cannot save provisioned dashboard".

## Found in review, fixed test-first

- **Redirects were followed.** Python turns a redirected POST into a GET. An `http://` URL behind an http-to-https redirect would have printed "created" for folders never made, and re-sent the token to the redirect target. The script now refuses redirects and names the URL to use.
- **A 403 on one dashboard stopped the whole run.** That happens for a copy in a folder the token cannot touch. It is now that dashboard's refusal. Only a 403 on the folders stops the run.
- **Timeouts, dropped connections and malformed JSON escaped as tracebacks.** They now end as error messages.

## Checks

- **`make dashboards-version-test`:** 54 tests OK, 20 of them for this script against the fake Grafana. Fourteen mutations, each run against only its own test, all killed for the right reason.
- **Live on Grafana 13.2.2, three throwaway instances:**
  - empty instance: dry run, import, identical re-run;
  - the labmonkeys layout, nine dashboards at set 1.0.0 in a hand-made folder, upgraded with the v0.15.2 tarball: all nine moved and updated, the old folder reported empty and left in place;
  - a provisioned uid: refused, exit 1;
  - Viewer, wrong and missing token messages.
- **Workflow lint:** actionlint and zizmor clean. `make docs` is green, and the rendered page checks out.
- **Not done:** running the guide's section verbatim on a fresh Grafana. The local Docker daemon stopped answering partway through. All the script output in the guide comes from the live runs above, against this same script. The two `curl` verify lines were not run verbatim. The downloads can only run after a release.

## Merge, then release promptly

The guide downloads the script from `v%%VERSION%%`, which resolves to the newest tag. Until a release carries the script, that link 404s, so cut a release right after merging.

author: multiservicioslavina-commits
body:
## Resumen

Segunda entrega de la especificación de Rita orquestador (constraints estructuradas, secciones 12-15). Hoy, cuando un rider pedía una ruta con restricciones ("máximo 300 km, no Guatapé ni Jardín"), todo quedaba en manos del criterio del modelo sobre una sola llamada a `buscar_ruta` — sin nada que impidiera de verdad ofrecer un destino que el rider ya había excluido.

## Cambios

- **Nueva herramienta `planificar_ruta`**: filtra `rita_rutas` por distancia máxima (siempre solo ida, igual que `buscar_ruta`) y excluye de verdad los destinos que el rider no quiere — una ruta excluida ni siquiera llega como candidata, no depende de que el modelo se acuerde de descartarla al redactar.
- Las **preferencias blandas** (curvas, paisaje, poco tráfico) no se filtran en la consulta — se devuelven para que el modelo las use al elegir/ordenar entre las candidatas ya válidas, nunca para descartar una opción que ya calificó.
- System prompt actualizado con la distinción explícita entre restricciones obligatorias y preferencias blandas.
- Se extrae la nota de "solo ida" (del PR anterior) a una constante compartida entre `buscar_ruta` y `planificar_ruta`.

## Verificación contra datos reales

Con límite de 300 km: Guatapé (79 km) y Jardín (138 km) matchean por `destino_norm` ("guatape", "jardin") y quedan correctamente excluidos cuando se piden, dejando el resto de rutas bajo 300 km como candidatas.

### Ejemplo de entrada/salida

Input (llamada de la herramienta):
```json
{"distancia_max_km": 300, "destinos_excluidos": ["Guatapé", "Jardín"], "preferencias": ["curvas", "paisaje"]}
```

Output:
```json
{
  "candidatas": [ /* rutas <= 300km, sin Guatapé ni Jardín */ ],
  "excluidas_por_peticion_explicita": ["Medellín – Guatapé", "Medellín – Jardín"],
  "restricciones_aplicadas": {"distancia_max_km": 300, "destinos_excluidos": ["Guatapé", "Jardín"]},
  "nota": "candidatas ya cumple las restricciones obligatorias..."
}
```

## Test plan

- [x] Verificado el filtro de distancia y exclusión contra datos reales de `rita_rutas` antes de escribir el código.
- [ ] Sin toolchain de Deno en este entorno para type-check — revisado el diff manualmente, sigue el mismo patrón que las demás herramientas del archivo.
- [ ] Una vez desplegado, probar en vivo: pedirle a Rita una ruta con límite de distancia y un destino excluido.

author: aburan28
body:
## What this changes

Adds the curves shaped like ECC2K-130 to `challenges/ecc`. These are `y² + xy = x³ + 1` over F₂ᵐ with order 4·prime, which holds for m = 41, 83, 97, 103 and 107. m = 131 (ECC2K-130 itself) and the matching a=1 records are added too. The generator change is one line in the Koblitz degree list. Regenerating added 12 curve files and their catalog entries and changed no existing record.

It also adds `ecc2k130/small/`, a Metal Pollard rho solver that works for any m ≤ 127:
- **Walk:** the same step as ECC2K-130, `R ← R + σʲ(R)` with `j = 3 + (HW/2 mod 8)`. HW is the Hamming weight of x in a normal basis, so the walk works on the classes {±σⁱR} and saves the factor √(2m).
- **Distinguished points:** a point is distinguished when HW is at or below a cutoff. The host keys each one by the smallest rotation of its normal-basis x.
- **Scalars:** lanes count how many times they took each j instead of tracking scalars. A reported point is ∏(1+λʲ)^count · (uP + Q).
- **Field:** the kernel uses a sparse reduction polynomial. `field.py` maps each challenge's field onto it by finding a polynomial root (Cantor–Zassenhaus).
- **Solving:** `run.py` checks that bookkeeping identity for both points of every collision and solves for k. It then verifies k·G = target in the challenge file's own field, using `generate.py`'s independent scalar multiplication.

## Why

ECC2K-130 needs about 2⁶⁰·⁸ iterations, which is out of reach locally. The smaller curves in this family let us run the same attack to completion and check the measured costs against √(πℓ/4m). Expected iterations are 2³⁷·¹ at m=83, 2⁴⁴ at m=97 and 2⁴⁹ at m=107.

## How it was verified

C/CMake checklist items don't apply: there are no changes under `src/`, `tools/` or `tests/`.

- `run.py selftest` on m = 41, 83, 97 and 107: GPU products, squares, inverses, normal-basis weights, one walk step and start points against `field.py`. 640 of 640 checks passed for each.
- `run.py solve` on the real `f2-koblitz-a0-m41` record: 3 of 3 collisions solved, and the log matches the published 0x2bb. A separate m=41 test curve solved 5 of 5.
- m=83 throughput on the M4 Pro: 267 M it/s with 16384 threads × 8 lanes.
- **m=83 is solved: k = `0x13636a4544aad4c8e9526`, with k·G = target checked in the challenge's own field.** It was solved twice from separate seed ranges and both runs got the same log.
  - Baseline arithmetic: 894 s at 258 M it/s, 1.50× the expected iterations. See `evidence/m83-solve.json`.
  - Optimized arithmetic: 114 s at 615 M it/s, 0.46× the expected iterations. See `evidence/m83-solve-optimized.json`.
  - A first attempt stopped on a false match: two seeds with the same start point walked one identical trail. That was with 6 bases (83⁶ ≈ 2³⁸ start points). There are now 12 bases, and the host skips identical trails.
- All five arithmetic switch combinations tested pass `selftest` on m = 41, 83, 97 and 107, and on a1-m107.

## Algorithmic changes

The rho algorithm is unchanged. The field arithmetic is faster, and each change is a compile-time switch so `run.py bench` can compare variants. Walk rates on the M4 Pro (GPU time, 8192 threads × 16 lanes):

| curve | baseline M it/s | optimized M it/s |
|---|---|---|
| a0-m83 | 237 | 619 |
| a0-m97 | 162 | 354 |
| a0-m103 | 164 | 384 |
| a0-m107 | 143 | 371 |

Where the speedup comes from:
- Karatsuba products.
- A 16-bit, 3-bit-mask carry-less multiply: 27 integer multiplies per 32×32 product instead of 32.
- 32-bit squaring.
- Table-driven normal-basis conversion, with σʲ and the inversion's long squaring runs done as rotations.

`README.md` has the per-operation microbenchmarks and the lane-geometry sweep.

> **Low Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Expands the ECC challenge corpus with **12 scaled-down ECC2K-130-style** binary Koblitz instances (`f2-koblitz-a{0,1}-m{41,83,97,103,107,131}`): catalog count **251 → 263**, new curve/inspect JSON, and a **one-line** extension of Koblitz degrees in `challenges/ecc/generate.py`. author: doriancollier
body:
Phase 1 of agent permissions. Refs DOR-2278. Closes DOR-2094.

## What changes for you

- **One place to decide what your agents may do.** Settings → Permissions sets each kind of work to **Allowed**, **Ask** or **Blocked** for every agent. Rooms is the first area: making rooms, adding or removing people, renaming, leaving, merging a room's work, and archiving.
- **Full power means Full power.** If you chose Full power when you set up DorkOS, DorkBot (and every agent) can now make and arrange rooms without asking. If you chose to keep being asked, they ask first, and that now includes merging a room's work into the main branch. If you never chose, nothing changes until you do.
- **One agent can be different.** Each agent's profile has a Permissions page. A row says "Same as everyone" until you change it, and has a Reset.
- **Agents can archive a room** they are in when the work is done. The room and its history are kept, and you can bring it back.
- **Every change is in a history** that says what changed, who made it and when, and it is never cleared. With login off it says "Someone on this computer", because DorkOS can't tell who is at the keyboard.
- **Blocked tools disappear** from an agent's tool list, with one line telling it to ask you.
- **Edits made outside DorkOS are noticed.** If an agent's settings file is edited directly (by you, or by an agent with file tools), the change takes effect, and the history records it as "Changed outside DorkOS". The agent's page marks that row.
- The per-agent **Manage rooms** switch is gone; your old choice carries over.

## Not in this PR yet

Phases 2 to 4: an agent asking for a permission from a card, the other areas (tasks, other agents, chat connections, packages, settings) moving onto this model, and the undo and Control Center surfaces. Until then only Rooms follows the preset.

## Limits we accept, on purpose

- **File edits.** Anything that can edit files on this computer can edit an agent's settings file, and login does not stop that. DorkOS records the change rather than blocking it. The record it compares against sits in DorkOS's data folder, which a determined agent with a shell can also reach.
- **A tokenless agent gets the default.** With login off, an agent that drops its token is treated as an unidentified caller and judged by the defaults, so an agent set stricter than the default can escape its own setting that way. Turning login on closes this.

## Where to look first

- `apps/server/src/services/core/capabilities/permission-enforcement.ts` and the three choke points (`registry.invoke`, `authorizeCapability`, the MCP tool gate).
- `apps/server/src/services/core/permissions/`: the single write path, the history, the upgrade sweep, and `permission-observer.ts` (three review rounds; every guard is mutation-checked).
- `PATCH /api/mesh/agents/:id` now refuses `permissions` (`USE_PERMISSIONS_API`); only `/api/permissions/*` and `/api/agents/:id/permissions` write it.

Reviewed adversarially on the branch before opening (three rounds, final verdict ship).

author: crvouga
body:
## Summary

- **#118:** the login and consent pages served `form-action 'self'`. Chromium applies that directive to the redirect that follows the form submit, so the final 302 to a cross-origin `redirect_uri` was blocked after the transaction had already been consumed. These pages now send `form-action 'self' <redirect origin | custom scheme:>` for the transaction's redirect URI. The `form_post` page already did this, and it now uses the same helper.
- **#119:** discovery, JWKS, token, userinfo (including the Google/GitHub aliases) and revoke now answer `OPTIONS` with `204`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, the requested `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` and `Max-Age`. Real responses reflect `Origin`, add `Vary: Origin`, and expose `WWW-Authenticate`. Interaction pages and `/` still send no CORS headers.

## Note on #119

The oauth README listed "cross-origin browser token CORS policy" as deliberately not modelled. This PR removes that line and documents the new behavior. Real providers that support public browser clients answer CORS on these endpoints (Cognito hosted UI `/oauth2/token`, Google's token endpoint), and the reporter was running a proxy to get it. If we'd rather keep the divergence, revert the CORS commit hunk and close #119 as not planned instead.

## Evidence

## Summary

author: drewbitt
body:
## Summary

Implements **PR 3** of the goals-plan: a single **active top priority per goal**, surfaced on the Goals, Today, Review, and Journey pages. Additive only — no changes to `completed`/`status` or verdict logic (PRs 1–2 territory).

### Schema — `007_priorities.ts`
- `priorities`: `id`, `goalId` FK → `goals.id` cascade, `text`, `description`, `checkInDate` (optional YYYY-MM-DD "by" date), `createdAt`, `completedAt` (NULL = active), `reflection`.
- One active per goal enforced at the DB level:
  ```sql
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_priorities_active_goalId
    ON priorities (goalId) WHERE completedAt IS NULL;
  ```
- `data.d.ts` regenerated via `pnpm run db:codegen`.

### tRPC — `priorities` router (`src/lib/trpc/routes/priorities.ts`)
- `list({ activeOnly })` — joined with goal title/color/orderNumber (`PriorityWithGoal`), ordered by `goals.orderNumber`.
- `listCompleted({ goalId?, startDate?, endDate?, limit?, offset? })` — for journey milestones.
- `upsert({ goalId, text, checkInDate?, description? })` — transaction: sets `completedAt` on the current active row, then inserts the new one (replaced priorities become journey milestones, per plan).
- `edit({ id, text?, checkInDate?, description? })` — partial update; `null` clears a field.
- `complete({ id, reflection? })` — sets `completedAt` (+ optional reflection); no-op → `NoResultError`.
- `clear({ goalId })` — hard-deletes the active row, so cleared priorities never surface as fake milestones.

### UI
- **Goals page** (`GoalPriority.svelte`, under each `GoalBox`): darker goal-colored banner `Top Priority | text | by <date>` (new `darkerHSLColor` util — lightness ×0.55) with edit ✎ and complete ✓ buttons; description textarea below it that autosaves via `priorities.edit`; dashed `+ top priority` button when unset. Complete flow prompts for a reflection.
- **Today page** (`PriorityCards.svelte`, above the intentions list): outlined `N : text` cards in each goal's color; `N : +` placeholders open `PriorityModal` for that goal.
- **`PriorityModal.svelte`** (shared, in `lib/components/shared`): text + `by` date + description (spec placeholder text) — used by today cards, Review, and journey `OutcomesBox`. Edits via `edit`, creates via `upsert`, `Clear` via `clear`.
- **`ReviewGoalBox.svelte`**: one additive line — `N : text by <date>` (goal-colored, top-right) or `N : + new top priority` button wired through optional `priority`/`onNewPriority` props, kept minimal since PR 1 is editing this file concurrently.
- **Journey**: `listCompleted` fetched over the visible date range (and extended in `loadMore`); each day renders `★ N completed top priority: text` in goal color under the header.

### Tests
`src/lib/trpc/routes/priorities.test.ts` — 9 tests incl. one-active-per-goal (both `upsert` rollover and direct DB-level unique-index rejection), edit/null-clear, complete+double-complete, clear producing no milestone, `listCompleted` filters, and goal-delete cascade.

### Verification
- `pnpm check` 0 errors/warnings · `pnpm lint` clean · `pnpm test:unit --run` 74/74 · `pnpm build` ok.
- Screenshots (seeded dev DB): Goals page banner/description/`+` button, Today cards + `+` modal create flow (created a priority end-to-end through the UI), Journey milestone row.

Note: `007` numbering leaves room for the sibling PRs' migrations (005/006) to land before it regardless of merge order.

author: edwilde
body:
## What

The `composer_outdated` report now lists outdated packages that have a release compatible with the project's PHP version and the installed major of the packages named in `compatibility-packages`. The rest are collapsed into a `<details>` block that shows what blocks their latest release. This is intended for release as `v3`.

- New inputs:
  - `php-version`: used only when `composer.json` has no `config.platform.php`, because composer treats that setting as the platform.
  - `compatibility-packages`: empty by default, which means only PHP requirements are checked. The action has no framework-specific defaults.
- Per-version requirements come from the Packagist p2 API. Packages the API can't resolve, and packages installed from a named branch such as `dev-main`, are listed as "compatibility unknown".
- Abandoned packages stay in the open table, with the reason they have no compatible update.
- If the `composer outdated` output can't be read, the report says so and points to the workflow log instead of showing an empty table.
- The report logic is written in PHP (`composer/semver`, `composer/metadata-minifier`). `entrypoint.sh` keeps the `composer outdated` call and writes the outputs. The README describes the compatibility rule.

## Verified

- `vendor/bin/phpunit`: 35 tests, 55 assertions, all passing. They use fixtures only, with no network access, and run in the new `Tests` workflow.
- I built the image and ran it against a sample project on PHP 8.1 (`--direct --locked`):
  - With a framework's packages in `compatibility-packages`, each package stayed on the framework's installed major, e.g. 5.0.4 -> 5.4.10 while the latest is 6.2.3.
  - With the input empty, only PHP was checked, so guzzle went to 8.2.0.
- With an invalid `composer outdated` flag, `composer_outdated` contains the failure notice.

## Needs a decision

- Tag `v3` after merge.
- `composer_outdated_abandoned` is declared in `action.yml` but has never been written. It could be dropped in `v3`.

Bound browser probes and separate browser operation deadlines from outer test and hook bounds without changing runtime behavior.

Re-applied against upstream, which meanwhile replaced the `--version` exec
probe with a live CDP probe (`chromiumCdpAvailable`). That covers the
exec-hang half of the original patch its own way, so this keeps upstream's
CDP probe and re-lands only the half still missing: one deadline over the
whole probe. `ensureChromiumExecutable()` can run `browsers.install()` — a
first-use Chromium download — with no bound of its own, so a slow or wedged
download still hung every importing suite during module evaluation. The
probe now takes injectable resolve/launch seams so the bound is testable
without a real browser, and announces the skip it takes. The original
commit's `--version` fake-script tests are replaced by tests against that
shape.

Spec-impact: none. Refs RIG-3377
