author: syntheit
body:
## Summary

raven (NixOS in the Pixel 6 Pro's AVF VM) now sends every Nix build to the Mac mini's aarch64-linux builder VM, the one harbor and vista already use for fajita. Nothing changes on the mini.

- **Why:** nixos-avf builds raven a patched 6.1 kernel (`avf.useGenericKernel` is off), a patched systemd and four Rust guest agents. None of that is on cache.nixos.org, so every nixpkgs bump compiled it on the phone, next to the website and status page.
- **Network:** raven only makes an outbound ssh connection over Tailscale to the mini's sshd, then hops to the VM on `localhost:31022`. This is the same ProxyJump path harbor and vista use. It doesn't matter that raven's VM sits behind the phone's NAT and isn't on the LAN.
- **Auth:** the same `mac_builder_ssh_key` harbor and vista use. It is already authorized on `daniel@mini` (port-forwarding only) and in the guest.
- **`max-jobs = 0`:** raven builds nothing itself. With local builds left on, Nix sends a build out only while the builder has a free slot and runs the rest locally. On Nix 2.34.6 with 6 builds, 2 builder slots and local `max-jobs = 4`, 4 of 6 built locally. With `max-jobs = 0`, all 6 went to the builder.
- **`maxJobs = 2`:** Nix counts builder slots per client. harbor's 4 plus raven's 4 would put 8 jobs into the 8 GiB guest, where harbor saw builds get OOM-killed.
- **Timeouts:** `ConnectTimeout` and `ServerAlive` are set on raven's ssh config, because with `max-jobs = 0` every build waits on that connection.
- **mini:** comment-only changes. The parsed AST of both mini files is unchanged, so the mini's system is unaffected.

## Before merging

- [ ] Add the builder key to `secrets/raven.yaml`. raven won't build until this is done, because sops-nix fails with `the key 'mac_builder_ssh_key' cannot be found`. Run this wherever you edit secrets:
  ```sh
  sops -d --extract '["mac_builder_ssh_key"]' secrets/harbor.yaml | jq -Rs . \
    | sops set --value-stdin secrets/raven.yaml '["mac_builder_ssh_key"]'
  # check: should print ...ZBQyarX, the jump key in hosts/mini/default.nix
  sops -d --extract '["mac_builder_ssh_key"]' secrets/raven.yaml | ssh-keygen -y -f /dev/stdin
  ```

## Test plan (on raven)

- [ ] `nixos-rebuild dry-build --flake ~/nix#raven`. The first switch still builds locally, because the builder config isn't live yet, so check it lists only small derivations.
- [ ] `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake ~/nix#raven`
- [ ] `cat /etc/nix/machines` shows `ssh-ng://builder@mac-linux-builder aarch64-linux … 2 4 …`, and `nix config show max-jobs` prints `0`.
- [ ] `sudo ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new mac-linux-builder true` exits 0. The first run records the mini's and the VM's host keys; Nix's own connections pin the VM's key separately.
- [ ] Force a remote build and look for `on 'ssh-ng://builder@mac-linux-builder'` in the output:
  `nix build --no-link -L --impure --expr '(builtins.getFlake "nixpkgs").legacyPackages.aarch64-linux.runCommand "offload-${toString builtins.currentTime}" {} "uname -a > $out"'`
- [ ] Next real rebuild: the kernel, systemd and Rust agents build on the mini.
- [ ] Optional: with the mini unreachable, a build fails with `local builds are disabled (max-jobs = 0)`, and `--max-jobs auto` builds locally.

## Checked in a sandbox

Private inputs aren't reachable from the sandbox, so foyer and llm-agents were stubbed. Neither is touched here.

- raven's full `system.build.toplevel` instantiates. `nix-diff` against `main` shows only `nix.conf` (`max-jobs 0`, `builders-use-substitutes`), `/etc/nix/machines`, `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`, the sops manifest (plus the key) and the nix-daemon restart trigger.
- OpenSSH 10.5p1 (`ssh -G`) resolves both Host blocks as intended. Our blocks come before `Host *`.
- Nix 2.34.6: with `max-jobs = 0` the builder still builds, trivial derivations go remote too, and an unreachable builder fails fast with the message above.

## Known trade-offs and follow-ups (not in this PR)

- With the mini down, raven can't rebuild, not even a one-line `/etc` change, unless you pass `--max-jobs auto`. Trivial derivations also make the ssh round trip.
- The harbor, vista and raven builder configs are near-copies and should become one shared module. I left harbor and vista alone because I can't evaluate them here.
- harbor and vista have no ssh timeouts, so a hung VM stalls their builds.
- vista's `maxJobs = 8` contradicts harbor's OOM reasoning.
- The jump host key is trust-on-first-use (`accept-new`) on all three clients.

body:
## Summary

Update Harness from t3code v0.0.38 to [v0.0.42](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases/tag/v0.0.42) (`719a76ca1dbf5490f1aa33ffb9966301e02be9a9`), preserving the existing TritonAI experience while adopting upstream web, desktop, mobile, server, and tooling changes.

- Preserve UCSD managed providers, credentials, approved Codex 0.151.0, branding, attachments, integrations, and controlled updates.
- Restore collapsible project folders and compact thread rows, including saved collapse state and keyboard navigation. Keep upstream drag, pin, snooze, and settle handling.
- Keep Runtime mounted during access-key restarts so reconnect progress and timeout messages survive. Give provider names room in the left list and place runtime version/update controls in the details panel. Rename the default Frontier label to Cloud models.
- Preserve catalog names such as GLM when rebuilding custom model picker entries; explicit user names still take precedence.
- Skip the upstream setup wizard because Installer owns managed setup; keep authentication and settings recovery. Remove the Dev label pill background.

This is one integration PR. Both release channels pin [Installer bf4de6e](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Installer/commit/bf4de6e9d9298513f373a323db7eccf32d004ad4), which pins [Plugins 8aee4ec](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Plugins/commit/8aee4ec28d41488f99632146134b0d869352c6fc). These are immutable build inputs. Separate queue, remote-file materialization, Lucid, and reasoning-trace work is outside this PR.

## Compatibility and release impact

Existing database migrations 1–46 retain their shipped identities; upstream migrations append as 47–55 with existing-Harness upgrade coverage. Effect moves to 4.0.0-rc.112, Electron to 44.1, and standalone/WSL packaging uses Node 26.8.2 with managed policy and plugins included. The read-only `.repos` tree matches the exact upstream tag.

The desktop loads external ESM-only Cua modules through dynamic imports, with a built-bundle regression check. Release follow-ups preserve controlled draft publication, validate archive path collisions, and pin setup dependencies. Stable/nightly identity, signing, Installer sequencing, and downstream nightly publication guards remain in place. This PR does not publish a release.

## Validation

- Earlier integration checkpoints passed the full 17,224-test suite (56 skipped), workspace typecheck, lint, Knip, release smoke, desktop/server/web/marketing builds, native mobile checks, and Rust tests. A later unchanged server-readiness timeout passed on focused rerun.
- Final UI batch: 334 tests across nine affected files, web typecheck, targeted lint, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Pinned Plugins contract and Installer composition checks passed at earlier integration checkpoints. The current plugin-enabled dev build admitted all five managed plugins; Electron created its window, the backend returned HTTP 200, and both managed providers reported ready. Authenticated plugin calls remain a separate user check.
- An extracted macOS ARM64 CLI archive previously booted with no system Node using the pinned SEA runtime. Signed Windows/WSL upgrade UAT remains a release validation step.

Application CI passed on `6d6255d43` ([run](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Harness/actions/runs/35960428844)); Greptile passed on that head. Independent review of the final UI batch found no actionable P0–P2 issues. CodeRabbit’s completed review identified an upstream-sync test-command issue; both the workflow and script default now use `vp run test`, with both focused sync tests passing. CodeRabbit’s follow-up is quota-limited despite its green status; no fresh verdict was produced for this two-line correction. No unresolved inline review threads remain.

The PR-size buffer fix was extracted and merged in #273 after its CI passed. A fresh labeler run on `f9639e828` passed. Merging that base update into this branch preserved the exact file tree from `6d6255d43`; all applicable application CI jobs passed for the new merge commit ([run](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Harness/actions/runs/35961974216)).

author: offgridwithjd
body:
#1236's third, fourth and fifth batches. Eighteen arms attacked across three
parts. **No test changed and no code changed** — the diff is the ledger rows,
the budget note and the CHANGELOG.

## Six mutations, predictions written before they ran

```
  veC    the elision predicate forced true               5 arms
  b190A  pgc_build_needs_clean never asks for a clean     5 arms
  b190B  the stamp writes an escaped literal (#898)       2 arms
  b190C  pgc_build_needs_clean always demands a clean     2 arms
  b190D  unknown provenance reported as a major, PG?      2 arms
  jvaB   the dim-side uniqueness refusal disabled         2 arms
```

**b190A and b190C are opposites and redden disjoint pairs**, which is the pair
worth reading. A guard that *never* cleans loses the five arms about when a
clean is required. A guard that *always* cleans loses exactly two — "building
the same major again needs no clean" and "but a tree with no objects at all
needs nothing, stamp or not". Only those two separate a correct guard from one
that is merely fail-closed, and a guard cleaning unconditionally would pass
every other arm in the part.

## Eighteen rows touched, fifteen newly dated

The other three are `validity_elision` arms **already dated 2026-09-18 under the
inverse mutation** — the elision predicate forced *false*, so every reader
expects a bitmap the writer did not write. This batch forces it *true*. Both
directions redden the same three arms, so those rows now carry both mutation
strings and the later date rather than the newer observation overwriting the
older. An arm reddened by a predicate in either direction is better evidence
than one reddened in a single direction.

## Re-derived on the merged tree, not carried forward

These six ran once before #1240 and #1241 landed. I re-ran all six against
`ac80762a` rather than merging the logs I had held, and every one reproduced its
earlier result **exactly — same names, not merely the same counts**:

```
  veC 5   b190A 5   b190B 2   b190C 2   b190D 2   jvaB 2      18 total
  all six sets identical to the held ones
  control: two unrelated sets DO compare as different
  restored all, pristine
```

So the held logs would have served. Re-running is what makes that a measurement
rather than an assumption: **"the check names still exist" and "the mutations
still redden them" are different claims**, and only re-running tests the second.
I had verified the first in advance, which proves less than it looks like.

Every anchor was dry-run first — apply, assert the digest moved, restore, assert
byte-identical — before a single suite ran.

**The two C mutations ran with a forced `make clean`.** PGXS here has no
`--enable-depend`, so a stale object after a *header* edit would leave `veC`
reddening nothing and reading exactly like a fixture fact — a false negative on
the one mutation whose subject is a decode predicate.

## Verification

```
  premise: no code changed vs main        empty diff for src/ and test/lib.sh
  ledger and budget agree                 never=1497  budget=1497
  harness_selftest  pg17a  rc=0   1138 checks, 0 FAIL
  harness_selftest  pg18a  rc=0   1138 checks, 0 FAIL
  validity_elision         rc=0   25 passed + 0 failed = 25
  native_join_vector_agg   rc=0   13 passed + 0 failed = 13
  docs_style.sh                   PASSED
```

Census re-derived by counting on this tree, not carried:

```
  awk -F'\t' '$5=="never"' test/check_ledger.tsv | wc -l   ->  1497
  1606 rows total, 109 not `never`,  1497 + 109 == 1606
  and 1512 - 15 newly dated == 1497
```

## Note on the reading list

This will push #1236's reading list **up**, not down, and that is the metric
behaving correctly rather than a regression. The list is "never, non-premise, in
a part where a sibling is dated", so the first attack on a part promotes its
unattacked siblings from invisible to suspect. #1244 did the same thing: 72 to
154, because part 400 went from zero dated arms to eight. Parts-with-a-dated-arm
is the monotone companion number.

author: rizanrizan93
body:
Fixes the timestamp integrity defect exposed by V193 parity.

Before:
- Supplement HTML times were always interpreted as Europe/London.
- Forex Factory can render its calendar in a different timezone depending on site/device/default settings.
- A page rendered in e.g. America/Los_Angeles could therefore be shifted by 8 hours when misread as London.

After:
- Parse the page-declared IANA timezone from "Calendar Time Zone".
- Convert each event from that declared zone to UTC.
- Persist the detected timezone and timestamp contract in page provenance.
- Fail closed if the fetched page does not explicitly expose a valid IANA timezone.
- Regression test reproduces 05:30 America/Los_Angeles -> 12:30 UTC for the Sep 11 2026 CPI release.

This changes research data integrity only. V193 remains blocked by TIMESTAMP_AUDIT_REQUIRED until corrected corpus/backfill/parity are rerun and audited.

author: canzovo
body:
# Pull Request 模板

## 合入门禁提醒

> **NPU CI 不会在 PR 新建、重开或 push 新 commit 时自动执行。**
>
> PR 新建、重开或 push 新 commit 后，GitHub 会自动把当前 head commit 的以下 7 个 NPU CI 分项状态标记为 pending，说明该 commit 暂未执行双平台 NPU CI：
>
> 1. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 01 环境、wheel 与运行时契约`
> 2. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 02 全量 OPP 构建`
> 3. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 03 torch_custom wheel 与 OPP 布局`
> 4. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 04 OPP 安装与 PyTorch 适配`
> 5. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 05 GDR Example/ST`
> 6. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 06 chunk_fwd_o 局部覆盖安装`
> 7. `NPU CI / A2+A5 / 07 报告与 commit 校验`
>
> 每个平台按上述顺序执行前 6 个分项；任一前置分项失败时，后续分项会标记为未执行，不再继续运行。失败结果会保留关键报错，并给出带 `CI_STAGE=<分项>` 的容器复现命令。汇总任务最后执行第 7 项。合入前，当前 head commit 的 7 个状态和自动执行的 `CI 契约测试` 必须全部成功，并且满足 GitHub 分支保护要求的 2 个 approval；如果本 PR 后续更新了 commit，旧 commit 的 CI 结果不再有效，需要仓库 Admin 权限账号重新触发。即使已有 2 个 approval，只要当前 commit 未完成 NPU CI，仍不可合入（`weinachuan` 可按仓库保护规则 bypass）。
>
> 触发方式：
>
> - GitHub `Actions` 页面选择 `NPU CI`，在 `Branch` 下拉框选择 CI 定义分支，点击 `Run workflow`，填写本 PR 编号。
> - 在 PR 评论区发送 `/run-npu-ci quick` 或 `/run-npu-ci full`；默认使用 PR 目标分支的 `ci.yml`，必要时可追加 `ci_ref=<branch>`。
> - 同一 PR 的同一 commit 如果已有 NPU CI 在排队或运行，重复评论只会更新机器人评论，不会再次占用 NPU。
> - NPU CI 会执行 `ci/example_st_cases.json` 中启用的 Example/ST 用例；当前 `case1_current_default` 保持原始 shape。新增 GVA、`Vdim=256` 等场景时，请在用例文件中显式填写 `B`、`T`、`chunk_size`、`query_head`、`value_head`、`Kdim`、`Vdim` 等 shape 字段，以及 `gate_source`、`gate_function`、`initial_state`、`output_final_state`、`qk_l2norm` 等行为字段。
> - Example ST 必须使用与平台匹配的已验证 PyTorch/`torch_npu` 组合；A2 与 A5 不得混用 wheel、Python ABI 或 CANN 镜像，也不要拉取 `op-plugin` 重新编译。
> - 修改算子 `def`、`aclnn` 接口入参类型，或修改 `torch` 接口入参类型等导致不满足 ABI 一致性的改动，必须由 `weinachuan` 在当前 head commit 上检视通过；ABI 敏感路径已由 CODEOWNERS 指向 `weinachuan`。
> - NPU CI 部署与排障教程见 [`docs/Fla-npu仓CI部署教程.md`](docs/Fla-npu仓CI部署教程.md)。

## 关联 Issue / 背景

- 关联 Issue:
- 背景与目标:
- 本 PR 解决的问题:

## 变更类型

- [x] Bug 修复
- [ ] 新功能 / 新算子
- [ ] 算子性能优化
- [ ] 算子精度 / 稳定性修复
- [ ] Tiling / InferShape / OpApi 调整
- [ ] 构建 / CI / 脚本变更
- [x] 文档 / 示例 / 测试更新

## 算子责任范围

请明确本 PR 修改的算子责任边界，便于审查、验收和后续维护。

- 涉及算子名称:
- 涉及目录 / 文件:
- 责任人 / 提交人: @Canzovo
- 修改范围:
  - [ ] `op_host` / 算子定义
  - [x] `InferShape` / 参数校验
  - [ ] `Tiling` 策略
  - [ ] `op_kernel` / Ascend C Kernel
  - [ ] `op_api` / aclnn 接口
  - [ ] `torch_custom` 适配
  - [ ] `Triton` 算子
  - [x] 单算子测试
  - [ ] `example / ST` 测试

author: luvchakra
body:
## Changes
- **Header search.** On HomeTalk, the header now shows the WonderHome mark and a **Search messages** box where the title used to be. On desktop it replaces the global search.
  - Results cover what the member said to WonderHome and what it said back, across their own conversations, newest first, up to 30.
  - Each result shows who said it, the day and time (in the household's time zone), and an excerpt with the match highlighted.
  - Tapping a result that is on screen scrolls to it and briefly highlights it. A result from further back opens in full inside the results.
  - The results have loading, empty and error states, and close on Escape or a tap outside.
- **API.** `GET /api/v1/households/{id}/conversation?q=` returns `{ matches }`, served by the new `searchMessages` in `conversation/repository.ts`.
  - It only reads the caller's own sessions. A conversation another member shared with the household is never searched, and RLS still applies.
  - The `ilike` pattern is escaped, so `%`, `_` and `\` are matched literally. The query must be 2–100 characters.
  - The OpenAPI document is updated.
- **No empty band above the tab bar.** HomeTalk no longer reserves the full 44px raised-button clearance above the tab bar. It now stops just clear of the button, which only rises about 15px.
  - This adds the `--wh-tabbar-raised-overhang` token and a `fill` prop on `AppShell`.
  - Scrolling pages keep the full clearance.
- **Kit and docs.**
  - `MobileHeader` has a new `search` slot, `AppShell` has new `headerSearch` and `fill` props, and `ChatMessage` has a new `id` anchor.
  - Design notes and a progress note are updated.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass.
- The core unit suite passes: 179 files, 2,613 tests, including the new `message-search.test.ts`.
- Checked in Chromium at 360×780 and 1280×860 against a QA household with real turns:
  - the disclaimer now ends 18px above the tab bar (it was 42px), just clear of the raised button;
  - there is no horizontal scroll, and the "Search messages" placeholder fits at 360px;
  - "grocery" returns 2 messages and "ADD" returns 4, so matching is case-insensitive, and "zzzqqq" shows the empty state;
  - picking a result scrolls to that message;
  - a request with another household's id returns 404.
- The QA user and household were deleted, and a count confirmed nothing was left.

This PR is part of a stack containing 10 PRs:

1. `main`

9. #84
10. #85
11. **"feat(auth-broker): restore complete metrics support" (this PR)**
<!-- end jj-vine stack -->

Reapply the full upstream metrics change set, including the opt-in serve flag, scrape-token authorization, renderer, and correctness follow-ups.

Re-applied against upstream, which meanwhile split the monolithic
`AuthStorage` into namespaced modules under `packages/ai/src/auth/`
(`9013268ba1`). The original diff's `auth-storage.ts` hunks could not be
replayed — the whole file conflicts, and taking the patch's side would have
reverted that refactor — so each hunk was ported to the module that now owns
its code, with no upstream behavior reverted:

- `#reportHasNoIdentity` / `#hasConflictingScopeAccountId` -> exported
  `usageReportHasNoIdentity` and a local helper in `auth/usage-report.ts`,
  beside the `usageReportMetadataValue` / `usageReportScopeAccountId`
  helpers they read.
- The `credentialKey` grouping preference -> `usageReportIdentifiers` in the
  same module, ahead of the weaker projectId/alias fallbacks.
- The `credentialKey` stamp and both `credentialId` request stamps ->
  `UsageService` in `auth/usage.ts`; `credentialId` itself onto
  `UsageRequestDescriptor` in `auth/usage-cache.ts`.
- The plan-normalization dedup -> `usage/openai-codex.ts`, which is where the
  inline copy `canonicalizePlan` replaces now lives.

Test seams moved with the same refactor: the aggregate-usage override is now
the store-level `AuthCredentialStore.fetchUsageReports` hook rather than an
`AuthStorageOptions` field, and `fetchUsageReports()` / `reload()` are now
`usage.reports()` / `credentials.reload()`.

author: tellang
body:
## 목적
tfx-live 로 이미 떠 있는 codex 에 붙을 수 있게 한다. tmux 안의 codex 는 기존 세션을 그대로 쓰고, tmux 밖의 codex 는 공유 app-server 데몬으로 붙는다.

## 배경
codex-cli 0.156 TUI 는 `features.daemon_auto_start` 가 켜져 있으면 공유 로컬 app-server 데몬 위에서 돈다. 근거는 두 가지다.
- 바이너리 문자열: `local daemon connection failed; starting embedded app server`, `--no-daemon`
- lsof: TUI 소켓이 데몬 accept 소켓과 짝을 이룬다

그래서 어느 터미널에서 띄운 TUI 든 데몬 소켓으로 닿는다.

프로토콜 사실(실측):
- `thread/loaded/list` 와 `thread/read` 로 스레드와 상태(idle, active)를 본다. `includeTurns` 는 `-32601` 로 실패한다.
- 다른 연결은 `thread/resume` 을 먼저 해야 turn/item 알림을 받는다. 안 하면 턴은 들어가지만 응답을 못 읽는다.
- active 스레드에 `turn/start` 를 보내면 같은 turn id 로 진행 중인 턴에 합쳐진다(steer).

## 변경
- `peer --attach-a/--attach-b`: 기존 tmux 세션 재사용. 새로 띄우지 않고 끝나도 종료하지 않는다. npm shim(`node`)으로 뜬 codex 도 ps 로 판정한다.
- `ask`: `--session 이름:창.pane` 타깃, 보내기 전 busy 검사(`--if-busy wait|fail|interrupt`, `--busy-timeout`). `stop` 은 pane 타깃과 pane/window id 를 거부한다.
- `ask --cli codex --transport uds --thread <id|auto>`: 데몬 위 TUI 스레드에 턴을 넣는다. 응답은 `final_answer` 와 `commentary` 를 나눠 준다. 바쁜 스레드는 `wait|fail|steer`.
- `orchestrate --codex-socket PATH|default`, `list-sessions --transport uds`.
- codex 0.156 대응: `model: loading` 화면을 준비 완료로 보지 않고, 응답 끝의 시각 줄을 뺀다.

## 검증
- 대상 테스트 6개 파일: 146 통과, 0 실패, 5 건너뜀(`packages/core` 에 원래 없는 파일의 sync 검사)
- biome, `lint:skills`, `release:check-mirror` 통과
- 실제 codex-cli 0.156.1 데몬과 TUI 로 확인한 항목: UDS ask(2초), busy 검사 세 경로, steer 판정, pane 타깃 ask, start 직후 ask, peer attach, UDS 와 tmux 를 섞은 freeform peer(4 hop, 마커 누출 없음), orchestrate 붙기 모드(spawn 없음)
- 리뷰: Claude 코드 리뷰의 P1 1건과 P2 5건, P3 대부분 반영

## 알려진 한계
- TUI composer 에 쓰다 만 초안이 있으면 붙여넣은 프롬프트와 합쳐진다.
- TUI 를 끈 뒤에도 그 스레드가 데몬에 로드된 채 남는다. 같은 cwd 에서 `--thread auto` 가 모호해지면 후보 목록 오류로 멈추니 `--thread ID` 를 지정한다.

author: federico2014
body:
**What does this PR do?**

Remove SM2/SM3 implementations, runtime engine selection, and Toolkit `--sm2` options. Simplify signing and hashing APIs to ECKey/secp256k1 and SHA-256, and update their callers and tests across the dependent modules.

Retain a startup-only compatibility check before storage or keystore initialization: an absent `crypto.engine` uses the default suite; explicit `eckey` is accepted with a deprecation warning; all other values, including `sm2`, null, and non-string values, fail with migration guidance. Add configuration and FullNode startup regression tests and document the migration requirements.

**Why are these changes required?**

The unused engine switch spans consensus-critical hashes, signatures, addresses, and Merkle roots. Removing it simplifies the cryptographic path, while the startup check prevents an existing SM2 deployment from silently switching algorithms against incompatible chain data. Implements the compatibility requirements discussed in tronprotocol/java-tron#6959.

**This PR has been tested by:**

- Focused configuration and FullNode startup tests passed, covering default startup, explicit `eckey`, unsupported values, and rejection before database-directory creation or keystore initialization.
- `./gradlew test :framework:checkstyleMain :framework:checkstyleTest --continue --console=plain` passed: 3,437 tests passed, 27 skipped, zero failures; both framework Checkstyle tasks passed.
- Manual live-node testing was not performed.

**Follow up**

Existing SM2/SM3 deployments must remain on a compatible release until a separate migration is completed. Changing the configuration does not convert chain data or keys.

**Extra details**

The cross-module changes are required by the removal of shared engine-selecting APIs. This breaks those Java APIs and removes SM2/SM3 support; the default ECKey/SHA-256 path is retained.

## Summary

#4 gave ring shaders a palette. This extends the identical uniform and helper to the `postprocess` preamble, which had no colour uniform at all, so window, cursor and screen effects could not follow a scheme either.

A preset opts in with the same `palette` key, defaulting to `false`. `rainbow-smoke`, `rainbow-waves`, `rainbow-radial`, `rgb-shimmer` and `rgb-border` read it; every other shipped effect keeps its own colours.

The key is read off the preset naming each effect, so window, output, region and global scopes opt in separately and nothing is inherited. A window preset with `palette = false` sees a count of zero whatever the global preset does. A shell rewriting `[colors]` moves every opted-in effect together on the next reload.

Each effect owns its palette by value: `fx_scene_postprocess` carries the colours inline, and a window effect gets `wlr_scene_rect_set_palette` beside the existing `wlr_scene_rect_set_postprocess`, mirroring `wlr_scene_border_set_palette` from #4.

The one deliberate difference from the ring scope: a ring falls back to `ring_base_color()` when the count is zero, and a postprocess pass has no base colour, so `umbriel_palette_at` returns opaque white there. A shader should test `umbriel_palette_count` rather than rely on it, which is what the converted effects do and what the docs show.

## Motivation

Same as #4, one scope further. A wallpaper-driven scheme updates `[colors]` and every window effect stays on whatever its GLSL hardcoded.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Testing

`just format`, `just lint`, `just test` and `just check` all clean. 66 unit, 215 harness, up one from #4's 214.

`209_shader_window_palette` uses a probe shader rather than a shipped effect, because every shipped one tints existing client content and so cannot isolate the uniform. It declares `scope = "window"` and configures no global preset at all, which is what makes the assertion meaningful: an effect reading a palette published for another scope would see nothing here. It asserts the palette reaches the window, that a `[colors]` reload changes it, and that opting out drops the count to zero, then swaps in `rainbow-radial` to confirm a shipped effect still compiles and runs with the palette on.

Negative-controlled by disabling the window opt-in: the check fails with `pixel 0 0 255`, the probe's opt-out branch, rather than a threshold wobble.

Two things about that check worth recording, since both cost real time to find and neither is obvious:

- the check must set `in_capture = true`. Postprocess effects are excluded from captures by default (`Shaders::inCapture` is `false`, honoured at `wlr_scene.c:5098`), so `grim` otherwise photographs the unfiltered scene and no assertion about a postprocess effect can ever hold.
- it must set `redraw = "continuous"` and keep a client mapped. A global pass is clipped to `data->damage`, and the tick that damages the whole output for continuous redraw only runs on output commit, so an idle headless output renders nothing.

`config_load` asserts the key parses on a preset.

## Manual Coverage

- [x] Tested in a nested Umbriel session
- [x] Tested in a native Umbriel session
- [x] Tested with native Wayland applications

In a nested session running a `scope = "window"` preset on `rainbow-smoke` with a four-entry ramp of one colour: the window rendered that single hue rather than the shader's hue wheel, a live rewrite of `[colors]` moved it to a second hue without a restart, and setting `palette = false` on that preset restored the full hue wheel. The client was a native Wayland terminal.

Not claimed: a native session, multiple monitors, scaled output, XWayland, and the two layouts. #4 covers those for the ring scope; this change shares that path but was not re-run against each.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is ready for review, or it is marked as Draft.
- [x] This change fits `SCOPE.md`, or its scope was agreed in an issue or on Discord first.
- [x] I read and followed the relevant guidance in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] I ran `just format`, or this PR has no C++ changes.
- [x] I ran the relevant build, test, lint, or verification commands, or explained why they were not run.
- [x] I functionally verified compositor behavior where automated checks are insufficient.
- [x] I self-reviewed the changes.
- [x] I checked for new warnings or errors.
- [x] I updated `docs/` and `examples/config.toml`, or this PR does not change user-facing configuration or behavior.
- [x] I used canonical names for config keys, IPC actions, paths, and identifiers.

`examples/config.toml` documents no shader preset keys, so the reference for this one lives in `docs/user/barrulus-shaders.md` beside `scope`, `in_capture` and `redraw`.

## Additional Notes

The ramp builder moved from `view/decoration.cpp` into `config/shaders.cpp` so both scopes share one definition rather than drifting apart. That is the only change in this PR to a file #4 touched.

Happy to split the five shader conversions out if you would rather take the plumbing on its own.

author: heisluka
adacovsk
body:
`summarizeHeartbeatRunResultJson` keeps the text fields and the cost aliases and drops everything else, so `num_turns` never reaches the stored run record — even though the adapter returns it and `heartbeat.ts:3582` already reads it live to detect a no-op run.

The consequence only shows up later. A run that dies at `maxTurnsPerRun` leaves `status: failed`, `errorCode: adapter_failed` and the message `Reached maximum number of turns (160)` — and no way to ask where non-failing runs actually land. Confirmed against the live instance: every persisted `resultJson` on this fleet carries exactly `{result, total_cost_usd}`, so the distribution cannot be read at any limit.

That matters for one open decision in particular: an agent already sitting at the highest turn cap of any role, and dying at it anyway, is the case where raising the cap again without a measurement repeats an intervention that has already failed once.

Kept under both spellings (`num_turns`, `numTurns`). `readNumericField` already distinguishes absent from present-and-zero, so a legitimate `0` is stored rather than dropped as falsy — covered by a test.

**Verified:** `pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm vitest run server/src/__tests__/` — 111 files, 555 passed, 1 skipped.

body:
closes https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/23189 ### This PR `process_properties()` now passes each nested object's `required` list into the recursive call instead of overwriting the loop variable, and forwards `allow_none_with_default` — the same two arguments `preprocess_schema()` already passes for the top level and for `definitions`. ### Why `required_fields` was rebound inside the `for key, schema in properties.items()` loop, so after the first nested object every later sibling was null-typed against the *nested* object's `required` list. The same input then validated differently depending on where a nested property happened to sit in the schema: * an optional sibling sharing a name with a nested required property was rejected for holding `None`; * a required sibling was silently **accepted** as `None`, because the leaked list no longer contained its key. Dropping `allow_none_with_default` on the way down meant that option — which `_validate_work_pool_job_variables()` passes as `True` for deployment/job variables (`src/prefect/server/api/validation.py:219`) — stopped applying below the top level.
Measured before / after (issue #23189 script, run against main at 148e9978 and then with this commit) ``` base this branch 1a optional 'plain', nested first ['None is..'] [] 1b optional 'plain', nested last [] [] 2a required 'plain', nested first [] ['None is..'] 2b required 'plain', nested last ['None is..'] ['None is..'] 3 nested field with a default, option ['None is..'] [] set to True ``` `['None is not of type 'string'']` abbreviated to `['None is..']`. Rows 1a/1b and 2a/2b are the same object validated against the same schema with only the property order swapped; row 2a is the direction where the base accepts a `None` the schema forbids.
### Behaviour change to be aware of Two things do change for schemas that nest, both intended: * a required property that a nested sibling used to "unlock" now rejects `None` again (row 2a above); * an optional nested property with a default now accepts `None` under `allow_none_with_default=True`, like the top level already did (row 3). I found no test in the suites below that depended on either old outcome. ### Local validation ``` uv run pytest tests/utilities/schema_tools/ -q -p no:randomly 242 passed uv run pytest tests/server/orchestration/api/test_validation.py 25 passed uv run pytest tests/events/server/test_automations_api.py -q \ -k "valid or schema" 15 passed, 43 deselected uv run pytest tests/server/orchestration/api/test_deployments.py -q \ -k "var or default or none" 34 passed, 136 deselected uv run pre-commit run ruff-check --files Passed uv run pre-commit run ruff-format --files Passed uv run pre-commit run mypy --files Skipped (paths outside the hook's `files:` pattern) ``` RED/GREEN for the new tests specifically: `pytest tests/utilities/schema_tools/test_validation.py -q -k "Leak or AllowNone"` gave `3 failed, 2 passed` before the source change (the two passing cases are the control orderings). Run locally on Python 3.12.11 / Windows; I did not run the full CI matrix. ### Docs No documentation change: this fixes the meaning an existing schema option already advertises ("We allow None values to be passed in for optional fields if there is a default value for the field", `src/prefect/server/api/validation.py`), rather than adding new behaviour to describe. ### Checklist - [x] This pull request references any related issue by including "closes ``" - [ ] If this is a complex change, a maintainer has confirmed the proposed approach on the linked issue. author: openwong2kim
body:
Implements **T5** of the unattended fan-out design (plan-fanout-autonomy-v2): a fan-out owner can read its open task panes, and type at them under the approval-typing guard, with identity taken only from sources main verifies.

## What

- **Owner lane** (`assertCallerMayAccessPty` in `src/main/workspace/ptyOwnership.ts`). It runs the existing `assertWorkspaceOwnsPty` first. If that check fails, the caller can still reach the pane when the pane's workspace is an **open** ledger task (`working` / `input_required` / `review_requested`) that the caller owns. The caller is identified by:
  - a validated commander token (`ctx.commanderWorkspace`), or
  - the workspace main resolves the caller's walked pane (`callerPtyId`) to.

  `params.workspaceId` is never used as identity. Plugin-hosted callers and remote callers get no owner lane. If any lookup fails (ledger, ownership), the lane denies. The same rule as the existing assert applies to the mirror: a mirror hit can only short-circuit an allow, and a deny always comes from the renderer round-trip.
- **Handlers** (`src/main/pipe/handlers/input.rpc.ts`):
  - `input.readScreen` and `terminal.readEvents`: allowed on the owner lane. The result carries `untrusted: true` and a note that the worker's screen text is data, not instructions, whatever shape the renderer returns. readScreen names the **task** workspace to the renderer, because the renderer re-checks the pty against `workspaceId`.
  - `input.send` (text): allowed on the owner lane, but only plain text. A `raw: true` write, or any C0 control byte other than tab and newline (EOT, `\x03`, ESC sequences, `\r`, DEL), is refused. Otherwise text could type the keys the lane withholds from sendKey. The submit receipt reads agent status from the **task** workspace, because that is where the mirror keeps the pane. `screenTail` gets the same untrusted label. The gate-held "exit" check uses the verified caller workspace.
  - `input.sendKey`: the owner lane covers only `ctrl+c` and `escape`. Every other key on a delegated pane is refused. The gate-held check uses the verified caller workspace, as in send.
  - `surface.new` and `pane.split` are unchanged.
- **Approval-typing guard for every caller.** `assertNotTypingAtAnApproval` now applies to every RPC caller except the human operator's in-process surface (`ctx.operator`). Before, it applied only to commanders. A pane agent cannot use `approval_press` (it needs a commander token), so the refusal it gets says the human answers the prompt in the pane. The deadlock lift that a policy-refused `approval_press` grants is now scoped to the brain whose press was refused. Every other caller stays blocked on that pane.

## Identity limit, stated plainly

`callerPtyId` is a request field. Main checks which workspace owns that pane, not that the caller *is* that pane. Refusing the lane on the external wire is not an option: PipeServer marks every request `externalWire`, and every MCP server arrives that way, pane agents and the Deck brain alike. The pipe also carries no peer identity (#113). So any same-user process holding the pipe token can name an owner's pane and act as that owner. This is the ceiling the design's threat model accepts: the lane is a runaway brake, not a boundary against local code. The limit is stated in the code comments and in the changelog.

## Outside the plan's file list, and why

- **`src/main/pipe/handlers/deck.rpc.ts`**: `deck.resolvePaneRoute` is confined to the token's own workspace. A commander brain has no pane ancestry, so without a route for a task pane its MCP layer throws ("External MCP callers cannot target an explicit ptyId…") before main ever sees the call. A pane in an **open task this brain delegated** now resolves to the brain's **own** workspace, not the task's. That way `params.workspaceId` never carries a foreign workspace id. The own-workspace assert fails, and the owner lane grants access from the token and labels the result. The grant stays in one place.
- **`src/mcp/index.ts`**: `terminal_read` and `terminal_read_events` never sent any caller anchor. All four terminal tools now forward `callerPtyId` = `MY_PTY_ID`, the walked pane (a hit only, never the env hint). This follows the channel, ledger and fan-out tools, because this field grants access. `senderPtyId` is unchanged: it can fall back to the weak env hint and is still only used by the reject-only self-loop guard. So its "never grants" comments stay true. The tool schemas did not change, and neither did the `tools/list` bytes.
- **Tests updated**:
  - `approvalPressBlock.test.ts`: "only a commander is blocked" became "the operator is not blocked", and there is a new case for a blocked pane agent.
  - `input.rpc.test.ts`: the ownership parity invariant accepts the wrapper and checks that the wrapper calls `assertWorkspaceOwnsPty`.
  - `hostedWorkspaceBinding.drift.test.ts`: the scanner recognizes the wrapper's call shape. It still finds all four methods.

## Behavior change to note in dogfood

Because the guard now covers every non-operator caller, **`wmux send` from a shell (a human's or an agent's) is refused at a pane that holds a hook-reported approval record.** The renderer never calls `input.send` over RPC, so in practice the operator exemption covers no current caller. This follows the design text ("applied to every caller, not only commanders"). The refusal tells the caller that the human answers the prompt in the pane.

## Why

The fan-out owner needs to see what its workers are doing, and to nudge or stop them, without the human switching workspaces. The threat model in the design applies: this lane is a correctness boundary for honest orchestrators, not spoof-proofing against same-user code (#113).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` (root): clean.
- `npm run build:mcp && npm run probe:mcp`: pass.
- New tests:
  - `input.rpc.taskOwner.test.ts`: pane-agent and commander reads are allowed and labeled, with the renderer receiving the task workspace (the mock runs the renderer's own ownership check), including a non-object answer; control bytes, ESC, `\r`, DEL and `raw:true` are refused on the lane, while the caller's own pane is unchanged; the commander lane on send and sendKey (text ok; refused at an approval and pointed at `approval_press`; `ctrl+c` ok, `enter` refused; a closed task refused); a commander on a stranger's pane or a closed task is refused; a non-local origin gets no lane; the caller's own pane is not labeled; `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled` tasks are refused; another owner's task is refused; `params.workspaceId` alone is not identity; a plugin-hosted caller is refused; an unreadable ledger fails closed; readEvents is labeled; send is allowed; send at a pending approval is blocked for a non-commander; `ctrl+c` / `escape` are allowed and `enter` / `down` / `ctrl+d` are refused.
  - `approvalPressBlock.test.ts`: a pane agent is refused `enter` and `down` at an approval but allowed `escape`; after a brain's policy-refused press, only that brain may type.
  - `ptyOwnership.test.ts` (6 cases): lane unit tests, including a mirror miss that round-trips before denying.
  - `deck.rpc.test.ts` (3 cases): an open own task routes to the home workspace; a finished task and another brain's task still fail closed.
- The affected suites pass. In the full `vitest run`, the only remaining failures are two suites that need a local Playwright browser binary (`hoverSurfaces.chrome.runtime`, `opencode-sync-render.runtime`), which is not installed on this machine. The first full run also had timeouts at load average ~48. Those suites passed when re-run serially with a longer timeout.
- eslint on the changed files: no new findings. The warnings are on unchanged lines. The `import/no-unresolved` on `src/mcp/index.ts:2` is on the untouched SDK import (a worktree resolver quirk).
- **Live dogfood on an isolated instance.** I ran the branch app with `WMUX_DATA_SUFFIX=-t5dog` and three workspaces: owner A, task B (an ope

author: leonnariley18-ui
body:
Three code changes and a README rewrite. **Nothing stored is migrated or rewritten** — no SQL to run, nothing to do on your end. If any of this turns out to be wrong, reverting the code puts things back exactly, because the data was never touched.

## The numbering bug

`HISTORICAL_REUPS` holds five pre-app hauls from V1 that own numbers 1–5. An unnumbered haul was matched against that list with `h.date===r.date` — a year-less display string. Everything else in the app grew a real year during V2; this one spot didn't.

So a future haul landing on the same month and day as a V1 haul, sharing any strain name with it, takes its number. `Jun 2` + Gumbo is a real collision, and re-copping favourites is the whole point of the app.

It's narrower than it sounds. `assignReupNumbers` skips anything already numbered, so the match is a one-time assignment that already happened and is saved. It re-runs in exactly one place: **deleting an empty re-up**, which strips every number and recounts so the sequence has no gap. That strip is what re-exposes the match.

**Two fixes:**

- `stripRenumberable` holds numbers `1..HISTORICAL_REUPS.length` back from the recount, in both shells. V1 history is settled and never renumbers; gap-closing still applies to everything above it. This alone makes the match unreachable from the delete path.
- The match itself now compares full ISO dates. `backfillIso` already pins pre-`dateIso` records to `LEGACY_DATA_YEAR`, which is the year the V1 hauls are from, so both sides resolve to the same day and a 2027 haul can't collide with 2026 history.

## The dead line

`StrainDetailWindow` still opened with `if(!selectedStrain)return null;` before its `useState` calls. The parent guards the component at its only call site, so it could never fire — but it read as a live rules-of-hooks violation to anyone (or any linter) opening the file. Removed, with a comment explaining why there isn't one.

## The README

It described an app that no longer exists. Three of its five "known rough edges" were fixed during V2, and it stated that re-up numbering is "sequential by array position — **never by date**," which is precisely the bug above.

Rewritten against what the code actually does, and extended to cover what a month of work never got written down:

- the reverse gear — convert a stale ready-to-try, delete one, un-finish a cop, delete an experience, backdate notes/experiences/mixes
- when a haul closes, and why un-finishing deliberately leaves it closed
- the terpene minimum (ready-to-try only), the mix rating requirement, what never-again locks
- the three cloud-read guards and why the failed-read path was a data-loss hazard
- a new **Invariants worth not breaking** section, since most of these have been "fixed" by accident at least once
- the dates section: store both, sort on `dateIso`, never on `date`

## Deploy — worth knowing

Pages serves `/docs` from `claude/cannabis-tracking-app-rebuild`, not `main`. **Merging PR #2 deployed nothing.** The live site is only current because that exact commit was pushed to the deploy branch before the merge.

Same applies here. After merging this, run:

```bash
git push origin main:claude/cannabis-tracking-app-rebuild
```

(verified as a clean fast-forward). Or point Pages at `main` `/docs` in repo settings and stop thinking about it. Both options are now documented in the README.

## Verified

Headless Chromium against a stubbed Supabase route, asserting on the intercepted save payload.

| test | result |
|---|---|
| 2027 haul on `Jun 2` + Gumbo | gets a fresh number, not #3 |
| **same test against the old matcher** | **collides — proves the test is real** |
| genuine 2026 V1 haul on `Jun 2` + Gumbo | still resolves to #3 |
| delete an empty re-up | V1 #1–5 byte-identical, modern #6 untouched |
| delete #7 with a #8 after it | gap closes, #8 → #7, V1 still untouched |
| desktop detail window after the line removal | opens, all four tabs switch, 0 page errors |

It checks out the site repository, so a keyword added here fails that step until the site is updated.

author: shawndibble
body:
## Summary

A Skill Plan's Booster was one fixed accelerator, always starting "now". A pilot planning to run one accelerator today and another at a future event had no way to model the second — the plan always costed as if only the first (or whichever overwrote it) applied.

This adds `startsAt` to the engine's `Booster` and moves a plan's stored Booster from a single field to an ordered `boosters` list, one after another (EVE has one booster slot, so at most one is ever live at a time):

- **Engine**: `computeSchedule`, `boostedStepIndices`, and the optimizer's `bonusSegments` walk now treat a Booster's start as a rate breakpoint alongside its expiry.
- **Persistence**: `PlanBooster.startsAt` (null = already running); `SkillPlanRecord.boosters: PlanBooster[]`, with the legacy `booster` field kept as a mirror of `boosters[0]` for one release.
- **Sync**: `RemotePlanDoc.boosters` round-trips; pushing still writes the legacy `booster` field (or a disabled row for an explicit empty list) so a device on the older build doesn't drop the plan's accelerator on its next write.
- **UI**: the inline single-Booster control in `PlanEditor.tsx` is extracted into `BoosterList.tsx` — a list with "Add accelerator", each row holding a start and an expiry. Overlapping rows are rejected inline (EVE's single booster slot) rather than reaching the plan; a quick pick measures from the row's own start rather than always from now.

Closes #1407.

## Deviations from the ticket

- The ticket's implementation plan sketched `normalizePlanBoosters`/`toBoosters` as free functions taking `(raw, legacy)`; landed the same shape but split out `normalizePlanBoosterRow` (single-row normalization), `clampBoosterOverlaps` (pure, read-time sequencing), and `hasOverlappingBoosters` (write-time validation for the editor) as separate exported functions, since the editor's inline-reject behavior needed the validation check independent of the clamping one.
- Empty-state UX: with no Boosters configured, the editor now shows only an "Add accelerator" button rather than a permanently-visible unchecked checkbox — a natural consequence of moving to a list, and the shape the ticket's own UI sketch describes.
- `main` gained a new shared `planSchedule.ts` (the plan editor / Calendar shared schedule call) after this branch started; wired the new Boosters list through it as part of the sync-with-main step (see the last commit).

## Review notes

- `BoosterList`'s per-row draft/blur/overlap state has no stable row id (keyed by array index) since `PlanBooster` rows carry none — acceptable given rows are only ever appended/removed at the edges in the UI, but worth a second look if row reordering is ever added.
- No e2e coverage of the overlap-rejection UX specifically (only a unit/component test); `e2e/skillPlanEditorNarrow.spec.ts` covers adding a second accelerator's tap targets at phone width.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` across engine, persistence, sync, and UI layers (4056 tests, all passing locally)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [ ] CI: `validate`, `test` (4 shards), `e2e` (4 shards)

author: bluecannonball
body:
Ink weight is currently an absolute pressure-to-width curve, which cannot serve two profiles whose pens report pressure on different scales.

Two real stroke files show the failure:

| profile | p10 | median | p90 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lighter pen | 0.080 | 0.244 | 0.466 |
| heavier pen | 0.098 | 0.595 | 0.853 |

The lighter pen's *ordinary* pressure sits below the heavier pen's *lightest*. So the older curve drew the lighter profile's median stroke at **0.72 px** (spidery), while the current absolute curve flattens the heavier profile to a **0.45 px** spread across its entire pressure range (no visible variation). Neither setting is right; they are calibrated to one pen each.

## Change

Map each profile's own 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile pressure onto `0.60`, `1.00`, and `1.40` times the pen width. Every profile then gets the same contrast and the same weight at ordinary pressure:

| profile | p10 | median | p90 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lighter pen | 1.38 px | 2.30 px | 3.22 px |
| heavier pen | 1.38 px | 2.30 px | 3.22 px |

- Add an optional top-level `inkWidth` to the stroke file for the pen width at ordinary pressure, defaulting to the existing `INK_WIDTH` of 2.3. This is the explicit override, so weight is a setting rather than a code change.
- Anchor on the median as well as the two tails, so profiles with different skew still agree at ordinary pressure.
- Fall back to a uniform `inkWidth` when a profile has no pressure, or none to calibrate against.
- Document the calibration in `docs/stroke-file.md`.

## Behaviour change to be aware of

The procedural parenthesis envelope is pressure-like data feeding the same mapping, so its taper now follows the profile's pressure scale rather than being nearly flat. That is arguably consistent with the rest of the change, but it is a visible difference for profiles with a narrow pressure range and is easy to make uniform instead if you prefer.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test` (25 unit + 4 integration passed)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`
- Rendered both profiles with the same seed; ink density is now comparable (mean darkness 213.9 vs 207.0, previously very different).

author: erikdarlingdata
body:
Refs #3898.

## Why
`get_latch_stats` served 1,027 characters on Darling and 1,372 on Lite before a client asked its first question.
This lane moves the reading guidance off `tools/list`, into the per-tool guide `get_tool_guide` serves on demand.
The guidance covers which fields are floors, which zeros are measurements, and which windows are fixed. Nothing is deleted.

## What changes
- `Darling/PerformanceMonitor.Darling.Service/Mcp/DarlingMcpLatchSpinlockTools.cs`: `get_latch_stats`'s
  `Description(...)` now carries a terse head, the `<<GUIDE>>` marker, then the entire original description
  verbatim as the tail.
- `Lite/Mcp/McpLatchSpinlockTools.cs`: same split, with Lite's own original text as its tail. The head text is
  byte-identical to Darling's (enforced by `McpToolGuideTests.EverySharedToolName_CarriesTheMarkerOnBothSkus_OrNeither_WithByteIdenticalHeads`).
- New head pins: `Darling/Darling.Tests/McpToolGuideHeads.Latch.cs` (`McpToolGuideHeadsLatchTests`) and
  `Lite.Tests/McpToolGuideHeads.Latch.cs` (same class name, `Lite.Tests` namespace).
- Budget: updated only the `get_latch_stats` lines in `Darling/Darling.Tests/McpToolsListBudget/DarlingMcpLatchSpinlockTools.txt`
  and `Lite.Tests/McpToolsListBudget/McpLatchSpinlockTools.txt`. `get_spinlock_stats`'s lines in the same two files
  are lane e5's, untouched here.

Darling and Lite genuinely differ in how this tool reads (D6). Darling sums each class's waits over the whole
`hours_back` window and ranks the top classes by that window total. Lite returns only the single newest snapshot
found within `hours_back`, paged to `limit` classes, heaviest last-interval wait first. The shared head states
both facts in one clause instead of picking one product's framing.

Darling-only fields (`severity`, `severity_banded_from`) and Lite-only fields (`truncated`, `captured_at`,
`age_seconds`) stay off the shared head. They live only in each product's own tail, the way `list_servers`
already does this for its Darling-only fleet fields.

### Served characters
| Tool | Darling before | Darling after | Lite before | Lite after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| get_latch_stats | 1,027 | 549 | 1,372 | 549 |

### Status routes (both products never return `status: "empty"` for this tool)
| Status | Condition | Darling | Lite |
|---|---|---|---|
| not_collected | `rows.Count == 0` and the target's engine cannot produce `sys.dm_os_latch_stats` (a non-SQL-Server target) | DarlingMcpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:78 | McpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:73 |
| unavailable | `rows.Count == 0` and the engine can produce it, but nothing was collected in the requested window | DarlingMcpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:79 | McpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:74 |
| error | an exception was thrown | DarlingMcpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:129 | McpLatchSpinlockTools.cs:116 |

## Corrections
One sentence was wrong on all three products, and the lane had copied it into the head as "means TempDB allocation contention".

- Darling and the Dashboard said: "High LATCH_EX on ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT or FGCB_ADD_REMOVE indicates TempDB allocation contention."
- Lite said: "High LATCH_EX on ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT or a page-latch class indicates allocation/page contention (often TempDB)."

Microsoft's [sys.dm_os_latch_stats](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/system-dynamic-management-views/sys-dm-os-latch-stats-transact-sql) page says ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT is "Used to synchronize child dataset access to the parent dataset during parallel operations." It says FGCB_ADD_REMOVE is used "to synchronize access to filegroups for add, drop, grow, and shrink file operations." It also says BUFFER "covers all possible uses of page latches", so this DMV has no separate page-latch class. The product's own latch-class text in `install/47_create_reporting_views.sql` says the same. `LATCH_EX` is a wait type, not a latch class, and this DMV reports no latch mode.

The head no longer makes the claim. The tails now say:
- Darling and the Dashboard: "ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT synchronizes child dataset access to the parent dataset during parallel operations, and FGCB_ADD_REMOVE synchronizes filegroup add, drop, grow and shrink file operations."
- Lite: "ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT synchronizes child dataset access to the parent dataset during parallel operations, and every page latch reports under the one BUFFER class, where contention can mean hot pages or slow I/O."

The Dashboard's `LATCH_EX` next-tool hint also dropped its "(ACCESS_METHODS_DATASET_PARENT / FGCB_ADD_REMOVE point at TempDB allocation contention)" note. The dropped-sentence check now reports `missing=1` on each product: the corrected sentence, and nothing else.

## D4 removals
None. This tool's description carried no issue references and no anecdotes.

## Re-pointed pins
None. `git grep` for `get_latch_stats` across `Darling/Darling.Tests` and `Lite.Tests` found no test asserting a
literal substring of the old head text. Every hit reads the tool body or SQL, which this PR did not touch. The rest
read the whole `Description` attribute for a substring that still exists in the preserved tail
(`McpLatestSnapshotStampTests`, `Lite.Tests/McpLatestSnapshotStampTests`).

The lane's own head-pin files changed in the coordinator pass. They follow the new head. A new test, `LatchClasses_KeepMicrosoftsMeaning_NotATempDbReading`, checks that the TempDB reading is gone from the head and the tail on both products.

## D9 traps
- **Q:** get_latch_stats on Darling ranks classes by their most recent interval's wait time.
  **Correct:** No. Darling ranks by the SUM of waits across the whole hours_back window, not the latest interval.
  **Prevents it:** "Darling sums waits over the whole hours_back window and returns the top classes by that total"
- **Q:** get_latch_stats on Lite aggregates every collection inside hours_back into one number per class, the way Darling does.
  **Correct:** No. Lite returns only the single newest snapshot found within hours_back. The window only bounds the search for that snapshot.
  **Prevents it:** "Lite: LATEST IS A TIME, only the newest snapshot within hours_back, paged to limit, heaviest last-interval wait first"
- **Q:** On Lite, the returned classes are sorted by their cumulative lifetime wait_time_ms.
  **Correct:** No. The page is ordered heaviest last-interval wait first, not by the cumulative total.
  **Prevents it:** "Lite: LATEST IS A TIME, only the newest snapshot within hours_back, paged to limit, heaviest last-interval wait first"
- **Q:** On Lite, the newest latch snapshot inside `hours_back` is 20 hours old. Does the tool skip it as stale and return nothing?
  **Correct:** No. Lite returns the newest snapshot found within `hours_back`, however old it is inside that window. LATEST IS A TIME: the snapshot is the moment it was captured, and the payload's `captured_at` says when.
  **Prevents it:** "Lite: LATEST IS A TIME, only the newest snapshot within hours_back"
- **Q:** severity is derived the same way as the window total, from every collection in hours_back.
  **Correct:** No. severity (Darling only) comes from the LATEST interval, the same single interval the per-second rates come from, never the window sum.
  **Prevents it:** "interval_seconds, both per-second rates and (on Darling) severity come from the LATEST interval only"
- **Q:** Lite's twin exposes a severity field too, since the head mentions it.
  **Correct:** No. The head marks severity "(on Darling)" specifically. Lite's payload has no severity or severity_banded_from field at all.
  **Prevents it:** "(on Darling) severity come from the LATEST interval only"
- **Q:** A row with waits_per_second: 0.00 on a restart means the class was momentarily quiet.
  **Correct:** No. When the interval is unknowable (a restart or first sample, stored as 0), the rates are null, never a real 0.
  **Prevents it:** "on a restart or first sample (interval unknowable, stored 0) they are null, never 0 or LOW"
- *

author: johnnyt
body:
Fixes se-29d.

## What was wrong

A durable subchart child runs on its parent's driver, so the child's effects reach the parent's feed buffer. An `Invoke dispatched` row names the block whose `<invoke>` fired by resolving the invoke's `state_index`, and `Execution.absorb/2` resolved it against the reading's own chart. That index is the child's. On `signup_onboarding` the wizard's two calls were shown as `myapp:signup on blk_so_wizard` and `myapp:signup on Tell the owner the child chart refused`. The parent's invoke mark also moved onto that `on_error` slot while the parent was still waiting on its subchart.

## The fix

- `Durable`'s executor tells the parent's effects apart from a child's by comparing the executor context's execution id with the drive's own id (`buffered_effect/3`). When the ids differ, the effect is buffered as `:effect_of`, carrying the other execution's id and content hash.
- The fold resolves that chart by content hash, looking at both compiles of every shipped document (`other_reading/1`). It only does this for an invoke, and it resolves each chart once per drive.
- `Execution.absorb/2`'s `:effect_of` clause names the block from that execution's own reading and sets the row's `source` to that execution's id. It leaves the reading's own invoke mark alone. Every other `:effect_of` effect folds as the reading's own, the same as before (`Execution.absorb/2`, the catch-all `:effect_of` clause).

## Test

`ChildExecutionRowsTest`, "a durable child's calls in the parent's reading", starts the existing `signup_onboarding` fixture. It asserts that the child's call rows read `myapp:signup on Collect email and password` and `myapp:signup on Send the verification email`, each carrying the child's execution id as its source, and that the parent's invoke mark stays on `blk_so_wizard`. The PR adds no fixture and no example.

Sabotage: I restored `durable.ex` and `execution.ex` to their `main` contents and the new test went red (the old labels, with no source). I then made only the `:effect_of` clause read the index against the parent's reading, and the test went red on the same two labels. Both files were restored from a copy and the test is green again.

## Provenance

- A comment in `durable_test.exs` described the child's calls as named against the parent's states. It now says that was how the feed behaved when the comment was written. The PR touches no assertion in that file.
- The bead names `Execution.absorb/2`. The executor, the fold and the resolver in `Durable` are the threading edits the fix forces. None of them adds a public function.

## Review (own, in turn)

I re-read the diff against the bead and its acceptance, and checked the new comments against the code:
- A child is created without tracing: `create_child/6` in statifier_persistence's driver creates the child with a `datamodel:` in `initialize:` and no `trace:`, and the driver adds only its registered types to it. A drive of `signup_onboarding` shows no child `Entered` rows.
- A finishing child's answer steps the parent on the same executor (`resolve_and_answer/4` there).
- The resolver takes the content hash that `resolve_chart/1` and `child_chart/1` also match on.

The first cut compiled a machine for every fixture on every drive and slowed the durable tests a lot. The resolver now compares source hashes first and compiles only the match.

Gate: full `mix quality` green on the committed tree (529 tests, 83.6% coverage; dialyzer clean).

Tier: gate. The change sits in a private fold of a non-published app, is well under the size threshold, and touches no public function signature, wire shape or corpus.

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Weekly reconciliation currently retranslates matching source pages across every locale, and forced retries overwrite pages that already finished.

## User Impact

Routine reconciliation translates only missing or changed pages at high reasoning effort. Operators can still request a full recovery with `force_retranslate=true`; use that explicit recovery when glossary or prompt changes must refresh otherwise unchanged translations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pending manifest now owns both routine and forced selection. Each receipt records that selection, and resumes inherit it: legacy full-run receipts retain their forced contract, while incompatible mixed receipts are rejected. Routine canaries sample pending pages and skip when none remain. Forced overwrite applies only to the first attempt, so strict passes and later retries preserve completed work.

## Evidence

- 51 focused Python control-plane tests passed, including changed/missing/forced selection, pending-empty canaries, receipt compatibility, frozen-source resume, and the real workflow worker loop with partial failure followed by retry. Each page was generated once and unrelated translations were preserved.
- All 51 extracted workflow Bash blocks passed syntax checks; the translation concurrency budget remains nine workers.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 passed for the three changed workflows with external analyzers disabled. The default invocation did not finish within five minutes; independent Bash syntax checks passed.
- One independent GPT-6 Sol/high autoreview passed with no actionable findings on `f98732c53b`; final head changes only two stale comments after that review.
- Direct Codex source inspection confirms [high effort parsing](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs#L118-L128); the pinned [docs translator forwards the requested reasoning effort](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f6eb26b1beda60044ee9b94cd352f37c63718e9/scripts/docs-i18n/translator.go#L261).
- Net production delta: Python +14 lines, workflow wiring +20; tests +104. The added state records the recovery selection needed for compatible resume.
- No production translation run was dispatched. Full dependency-backed CI remains for the PR.

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

  修复 Android 环境下使用 JSON.parseObject、JSON.toJSONString 等方法时抛出的 NullPointerException。

  在 Android 平台上，MethodHandles.Lookup.in() 方法可能返回 null，导致 Lambda 创建失败并抛出异常。此 PR 使 PropertyAccessorFactoryLambda 在 Lambda
  创建失败时能够回退到父类的反射实现，而不是直接抛出异常导致程序崩溃。

  Fixes #4011

### Summary of your change

修改 PropertyAccessorFactoryLambda.create() 方法，在 Lambda 创建逻辑外层添加 try-catch 块。当 Lambda 创建失败（抛出 Throwable）时，捕获异常并忽略，然后继续执行到最后的
  return super.create(...) 语句，回退到父类的反射实现。

- [x] Made sure tests are passing and test coverage is added if needed.

body:
## Scale the player-card photo up 50% to fill the frame

The consented photo on a player card used `object-fit:contain` across the full card box, so a tall cutout (e.g. Liam's) sat small with a lot of empty background around it.

### Change
`.cf2-photo` gets `transform:scale(1.5)` with `transform-origin:bottom center`. The cutout enlarges 50% and stays anchored at the base of the card, so the player fills the frame as a hero image. The number / name / position overlays are unaffected (higher z-index, separate elements).

Applies to **every** player's card through the shared `buildFront` render - not special-cased to one player - so all photos get the same fuller framing, and photo-less cards are unchanged (no image to scale).

### Verify
Rendered Liam's real cutout at scale 1 vs 1.5 (headless screenshot): the 1.5x version fills the card cleanly, feet anchored at the bottom, hair just meeting the top edge. Scripts compile clean, banned punctuation clean, sections balanced 12/12, no backend change.

Frontend-only (`index.html`, one CSS rule).

author: drunkonjava
body:
## Summary

Walls, curtain walls, floors, building pads, ceilings, roofs and railings are now named as Revit's own IFC export names them (RE-63):
- `Name` is `Family:Type:ElementId`, for example "Basic Wall:8" Interior Partition 3 Hour:20796" instead of "Wall-20796";
- `ObjectType` is `Family:Type`.

Family instances already were (RE-38). A system family's type name is in the file (#322), but the family's is not: Revit derives it. RE-61's rule gives it:
- a curtain wall is a Curtain Wall, and a railing a Railing;
- a floor is a Floor, and a building pad a Pad;
- a wall, ceiling or roof whose type has compound layers is a Basic Wall, Compound Ceiling or Basic Roof. The type is checked, not the element: another element of the type drawn in layers counts, and so does the type's own data.

The name is recorded with `FamilyNameSource` `system_family_by_category`.

Measured against Revit's own exports (`tools/re/names_vs_ifc.py`), over every system-family element matched by `Tag`:

| file | walls | curtain walls | floors | ceilings | roofs | railings |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Snowdon Towers (local only) | 1,077 of 1,077 | 42 of 42 | 167 of 182 | 68 of 68 | 20 of 20 | 101 of 131 |
| 2024_Core_Interior | 360 of 360 | — | 100 of 100 | — | — | — |
| RE1 Architecture | 7 of 7 | 1 of 1 | 2 of 2 | 6 of 6 | — | 0 of 1 |

- On Core Interior, all 854 matched elements now carry Revit's own name.
- The 15 Snowdon floors are ones Revit exports in two parts (a second with a `:2` suffix), and their `ObjectType` is equal.
- The railings not named have no type name read.
- Family-instance names are unchanged.

## Changes

- src/partition_schema_mvp.rs:
  - `system_family` (replacing RE-61's `layered_system_family`);
  - `attach_system_family_names`;
  - `FAMILY_NAME_SOURCE_FIELD` and `SYSTEM_FAMILY_SOURCE`.
- src/ifc/export_content.rs: the `FamilyNameSource` property.
- tests/element_names.rs, the existing corpus name tests:
  - Core Interior's pinned count moves from 394 to 854, and RE1 Architecture's from 57 to 73;
  - the system-type check now also compares each derived `Family:Type` with Revit's `ObjectType`.
- tools/re/names_vs_ifc.py, reports/element-framing/RE-63-system-family-element-names.md, README, status, the support-matrix row, CHANGELOG.
- research/witness/magnetar-2024-core-interior{,-slim}/observations/rvt-rs.json regenerated for the new property values. Both verdicts PASS.

## Testing

- `rvt-ifc` on Snowdon, Core Interior and RE1, then `tools/re/names_vs_ifc.py` (the table above).
- The CI witness steps, replayed locally: both verdicts PASS with `--compare-committed`, `--witness-agreement` holds, and `ifcopenshell.validate` reports nothing.
- Local gates:
  - fmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings;
  - the workspace suite;
  - the corpus tests under `--profile ci` (48 binaries);
  - `cargo +1.85.0 check` and the fuzz workspace check.

## Audit-honesty checklist

- [x] Every count is measured against Revit's own export. The derived family is labelled with its source.
- [x] RE finding: report and scorer.
- [x] No emojis, private paths or personal data.

## Legal and contribution hygiene

- [x] Apache-2.0
- [x] Clean-room: Revit's own exports as oracles.
- [x] Snowdon stays local.

## Related issues

Refs #322.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes IFC identity fields and naming logic for a large class of building elements; behavior is test-backed against Revit exports but affects downstream consumers that relied on Class-ElementId names.
> 
> **Overview**
> **RE-63** extends Revit-style naming from family instances to **system-family** elements: walls, curtain walls, floors, building pads, ceilings, roofs, and railings now export with **`Name` = `Family:Type:ElementId`** and **`ObjectType` = `Family:Type`**, matching Revit’s IFC export instead of `Class-ElementId`.
> 
> The system family label is **derived** (RE-61 rules, expanded in `system_family(class, has_layers)`): curtain walls → Curtain Wall, railings → Railing, floors/pads → Floor/Pad, and walls/ceilings/roofs → Basic Wall / Compound Ceiling / Basic Roof when the **type** has compound layers (from layer fields on instances or `scan_type_layers` on types). `attach_system_family_names` writes `m_family_name` plus **`FamilyNameSource` = `system_family_by_category`** so derived names are not confused with file-read names. IFC export surfaces that source on the element property set.
> 
> Corpus name tests widen to include these elements (e.g. Core Interior **394 → 854** matched names; RE1 Architecture **57 → 73**). Docs, support matrix, CHANGELOG, witness observation hashes, and **`tools/re/names_vs_ifc.py`** document and measure parity with Revit exports.

author: zerone-agent
body:
## Problem

`validateSkillDir` rejects `SKILL.md` files with CRLF line endings — the frontmatter delimiter regex is LF-only (`/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/`).

But both the Hub and the runtime accept CRLF:

- **Hub validator** (`skill_validator.go`): "Normalise CRLF so the `---` delimiter check is line-ending-agnostic" — `strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")` before matching.
- **SDK** (`agent-sdk/src/skills/yaml.ts`, `parseSkillMarkdown`): `content.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")` before matching.

Effect: bundle uploads containing any CRLF `SKILL.md` are falsely rejected by the CLI even though the Hub accepts the zip and the runtime registers the skills.

Reproduced with `lijigang/ljg-skills`: `ljg-plain` and `ljg-word` have CRLF line endings upstream (since 2026-03), so the whole 22-skill bundle currently fails validation with:

```
ljg-plain/SKILL.md: frontmatter 缺失或未闭合（必须以 --- 开头并以 --- 结束）
ljg-word/SKILL.md: frontmatter 缺失或未闭合（必须以 --- 开头并以 --- 结束）
```

## Fix

Normalise CRLF → LF before the delimiter match in `validateSkillDir`, mirroring Hub/SDK behaviour exactly. Packing still uses raw bytes (unchanged); only validation becomes line-ending-agnostic.

## Verification

- New test `CRLF line endings in frontmatter are accepted (SDK/Hub normalize)` — fails before the fix, passes after
- Full CLI suite: `bun test` → 176 pass / 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → clean

body:
### Description

This PR hardens convolution-nchw and unpooling-nhwc operators against
integer overflow vulnerabilities during operator reshape operations:

1. **Convolution NCHW (`src/operators/convolution-nchw.c`)**:
   - Guard `input_batch_stride` and `output_batch_stride` with `xnn_safe_mul`
     and return `xnn_status_out_of_memory` on overflow.
   - Guard `zero_size` with `xnn_safe_mul` and `xnn_safe_add` to prevent
     under-allocation of the zero padding buffer. Fix display size in
     error message.
   - Guard `output_height_stride` and `output_channel_stride` with
     `xnn_safe_mul` returning `xnn_status_out_of_memory`.
   - Guard `input_size` and `scaled_input_size` in SPMM path.

2. **Unpooling NHWC (`src/operators/unpooling-nhwc.c`)**:
   - Guard `range[0] = batch_size * input_height` with `xnn_safe_mul` in both
     valid batch size cache path and full reshape path.
   - Guard stride calculations (`input_pixel_stride_in_bytes`,
     `input_height_stride`, `index_width_stride`, `index_height_stride`,
     `indirect_output_width_stride`, and `indirect_output_height_stride`)
     with `xnn_safe_mul` returning `xnn_status_out_of_memory`.

3. **Tests**:
   - Added `reshape_overflow_batch_size` and `reshape_overflow_stride` tests
     to `test/operators/unpooling-nhwc.cc`.
   - Added `reshape_overflow_batch_stride` test to
     `test/operators/convolution-nchw.cc`.

body: ## Why Online connections need to recover when proxies drop or silently stall streams, without losing moves. - Reconnecting sends the full public action log rather than maintaining an SSE replay buffer. Moves retain their existing version-checked POST endpoint. - Successful writes notify in-process subscribers; idle streams do not poll storage. Future replicas sharing storage will also need cross-instance notifications, but no broker is added for the current monolith. - Local two-player testing uses two ports on one backend instead of making the production stream depend on the test topology. - Deployment requires unbuffered proxy responses and an idle timeout above the 15-second heartbeat interval. Production proxies have not been tested. ## Validation - Formatting, typechecks, lint, build, 153 client unit tests, and Go race tests passed. - Nine browser smoke tests passed, including socket drops, HTTP 503 recovery, missed moves, and rollback after a failed resync at the same version. - Server tests cover subscription/write races, coalescing, cleanup, rejected writes, and zero storage reads while idle. - The reconnect scenario was rerun at 320 x 568 to capture the screenshots below. ## Review media The screenshots show the waiting room and the battle after simulated connection failures. body:
## 这是什么

ADR-112 第四节施工顺序的第 2 步：IG 话题页（`fetch_hashtag_posts`）的解析器、来源类型，以及与主页作品样本共用的视频判定。**只解析，不接入**：不发请求、不分派，采集入口不调用它，行为不变。话题路线要等第 3 步接上入口，并且只有运营在任务配置里显式写 `ig_route: "hashtag"` 才会走。第 1 步（#167，价目）已合入。

需求登记表不动：D15、D11、D6 的改动按 ADR-112 第四节，随第 3 步入口一起写。

## 解析的依据

字段全部来自 ADR-112 第五节，即你在本地只读核对过的话题样本：
- 列表在 `data.data.items`；
- 作者是 `user.username`；
- 文案字段是 `caption_text`，Reels 与 general 用的是 `caption.text`；
- 图文、轮播和视频混在同一页。

没有发任何请求，也没有付费采样。

## 改了什么

- **`isInstagramVideo`**：把主页作品样本里原先那一串视频条件原样搬出来，主页样本改为调用它，行为不变（ADR-112 第二节：两处共用一个判定）。
  - 五个信号任一成立就算视频：`is_video` 为 true、`media_type` 为 2、`media_format` 为 video、`media_name` 为 reel、`product_type` 为 clips。
  - 话题页里的图文（media_type 1）和轮播（media_type 8）不算。
  - 这段判定原先没有任何变异守着，这次补上了。
- **`parseInstagramHashtagPage`**：
  - 文案取 `caption_text`，不认 `caption.text`。
  - **播放数只给视频条目**。图文、轮播即使带着 `play_count` 也不写：那类媒体的播放字段语义没有确认过，写进去就是把「不知道」当成真实的数（P1）。
  - 来源端点记为话题页，搜索词原样保留，开头有 `#` 也不去掉。
  - **不交回续页令牌**：话题页翻不翻另议（ADR-112 第二节）。如果交回，入口会拿它去翻 Reels。
  - 条目数按供应商返回的条目算，不按人数算。
- **来源类型**加一项话题页端点，显示名为「Instagram 话题搜索」。

## 按「接口 → 测试（先红）→ 实现 → 变异」提交

- 92e2150 接口：两个函数的函数体先抛「尚未实现」，契约写在说明里。
- 58e778b 测试：49 条断言，由没读过实现的上下文写成。
  - 期望只取自 ADR-112 第二、五节与 D11、P1、D15 原文。
  - 对着接口 48 条红；绿的那 1 条是显示名，它随接口一起落了地。
  - 一处如实交代：写测试的上下文按行号读 `pickList` 的说明时，函数体末尾十来行进入了视野，它没有据此另加判据（写在该提交说明里）。
- 0361a3e 实现：48 条红转绿。
- 02f5e00 变异，共 9 条，逐条打进代码跑 `test.ts`，红的都是配给它的那几条：
  - M-D15-k 来源冒充 Reels；
  - M-D15-l 搜索词被去掉 `#`；
  - M-D11-o 文案按 Reels 的字段取；
  - M-D11-p 作品 id 取了文案的标识；
  - M-P1-aa 图文、轮播也写播放数；
  - M-D8-d 视频判定漏认一个信号；
  - M-D8-e 把轮播也算成视频；
  - M-D6-bb 交回续页令牌；
  - M-D6-bc 条目数按人数算。
  - 另外：话题解析照 Reels 解析写了同一行取作品 id 的代码，现有 M-D11-b 的锚点于是出现两处（#163 会整跑拒绝）。把它的锚点连同下一行一起写，只落在 Reels 那一处。

## 验证

- 本地 `npm run check` 全链在 02f5e00 上通过（对比的是合入 #168 之后的主干 6d6770a）：
  - 体量：源码新增 77 / 350 行，测试 206 / 450；
  - 需求、决策记录一致，类型检查通过；
  - 测试全绿，546 个变异全部被抓到；
  - 脚本自检与审计通过。
- 没有发任何真实请求，也没有新增付费采样。

## PR 评审记录

- CodeRabbit：视频条目缺播放字段、赞数为 null 时，作品对象上留着值为 `undefined` 的键 → 档：驳回。这个仓库里「缺席」指读出来是 `undefined`，Reels 路线同一写法；落盘经 JSON 序列化后键就不在了，读侧没有一处按键在不在区分。理由写在线程里，线程已解决。
