author: adamglin0
body:
`SkikoParagraphBuilder` never adds the characters covered by a placeholder to the Skia paragraph; Skia represents each placeholder as a single U+FFFC. When an inline content item uses an alternate text longer than one character (e.g. `appendInlineContent(id, "[icon]")`), every Skia offset after it is shifted by `length - 1` relative to the Compose text. `SkikoParagraph` passed Compose offsets to Skia unconverted, so hit testing, cursor rects, selection paths, line start/end and word boundaries after an inline item were wrong on all Skiko platforms, and a link placed after an inline item could not be clicked.

This change introduces `PlaceholderOffsetMapping`, built once per paragraph from the placeholder ranges (`null` when every placeholder is one code unit, so the common case only pays a null check), and routes every offset that crosses the Compose/Skia boundary in `SkikoParagraph` through it:

- Compose → Skia at the API boundary: `getPathForRange`, `getCursorRect`, `getLineForOffset`, `getHorizontalPosition`, `getBidiRunDirection`, `getBoundingBox`, `getWordBoundary`.
- Skia → Compose on outputs: `getOffsetForPosition`, `getLineStart`, `getLineEnd`, `getWordBoundary`.
- Internal Skia-space loops (`getBoxForwardByOffset` / `getBoxBackwardByOffset`, trailing-whitespace handling) are bounded by the Skia text length and read characters through the mapping.

Semantics: a Compose offset inside a placeholder range maps to the placeholder itself (caret before it, like Android's `ReplacementSpan`); a hit inside the placeholder resolves to its start or end depending on which half was hit, matching Android. The builder's single-U+FFFC contract and the public API are unchanged.

Fixes https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/CMP-9009

## Testing
- `DesktopParagraphPlaceholderOffsetTest` (ui-text `desktopTest`, 12 tests): `getOffsetForPosition`, `getCursorRect`, `getBoundingBox`, `getHorizontalPosition`, `getPathForRange`, `getWordBoundary`, line APIs, accumulated deltas with two placeholders, the single-character identity path, mixed single- and multi-character placeholders, a multi-line paragraph and an RTL paragraph. All positions are derived from the fixed-advance test font and `placeholderRects`, not from the APIs under test.
- `BasicTextInlineContentOffsetTest` (foundation `skikoTest`, 2 tests): the reported scenario, clicking a link placed after an inline item with a multi-character alternate text.
- With the mapping stubbed out, 11 of the original 13 new tests fail; only the identity-path test passes.
- `:compose:ui:ui-text:desktopTest` and `:compose:foundation:foundation:desktopTest --tests "androidx.compose.foundation.text.*"` pass.

## Release Notes
### Fixes - Multiple Platforms
- Fixed wrong hit testing, cursor and selection positions after inline content whose alternate text is longer than one character (e.g. links after an inline element could not be clicked). _(CMP-9009)_

## Summary

Custom domains can now be configured per stage (#133, #134), but each domain's DNS record needs a target, and the stack didn't output it for lesson media or the APIs.

- **`MediaBucket`** now outputs its distribution's generated `*.cloudfront.net` hostname as `DistributionDomainName`, the same output `StaticWebsite` already gives the three portals. It's always the generated hostname, even when a custom domain is configured, because that's what the custom domain's CNAME points at.
- **`RestApi`** (used by `CoreApi` and `InstructorApi`) now outputs `<apiName>DomainNameAlias`, the custom domain's `d-*.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com` hostname, and `<apiName>DomainNameAliasHostedZoneId`, the hosted zone ID a Route 53 alias record needs, whenever a custom domain is configured. The `…Endpoint` output that CDK's `RestApi` adds by default is the API's own URL (with a `/prod/` stage path), which isn't a valid DNS target for the custom domain.

After deploying, the core stack's outputs list the DNS target for every custom domain:

| Output | DNS target for |
|---|---|
| `CoreApiCoreApiDomainNameAlias…` (+ `…HostedZoneId`) | core API custom domain |
| `InstructorApiInstructorApiDomainNameAlias…` (+ `…HostedZoneId`) | instructor API custom domain |
| `LessonMediaBucketDistributionDomainName…` | lesson media custom domain(s) |
| `Student/Instructor/AdminPortalDistributionDomainName…` | portal custom domain(s) (existing) |

## Test plan

- [x] `media-bucket.test.ts`: the output holds the generated CloudFront domain even with a custom domain and certificate configured.
- [x] `rest-api.test.ts`: with a custom domain, the outputs hold the `AWS::ApiGateway::DomainName`'s `RegionalDomainName` and `RegionalHostedZoneId`; without one, there are no alias outputs.
- [x] All 18 `@wattle/common-constructs` tests pass. `pnpm nx affected --target lint` passes.
- [x] Synthesized `wattle-development` with its real domain variables from its GitHub environment: all outputs in the table above appear in the CoreStack template. Their absence without a custom domain is covered by the unit test above.
- [ ] After the deploy, the API outputs match the API Gateway custom domains' `regionalDomainName` (currently `d-stzuapu9h0…` for core-api and `d-cksi6gcrx7…` for instructor-api in `wattle-development`).

author: sfroment
body:
## What

- Probe `ListServicePools` in the pool acceptance tests' `PreCheck` and skip with a clear reason when the target Koyeb API cannot serve service pools
- Applies to `TestAccKoyebServicePool_Basic`, `TestAccKoyebServicePoolClaim_Basic`, `TestAccDataSourceKoyebServicePool_Basic`

## Why

Since #83 merged, main CI fails on the three pool acceptance tests with `Provider produced inconsistent result after apply — Root resource was present, but now absent`.

Root cause is the target environment, not the provider:

- On `app.koyeb.com` the pool endpoints are not served yet: `GET /v1/service_pools` returns `404 url_not_found`, while `POST` with a valid body returns 200 with an empty `service_pool` — so create sets an empty ID, the read 404s, and Terraform reports the resource as vanished. Nothing is actually created (no orphans).
- The feature also ships behind the `serverless_container_sandbox_pool` org/workspace flag (default off, failing closed), so a fully-deployed API still refuses orgs without the flag.

The probe covers every state: 404 (routes not deployed), 401/403 (flag off), 200 (feature live) — and self-heals the moment the CI org gets the feature, no workflow or env-var changes needed.

## Verification

- Against an API without pools: all three tests **skip** via the new gate (`service pools are not available on the target Koyeb API: ...`)
- Against an API that serves pools: `TestAccDataSourceKoyebServicePool_Basic` **passes end-to-end** (create → read → datasource lookup → destroy, ~5s) — provider create/read/delete round-trip is correct
- Pool test configs keep `micro`/`tyo`, matching the service acceptance tests that already pass on the CI org

## Note

The full pool suite will only execute in CI once `app.koyeb.com` serves the endpoints and the CI org has the `serverless_container_sandbox_pool` flag enabled — until then these tests skip, and main stays green.

body:
## 这一批是什么

首发前的「小而硬」六项（调研报告 `research_report_UI与设置升级_2026-09-23.md` 的发布前最小集），
外加批末零上下文独立审查的处置。计划文档：`.codebuddy/plans/首发前收口批_小而硬六项_2026-09-23.md`。

**不做大范围 UI 重构**：命令面板、表格交互、回顾报告、Offer 对比、数据目录迁移、demo 数据一律
排发布后（已进候选池）。

## 六项

1. **危险操作分级确认**（笔 1）：统一的确认原语（`confirm` / `phrase` / `name` 三档）+ 5 秒撤销条；
   两者绝不叠加（一个总被点过去的弹窗会削弱所有弹窗）。
2. **快照一键还原与演练**（笔 2）：演练**只读**，列出会覆盖几个 / 补齐几个 / 哪些文件保留不动；
   确认后才动手，且**还原前自动落回滚点**。语义：还原**只覆盖 + 补齐，从不删除**。
3. **窗口位置尺寸记忆**（笔 3）：下次开窗回到原位；显示器拔掉后回落主屏居中，不会跑到屏幕外。
4. **诊断包导出**（笔 3）：版本 / 平台 / 自检摘要 / 主进程日志尾部一个 zip；不含工作区数据文件与
   访问凭证，家目录脱敏，日志只留尾部。
5. **设置页找得到 / 退得回 / 知道何时生效**（笔 4）：关键词搜索（中英都能命中）、分组、`@modified`
   只看改过的；每项列出当前值、生效方式与单项还原。
6. **到点提醒最小形态**（笔 5）：今天的面试 / 下次动作 / 已过截止 → 一条系统通知（一天一次，可关）；
   **关窗即停，不驻留后台、不建托盘**。

笔 6（中文排版两条下限）核对结论是**两条都合规**，因此不为了改而改，只固化断言。

## 批末独立审查的处置（verdict = With fixes）

- **CRITICAL**：快照条目路径原先"先判定后归一化"，`config/./imap.json` 这类写法能绕过凭证排除，
  落盘时由 OS 归一化后正是 `config/imap.json`——**明文邮箱授权码会被还原回工作区**。已修 +
  演练的「保留不动」集合同源同修（那个数字是用户按下"还原"前唯一的凭据）。
- **MAJOR**：还原改取**全仓六把**工作区锁（原先只有 tracking + jobs，而快照含简历 / 笔记 /
  偏好文件）；中途失败要报出**回滚点名**（新错误码 `sys.snapshotRestoreFailed`）；诊断包脱敏改为
  不区分大小写 + 两种分隔符并补隔离文件名清单；`filterEntries` 从死代码接上界面；窗口以主屏为
  基准并让"关窗即停"在 macOS 上也字面成立；偏好观察器不再盯 `style`（避免每次写属性都换来一轮
  IPC + 全页重渲染）。
- 顺带把 `main.py` 的路由注册段外提到 `routers/registry.py`：它没有水位豁免（300 行），而本批
  三笔各自都要加一行，余量被吃光；外提后 283 行。`pyinstaller.spec` 的 hiddenimports 同步补模块。

## 明确不做（取舍写在这里）

- 不做大范围 UI 重构与命令面板 / 表格键盘导航（发布后）。
- 诊断包仍走 `GET`，而自检在遇到无法解析的表文件时会把它们移入工作区 `quarantine/`——这是与
  界面上「自检」完全相同的行为，已在包内 README 与设置页描述里写明（存量形态，未改）。
- MCP 协议级强制介入点、`paths.py` normcase、`prefs.py` 无锁写、`copy_tree` 只增不删、列表虚拟化
  维持原样（各自的理由在既有记录里）。

- `pytest tests/ -q` = **1256 passed / 10 skipped**
- 七个扫描器 + `skills check` 全绿（size / i18n / legacy-imports / four-ends / ui-tokens / domains / themes）
- 桌面壳自检：`zoom` / `window_state` / `reminders` / `check_packaging` / `url_guard` 全过

- **Playwright 全量 105 passed**（含新增的 `snapshot` / `diagnostics` / `settings` 三个 spec）

## 未做（等放行）

发布动作本身仍等你点头：`docs/release-checklist.md` 成文、版本号落章与 bump、`release.yml` 的
dry_run 演练、打 tag、真机安装冒烟、14 天稳定窗口计时与人眼验收四项。

author: falkobuttler
body:
## Problem

When AirPlaying an HTML5 video, two related issues caused the **video to stay on-device while only the audio streamed**:

1. On some sites/players, invoking AirPlay via the toolbar transferred only the audio.
2. With an AirPlay route already active, navigating to a new page would auto-connect the new video's audio, but the video wouldn't stream until the toolbar icon was clicked.

## Cause

In WebKit, wireless **audio** playback is always permitted, but **video** AirPlay is opt-*out*: a page or its player can disable it via the `x-webkit-wirelessvideoplaybackdisabled` attribute (or the `webkitWirelessVideoPlaybackDisabled` property). Many players set this. When it's set, the audio routes but the video stays on-device.

See Apple's [Opting Into or Out of AirPlay](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/AudioVideo/Conceptual/AirPlayGuide/OptingInorOutofAirPlay/OptingInorOutofAirPlay.html): *"Wireless audio playback is always allowed."*

## Fix

Added an `enableVideoAirplay(video)` helper that re-enables video routing on an element:

- set `x-webkit-airplay="allow"`
- remove `x-webkit-wirelessvideoplaybackdisabled`
- clear `webkitWirelessVideoPlaybackDisabled` (guarded in a `try/catch`, since it's non-standard and may be read-only)

It is applied in two places:

- **On the target before showing the picker** (toolbar click) — fixes issue 1.
- **On every video as it's discovered** in `updateVideoElements()`, which runs via the MutationObserver, on window focus, and once at load — fixes issue 2, so a new page's video routes automatically when it connects to an already-active AirPlay session.

The helper is idempotent and the observer watches `childList`/`subtree` (not attributes), so there's no feedback loop. No behavior change when video AirPlay was already allowed.

author: danielbrisch
body:
Phase 5: fixes a bug found in the audit. The regression test was written first and failed before the fix.

**The fix**
A controller is built lazily on its first request, so one whose constructor takes arguments and was never registered in the injector used to pass `startServer` and fail every request with a 500.

- `RouteBinder.bind` registers a check on the registry for each controller. The check passes when `Injector().contains<C>()` is true or the definition has a `create` constructor, and it does not build the controller.
- `RatelRegistry` holds the checks. `registerControllerCheck` adds one and `verifyControllers` runs them all.
- `RatelServer.startServer` calls `registry.verifyControllers()` after `onStartup` and before binding the port. A controller registered in `onStartup` is still accepted.
- The error message is the one the request path already threw. It is now shared by both paths.
- The README Dependency injection section documents the check.

**Reproduced before the fix**
In packages/ratel/test/binding/controller_injection_test.dart, the test 'startServer refuses an unregistered controller before binding' serves InjectedGreetingController with an empty injector. Before the fix it failed:

`Expected: throws <Instance of 'StateError'> ... Actual: <Instance of 'Future<void>'>`

In other words, startServer completed and bound the port.

**Tests**
- controller_injection_test.dart:
  - The old test that expected the StateError from a request now expects it from startServer, with boundPort still null.
  - A new test registers the controller in onStartup and checks that the route serves.
- route_binder_test.dart: the group that registered GreeterController after the server had started now registers it before startServer, and the 500 test became "stops startServer when nothing can build it".
- packages/ratel `dart test`: all 147 tests pass.
- Format, analyze and the hygiene check are clean.

body:
Refs #6035

**행위 중립 준비 PR(S1 분할 1/2).** #6035 S1(settled frontier 봉인 + phase 2 우회 방지)은 필수 회귀 테스트만으로 PR 상한(+800)을 넘었습니다. 그래서 설계 v2 §8.3에 따라 하네스 준비를 먼저 착지하는 PR입니다. S1 행위 변경(phase 1 봉인, phase 2 우회 방지, 필수 회귀 테스트 F1–F3·T1–T9·T6b·T11·T12)은 전부 후속 PR 하나에 들어갑니다. 이 PR은 동작을 바꾸지 않습니다.

## 옮긴 것
- `catch_up.rs`의 `CatchUpDiscordApi` trait와 `SerenityCatchUpDiscordApi` 어댑터를 `catch_up/api.rs`로 그대로 옮겼습니다.
- **fetch seam:** `fetch_messages`가 이제 `serenity::builder::GetMessages` 대신 `CatchUpFetchRequest{limit, cursor: After|Before|None}`를 받습니다.
  - 어댑터의 `into_get_messages`가 이전과 같은 `GetMessages::new().limit(..).after/before(..)`를 만듭니다.
  - 호출부 3곳은 표현만 바뀌었습니다: phase 1 After, phase 1 Before, phase 2 최근 20개.
  - 이렇게 한 이유는 `GetMessages`에 공개 accessor가 없어서, 테스트가 요청한 페이지를 읽어볼 수 없기 때문입니다.
- **enqueue seam:** 두 phase의 enqueue가 `CatchUpDiscordApi::enqueue_intervention`을 거칩니다. 기본 구현은 기존 `mailbox_enqueue_intervention`을 그대로 호출합니다.
- 기존 테스트 API 2곳(`catch_up_recovery_tests`, `classification_order_tests`)은 `fetch_messages` 시그니처만 갱신했습니다.
- `catch_up/frontier_sweep_tests.rs` 하네스:
  - `StrictApi`: Discord After/Before/None 페이지 의미(newest-first, `after`는 커서 뒤의 가장 오래된 id)를 따릅니다. fetch 시점에 공개된 retry cursor snapshot을 기록하고, Defer hook을 지원합니다.

author: jay739
body:
## Problem
Announcements and newsletters abort entirely when any `{{ placeholder }}` is left unfilled, because jfa-go's template engine treats leftover double braces as fatal. The common trigger is `{{ server_name }}`: `ServerInfo` is fetched once at startup, so if Jellyfin boots slower than omnifin (the batcave boot-order race) the cached name is empty for the lifetime of the process.

## Change
- `buildAnnounceVars` falls back to a live `GET /System/Info/Public` (4s timeout), then to the configured email `from` name, when the cached server name is empty.
- `substituteAnnounceVars` matches `{{ var }}` with any inner whitespace via one regex and **removes** placeholders that have no value instead of leaving them intact.
- New `api-announce-vars_test.go` covers tight and spaced braces, uneven whitespace, unknown placeholders and an empty `server_name`.

## Behaviour change to review
Unknown placeholders used to be left visible so an admin could spot a typo. They now render as empty text. That trades visibility for the send not failing. If you would rather keep typos visible, the alternative is to strip only known keys and reject unknown ones at template save time.

## Verification
- `go test -tags "e2ee goolm" -run TestSubstituteAnnounceVars .` passes (6 cases).
- `go vet` reports no findings in the changed files; the remaining findings are the pre-existing upstream ones noted in `test.yml`.

## Context
This fix had only ever existed as an uncommitted edit in an old build checkout on batcave. The deployed `ghcr.io/jay739/omnifin:latest` image was built without it, so the newsletter failure is likely still live until this merges and the image is rebuilt.

author: mishan
body:
Replaces the phone's tab strip and ⋯ menu with a drawer from the left, and moves this browser's preferences out of the title bar into one Settings dialog on every screen size.

**Phone (≤44rem)**
- **Drawer.** ☰ opens the rail as a drawer from the left, mirroring the roster on the right. Like the roster, it stays inside the pane area so ☰ remains on screen to close it. It closes on ☰ again, the scrim, Escape, or picking anything in it, and the drawer and roster are never open together. `visibility` changes along with the slide, so a closed drawer is also out of the Tab order.
- **Title bar.** It keeps ☰, the server name, the status dot and People. You, Mail, Notify, Install, Identity and Settings move to the bottom of the drawer. They are moved, not copied, so each is still the one button that paints its own badge and state.
- **Unread dot.** ☰ shows a dot when anything behind it is unread: conversations, mail, followed news or open reports.
- Between 44 and 60rem the rail is still the strip of tabs it was.

**Settings dialog**
- Theme (System / Light / Dark), Render markdown, the self-view preview, and a button that opens the debug drawer.
- These settings belong to the browser, not the account. Each takes effect as it's changed, so the dialog has Done and no Cancel.
- On a desktop the title bar drops Auto, Markdown and Debug and gains Settings. ⇧⌘D and the status dot still open the debug drawer.

**Not done:** swipe to open. An edge swipe conflicts with iOS's own back gesture. mullion 0.3.0 shouldn't interact with this: on a phone the drawer is the untiled rail, and on a tiled desktop the drawer's footer is empty and hidden.

**Tests.** The phone test in `tiler.spec.ts` now drives the drawer on a 320px touch screen: opening it, and closing it by a pick, the scrim and Escape. It also opens Settings from the drawer and checks that the drawer and roster exclude each other. A new test checks that a theme applies as soon as it's picked. The news test switches markdown off and on through the dialog. Typecheck, `npm test`, `check:package`, `vite build` and the full Playwright suite pass locally.

author: noahsaso
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of custom themes: a theme-building assistant beside the preset editor, like the workflow builder's. It edits the draft conversationally ("warmer", "teal accent", "higher contrast", "make the dark side deeper") and the whole app previews live. It is built on the existing page-editor framework as a second editor kind.

**Shared contract** (`packages/shared`)
- `assistantEditorSyncSchema` is now a discriminated union on `kind: 'workflow' | 'theme'`, so each kind's fields are rejected on the other kind. The workflow wire format and its tests are unchanged.
- The theme operations, in `theme-assistant.ts`:
  - `set-palette`: patch or clear seeds, contrast and status. `primary: null` clears the palette.
  - `set-overrides`: per-token overrides for one variant. `null` removes a token.
  - `set-base`: changes the base theme and reshapes the variants for it.
  - `rename`, and `clear-overrides`.
  - Plus `documentJson` and undo/redo.
- `applyThemeOperations` is pure. The server always re-validates the result with the existing preset validator.
- Per-kind instructions (palette-first, status stays semantic unless asked, contrast-aware, edits apply live) and per-kind tool definitions, shared by the backend agent and the voice bridge.
- **Insights:** derivation runs against the browser's CSS cascade, so the web host syncs bounded, validated insights per variant: resolved key colors as hex, and contrast warnings. `read` returns them, so the model can judge the rendered result.

**Core**
- The `theme` adapter authorizes on the owner's `chat:send`, since themes are personal. It validates with the preset validator and exposes a contract (token catalog, palette docs, built-in bases).
- Propose and read dispatch per kind. The system-manager runner picks instructions by the editor's kind, for both the conversation agent and page-editor delegates.

**Web**
- `PageEditorAssistant` takes its title, copy, instructions and tools as props. The workflow builder passes today's values.
- The preset editor gets the assistant panel, gated on `chat:send`, with a responsive layout.
- Undo/redo is shared between manual and assistant edits. Assistant edits are rejected when stale or invalid, and applied through the preview slot otherwise.
- Nothing is saved until the user presses **Save**; the assistant can't save.
- **My themes → New theme with assistant** opens the editor with the assistant focused. Voice works through the existing bridge.

**Docs**
- An Assistant section in `docs/wiki/theme/custom-themes.md`.
- The outdated "Assistants embedded in editors" section in `voice-assistants.md` is rewritten: the tools are `read`/`edit`, there is no Apply button and undo is shared, and it explains how to add a page kind.
- The outdated "Undo assistant edit" mention in `workflows.md` is fixed.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run lint` and the relevant `bun test` suites pass locally:
  - `bun run lint`: 0 errors. `bun typecheck`: clean.
  - `web test:ci`: 2,725 tests across 343 files, after rebasing onto main with #186.
  - Shared editor, theme-assistant and custom-theme tests: 72 passed.
  - Core `routes/assistant.test.ts` and `system-manager-runner.test.ts`: 59 passed. That includes new theme-kind sync, read, propose, revision conflicts, invalid rejection, undo/redo, close and cross-user 404, plus instruction selection by kind.
  - Full Core suite on the pre-rebase branch: green except the known intermittent `manager.watch.test.ts` failure (#59).
- Real browser, on a throwaway instance with a virtual passkey:
  - **New theme with assistant** focuses the panel.
  - The captured sync request carries `kind: 'theme'` with insights that match the computed colors.
  - A `set-palette` proposal sent through the page-editor API repaints the whole app within the poll window with the derived teal; Undo reverts it; nothing is saved.
  - **Not exercised:** a real model turn. The throwaway instance had no AI provider configured.
- [x] Docs updated if behaviour or configuration changed.

body:
## Summary

Natural-event source timeouts currently report the request/body phase but cannot show whether a request was sent locally, whether body bytes arrived, or whether the HTTP body completed. Add passive, request-correlated Undici measurements to existing failure messages, plus failed-source last-success and remaining-retention context after publication.

Counters cover the latest redirect hop and encoded payload bytes. A local send observation does not prove remote receipt; HTTP completion does not prove valid JSON. Unobserved transports remain explicitly unknown. Successful attempts emit no new diagnostics; retries, deadlines, dispatchers, payloads and freshness metadata remain unchanged. Include the helper in the climate bundle deployment watch list.

## Verification

- 52 focused native transfer, retry/deadline, source recovery, GDACS and NHC consumer tests passed.
- 142 Railway registry tests passed.
- Native HTTP fixtures cover concurrent requests, header waits, partial bodies, gzip completion, malformed JSON, redirects, cleanup and log privacy.
- Regression test failed before integration because failure messages lacked progress records, then passed after integration.
- `git diff --check` and commit Unicode check passed.

Local tests use Node 24.20.0. Production Node 24.10.0 / bundled Undici 7.16.0 hook compatibility was checked against upstream source, but this change has not been deployed or accepted through a natural production run. It improves failure evidence; it does not claim to prevent upstream outages. No UI or public API contract changes.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] Other: natural-event worker failure diagnostics

## Checklist

- [x] No API keys or secrets committed
- [x] Frontend and API type checks passed through the pre-push gates
- UI variant testing: not applicable; worker diagnostics only
- RSS proxy allowlist: not applicable; no new feeds
- Health-probe cutover: not applicable; no probe or activation changes

## Documentation Alignment Checklist

Not applicable: no public documentation, API/MCP, generated-contract, or Redis writer/reader contract changes.

## Screenshots

Not applicable: no UI changes.

## Review follow-up

Body byte counts now remain `null` until a chunk event is observed. Request/header/completion hooks alone do not establish byte telemetry support. A regression test reproduces the missing-hook case; native transfer tests still verify measured byte counts.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Failed data-source requests now include details about how far the request progressed, making incomplete responses easier to distinguish from requests that did not receive a response.
  * Warning logs for failed sources now indicate whether retained data is still available and, when applicable, how long it will remain available. This additional detail does not change published health information.
  * Request diagnostics omit response content and request URLs.

- exact old live SHA required
- exact target branch + SHA pinned
- target must be a single direct child of live SHA
- exact 15-file Email-only diff allowlist
- includes protected-release bounded E6/E7 Email readiness workflow to satisfy production SCP bounds policy

- isolated worktree Email tests + SCP bounds + typecheck + production build before mutation

## Que cambia

Dos cosas, y ninguna toca autenticacion, rutas, backend ni contratos.

### 1. El logotipo oficial en el inicio de sesion

`shared/ui-kit/marca/` estrena «Nexus Battles VI — Return of the Warriors» en **WebP (247 KB)** con **PNG cuantizado de respaldo (225 KB)**. El original pesaba 2,5 MB: demasiado para la primera pantalla del juego. Se sirve a 1200 px y se muestra a **520 px en escritorio y 320 en movil**, con `width`/`height` en el marcado para que la maqueta no salte mientras carga.

En `login.html` ocupa el sitio del texto grande y **sigue siendo el h1**: el nombre va en el `alt`, asi que un lector de pantalla oye exactamente lo que oia. El sobretitulo «Return of the Warriors» deja de repetirse encima porque ya viene dentro del logotipo. El lema, los tres puntos, el formulario, los enlaces y la cabecera **no cambian**. Las otras tres vistas de entrada (registro, restablecer) siguen con el texto: este cambio es del inicio de sesion.

| Escritorio 1440 | Movil 375 |
|---|---|
| logotipo en la columna de identidad, formulario intacto a la derecha | formulario primero (como ya era), logotipo debajo a 320 px |

### 2. Botones con respuesta de videojuego

`.boton` gana respuesta fisica **sin cambiar de aspecto en reposo**:

| Estado | Que hace |
|---|---|
| hover | sube 1 px y escala un 2 % con `--sombra-2`; los solidos encienden un brillo azul/violeta |
| pulsar | se hunde al 98 % con `--duracion-instantaneo` |
| foco | el anillo global de `base.css`, separado 1 px mas para no pisarse con el brillo |
| deshabilitado | no responde a nada |

El principal tiene ademas **una luz que recorre su borde una sola vez** al entrar el cursor: un anillo de 1 px con gradiente conico recortado por mascara, cuyo angulo se anima con `@property`. Sin `@property` el anillo no aparece y el boton es el mismo boton. **Nada parpadea ni se repite.**

**`prefers-reduced-motion`**: las duraciones ya caian a cero por `tokens.css`; aqui ademas se anulan desplazamiento y escala, y la luz del borde solo se declara bajo `no-preference`. Comprobado con Playwright:

```
reduced-motion → transform: none            | animacion ::after: none
normal hover   → transform: matrix(1.0197…) | animacion ::after: luz-del-borde
```

**Paleta**: tres tokens nuevos junto a las sombras (`--brillo-primaria`, `--brillo-acento`, `--sombra-marca`). `componentes.css` sigue **sin un solo hex ni rgba** fuera de comentarios; el color se mezcla con `color-mix` sobre los tokens que ya habia.

author: russellfeinstein
body:
Closes #215.

## What was wrong

`st.unanswered`, the record of a confirm the auction house never answered, lived only on
`self._restock` and reached the persisted pending store through `_RestockSearchTeardown`, which runs
on a reset or a new search. A `/reload`, logout or disconnect before either forgot it, the next
search offered the row as though nothing had been bought, and real gold went out twice. That is the
symptom #209 was built to stop, surviving in the one case the entry exists to cover.

## Findings 1 and 4 are one change

Parking the record eagerly is only safe if a late `COMMODITY_PURCHASE_SUCCEEDED` can **settle** the
parked quantity and a late `COMMODITY_PURCHASE_FAILED` can **reverse** it. One summed `qty` under one
`unconfirmed` boolean can express neither: it read 10 confirmed beside 5 unconfirmed as "15 bought,
result unknown", which is finding 4, and that is the blocker for finding 1 rather than a smaller
sibling of it. The issue's own fix candidate names the settle direction and not the reverse
direction, which is the half that keeps the gold accounting honest.

So the entry holds `qty` and `unconfirmedQty` apart, with `unconfirmedAt` beside `at` because
`_RestockAddPending` deliberately keeps the earliest purchase time and a park landing on a
three-hour-old entry would otherwise render that age for a purchase made five seconds ago.
`GBL:_RestockPendingParts` is the one place either number becomes a reading, and the boolean is
derived there rather than stored beside them. It also reads a pre-split entry as wholly unconfirmed,
so nothing migrates: the store is per guild, local and unsynced.

`_RestockOnStepTimeout` and `CancelRestockPurchase` write the entry themselves now and mark the
record `parked`. `st.unanswered` stays as the session marker that blocks a new start and carries the
late credit, and the teardown is the retry for a park the store refused rather than the first
attempt.

## The rest of the issue

- **Finding 2.** `StoreTx` replaces an invalid timestamp with `GetServerTime()` **in place** before
  the hook runs, so no later reader can tell a record that carried this time from one that was given
  it. It passes `{ timestampRewritten = true }` now and the hook refuses, so a sync-received copy of
  an old deposit with a corrupt or epoch-0 timestamp (#93) cannot clear an entry whose purchase is
  still in the mail. Refusing is the safe direction: a wrong keep costs one click on Clear, a wrong
  clear costs the gold again. `StoreBatchRecords` needs nothing, because the scan path does not
  rewrite.
- **Finding 3, worse than filed.** The universe walked layout items then reserve-only items, so a
  pending entry for neither had no row and therefore no Clear. The filed text stops there; the view
  also short-circuits on an empty universe with "No items in your bank layout yet", so a player who
  cleared their display tabs with a purchase in the mail **could not reach the entry by any route.**
  A third pass gives those entries a group of their own, beside the Reserves precedent.
- **Findings 6, 7, 8.** `parkUnanswered` keeps the record when the add is refused; the `buyer` key is
  guarded, which was a live `table index is nil`; and both readers reach a string-keyed entry and
  re-key it by number, the way `InitSync` consolidates a stale peer key.
- **Finding 5** stays recorded and not fixed, as filed.
- **Finding 9 was half dead.** It asked that the `_RestockOnSearchEnd` park be kept for #214 and that
  CLAUDE.md be corrected. #214 went the other way and deleted that park for one teardown, and
  CLAUDE.md was corrected then. The stale claim had moved: `docs/PLAN-restock-ux.md` still said "the
  two parking sites". Fixed here.
- The **"To #214, not here"** item was already done: `inmail` shipped as a status of its own.

## Two things the work found that the issue does not name

- **The teardown cleared `st.unanswered` unconditionally**, after `parkUnanswered` had decided to keep
  it. That is a third way a purchase was forgotten with no line, beyond the two finding 6 names, and
  the keep does not work until that line goes.
- **PR A's review had declined to park at Cancel**, on the grounds that parking left the row buyable
  and the late result landed on the next purchase. That reasoning was about parking *instead of* the
  unanswered record; both are set now, so the record still blocks every start. The #211 case that
  pinned the old behaviour is updated with the reasoning rather than quietly flipped, and a mutation
  confirms it still pins something.

## Four copies of the entry shape, one stale since #209

Grepping the prose rather than the symbol found the shape written out in four places, and
`src/Restock.lua`'s own header omitted `buyers`, which `_RestockAddPending` has written since the
feature shipped. A reader had four statements of one fact and no way to tell which was current. All
four are corrected, each written from the function rather than from another copy, which is also why
the pre-split fixture in the specs is built from `_RestockAddPending`.

## Not closed, and said so rather than claimed

A reload inside the roughly five seconds between a confirm going out and the step timer firing still
loses the record. Parking at confirm-issue would close it and is declined: it writes to
SavedVariables on every purchase and doubles the `Restock pending:` lines in a system capture bounded
at 300 entries, which is the readability constraint #199 was built around. Recorded on the issue and
in `docs/PLAN-restock-ux.md` section 6.

## The code review found a fix that could not fire

Worth reading before the rest. The `timestampRewritten` guard shipped in the
third commit was **dead code**: `StoreTx` has one production caller, inside the
sync receive, and `reconstructSyncRecord` rewrites an invalid timestamp before
the record reaches it, so `StoreTx`'s own check never failed there. The spec
passed only because it called `StoreTx` directly with a state the sync path
cannot deliver, and the CHANGELOG line claiming the fix landed was false. The
flag now comes back from `reconstructSyncRecord`, which is the function that
actually rewrites.

Eleven more findings were reproduced against the real code and fixed, each
red-first. The ones that mattered most: settling was a try-then-add, so a late
result re-added a quantity the player had cleared by hand or a deposit had
already settled, reversing the player's own Clear; `normalizeEntry` indexed
whatever `takeEntry` returned, so a corrupt SavedVariables value raised
mid-purchase; the deposit window read a missing purchase time as zero and
therefore accepted every deposit ever recorded; a refused deposit rewrote the
entry it had just refused; and the new rows for an item the layout does not name
could not reach the `inmail` status, so all three encodings read "in stock"
beside the row's own "in the mail N".

**One of the review's own premises did not hold, and the real shape was
different.** It reported the refused park as coming from a cold store. But
`GetGuildName` caches, so the store can only refuse before any guild name has
been read this session, which for this flow is close to unreachable. The
reachable refusal is a nil quantity, and that one is *permanent*: keeping the
record blocks every buy while it stands, and the same teardown drops the buy
events, so nothing can ever clear it. So `_RestockAddPending` names its reason
now, a store that cannot take it yet keeps the record and retries on the next
tab show, and a record there is nothing to write is dropped with a line.

Six more prose claims this PR had made false went with it, including Cancel's
own header and the matching CLAUDE.md sentence, which both still forbade the
park two lines above it. The fourth commit of this PR exists to reconcile four
copies of this feature's shape; these were the next six.


## Mutation pass

Thirteen mutations against `src/Restock.lua`, `src/Ledger.lua` and `UI/RestockView.lua`, one live at

## الملخص
الطلبُ الثاني من خطّة تغطية غياب المعلّم (قراراتُ المالك 2026-09-23 و2026-09-24). **مبنيٌّ فوق #515** ويُنقل إلى `main` بعد اندماجه.

- **مع معلّمي الشعبة نفسها وحدَهم:** في بطاقة كلّ حصّةٍ للغائب خيارٌ «أو تبديل مع معلّمي الشعبة» (يُحمَّل حين يُفتح). يعرض معلّمي الشعبة المتفرّغين في تلك الحصّة، ولكلٍّ يومَ الردّ: أقربَ يومٍ بعد الغياب يكون الغائبُ فيه متفرّغاً لحصّة ذلك المعلّم في الشعبة. فلا يزيد نصابُ أحد.
- **تبدأه القيادة** (النائب الأكاديميّ، المدير، المطوّر، ومن كُلِّف عن النائب): يُنفَّذ فوراً ويُبلَّغ الجميع.
- **يبدأه المنسّق:** بدؤه توقيعٌ عن جهته ← يوافق المعلّمُ الآخر ← يوقّع منسّقُ مادّته ← **ينتظر النائب** (`pending_vp`) لا التنفيذ ← يعتمده النائبُ أو المكلَّفُ بأعبائه (`StaffAssignment`) فيُنفَّذ. والنائبُ يُبلَّغ مسبقاً عند البدء.
- **يعود الجدولُ وحده** بعد الحصّة الأبعد: التبديلُ يقع على `Session` ليومَيه (`SwapService.execute_swap`) لا على القالب.
- **الغيابُ «مغطّى»** حين تُغطّى كلُّ حصصه بإشغالٍ أو بتبديلٍ نُفِّذ (`refresh_absence_status`).
- **السجلّ:** `TeacherSwap` بحقل `absence` — من غاب ومن بدّل ومن وقّع ومتى ومن اعتمد.
- الخدمة في `operations/services/absence_swap.py` جديدة؛ والشاشاتُ في `views_swap.py` لأنّ `views_schedule.py` عند سقف حجمه (1567 من 1568).

لا هجرات.

author: lsdsjy
body:
New session, session search, and switching workspace are the three actions reached most often from the sidebar, and all of them were mouse-only. This adds a consistent keyboard path to each, ending where the user wants to type.

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `Cmd/Ctrl+J` | New session in the active project |
| `Cmd/Ctrl+K` | Toggle the sidebar session search and focus its input |
| `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` | Open the workspace selector |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Move the highlight in the selector, wrapping at both ends |
| `Enter` | Switch to the highlighted workspace and focus the composer |
| `Escape` | Close the selector without switching |

`Ctrl+Alt+N` keeps working unchanged.

The workspace chord is `P` rather than the more obvious `J` because Chrome owns the `J` variants: `Cmd+Shift+J` opens the Downloads page on macOS and `Ctrl+Shift+J` opens the DevTools console, so a page cannot count on winning either. No Chrome shortcut takes `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` on any platform ([Chrome keyboard shortcuts](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/157179)). `P` also reads as "project", and the chord keeps the shape of the other two: `Cmd+J` for a new session, `Cmd+K` for search, `Cmd+Shift+P` for the workspace.

## Implementation

- **Pure matcher, thin hook.** The shortcut decision lives in `lib/global-shortcuts.ts` as `matchGlobalShortcut`, so it is unit-testable without a DOM. `useKeyboardShortcuts` only reads the module-level handlers, dispatches, and calls `preventDefault`. `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` is checked before the plain chords, which reject any shifted event. A test pins `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J` as unclaimed so the Chrome collision cannot come back unnoticed.
- **Registry for sidebar-owned state.** `SessionSidebar` owns `sessionSearchOpen` and the selector, while `AppShell` owns the listener, so the sidebar registers both the same way `ChatWindow` already registers the Esc abort handler. The toolbar buttons and the shortcuts now share one `toggleSessionSearch` / `openProjectDropdown`.
- **The terminal wins.** `Ctrl+J` (LF) and `Ctrl+K` (kill line) are real readline bindings, so all three chords are ignored while the event comes from inside `.xterm`.
- **No repeat storms.** Every chord ignores key repeats, so holding one does not spawn sessions or reopen the selector.
- **Keyboard navigation in the selector.** Rows carry `data-project-index`, `role="option"`, and `aria-selected`, the list is a labelled `listbox`, and the highlight follows hover so mouse and keyboard share one cursor. The active row scrolls into view with `block: "nearest"`. The listener lives on the window while the selector is open, so it also works when the project filter input owns the focus; changing the filter resets the highlight to the first row of the shorter list. The selector opens on the current workspace, so `Enter` keeps it and the arrows move away from there.
- **Composer focus after a pick.** `ChatInputHandle` gained `focus()`, since picking a workspace is followed by typing. `AppShell` waits two frames first, because the workspace switch bumps `sessionKey` and remounts `ChatWindow`.
- **Discoverable on hover.** All three buttons show their shortcut in the tooltip (`(⌘J)`, `(⌘K)`, `(⌘⇧P)`) and declare `aria-keyshortcuts`, which needed a new `sidebar.shortcutHint` message in all three locales. The hints resolve after mount so server and client markup stay identical and no hydration warning appears.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 1317 passing (10 new in `lib/global-shortcuts.test.mjs`), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean.
- Browser-checked on macOS: `Cmd+K` opens the search panel and focuses the input; `Cmd+J` starts a new session draft; `Cmd+Shift+P` opens the selector on the current workspace, both arrows wrap, filtering resets the highlight, `Enter` switches and leaves the caret in the composer, `Escape` closes without switching, clicking a row behaves like `Enter`; `Ctrl+J`/`Ctrl+K` still reach the shell while the terminal is focused.

author: claudio-michel[bot]
body: ## Why A host sometimes needs to mark nodes in a document it generates or stores, for example the preset that produced a node, and read those marks back later. The engine should neither care about nor be affected by these marks. Until now, any extra key on a node was an authoring error, so hosts had nowhere to put them. ## Semantics Every node kind accepts an optional `metadata` field. - **Object only.** When present, it must be a plain object. A string, array, number, boolean or `null` is refused with an error that names the node, such as `workflow.root.steps[0] (draft): metadata must be a plain object of host markers`. Keys and values are any JSON and are never inspected. - **Opaque.** The interpreter never reads it. Desugaring, `dryRunWorkflow`, `runWorkflow` and the author's candidate loop carry it through verbatim. A prose artifact that desugars to `report` keeps it. - **Never in state or events.** It also never reaches prompts, judge requests or effect idempotency keys. Hooks that receive the node object, such as `runEffect` and recovery, see it as part of the node. - **In the digest.** `workflowSha256` hashes the whole document, so changing a marker changes the digest. The field lives in a new `HOST_NODE_FIELDS` constant, not in `NODE_FIELDS`. The validator admits it on every kind. The author contract states it once: "Every kind also accepts `metadata`, an object the host owns and the engine never reads; set only the keys the host addendum names." A new optional `AuthorHostAddendum.metadataKeys` names the keys authors may set. As with `rules`, the host enforces them in its acceptance checks, so the candidate loop is unchanged. The editor schema admits `metadata` as an open object on all 17 kinds. `NodeMetadata` is exported. The interpreter's run path is unchanged. The only source changes are the node types, the key allow-list, one shape check and the contract text. ## Tests (`packages/dsl/test/node-metadata.test.mjs`) The tests use the 40 Lean conformance cases plus one extra workflow for the kinds that corpus lacks: decide, extract, sift and a prose artifact. Together they cover all 17 node kinds. - Metadata on every node gives the same validation verdict and error list, with and without input keys, and survives desugaring verbatim. - A non-object metadata (string, array, number, boolean, `null`) is refused with the node named. A node without a label is named by its kind. - A run with metadata on every node matches the same run without it, byte for byte, in: result, state, output, every event (with `duration_ms` normalized), checkpoints, and every `runNode`, `runJudge` and `runEffect` request. This holds for 34 runnable cases. - Dry runs are equal with and without metadata. The digest changes when metadata is added and stays stable across repeat runs. - The author contract names `metadata` once. `metadataKeys` renders in the addendum. `candidatePolicyErrors` and `applyHostOutputTypes` are unaffected. `authorWorkflow` returns a metadata-bearing candidate verbatim. ## Lean - New conformance case `spec/lean/conformance/node-metadata.json` puts metadata on chain, extract, parallel, agent, decide, code and report nodes. Some metadata values are named `as` and `label` to show they are not read. The case validates and completes, and its state and events contain no metadata. - The Lean JSON front end already ignores fields the model does not use, so the validator mirror admits `metadata` by construction. Doc comments in `Json.lean` and `Validate.lean` now say so. - `lake build` is green, with zero `sorry` and a green axiom audit. - `lake exe conformance`: 40/40 cases agree with the model. The TypeScript side of `lean-conformance` passes too. - Validator sweep: 1312 validations, 983 accepted by TypeScript, 0 rejected by the model. 93 of the swept workflows carry metadata, and 75 of those are accepted. ## Release - Bumped to `0.1.0-beta.4` in the workspace and all three packages, with exact internal dependencies and the lockfile updated. - `docs/dependencies.md` is regenerated. - The CHANGELOG has a new `0.1.0-beta.4 (unreleased)` section. - Install commands in the READMEs and the starter still point at the published `beta.3`, following `docs/releasing.md`. - Not published. ## Checks `npm run check`, `npm run export:source`, `node scripts/check-generated.mjs`, `npm run verify:packages` and `npm run verify:source` all pass. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? ## Summary
Roadmap discussion: the real adoption blocker isn't marketing, it's that the only LLM backend today is a paid hosted API - real friction for self-hosted/cost-sensitive/air-gapped shops. Revises slice 10 onward to sequence around that:

- **Slice 10** reframed: Ollama (not OpenAI) is the second LLM backend, because it answers a real blocker rather than just proving the interface abstracts. Same slice's webhook receiver reframed as the one mechanism that unlocks SonarQube/Falco/etc at once, since neither exposes a Kubernetes CRD the way Trivy does but both can already POST a webhook on their own.
- **New slice 11**: GitLab as a second `internal/gitops.Opener` implementation - already a clean interface with one implementation, so this is contained.
- **New slice 12**: fixture suite + published per-model accuracy - the evidence gap #7's answer already promises and doesn't exist yet.
- **New deferred item**: a fine-tuned/distilled model for the target tool set. Explicitly sequenced *after* slice 12 - training one before there's a way to measure it against an off-the-shelf model would be the unverified-claim failure mode this whole project argues against.

author: iluzdaf
body:
## Summary
- A walk from a standstill to a stop on flat ground costs the same and sweeps the same cells however far along the floor it starts, so `PlatformerConnectionCache` now keeps a `RememberedWalk` per length and body (cost, or none past the simulation limit, plus the sweep as offsets from the start). A simulation with a cache reads each length after the first time it is simulated; without a cache every walk is still simulated. A break leaves the walks kept, since no tile decided them.
- Premise checked on a 40-cell floor from every start cell, for two body sizes, at the map's edges too: every length costs the same from every start, in both directions.
- Warm-up (release) drops from 1.6 / 6.1 / 8.8 ms to 0.8 / 2.8 / 2.6 ms across the three levels. A level 1 break's 30 cells take 2928 ticks instead of 11516, so `NavigationRefillTicksPerStep` comes down from 500 to 250: worst step stays about 0.05 ms and the refill takes 9 steps instead of 16.
- The overlay totals gain a `walks` line.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests: the cache keeps a walk per length and body, replaces on keep, leaves walks through a break, drops them on clear, and validates the body; a second cell on a floor simulates fewer ticks, remembers no new walk, and has the same connections and footprint as it would alone; a simulation without a cache still simulates every walk.
- [x] `ctest` 424/424, clang-format 18, clang-tidy 22, header self-containment, game run with the overlay open.

author: monkeypants
body:
Uses julee 0.5.10's contribution reading (julee#213), and undoes a wart I introduced earlier in this work.

## The wart

The kit ships three Sphinx extensions and a contribution point could hold one path, so it declared:

```python
"sphinx.extension": "julee_viewpoints.sphinx_hcd",
"sphinx.extension.c4": "julee_viewpoints.sphinx_c4",
"sphinx.extension.semantics": "julee_viewpoints.semantics",
```

`sphinx.extension.c4` and `sphinx.extension.semantics` are not contribution points anybody consumes. They were invented to fit the shape. There is one point now:

```python
"sphinx.extension": (
    "julee_viewpoints.sphinx_hcd",
    "julee_viewpoints.sphinx_c4",
    "julee_viewpoints.semantics",
),
```

**The order is load order and it matters** — `sphinx_c4` borrows a persona through `c4_bridge`, so it wants the HCD side registered first. That is now expressed rather than implied by three separate keys.

## A solution asks instead of naming

```python
extensions = sphinx_extensions(Path(__file__).parent.parent)
```

Six integration tests build a project whose `conf.py` **contains no module of this kit**, and check all three extensions arrived — one assertion per extension, so a missing one names itself. Plus one test that naming them by hand still works, since asking is a convenience and not the only way in.

A conf.py that names modules goes stale when a kit gains one. That is what happened here: `semantics` was added this session and every existing conf.py would have silently lacked it.

`julee-viewpoints` **0.4.0** — a solution's conf.py can keep working unchanged, but the manifest's shape changed and anything reading `contributes` directly would see it. Floor moves to `julee>=0.5.10`.

`make check` green: 1353 unit, doctrine green for all five kits, **112 integration**.

AI 披露：本改动由 AI 编码代理辅助完成，我已逐行审改。

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Serializing a Kotlin class without `kotlin-reflect` on the classpath throws an NPE: `KotlinUtils.getKoltinConstructorParameters` returns `null` when kotlin-reflect cannot be loaded, but the writer still reads the array length unconditionally. Fixes #7749.

### Summary of your change

Match constructor parameter annotations only when parameter names are available; when they are not, skip this optional mapping and continue serialization. Adds regression test `Issue7749` (`@Tag("regression")`) simulating a class whose Kotlin parameter names cannot be resolved.

Testing: `./mvnw -pl core -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect -Dtest=Issue7749 test`

author: yourwilddad
body:
## Summary

Adds a plugin system in the webpack/tapable style. The core flow stays hard-coded. Objects fire hooks as they come into being and hand themselves to plugins, which see them only through a narrow public interface.

- **Plugin contract** (`@excitedjs/dreamux-types`, `plugin.ts`):
  - A plugin is a zero-argument factory. It returns `{ name, api?, config?, contribute?, server? }`.
  - `contribute` registers channel/runtime providers.
  - `server` taps hooks.
  - Neither may do IO: `doctor` runs both without starting the service.
- **Hook tree:**
  - `host.hooks.dispatcher` → `dispatcher.hooks.{beforeLaunch, team}` → `team.hooks.{beforeTeamLeaderLaunch, created}`.
  - `host.hooks.plugin.for(name)` hands a plugin's `api` to other plugins once, at the end of loading, so plugin order does not matter.
- **Launch drafts:**
  - Launch hooks append to a draft `{ instructions, skillSources }` that starts empty, so built-in prompts and skills stay out of plugin reach by construction.
  - Core merges the instructions into both `replace` and `append`, and plugin skills pass the existing skill fence.
- **Tap isolation:**
  - Core installs a `register` interceptor on every hook it creates, following webpack's `processAssets` pattern, and calls `hook.call` / `hook.promise` normally. Plugin interceptors run.
  - A failing launch tap loses only its own sub-draft. Other runtime taps are isolated, and the error is logged with the owning plugin.
  - The owner is recorded when the tap registers and is carried through `AsyncLocalStorage`.
  - `plugin.for` taps are load phase: a throw fails `serve`.
- **`team.hooks.created`:**
  - It fires once after a new Team is published.
  - It runs as a tracked background task, so a plugin cannot hold up the create reply.
  - Dispatcher stop drains it.
- **Config:**
  - New optional top-level `plugins[]`. Each entry is a ref string or `{ ref, config }`, using `builtin:` or `npm:`.
  - A same-name plugin, provider, Feishu tool (per caller) or card action key is an error that names both sources.
- **Feishu:**
  - Feishu becomes an always-loaded built-in plugin. It publishes `extensions.register(ext)`, where an extension carries tools, card actions, and a per-instance `initialize` / `start` / `close`. Handlers receive their own instance state.
  - Extensions also get an instance API: `owner`, `readMessageRoute`, `bindTeam`, `sendCard`, `editCard`, `submitToTeam`.
  - `builtin:feishu` keeps working unchanged.
- **Built-in `bootstrap` plugin** (`@excitedjs/dreamux-plugin-bootstrap`, enabled by listing `builtin:bootstrap`):
  - When `identity.md` or `user.md` is missing under `<dispatcher cwd>/.workspace/`, it writes and injects a first-run guide for the Dispatcher only.
  - Once both files exist, it deletes the guide and injects both files into the Dispatcher and TeamLeader launch drafts.
- **`doctor`:**
  - It lists plugins, their providers and their top-level taps.
  - Feishu extension tools and actions are listed under each Feishu channel row.

## Upgrade impact

- BREAKING: `dispatchers[].cwd` is now required on every entry, enabled or not. Rebuild: add `"cwd": "<absolute dir>"` to every `dispatchers[]` entry that lacks it. See the change file.
- `@excitedjs/feishu-channel`'s default export is now the plugin factory. `builtin:feishu` is unaffected. A config that referenced `npm:@excitedjs/feishu-channel` as a provider must use `builtin:feishu`.
- `@excitedjs/dreamux-types` now depends on `tapable`, used by type only.
- Plugin APIs carry no compatibility promise yet.

## Before merge

- The new npm package `@excitedjs/dreamux-plugin-bootstrap` needs npm trusted-publisher setup.

## Known open review items (not fixed in this PR yet)

- An `async` function tapped with `tap` on a sync hook can reject unhandled and crash `serve`. Fix: catch thenables in the interceptor wrapper or reject async taps on sync hooks.
- A plugin `call` interceptor can see the launch composition and push unfenced skill roots.
- A plugin interceptor that throws at the non-`created` call sites propagates into `Server.start` / `team.create`. The api-publication interceptor throw is not reported as a doctor failure row.
- Concurrent Feishu teardown can finish session close before extension cleanup.
- `configuredDispatcherCwd` throws a bare `TypeError` for an id that is not in config.
- Empty Feishu extension tool names are accepted.

## Test plan

- `rush build`, `lint`, `typecheck:tests` and `test` pass.
- New unit tests cover the loader, hooks/interceptors, Dispatcher/Team trigger points, doctor, Feishu extensions, bootstrap, and the package-boundary guards.

author: simonp0607
body:
El healthcheck de `desplegar.sh` comprueba si el servicio que acaba de subir contesta. **No** comprueba si al subirlo ha empujado a otro fuera de la RAM.

El 24-sep eso costo el entorno entero: se desplego ms-ecommerce sobre un host que ya sostenia ms-finanzas, ningun contenedor murio, ningun healthcheck fallo — el CD lo dio por bueno — y unos minutos despues ni el borde respondia.

## Umbrales, medidos

| estado | disponible | swap libre | resultado |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| 9 MVP + identidad | 312 MiB | 493 MiB | sano |
| + ms-finanzas | 318 MiB | 52 MiB | sano |
| + finanzas + cumplimiento + ecommerce | 187 MiB | 106 MiB | sano, al limite |
| + ecommerce sobre finanzas, en caliente | 67 MiB | 0 MiB | **thrashing** |

El salto esta entre 106 y 0 MiB de swap libre. Los umbrales van del lado seguro:

`
ANTES    no empezar si disponible < 150 MiB o swap libre < 150 MiB
DESPUES  revertir si disponible <  80 MiB o swap libre <  50 MiB
`

Los 80 MiB ya estaban en CAPACIDAD.md. Lo nuevo: mirarlo tambien **antes**, mirar el **swap** (el que se agoto primero las dos veces) y comprobar que el **nucleo del MVP** sigue contestando despues, no solo el servicio nuevo.

Si la compuerta de despues salta, se apaga lo recien desplegado con `apagar.sh`. Se revierte el servicio nuevo, nunca el MVP.

Refs #430, #707

body:
Bu PR, Eylül 2026 gözden geçirmesinde md. 157-206'ya aykırı bulunan kusurları düzeltiyor. Plan, durum ve geçiş notları `docs/gelistirme-plani-2026-09.md` dosyasında. Her kusur önce bir testle yeniden üretildi; bu testler `backend/apps/disiplin/tests/test_mevzuat_uyum.py` içinde.

## Hukuki sonucu doğrudan yanlış olanlar
- **md. 163/2, 169/2:** Onaylanmamış karar artık tebliğ edilemiyor. Kesinleşmiş sayılmıyor, e-Okul'a işlenmiyor ve davranış puanını düşürmüyor.

- **md. 175/2:** Tedbirde her uzatma ayrı bir süre sayılıyor: en fazla 10 iş günü, en fazla iki kez. Uzatma, Millî Eğitim Müdürü onayı işaretlenmeden kaydedilmiyor. Bu kural okul yönetiminin teyidiyle belirlendi.
- **md. 191:** Toplantı yeter sayısı ile şikâyetçi ya da zarar gören üyenin toplantıya katılamaması denetleniyor.

author: danzeroum
body:
**SHA inspecionado:** `296226eb803adbe380f1473c25c5a22ebb857029` (main pós #43)

## O que muda

Um analyzer novo, **`pitch_f0`**, com check_id próprio (`pitch_f0.median`), métrica `f0_median_hz` e rule_id **`AS-DESC-008`** (descritivo).

- **Método:** YIN (de Cheveigné & Kawahara, 2002). Função de diferença + CMNDF, primeiro vale abaixo do limiar absoluto (0,15), descida até o fundo do vale e interpolação parabólica. Vetorizado por FFT em lotes, **numpy puro** (R2+).
- **Vozeamento explícito:** um quadro sem vale abaixo do limiar é não vozeado e fica fora da estatística. O gate de energia é relativo ao quadro mais forte (−40 dB) e define os quadros ativos.
- **Evidência:** mediana (valor), p10/p25/p75/p90 em Hz, IQR, faixa p10–p90 em semitons e fração vozeada.
- **R1:** só `pass` (observation), `not_applicable` (silêncio) ou `indeterminate` (sinal presente sem quadros vozeados, como ruído). Nunca `fail`.
- `pitch_stab` **não foi tocado**. O `deepfake` importa `_pitch_track_autocorr` dele, e trocar o tracker mudaria dois analyzers.

## Verificação: Hz certos em sinal conhecido

Tudo com o fixture seed-based `gen_harmonic` (novo, em `tests/fixtures/generators.py`), sem arquivo gerado novo e com o manifest inalterado.

| sinal | esperado | medido | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| harmônico 120 Hz (22,05 / 44,1 / 48 kHz) | 120 ± 2 | 120,00 | pass |
| harmônico 220 Hz | 220 ± 3 | 220,00 | pass |
| 120 Hz, fundamental −20 dB | sem erro de oitava | 120,00 (p10/p90 dentro de ±½ oitava) | pass |
| 220 Hz, fundamental −20 dB | sem erro de oitava | 220,00 | pass |
| varredura exp. 150→300 Hz | mediana 212,1 / p10 160,8 / p90 279,8 | todos a < 25 cents | pass |
| `gen_speech_like` (pulso de 150 Hz) | 150 ± 3 | ✓ | pass |
| silêncio | — | `None` | **not_applicable** |
| ruído branco (sementes 0, 1, 2) | — | `None` | **indeterminate** |

## Validação: as vozes reais do estúdio dos Guardiões

Faixas de cada falante (`filmes/<id>/baseline/vozes/<voz>.wav` do `danzeroum/estudio-suite-guardioes-governanca` @ `6608628`), medidas localmente e só para leitura com `audio-suite analyze <wav> --profile <perfil com pitch_stab + pitch_f0>`:

| filme | falante | `pitch_drift_cents` (hoje) | **F0 mediana (Hz)** | p10–p90 (Hz) | fração vozeada |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| jornada-dado | aguia | 5022,34 | **170,70** | 143,4–193,9 | 0,32 |
| jornada-dado | coruja | 4934,42 | **169,19** | 126,0–199,6 | 0,36 |
| jornada-dado | elefante | 5456,07 | **173,73** | 115,0–213,2 | 0,36 |
| jornada-dado | narrador | 4851,03 | **156,95** | 143,4–214,6 | 0,34 |
| jornada-dado | raposa | 4923,89 | **173,22** | 156,9–190,9 | 0,29 |
| jornada-dado | tartaruga | 5445,84 | **171,42** | 124,0–218,8 | 0,47 |
| legitimo-interesse | coruja | 5444,25 | **162,53** | 114,3–225,1 | 0,30 |
| legitimo-interesse | elefante | 5058,44 | **167,47** | 114,8–203,4 | 0,39 |
| legitimo-interesse | narrador | 4867,10 | **163,89** | 130,0–184,9 | 0,50 |
| legitimo-interesse | tartaruga | 5444,95 | **163,37** | 116,1–197,0 | 0,44 |

### ⚠️ A evidência contradiz o que o pedido esperava

O pedido previa que esta tabela mostrasse o descritor *separando* as vozes. **Ela mostra que hoje as vozes não se separam em altura:** as 10 medianas cabem em 157–174 Hz, ≈1,8 semitom do extremo ao extremo. Isso não é falha do descritor. É o pipeline do estúdio: um único modelo de voz (`pt_BR-faber-medium` no `voz.lock`) e `pitch_aplicado: false` no manifesto da dublagem, porque o timbre da CP-005 muda a cor e não a F0.

A diferença que importa:
- **drift:** 4.851–5.456 cents para todos. É ruído de medida (salto vozeado/não vozeado) e não diz nada sobre a voz.
- **F0:** um número por falante, com unidade física, que diz *"estão todas na mesma altura"*. Esse é o dado de entrada da proposta de pitch por guardião no estúdio (CP-010).

**Controle positivo em fala real** (a mesma faixa reamostrada para deslocar a F0 em ±3/±6 st):

| falante | −6 st | −3 st | +3 st | +6 st |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jornada/elefante | −19,4 c | −9,4 c | −3,4 c | +35,5 c |
| jornada/raposa | −10,8 c | −4,6 c | +10,0 c | +14,2 c |
| legitimo/narrador | −34,8 c | −28,0 c | +7,5 c | +22,5 c |

O erro fica em ≤ 36 cents (< 0,4 st). Quando há diferença de altura, o descritor a vê.

**Sensibilidade ao limiar YIN** (0,10 / 0,15 / 0,25): a mediana varia ≤ 14 Hz (elefante 178,5 / 173,7 / 164,5; raposa 173,2 / 173,2 / 171,7; narrador 165,9 / 163,9 / 160,6). A conclusão não muda. O default 0,15 é o da literatura. Ele é parâmetro de método, não tolerância, e fica exposto no `profile_schema` (`yin_threshold`).

## Portões (local, Python 3.11, numpy 2.1.3, scipy 1.14.1)

- `pytest tests/unit tests/property tests/architecture tests/contracts tests/e2e tests/conformance tests/metamorphic tests/corpus tests/golden -q` → **349 passed, 1 skipped** (oráculo Rust sem `MIXLIROUS_CLI`, por design)
- `pytest tests/fuzz -q` → 13 passed
- `ruff check audio_suite tests scripts && ruff format --check audio_suite tests` → OK
- `python scripts/lint_rule_registry.py` → OK. **DoD R1:** `Status.FAIL` injetado no `pitch_f0` → 4 violações (probe + scan estático); restaurado → OK
- `python scripts/check_no_large_binaries.py` → OK (0 áudio versionado)
- `mypy audio_suite --ignore-missing-imports` → 0 erros no arquivo novo (os 12 existentes são do main)
- **Golden Master:** `tests/golden` verde e **inalterado**. O `gm_profile.yaml` não roda `pitch_stab`/`pitch_f0`. Não rodei `golden freeze` e a label `golden-regen` não é necessária.

## Pontos de decisão (humanos)

1. **ID de backlog:** o descritor não tem ID no Documento Mestre. Pelo §10, sugestão nova passa por triagem antes de ganhar ID. O título usa `W5` + o rule_id e **não inventa ID**. Se aprovado, sugiro registrá-lo como refinamento de CONTR/PROF-08 ou como `DESC-*` novo.
2. **Default fora dos perfis shipped:** `pitch_f0` não entrou em `default_profile.yaml` nem em `profiles/*`. Quem quiser a medida declara no perfil, como faz o `guardioes-vozes.yaml` do estúdio. Incluir no default é decisão à parte.

author: ybx-jp
body:
First slice of the feature-dimensions campaign. Targets `dev/feature-dimensions`, which merges to `master` when the campaign is complete.

## What changed
- `src/thalamus/contract/capabilities.py` (new, vocabulary layer): a `Dimension` declares only what may be set, as a closed list of keys each with a closed list of values. Named `Preset`s are the operator's, defined in `presets/<dimension>.yaml` under the config root. `inherit` is built in, sets nothing, is the default, and cannot be redefined. One dimension is declared: `cost`, with `model_class` (light/standard/strong/frontier) and `effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max).
- `thalamus preset list | set | remove`: define, replace and delete presets. `set` validates before writing. `remove` is refused while any manifest selects the preset. The CLI rewrites the file, so comments in it are not kept.
- `ExpertManifest.cost`: the name of a preset. `load_manifest` resolves it against the presets file in the same config root. An undefined name, or an invalid presets file, fails the load and names the manifest's path.
- `pin.render_agent`: writes the resolved preset into the generated agent file as `model:` (class mapped to the Claude aliases haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) and `effort:`. The same file carries both a `--agent` pin and a subagent spawned by name. `inherit` renders `model: inherit` and no `effort:` line, as before.
- `config/presets/cost.yaml`: three example presets (frugal, balanced, max) for the shipped example roster.
- Docs: `docs/concepts.md` (the `cost` field; ledger entries A0158, A0159) and `docs/cli.md` (`thalamus preset`). A0023's `ExpertManifest` ground is corroborated.

## Not in this change
- Codex profiles and Cursor launches do not read `cost`.
- Token and tool-call budgets: no enforcement point exists yet. Claude Code's agent `maxTurns` frontmatter is a native turn cap that a later settings key could project to.
- Constraints between dimensions (requires/excludes): deferred until a second dimension exists.
- No manifest selects a preset, so every generated agent file is unchanged. An operator config root has no `presets/` directory until `thalamus preset set` creates one.

## Verification
`pytest` 2122 passed, 3 skipped; ruff, ty, `arch rules --gate`, `arch scan --check`, `arch dead --gate` and `claims-ledger check` are all clean.

author: mearman
body:
Addresses the `src/odf/odt/read.ts` entry of the #1295 worst-offenders table. The baseline was re-measured locally and cold before any change and matched the issue's own table exactly.

Refs #1295

## What changed

- **38 new tests in `src/odf/odt/read.test.ts`** (1 before, 39 now) driving `readOdtContent` over hand-built ODT packages, with expectations derived from the odf.js block-counting mirror and the `spliceBlocks` contract rather than from observed output:
  - the formula walk: consumed formula-only paragraphs (including whitespace-only and comment-node filler, both still consumed), paragraphs kept when they carry real text or an unrecognised element, two frames in one paragraph, an absolute frame as a direct `office:text` child with its exact frame box, deep detection inside table cells and `text:section` (the construct-marker index interplay pinned as it stands), list items, nested lists, a bare frame under a list item, headings at body scope and inside a list item, and a stray non-list-item child of `text:list`;
  - the vector walk over the same container matrix, plus a drawing block grouping a container's primitives with their exact recovered frames, the drawing block frame pinned to the section page size, and the shallow-versus-deep asymmetry between the vector pass (direct children only, so a vector inside a cell is genuinely undetected) and the formula pass (a deep walk) pinned by two tests;
  - the image walk and its never-consumes asymmetry (an image-only paragraph keeps its empty block);
  - the merged splice: formula/image interleaving in both concatenation orders (kills sort removal and comparator arithmetic), empty and whitespace-only paragraphs surviving, and the multi-section guard with the detected content placed inside the guarded section's observable range so the guard's mutant is actually observable.
- **One behaviour-preserving restructure in production**: the `formulaPlacements.length > 0 || vectorPlacements.length > 0 || imagePlacements.length > 0` early-out around the combined splice is gone. A placements list is empty exactly when its own pass's consumed set is empty (a consumed index is only ever recorded alongside at least one placement in the same pass), and `spliceBlocks` over zero placements with an empty consumed set is the identity over the blocks array, so the guard was provably redundant and its mutants unkillable. No behaviour change: the full 4143-test unit suite and the 68 smoke tests pass.

## Measurement

CI cannot measure this package's mutation score: the mutation workflow's documents.js shard times out (#1298) and its pull-request runs are cancelled by newer pushes (#1294). Every number below is a local scoped Stryker run (`stryker run stryker.config.ts --mutate src/odf/odt/read.ts` from `packages/documents.js`) at the config's capped concurrency, cold-measured with the incremental cache moved aside, so none of them is CI-equivalent.

- Baseline on main, before this PR: **95 survived / 15 no-coverage of 218 valid mutants, 49.54% scoped score** (108 killed; 177 compile-error mutants excluded), matching the issue's table.
- With this PR: **0 survived / 0 no-coverage of 203 valid mutants, 100.00% scoped score** (203 killed; 177 compile-error mutants excluded).

`.inputObjects` sets `climateVariables` (since #40) and `rasterToMatchLarge`, but neither was a declared input. SpaDES restores only a module's declared inputs from a cached `.inputObjects`, so on a cache hit both vanished. The Mackenzie relaunch then failed in canClimateData's `Init` with "`.l` must be a list, not NULL" (`purrr::transpose(climateVarsList)`), even though the first run, a cache miss, had worked. A two-module toy reproduced it: correct without a cache and on a cache miss, and missing on a cache hit. Declaring the object as an input fixes that, while canClimateData still leaves `climateVariables` to this module and a user-supplied value still wins.

Both are now declared inputs (and `climateVariables` stays an output). A new test parses `.inputObjects()` and fails if it assigns any `sim$` object that is not a declared input; it found `rasterToMatchLarge`. Full module suite: 43 tests pass locally (2 skipped). Version 1.2.0.9009.

author: singhpratech
body:
Adds `docs/compatibility.json`: for each of the 53 entries, the per-OS result with whatever the cell says beside the verdict, plus the driver quirks the harness actually applies.

The reasoning: verified per-database, per-driver, per-OS capability data for ODBC drivers does not exist anywhere else, and a table only a human can read cannot be consumed by anything else. This makes the project useful to people who never install it.

## Generated, never edited

`scripts/gen_compatibility_json.py` reads `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` and the `DBS` dict in `tests/compat/test_matrix.py`, so the quirks come from the code that runs rather than from prose. Connection strings and fixture plumbing are excluded — local detail, and a published connection string invites copy-paste.

## Two things it refuses to guess, both learned while writing it

**The two tables are in different orders.** Joining them by position put QuestDB's results under Microsoft Access's name. Falling back to matching the entry id against the display name looked safe and was worse: it silently paired `db2` with *"Db2 for i"* and `ibmi` with *"**IBM I**nformix"*, and because each had exactly one candidate, an "exactly one match" check passed both. The mapping is now written out for all 53 entries and asserted to be a bijection, so a row added to one table and not the other fails the build instead of producing plausible nonsense.

**The per-OS totals are counted and then checked** against the 53 / 45 / 48 that `README.md`, `docs/index.md` and the landing page quote. The generator exits rather than emit a figure that disagrees with its source. It also forced me to fix my own result parser: an early version counted macOS at 33 because it only understood `PASS (detail)` and not `PASS (detail) — prose` or `PASS with <driver> …`, while treating `driver unavailable: …` and `server not runnable here: …` as their own statuses rather than failures. With that right, the count matches the published figures exactly.

## Drift protection

CI regenerates the file and diffs it, alongside the existing version-agreement and `rust/csrc` checks. So the data cannot fall behind the table, and a matrix change that would alter the published counts fails the build rather than going out quietly.

`docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` and the README both point at it.

author: thomasmichon
body:
Fixes #3512. Confirmed empirically (many real runs, both directions): GitHub's workflow_run event always reports head_branch as the repository's default branch (main), never the branch that actually produced the triggering run -- even for genuinely successful push-triggered CI runs on dev. This made both validation-gate.yml's branches: [dev] filter and promote.yml's identical filter permanently dead: 0 real Promote executions ever, confirmed via the Actions API.

Fix: drop the unreliable branches: filter from both workflow_run triggers, and instead verify real dev-ancestry with git merge-base --is-ancestor <head_sha> origin/dev in an explicit early gate step/job. Validation Gate gets a new leading gate job whose output every other job depends on; Promote gets an equivalent early step gating its own remaining steps.

Also needs bootstrapping directly onto main (follow-up PR) since workflow_run reads its trigger definition from the default branch, not dev -- same class of issue as the fetch-depth fix in #3519/#3520.

author: eyadsofian
body:
## Why
The physical Windows device remains online for presence while `/v1/media/agent/session` polling stops, leaving Live Now at `TIMEOUT` after sleep. A synchronous named-pipe write during sidecar stop can block its sole media polling thread. A DXGI capture worker can also exit after startup while the sidecar and server still report the session as live. The old updater downloads new versions but waits for an employee to approve a restart and only checks at launch/focus.

## Changes
- Terminate the media sidecar without a potentially blocking pipe write, preserving the kill-on-close job safeguard.

- Install signed desktop updates automatically, restart the app, and check every five minutes as well as on launch/focus. Signature verification remains enabled.
- Repair the deployed synthetic media smoke harness to match the current video-only API.

author: shaurya703
body:
## Summary

On the OpenAI-compatible transport, a 429's `Retry-After` header never reached the retry layer. `provider_error` hardcoded `retry_after_ms: None`, and by the time the error was built the response's headers were already gone: `checked_response` called `response.text()` first. The Anthropic transport reads the header before consuming the body and fills the field from it, so a server-supplied wait was honoured on one provider and silently dropped on the other. Reported downstream as tinyhumansai/openhuman#6504, where this is the managed-backend path.

## Behavior change

- `OpenAiModel::checked_response` reads `Retry-After` before `text()` and passes it into `parse_error_body`.
- `parse_error_body` and `provider_error` take a `retry_after: Option<&str>` and set `retry_after_ms` through the shared `tinyinference_core::parse_retry_after_ms` (delta-seconds or HTTP-date, capped at `MAX_BACKOFF_MS`), the same call the Anthropic transport makes.
- Transport failures (no response) and mid-stream `error` events (no headers) pass `None`, so their errors are unchanged.
- No public API change: both functions are crate-private.

## Verification

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p tinyinference-llm --tests
cargo test -p tinyinference-llm --lib -- providers::openai   # 177 passed
```

New test `parse_error_body_carries_retry_after_into_the_structured_error`: a 429 with `Retry-After: 7` yields `retry_after_ms == Some(7000)`; the same body with no header, or with an unparseable value, yields `None`. The header-present case fails on `main` (`Some(7000)` vs `None`).

author: asadshah7950
body:
### Description of changes

Fixes an issue during PostgreSQL schema synchronization and migration generation where columns with explicit typecasts in their default callbacks (e.g. `() => "'VALUE2'::enum_def"` or `() => "ARRAY[]::enum_def[]"`) or empty array defaults (`'{}'` vs `ARRAY[]`) continuously trigger phantom `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT` diffs on every `migration:generate`.

### Root Cause
1. `PostgresQueryRunner` (lines 4147-4155) strips typecasts when reading column defaults from `pg_catalog` via `/::[\w\s.[\]\-]+/g`, so the database snapshot stores defaults like `'VALUE2'` or `ARRAY[]`.
2. `PostgresDriver.normalizeDefault()` retains the full explicit cast string when the entity default is defined with a function or array representation.
3. In `defaultEqual()`, comparing `"ARRAY[]::enum_def[]"` against `"ARRAY[]"` (or `'{}'` against `ARRAY[]`) always evaluates to `false`, causing TypeORM to flag the column as changed on every run.

### Solution
- In `PostgresDriver.defaultEqual()`:
  - Added a fallback comparison that normalizes explicit typecasts (`/::[\w\s.[\]\-]+/g`) on both sides to align with `PostgresQueryRunner`'s catalog parsing.
  - Handled semantic equivalence between empty PostgreSQL array literals (`'{}'` and `ARRAY[]`) for array columns (`columnMetadata.isArray`).
- Added unit tests in `packages/typeorm/test/unit/driver/postgres-default.test.ts` verifying `defaultEqual` across identical strings, typecasted enum defaults, array typecasts, and genuine diff detection.
