author: grapefruit0205
body:
## Summary

This adds **Click CI**, a GitHub Action and CLI. It skips a test or check command on a pull request when nothing the command read has changed since its last passing run on the default branch. It works for any language and needs no adapter or configuration: you wrap the command you already run.

```yaml
- uses: grapefruit0205/click/ci@<ref>
  with:
    run: pytest -q
```

There are three modes:

- **record** (pushes to the default branch):
  - Runs the command under `strace -f --seccomp-bpf`.
  - `ci/click_ci_trace.py` turns the trace into a per-path state: read, looked up and not found, listed, executed, produced by the run, or changed after being read.
  - A passing run is saved with `actions/cache`. The record holds content digests plus a fingerprint of an allow-listed set of environment variables.
- **select** (pull requests, merge queues, other branches):
  - Digests every recorded input again in the new checkout.
  - Skips only when all inputs and the environment are unchanged. Otherwise the command runs without tracing.
- **shadow**: decides as select would, runs the command anyway, and reports `false_skip`.

**Split by paths.** A whole-suite command reads nearly every source file, so almost any change reruns it. Instead, write `{paths}` where the command takes its test files and give globs:

```yaml
    run: pytest -q {paths}
    paths: tests/**/test_*.py
```

- Record mode observes each group of paths as its own command.
- Select mode runs only the groups whose inputs changed, together in one invocation. When none changed, it skips the step.

Click CI still knows nothing about the runner: it substitutes paths, so pytest, jest, vitest, rspec, phpunit, bats and `go test` packages all work. Each path is its own group up to 32 paths; beyond that, paths go into 32 stable hash buckets, so adding a file changes only its own group. On macOS and Windows the paths are expanded and everything runs.

It fails closed. A record is marked volatile, and the command always runs, when the command:

- changed a file it had read, read a partly written file, or lost an input;
- connected to a non-loopback address, to DNS, or to a local socket it did not create;
- used ptrace;
- left processes running;
- produced a trace line the reducer could not place.

Tracing never decides pass or fail. A command that fails under observation runs again without it. That second result becomes the step result, nothing is recorded, and a warning annotation names the cause. Default-branch pushes always run, so a wrong skip on a pull request shows up when the change merges at the latest.

Limits:

- Linux only, because it needs strace. On macOS and Windows runners the action runs the command unchanged.
- Without `paths`, the command is the unit of skipping; with `paths`, each group of paths is.

## Measurements (local, on this repository)

| Command | Plain | Recorded | Inputs | Decide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unittest tests.test_click_gate_lifecycle` | 4.6 s | 16.5 s | ~440 | ~0.04 s |
| CI partition 4/4, 304 tests, 6,356 processes | ~150 s | 338–367 s | 18,903 (2.2 GB) | 5.8–6.1 s |

- Decide time is the cost of a skip: every input, toolchain included, is read once. It was 8.2–9.0 s before digesting moved to a thread pool. Repository files are checked first, so a pull request that changes a source file stops early.
- On module-sized units, changing `platforms/claude/hooks.json` reran only `test_click_host_coverage`. Documentation-only changes skipped.

Running partition 4 under observation found five problems, all fixed and covered by tests:

1. git's `O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL` index lock was read as a changed input. An exclusive create is now treated as a product.
2. An `execve` called from a non-leader thread (`<pid changed to N ...>`) left two lines unplaced.
3. A process SIGKILLed at a syscall stop showed up as `???( … ) = ?`. That call never ran, so the reducer now ignores it.
4. Click's own observer tests run strace inside the traced command, and the nested ptrace fails. Of three failures under observation, the two caused by tracing passed when run again without it; the third is the known local `rg` failure. `ptrace` is now traced and reported as `nested-ptrace`.
5. npm opens its debug logs as `O_RDWR|O_APPEND|O_CREAT`, which does not say whether the file already existed, so every npm run looked volatile. Such files are now settled after the run by their `statx` birth time. A file born during the run is a product. Anything else, including an unknown birth time, still fails closed.

Commands that run git on the checkout read `.git/HEAD` and the index, which change with every commit, so they always run. The README documents this.

### Click's own suite split by paths: a worst case

This records all 97 test modules as 30 groups, then replays the files changed by each of the last 20 main commits against those records.

- Recording took 2,737 s. That includes unobserved reruns of the groups that failed under observation.
- With no change at all, 22 of 30 groups (96.8% of traced time) still run:
  - 10 groups have no record. 8 of them fail only under observation, because Click's observer tests nest strace. The other 2 also fail without observation because `rg` is missing locally.
  - 6 groups are volatile: nested ptrace, a D-Bus socket, or npm log rotation (fixed afterwards).
  - 6 groups read `.git` metadata.
- The remaining 8 groups skip for most commits. Commits touching 26–49 files rerun everything.

Click is the least suitable repository for this, because its tests run strace, git and npm themselves. These numbers show that selection works, but they do not predict savings for an ordinary project.

The split recording also found two reducer gaps, now fixed:

- npm deletes its oldest `~/.npm/_logs` file on every start. `.npm/_logs` is now ignored like `__pycache__`.
- A killed process can end at `???(` without a resumed line. That call never ran, so it is now dropped.

## Test plan

- [x] `env -u SENTRY-TRACE python3 -m unittest tests.test_click_ci`: 19 tests, covering reducer units, birth-time settling, and a real strace cycle of record → select skip → change → shadow, a split record → select that reruns only the changed file's group, glob/substitution/grouping units, plus a failure that happens only under tracing.
- [x] `tests.test_repository_policy`, `tests.test_repository_shard_inventory`, `tests.test_distribution_validation`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] CI

author: fyliuuuuuu-dev
body:
## 概述

通读 0.3.0 全部源码后修了 5 个网络层问题，按影响排序。每个都是小改动，共 +155/−7 行，新增 4 个测试（20 → 23 项全过，`cargo clippy --all-targets` 无新警告，`rustfmt` 通过）。

## 修复的问题

**1. 接收失败时发送方只能看到"连接已断开"，协议中的失败回执从未生效**

接收方发出 `Reply(accept=true)` 之后如果失败（哈希校验不过、磁盘满、接收中途取消等），只是断开连接。发送方等待 `Receipt` 超时后显示笼统的"连接已断开：对方可能已取消，或网络中断"。协议本身定义了 `Receipt { ok: false, reason }`，发送方也有对应处理分支——但接收方从不发送，这段逻辑是死代码。现在接受之后出错时会尽力把原因发给发送方（`network.rs` 的 `receive_files`）。

新增测试 `the_sender_is_told_why_a_transfer_failed`：坏哈希上传后，原始客户端能读到 `ok=false` 且原因含"校验"。

**2. 单台电脑可以占满全部 8 个接收名额**（0.2 审阅报告"未修改的建议"第一条）

任何局域网设备开 8 个连接就能占住接收服务。现在同一地址最多 3 个并发连接（`MAX_PER_IP`，`serve()` 用一个 `HashMap<IpAddr, usize>` 计数），两个以上设备仍可同时传输，一个 NAT 出口后 3 个也够用。常量可按需调整。

顺带修了 `serve()` 的一个小问题：`listener.incoming()` 持续出错时（如 fd 耗尽）原来会全速热循环，现在错误后暂停 200 ms。

新增测试 `one_address_cannot_hold_every_connection`（覆盖 `admit`/`release` 计数逻辑）。

**3. 顶层符号链接被跟随发送**

`scan()` 用 `fs::metadata`（跟随链接），所以单独选择一个指向文件夹的符号链接时，会被当作真实文件夹递归发送；而 `walk()` 对嵌套链接是跳过的，README 也写明"跳过符号链接"。改为 `fs::symlink_metadata`，顶层链接与嵌套链接行为一致（Windows 上 junction 同理）。

测试 `folders_skip_links_and_system_files` 补充了顶层链接的断言（仅 unix）。

**4. Offer 大小上限偏小，合法大批次会被误拒**

`MAX_OFFER` 为 8 MB，但允许 10 000 个条目、每个路径最长 1 KB——合法请求的 JSON 可达约 10.7 MB，会被"请求内容过大"拒绝，且发送方只看到连接断开。上限提高到 16 MB。

**5. 未读文字无上限，未信任设备可刷屏**

每条文字都会自动接收、弹模态框并把窗口带到最前。局域网内任何设备可以无限叠加弹窗。现在未读文字达到 8 条（`MAX_PENDING_TEXTS`）后带原因拒收新的文字；关掉对话框或信任设备后即恢复。

新增测试 `unread_texts_are_limited`。

## 文档

- README 的工程结构列出了 `localsend/`，但它在 `.gitignore` 中、仓库里不存在，补了一句"仅本地保留，未提交到版本库"。
- `tests/README.md` 与 README 的测试计数同步为 23 项。

## 验证

- Windows 11 x64，Rust 1.98.1（`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`）：`cargo test --release -- --test-threads=1` 23 项全过；`cargo clippy --all-targets` 除基线既有的 23 条 `f32` 推断提示（新编译器对旧代码的 deprecation，与本次改动无关）外无警告；`cargo fmt --check` 通过。
- 未在 macOS 实机验证；macOS 相关路径本次未改动。

## 未改动的发现（供参考）

- **`sender_cancel_while_waiting_withdraws_the_request` 在 Windows 上偶发超时**：全量运行时约 1/3 概率在某个 `wait_for` 处 20 秒超时，单独运行则稳定 0.3 秒通过。**在未改动的 4de9dbc 基线上同样复现**，疑似 Windows 下 `peer_closed()` 的 peek/shutdown 时序问题或测试间相互影响，值得单独排查。
- **仓库没有 LICENSE 文件**（GitHub 也显示无许可）。打包脚本会附带依赖的第三方声明，但项目本身的许可缺失会影响他人使用/贡献。
- **握手总时长没有上限**：10 秒读超时是单次读取的，恶意方可每 9 秒发 1 字节长期占住连接名额（slowloris）。本次的每 IP 限额把影响限制在每地址 3 个，彻底解决需要握手总时限（每连接一个看门狗线程或整体 deadline）。
- 核实过 `open` 5.4.4 在 Windows 上 `that_detached` 走 `ShellExecuteExW`，收到文字里的"打开链接"没有命令注入风险；`first_link` 也已过滤引号与空白。

以上如有不认同的（尤其第 5 条的阈值和第 2 条的限额值），说一声我来调整。

author: xelajr
body:
This follows up on webadderallorg/Recordly#904 for Hyprland/Wayland recording. In the current branch, a failure to load the X11 `uiohook` can also stop evdev capture, leaving mouse clicks unavailable even when `/dev/input` is accessible. Delayed evdev callbacks can overlap and share a buffer, which can corrupt click events.

- Keep evdev capture running when the X11 hook is unavailable.
- Serialize reads per device and retain partial Linux input events between reads.
- Read the 64-bit mouse capability mask without losing low bits to JavaScript number rounding.
- Limit the second countdown to Linux portal recordings and remove temporary debug output.

Validation: `npx tsc --noEmit`, Biome on changed files, and 76 focused tests. I also merged the branch with current upstream `main` locally, resolved its two source conflicts, built a Linux AppImage, ran the packaged-binary smoke check, and passed the full suite (1,410 tests). The desktop app starts in a Hyprland Wayland session, and a direct `j/cursorpos` query matches `hyprctl cursorpos`. Live click capture remains unverified because the test account is not in the `input` group.

author: jcrpaquin
body:
# Search acknowledgements without synonyms
## Why?
The public unfielded search defaults omitted the acknowledgements field, so a term found only in a paper's acknowledgements could not find that paper.

## What?
Add the existing `ack_nosyn` field, which holds literal acknowledgement text without synonym expansion, to the public handlers' unfielded field lists and query field defaults at the existing low boost. An unfielded query for a token found only in acknowledgements can then return the record without synonym expansion across acknowledgement text, avoiding additional clauses that could push the query above Lucene's 2,048 clause limit. Reload Solr configuration; `ack_nosyn` is already indexed, so no reindex is needed.

author: mikesweet23
body:
A recirculating unit (mixed AHU, close-control, room units + ventilation) spilled nothing by default. The spill setting defaulted to **0% of supply**, so every litre of fresh air was reported as a surplus "out via doors/relief", and any heat recovery sat idle with nothing to work against.

Fresh air taken in at the mixing box has to leave again, so the spill now **matches the fresh air by default**: fresh air less whatever the LEV already takes straight out of the room.

## Before / after

Every arrangement was run through `solve()` before and after:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Mixed AHU / close-control / room units + vent | 0 spill, 200 l/s surplus | **200 l/s spilled, balanced** |
| + LEV 150 l/s | 0 spill, 50 l/s surplus | **50 l/s spilled, balanced** |
| + LEV 300 l/s (more than the fresh air) | 100 l/s shortfall | 100 l/s shortfall, still flagged (it's real) |
| + plate heat recovery | idle, heater 29.0 kW | **working, heater 24.4 kW** |
| Fresh-air-only | balanced | unchanged |
| Spill typed in (% or fixed) | as set | unchanged |

Results without heat recovery are unchanged, because spilling room air does not change the mix. The heater drop with recovery matches a hand check (0.26 kg/s × 26 K × 0.65 ≈ 4.4 kW).

## Solver
- One `spillOf()` rule replaces two duplicated expressions and an unused helper whose "balance" branch was wrong for any fresh-air basis other than % of supply.
- **"Matches the fresh air"** is the default and first option. "% of supply" and "Fixed rate" stay as overrides for a unit that genuinely spills a different amount, or none.
- Fresh-air-only units already balanced (supply less LEV) and ignored the spill setting, so those controls are now hidden for that arrangement.

## Saved projects
- Schema 4. A save from before this change that still carries the old untouched default (0% spill) opens on "Matches the fresh air". Any spill that was actually set is kept, as is anything saved from now on.
- `CALC_VERSION` is now `1.7.0-guided`, since results change.

## Reporting
- The balance checks spell out fresh in, spill (and how it is set) and LEV. The shortfall check says how much fresh air closes it.
- The **"Do this" fixes depend on the situation**. When the LEV exceeds the fresh air, the fix is more fresh air (linking to Airflow), not "spill less", since the spill is already zero. When recovery is idle because the LEV takes everything, it suggests a run-around coil on the LEV discharge. A `FIXMAP` section may now be a function of the result.
- The ladder's "Extract make-up" said it replaced the spill too; it only ever used the LEV.
- The equipment table notes how the spill is set, and the room label reads "spill + LEV match fresh air".
- Hints that quote results are refreshed after each solve, so they no longer lag one keystroke behind. This also fixes the reheat-duty hint.

## Verification
Headless Chromium, no JS errors:
- Solver matrix across all arrangements, LEV cases, recovery, warm-up and each spill override (table above).
- Check text, "Do this" advice and the section each finding links to, for the balanced, shortfall, surplus and idle-recovery cases.
- Fresh-air-only hides the spill controls.
- Save migration: a schema 3 save on 0% moves to matched; schema 3 saves with 10% or a fixed rate are kept; a schema 4 save on 0% is kept.

author: maxwellb13
body:
Generation recurses on kind: one function makes a column of any dtype, the scalar path handing a plan to the engine, a List wrapping the column its elements make, and a Struct gathering the columns its fields make -- each by calling back into itself. So a Struct generates, and with it a List(Struct), a List(List), an Array(Struct) and a struct of either, as deep as the dtype goes. The list of lists the roadmap said was waiting on the struct decision fell out of making it.

A field is drawn by the code that draws a column of its dtype, from what fields says or its dtype alone, and is seeded under its parent by name: renaming a struct column keeps every field, adding a field beside one moves nothing, and a struct is a window under batching and a scan like any other column. A field is never null -- a null cell is the whole struct -- which is the rule a List's elements already followed.

test_roundtrip.py no longer lists the dtypes that cannot be generated, because there are none; it asserts that every dtype in the coverage table, nested both ways two levels deep, round-trips. The roadmap section that said coverage was incomplete says it is complete, and records the question it answered.

author: agentydragon
body:
Cilium matches a `toFQDNs` rule only against addresses its DNS proxy saw a name resolve to, and the proxy only sees queries covered by a DNS rule (`toPorts.rules.dns`). A policy with `toFQDNs` egress and no such rule validates and applies, but allows nothing. google-mcp's calls to Google timed out for exactly this reason until #7820 added the rule.

- **`cilium.network_policy()`** now raises `ValueError` when a policy's egress has a `toFQDNs` rule but no DNS rule, so the mistake fails manifest generation instead of reaching the cluster.
- **`test_cilium`** covers both shapes that must fail (plain port-53 egress, which was google-mcp's shape, and no DNS egress at all) and three that must pass (`dns_egress(resolves=["*"])`, `fqdn_fence`, and a policy with no FQDN rules).

Every policy in the tree already pairs the two rules. Regenerating the manifests produced no diff.

**Deviation from what I offered:** I suggested making `egress_to_fqdns` emit its own DNS rule. Every caller already pairs its FQDN rules with one policy-wide `dns_egress(resolves=["*"])`, so that would only add a redundant per-host DNS rule to each generated policy. The check gives the same guarantee without changing any manifest.

The check requires the DNS rule to be in the same policy. Cilium itself would also accept one from another policy selecting the same pods, but no policy here relies on that.

author: aterrylu
body:
## What & why Terry: *"I type into an agent CLI, nothing happens, it keeps saying Connected, and it only flips to Disconnected after a while."* After trying revision 1 at the live gate: *"12s is a little bit too long… Maybe the gate should be when I type but the server isn't receiving it? Even 5s might feel too long."* **Revision 2 does exactly that.** Every keystroke is acknowledged by the server once it has been written to the agent. The pane knows **~1s after your first unanswered key**, with no heartbeat timeout to wait out. Measured on an isolated rig (own port and config dir, real Claude Code and Gemini agents, a pausable TCP proxy for true half-open links; never :3100, exact-PID kills only): | Failure | Before | Revision 2 (live) | |---|---|---| | I type, the server isn't receiving it | **Connected, forever** | **"Not reaching server… · N keystrokes waiting" at 1.28s**; give up at 3.1s; the abandoned keys **never reach the agent** | | Hung agent (SIGSTOP) | green "Connected" + "Ready" **forever** | subtle **"Waiting for agent…" at ~2s**, then **"Agent not responding · Ns" at ~5s**; status bar stays Connected (truthfully) | | Server stall / half-open link | red after **15.6s / 33.7s**; the terminal socket **never closed** | status bar **"Reconnecting… last heard 5s ago" at ~5s**, "Disconnected · retrying" at 20s; the pane already flagged it at 1s; recovery in ~0.03s | | Keys typed during an outage | **delivered as a late burst** (double-submit) | counted and shown; **never delivered late** | Healthy baseline (the false-positive budget): at load avg 23–47, idle and mid-turn, **ack p99 ≤ 31ms and first-echo p99 ≤ 67ms**. Every threshold sits 15–30× above that. Decision record: **ADR-113** (`docs/decisions/`). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant P as Pane (xterm) participant S as Server participant A as Agent PTY P->>S: binary [0x01][seq][sentAt][key] S->>A: pty.write(key) S-->>P: binary [0x02][seq] (ack, p99 ≤ 31ms) A-->>P: echo (text frame, p99 ≤ 67ms) Note over P: no ack at 1s → "Not reaching server… · N waiting"
no ack at 3s → give up: counted NOT sent, reconnect
acked, no echo 2s → subtle "Waiting for agent…"
acked, no echo 5s → "Agent not responding · Ns" Note over S: frame older than 2.5s → dropped, never written, never acked
(below the 3s give-up, so a given-up key can never land late) ``` ## How - **Acked input, capability-negotiated.** The pane asks with `?inputAck=1`. A server that supports it adds `;input-ack=1` to the end-of-replay OSC 7777 marker. Only after that does the pane send keystrokes as binary frames `[0x01][u32 seq][u32 sentAtMs][utf-8]`, and the server acks `[0x02][u32 seq]` **after** `pty.write` succeeds. Terminal bytes stay in text frames both ways. - Old server + new dashboard: never asked, so the pane uses the plain text path plus the revision-1 `/io` watchdog. - Old dashboard: never asks. - A negotiated socket treats binary as ack frames **only**. A malformed or unknown frame is dropped and logged, never typed (found live, see Validation). - **Nothing new on the text channel**, because unknown JSON there falls through to `pty.write()` on older servers. - **No late keystrokes.** The server refuses frames older than 2.5s (below the pane's 3s give-up), so a key the pane has reported "not sent" can never be written later. This also closes revision 1's stated residual: a stalled *server process* writing keys when it resumes. Two further server mechanisms stay: a superseded-socket **fence** (`?client=&gen=`) and a **WebSocket protocol-level ping** (1s; terminate after 4s of silence, with a fresh deadline after the server's own stall). - **Status bar = heartbeat, tighter.** `/ws/agents` pings every 2s (was 30s before this PR). Stale at 5s → "Reconnecting… last heard Ns ago"; 20s → "Disconnected · retrying". A stale socket is abandoned and replaced at once, because `close()` on a half-open socket never fires `onclose`. - **"Waiting for agent…" is deliberately quiet** (Terry): same box and position as the loud chips (no layout shift), gray dot, muted text, no border or shadow. It usually resolves on its own. - **Kept from revision 1:** typing is never blocked, and keys the pane can't carry are counted and shown (Esc/Ctrl+C included; mouse and focus reports excluded). The agent chips are suppressed while the agent is at a permission prompt (`needs_input`) and enabled only for providers measured to echo while busy (Claude Code 2.1.281, Codex 0.154.0, gemini-cli 0.46.0). The pre-existing replay bug (xterm re-answering scrollback queries, e.g. `1;2c` typed into gemini's prompt) stays fixed via the OSC 7777 marker. **Stated plainly:** when only the browser→server direction dies, the server's liveness ping closes the socket ~3s in. A key typed later than ~2s into that stall therefore goes straight to "Connection lost", and its notice says "**may** not have been sent", because a socket closed under a key younger than the give-up can't prove the key never landed. Measured: pause at t, keys at t+2.37s, "lost" at t+3.03s. **Mixed versions:** a new dashboard against an older server (30s heartbeat) would cycle "Reconnecting". This is accepted because the dashboard is served by its own server. ## Screenshots — real dashboard, isolated rig, real Claude Code agent **Revision 2** (crops: the pane's top-right chip, plus the prompt and status bar): | State | Dark (Void) | Light (Daylight) | |---|---|---| | **Server not receiving** — 1s after the first key; status bar truthfully Connected; the prompt got nothing | | | | **Agent slow** — subtle "Waiting for agent…" at ~2s (no border, no shadow, no alarm color) | | | **Unchanged from revision 1** (same wording; only the timings above changed): | State | Dark (Midnight) | Light (Daylight) | |---|---|---| | **Link lost** — status bar | | | | **Link lost** — pane | | | | **Recovered** — pane notice (8s) | | | | **Hung agent** — "Agent not responding · Ns" | | | ## Testing / Validation **CI-equivalent:** every push went through the lefthook pre-push gate, which runs the exact CI (biome check + `make check`). One run hit a flaky gate; the immediate re-run passed. **New tests (mutation-verified RED):** - **Server** (`terminal-input-fence.test.ts`, 22 tests): frame decode; the age drop (a frame older than 2.5s is never written and never acked); ack only **after**

author: sjawhar-agent[bot]
body:
The Go daemon's Agent Sandbox runtime could launch the Stage 4a stub on production, but not the pods a real tree needs. Those pods had no way to reach a model without a provider key. Two trees could share a node sized for one. An operator's `$(…)` or `$$` in the prompt reached the agent altered. A failing watch left `Probe` answering Alive from a frozen store. This PR makes the runtime ready for real agents, and makes their Oh My Pi reach models through the gateway alone.

**This PR carries three tasks of LEGION-208 Stage 4b, and its squash commit lands all three:**
- **Task 4b.7:** the Sandbox runtime changes described below.
- **Task 4b.10, #1297:** a pod's Oh My Pi reaches its models through the gateway alone, and the image probe proves it with a model round trip.
- **Task 4b.10b, #1301:** a repository's own Oh My Pi settings cannot unpin a pod's gateway route.

#1297 and #1301 were approved on their own PRs and merged into this branch (they were stacked on it). This branch was then rebased onto `main`; the rebase also adds one `install-omp` action for CI, `cd7fe0da`. The last commit, `1f1f9a98`, fixes what the review of the combination found; see "Review of the combination" below.

## What changes (Task 4b.7)

- **Model gateway (C6, decision 1).** `sandbox.Options.Gateway{URL, Audience, ServiceAccount, TokenExpiry}` is required, and `TokenExpiry` must be at least 10 minutes. `gatewayTokenVolume(Gateway)` returns the one projected `serviceAccountToken` volume and its read-only mount at `/var/run/legion/gateway`. Every worker pod runs as `Gateway.ServiceAccount` and mounts that volume in the worker container only. The worker container is told `LEGION_MODEL_GATEWAY_URL`. `automountServiceAccountToken` stays false.
- **One tree per node (decision 2).** Every tree pod has a required pod anti-affinity against pods whose `legion.dev/tree` label is set and differs from its own. It sits beside the existing affinity to the pod's own tree. The NodePool's `instance-cpu Gt 3` floor (agent-c #20006, live) sizes the node, so the Stage 4a harness drops its `instance-cpu` selector.
- **Refusals in `configure`.** `configure` refuses any configured `legion.dev/pool` key, and any tree volume size that is not positive. The runtime's own 20Gi fallback is gone; the config supplies that default.
- **Prompt text.** Every `$` in each container's command and literal env values is doubled. The kubelet's expansion then hands the process the text as written.
- **Failing watch.** Each informer now lists and watches through a wrapper that records each request's outcome. While either store's latest request has failed, `evaluate` answers Uncertain. It answers from the store again once a request succeeds. The watch-error handler could not do this: client-go retries a refused watch without calling it.
- **Orphan sweep.** The sweep leaves Sandboxes labelled `legion.dev/probe` alone. I corrected the header comment in `probe.go` (4b.10's file) to match.
- **Carried cleanups.**
  - The root check is `claim.IsTreeArchitect`.
  - Secret keys are named once; `prepare` keeps only the one check that can fire; the boot token is one of `l.secrets`; `launch.repo` is gone. These are from #1284's quality pass.
  - `ensureSandbox` returns no `created` flag, the resume path is translated once, and `stopGracefully` is inlined. These are #1264 N4.
- **Stage 4a harness.**
  - It is split into four files, and one ordered check table drives the run.
  - Its internal copies are gone (#1271 item 3).
  - It decodes the App key with the new `config.DecodePrivateKey`, which `resolvePrivateKeySecret` now uses too. That is a small commit in `internal/config/stage3.go`, which Main approved.
  - A new `gateway-token` check reads the root pod's token into memory. It asserts the token's audience, subject and lifetime, and that no API-server token is mounted.
  - `concurrent-provision` also asserts that the second tree runs off the first tree's node.

**Pending: a follow-up PR, 4b.7b.** The Stage 4a script and its README change in a small follow-up PR, not here. I open it once this PR and Task 4b.11a (`legion/LEGION-208-4b-e2e-lib`, which moves the lib the script uses) have both merged. It drops the script's own `case "$from"` list. The harness already refuses a bad entry point, and the list lacks `gateway-token`. It also fixes `scripts/e2e/README.md` lines 310-311 and 353-357 for the removed instance-cpu selector, updates the `no-affinity` and `concurrent-provision` rows, and adds a `gateway-token` row. Until then, a development run with `STAGE4A_FROM=gateway-token` is refused by the script's list. A full run is unaffected.

## Contract change census

The boundaries this tightens are `sandbox.Options` (new required `Gateway` and `TreeVolume`, `Scheduling.NodeSelector` may not set `legion.dev/pool`) and the pod shape (`serviceAccountName`, a projected token volume, the pod anti-affinity).

Searches:
- `rg -n 'sandbox\.Options|sandbox\.New\(|configure\(' packages/daemon-go`
- `rg -n 'NodeSelector|instance-cpu' packages/daemon-go scripts docs`
- `rg -n 'serviceAccountToken|automountServiceAccountToken' packages/daemon-go`
- agent-c `meta/infra/pulumi/components/legion/__init__.py`, the `legion-sandbox-pods` policy validations (the plan's agent-c search)

Hits:
- There is no production caller yet; 4b.8 wires the daemon.
- The unit rig (`testOptions`) and the live harness (`startRuntime`) are updated here.
- `probe_test.go:420` sets a `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` node selector. It does not name the pool key, so the refusal leaves it alone.
- `probe.go` builds its own pod and is not affected; 4b.10 mounts the helper there.
- The e2e README and docs/solutions `instance-cpu` lines: the docs/solutions doc is updated here, and the README goes in follow-up PR 4b.7b.
- agent-c's `legion-sandbox-pods` refuses the projected token until Task 4b.1 amends it.

- **The later `Gateway.URL` refusal:** `configure` refuses a URL that `modelroute.AnthropicRoute` refuses. The reviewer re-ran the caller search: the unit rig, the golden options, and the live harness's production URL all pass the check.

Rollout: immediate refusal. No deployed daemon runs the Go sandbox runtime; its only caller before 4b.8 is the live harness in this PR. The pool-key refusal closes a real hole: a configured selector would have replaced the pool that agent-c's admission policy requires.

## Verification

All by the implementer on the devbox:

- **Red first** for each behaviour: pool key, tree volume, gateway pod shape, anti-affinity, `$` expansion, the probe surviving the sweep, and the failing watch. Each new test failed before its change and passed after. The expansion test showed `$$`→`$` and `$(LEGION_ISSUE)`→`LEGION-208` before the fix. The watch test answered Alive for 10 s with every list and watch refused.
- **`go test -race ./internal/runtime/sandbox/`:** ok.
- **CI recipe at `189c6d8e`** (then `7fc0f2f8`, the simplify pass: a constant moved and three comments rewrapped; sandbox unit tests and `go vet -tags e2e` re-run green):
  - `go vet -tags e2e ./...`: clean.
  - `go test -count=1 ./...`: every package ok except intake, admit and workflow, whose NATS test-container tests time out at about 31 s on the loaded devbox Docker. Rerun with `-p 1`, admit and workflow pass. Three intake tests still time out, and each passes alone. None of those packages is touched here.
  - `bash scripts/e2e/stage1-skeleton.sh`: `stage 1 e2e: PASS`.
- **GitHub CI at `189c6d8e`:** green. `daemon-go` passed (run 35979998878), as did `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `pr-title` and `changes`.
- **`config.DecodePrivateKey` on the real key:** it decoded the real stored implement-App key to an RSA PEM that parses as a private key.
- **Stage 4a live proof on production at `68f89462`: `stage 4a e2e: PASS`, all 21 checks** ([issuecomment-5825746849](https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1293#issuecomment-5825746849)). It ran on image `ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker@sha256:1f547c64

author: andrewgodowsky-aoa
body:
Record: `docs/implementation/2026-09-24-h08-durable-controls.md`.

## What shipped
- **One control contract.** It is revision `2026-09-24.1` of the work-control contract, additive only, so `WORK_CONTROL_CONTRACT_VERSION` stays 1.
  - Six distinct commands: `steer`, `queue`, `stop`, `resume`, `retry` and `fork`.
  - **Replay:** the same command id with the same payload returns the same receipt, including after a restart. The same id with a different payload gets 409 `control_command_conflict`.
  - Controls share the project's command namespace with Work starts. Work a control starts gets the derived id `<commandId>:work`, so a restart mid-control replays that start instead of making a second one.
  - Every control, refusals included, leaves an append-only `ControlReceipt`. It records who asked and when, the target, the route answer it was judged by, the outcome (applied, queued, refused with a code, or uncertain), who performed it (Diomedes or the route's engine, never a model), the result, the lineage, and the checks re-run.
- **Capabilities decide what's offered.** `workControlProfile()` reads the same route contract as H04's `sessionControls`.
  - The server enforces it and the Console offers only what the route supports.
  - `DurableControls.registerDriver()` is the seam where H03 and H05 plug in their native Steer, Resume, Retry and Fork.
  - A "host" steer is presented as Queue, and labelled as a queue.
- **Semantics.**
  - Retry and Resume are blocked while an approved write is pending, conflicted or otherwise unconfirmed.
  - Resume re-checks route, consent, permission, model and source versions, and refuses if the thread's permission is now wider than the stopped run had.
  - Fork creates a new task and thread that refer to the origin run. The fork starts at "Show me first" and starts no run, and the origin's records are unchanged.
  - Each run now records its inputs at admission (`Session.inputs`). Runs admitted before this change are refused for Resume and Retry, with that said.
- **Console.**
  - `RunControls` sits in each run's record: Stop while the run is live, with only the scopes the route supports; Resume, Retry and Fork once it has settled. Resume and Retry ask once before sending.
  - Steer and Queue both live in `FollowUpQueue`.
  - The Stop options menu works by keyboard.
  - Receipts appear in the thread timeline, and fork receipts link to the other side of the fork.
  - The Run inspector lists all six controls and adds a Lineage row.

## Tests
- `tests/h08-durable-controls.test.ts` (12, over real HTTP)
- `tests/h08-control-profile.test.ts` (7)
- `tests/h08-durable-controls.spec.ts` (2 Playwright). One covers all six controls on the test-mode fixture route, including Resume by keyboard and Fork navigation. The other covers the sample route, which offers only Stop and Queue.

## Gates (worker's final run, Linux, main merged)
- tsc: clean
- vitest: **6418 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed**
- vite build: ok
- Playwright ui + native-ui + field + h08: **38 passed**

## Known gaps
- No provider route offers Steer, Resume or Fork on Work runs yet. Real routes get Queue and Stop everywhere, and Retry everywhere except sample. The rest is proven on the test-mode fixture until H03 and H05 register their drivers.
- H04's kept-session endpoints and conversation turns are not yet folded into receipts.
- Control receipts are not validated fail-closed on load.

## Open questions for Andrew
Two new `QUESTIONS.md` entries are proposed:
- Should Resume and Retry keep their confirmation step? (Whether a click runs an action or selects it is Andrew's call.)
- May a person acknowledge an uncertain effect and retry anyway?

author: klponce
body:
## Summary

First step toward a deployable v0.1: the runner base image and the template provisioning scripts, plus two worker fixes found along the way.

### `images/runner-base/` (Packer)
- **Contents:** Ubuntu 26.04 cloud image, pinned to a dated release and its SHA-256, plus `qemu-guest-agent`, the `runner` user (UID 1001, passwordless sudo) and apt background updates switched off.
- **What it doesn't include:** the runner and toolset come from the template build, so a new runner release needs only a template rebuild.
- **Size:** about 1.1 GB compressed, with an 8 GB disk.

### `images/ubuntu-26.04/` (run by `parcon template build`, next PR)
- **`10-runner.sh`:** `actions/runner` 2.337.0, pinned by checksum, in `/opt/actions-runner`. It writes the job environment (`ImageOS`, tool cache) to `.env` and creates `/home/runner/work`.
- **`20-par-runner.sh`:** the one-job units.
  - `par-runner.path` waits for `/run/par-runner/jitconfig`, which `tmpfiles.d` creates at boot, root-only.
  - `par-runner.service` hands the file to `runner` and passes the config in `ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG`, never on a command line.
  - It deletes the file, runs one job, and powers the VM off when the runner exits for any reason.
- **`30-minimal-tools.sh`:** native Docker (buildx and compose), git, build tools and Python.

### `images/common/cleanup.sh`
Shared by every image. It resets the machine ID, SSH host keys and cloud-init state, and removes the Packer build user on first boot.

### Fixes
- **`ciupgrade=0` on workers.** Proxmox's cloud-init upgrades every package on first boot by default, which would delay every job.
- **`agent=1` on workers**, set explicitly because the controller reaches them only through the guest agent.
- **Runner work folder** is `/home/runner/work` (`github.WorkFolder`), as on GitHub-hosted runners.

### Dev container
Adds QEMU, OVMF and xorriso, passes `/dev/kvm` through, and caches Packer plugins and downloads in the cache volume, so image builds run locally.

## Test plan

- [x] `local-test.pkr.hcl` builds the base image, boots it, runs every template script twice to prove they are idempotent, and passes all checks:
  - the runner user, sudo and docker group
  - the runner installed and owned by `runner`
  - the path unit enabled and waiting
  - the JIT directory root-only
  - Docker working for `runner`
  - no systemd ordering cycles, `ssh.socket` listening, and the build user gone
- [x] The same test runs the one-job flow with a stand-in `run.sh`: the config reached the runner as `runner` through the environment, and the file was deleted before the job started
- [x] `shellcheck`, `packer fmt -check` and `packer validate` pass
- [x] Go: build, `go test -race ./...`, vet (including `-tags integration`), gofmt, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), rebased on #7
- [ ] On a real node, via `parcon template build` (next PR)

Local builds caught five bugs before this PR:
- an `ssh.socket` ordering cycle that removed SSH from every image
- a trap referring to an out-of-scope variable
- `install /dev/stdin` failing when a script ran a second time
- the path unit not being started in the build VM
- `sudo -E` being ignored by `sudo-rs` on Ubuntu 26.04

author: fatihakdag
body:
Picking the jet calls one in from a random edge. It makes one fast pass
(5.5-6.5s to cross; the helicopter takes 9-14) and leaves by the far side
without turning back. FIRE, while it is over the field, drops a stick of
three bombs that leave with the jet's speed and fall under gravity and
wind, so the drop has to be led well ahead of the target.

The jet flies a route on the match clock like the helicopter: announced
once in a new `jet` message, carried in `turn`, its result and every
snapshot, and met by a shot at the shot's own time. It stays up after
its drop, so the next seat can shoot it; a shot-down jet keeps most of
its forward speed, holds the turn until it lands, and crashes through
heliCrash, crushing a tank it comes down on.

The protocol goes to 4 in both the game and the relay. The desktop
panel's weapon row now shares its width so seven buttons stay on one
line.

## 概要

`X-<Brand>-*` 自称ヘッダ検出に新たに 3 族を追加:

- **D815 敷金・原状回復精算印**: `X-Shikikin-*`/`X-Genjoukaifuku-*`/`X-Genhuku-*`/`X-Depositrefund-*`/`X-Securitydeposit-*`/`X-Moveoutclean-*` 等 51 印。敷金・原状回復業者の偽装 (退去後の過剰精算請求・ハウスクリーニング代金を装ったなりすまし) の兆候を検出。
- **D816 礼金・更新料印**: `X-Reikin-*`/`X-Koushinryou-*`/`X-Koushin-*`/`X-Renewalfee-*`/`X-Keymoney-*`/`X-Moveterms-*` 等 51 印。礼金・更新料業者の偽装 (契約更新手数料・礼金分割請求を装ったなりすまし) の兆候を検出。
- **D817 孤独死・特殊清掃印**: `X-Kodokushi-*`/`X-Tokushusouji-*`/`X-Tokushuseisou-*`/`X-Biohazard-*`/`X-Hazardcleanup-*`/`X-Crimesceneclean-*` 等 51 印。特殊清掃業者の偽装 (消毒・消臭費用・残置物処分料を装ったなりすまし) の兆候を検出。

賃貸審査 (screening 機)・立ち退き (tachinoki 機)・家賃保証 (chintaihoshou 機)・遺品整理 (ihinseiri 機)・消臭 (shoushuu 機) は既存族で検出済みのため別テーマに差し替え。cross-family prefix 衝突・シャドウ 0 件を検証済み。

各族は `Envelope` への `<brand>_marks` フィールド、`has_<brand>_marks` 検出関数、`commands.rs` での `render_risks` 兆候報告の 3 点セットで実装。

## 変更タイプ

- [x] セキュリティ修正 (脆弱性対応)

## DRI 確認

このPRは以下のモジュールに影響します:

author: vshekhawat-hlab
body:
## Summary

`RotaryEmbedding.forward_xpu()`'s fallback-kernel branch (used when `head_size` is not in `[128, 256, 512]`) calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding(positions, query, key, self.head_size, self.cos_sin_cache, self.is_neox_style)` without slicing to `rotary_dim` first. That compiled kernel asserts `rotary_dim == head_size` internally and raises:

```
RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size
```

for any model with partial rotary embeddings (`rotary_dim < head_size`). This affects GPT-NeoX-style architectures with `partial_rotary_factor < 1.0` on XPU (e.g. `adept/persimmon-8b-chat`, `microsoft/phi-2`, `stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b`, `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t`, `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b`), independent of the `--attention-backend` choice (`triton` or `intel_xpu`), since rotary embedding dispatch is keyed on device type (`is_xpu()`), not attention backend.

The fix adds an `elif self.head_size != self.rotary_dim` branch that falls back to `forward_native()`, which already implements generic partial-rotary math correctly (splitting `query[..., :self.rotary_dim]` / `query[..., self.rotary_dim:]`). This mirrors the existing pattern where `forward_cpu`/`forward_npu` already fall back to `forward_native` for their own unsupported cases, and the aligned-head_size branch of `forward_xpu` itself already slices to `rotary_dim` before its fused call.

## Test plan

Hardware-validated on Intel XPU with the patched build, running a 20-example accuracy smoke check per model (server + client, real GPU):
- `adept/persimmon-8b-chat` (intel_xpu backend, gsm8k) — passed, no crash
- `microsoft/phi-2` (triton backend, gsm8k) — passed, no crash
- `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (triton backend, hellaswag) — passed, no crash
- `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b` (triton backend, gsm8k) — passed, no crash

All four previously failed with `RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size` on this code path; all four now serve and produce results after the fix. `stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b` hits the same root cause and is also fixed by this change.

author: cjhwong
body:
## Why

A running server keeps the code it started with. The installer replaced the files, then found the old server healthy, printed "server already warm, nothing to do" and left it running. An upgrade kept the old rules until the server died. A server in another mode was only reported.

On one machine, a server started by hand as `uv run pii-server.py` from the hooks directory kept the old rules for five days after an upgrade.

## What changes

- `install.sh` stops the server on the port before the pilot run. It finds the server by the script name and the port (`pii[-_]server.py ... --port $PORT`), so it also finds a server started by a relative path. A server on another port is left alone.
- It waits up to 10 s. A server that does not stop is reported with its pid, not killed harder, and the pilot is skipped.
- It stops the server with `--no-pilot` too, so the next hook call starts the new code.
- A server that answers on the port but cannot be found by name is reported, not killed.
- `pgrep` joins `curl` and `jq` as a required tool. It ships with macOS and Linux procps.

The "already warm" and "mode mismatch" messages are gone. Their two tests are replaced.

## Verified

- 282 offline tests pass, 7 of them new for this change. `install.sh` has full line coverage and a clean shellcheck.
- A plain `curl | bash` install from this branch, with no manual stop, on four machines: two Apple Silicon Macs in `redact-torch`, one in `redact-torch` with a server started by hand by a relative path, and a Linux box in `rules`. On each, the old server stopped, a new one started from the installed path, and the hook script gave the right answer in all 8 prompt cases.

author: kurtlieber
body:
## Summary

Adds a Keep open switch at the bottom of the Super+K card. It is meant for a multi-monitor setup: open the guide on a secondary screen, turn the switch on, and leave it there as a reference while you work on the main screen.

With the switch off, the guide behaves as it does today. It still opens beside the bar icon at the same size, click-away and the other-monitor click catchers still dismiss it, Esc follows the current rules (a typed search clears on the first Esc, and the next Esc closes), and running a shortcut still closes the card. The 2.5-second reload is unchanged.

With the switch on, that same card stays where it is:

- Clicks outside the card reach the apps underneath, and the keyboard is released so you can keep typing on the other monitor.
- Clicking the card focuses it. Esc then closes it with the same rules as today.
- The Esc badge, Super+K, and this bar icon still close it.
- Other bar menus open and close on their own and leave the guide up.
- Running a shortcut from the card still runs it, and the card stays open.
- The context tab keeps following the focused window, and the 2.5-second reload keeps running while the card is visible.

The switch is mouse-only, starts off, and lasts only for this opening. Closing the card clears it. Nothing is written to settings, and the card does not become draggable.

Omarchy's shell popup has no API today for turning off its full-screen click catchers. The pinned state is a workaround until, and unless, the shell grows that capability: while the switch is on, this same card is shown on a card-sized layer at the same position. Until the switch is turned on, the guide still uses the existing popup.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open the guide and click outside it. It closes, as it does today.
- [ ] Run a shortcut with Keep open off. The card closes, then the shortcut runs.
- [ ] Turn Keep open on from the secondary monitor's bar icon. The card stays put, and clicking the main monitor focuses the app there.
- [ ] Click the pinned card and press Esc. A typed search clears first. The next Esc closes the card.
- [ ] With the card pinned, open another bar menu. The guide stays up.
- [ ] Run a shortcut from the pinned card. The shortcut runs and the card stays open.
- [ ] Change the focused window. The context suggestions follow it within the existing refresh.
- [x] Close the card and open it again. Keep open is off.

author: wesleysmits
body:
Feature 4 proposed marking a message as read, but Spark's available Done action archives a message by ID and does not accept a mailbox selector or conditional thread version.

This PR brings the proposal and approval work into `main`, changes the action to Spark `markAsDone`, and connects a guarded local execution path. A person proposes one selected message, approves the exact proposal, then confirms execution separately. The server checks the current Inbox and thread, stores its own approval and a durable receipt, sends one ID-only Spark command, and confirms the result from Archive and Inbox. Uncertain attempts cannot be retried automatically. The action endpoint requires loopback and a literal local host with a matching Origin, and is disabled by default.

**Validation:** TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Fallow, 1,336 local tests, 304 Storybook tests, and production build passed. The safety review's two findings on host validation and receipt wording were fixed and rechecked.

**Limit:** Spark Desktop did not answer the read-only probe in this session, so no live mailbox action or provider readback was performed. The command acts by message ID; another visible copy may change, and a new message may arrive between preflight and action. Enable `SPARK_DONE_ACTIONS_ENABLED=1` only for an approved local test message.

Model and harness: GPT-6 in Codex desktop, with a Sol implementation agent and a Luna safety review agent.

body:
Fixes the 14.4.0 startup hang and closes #12.

- **Startup hang (all platforms).** The starting and ready MaterialApps shared a navigator key, so the ready app inherited the spinner route. Only the ready app takes the key now. New `integration_test/app_startup_test.dart` starts the real app and requires it to reach its first screen; it fails on 14.4.0 and passes here, on Windows and on an Android emulator (play flavor).

author: obusk
body:
## What and why

This PR fixes audit findings **H1**, **M3** (the options part), **L2** and **L3**.

### H1: CPU DoS via `diffFiles` globs
libnpmdiff compiles every `diffFiles` pattern with minimatch, brace expansion included, for every tarball entry, and it does this synchronously. The auditor measured `{a,b}` repeated 17 times at about 120 s for a small package. The new `parseDiffOptions` (`src/lib/query/parseDiffOptions.ts`) now rejects input before `npmDiff` runs when:
- there are more than **10** patterns
- a pattern is longer than **256** characters
- a pattern's brace expansion has more than **64** alternatives. This is computed with `braceExpand(pattern, { braceExpandMax: 65 })`, which caps the expansion work, so the check stays cheap (under 1 ms) even for hostile input.

Braces are still allowed (`{lib,dist}/**` works). Patterns are never dropped or rewritten, only rejected. `minimatch@^10.2.6` is added as a direct dependency. That version was already in the lockfile through libnpmdiff.

### M3: unvalidated option values
- `diffUnified` must be an integer from 0 to 100. `parseNumber` no longer uses `parseInt`, so `3abc` gives `NaN` instead of `3`, and invalid values are rejected rather than coerced.
- `diffSrcPrefix` and `diffDstPrefix` can be at most 64 characters.

### L2: invalid input returned 500
- New shared helper `parseParts` (`src/lib/utils/parseParts.ts`). It decodes (page only), splits, validates specs and runs `versionsToSpecs`, and it returns `null` instead of throwing.
  - API: returns **400** `"Invalid package spec"`.
  - Page (`generateMetadata` and `DiffPageInner`): calls `notFound()`.
- The same options helper is used by both entry points.
  - API: invalid options return **400** with a short message.
  - Page: invalid options render an `ErrorBox` ("Invalid options" plus the message) instead of throwing, because production would redact a thrown message.
- Registry not-found while resolving specs:
  - API: **404**.
  - Page: `notFound()`.
  - Other errors still return 500.
  - `canonicalSpec` is a `"use cache"` function, and in production an error thrown across that boundary loses its `code` (I confirmed this on a local build: the caller only saw the redacted error with a digest). So the E404/ETARGET check now happens inside the cached function, which returns `null` and caches that for `minutes`. A thin non-cached wrapper then throws `SpecNotFoundError`, which the route and page check with `instanceof`.

### L3: query strings rebuilt without encoding
- The page's canonical redirect and `goToDiff` on the landing page now use `URLSearchParams`, via `toSearchString`. Each value of an array gets its own `append`.
- The API redirect uses `append` instead of `set`, so repeated keys are kept.
- The API now reads repeated `diffFiles` params as an array (`fromSearchParams`), matching the page. Before, only the last value was used.
- `ViewTypeSwitch` rebuilt its link with `Object.fromEntries(searchParams)`, which dropped repeated `diffFiles`. It now copies the `URLSearchParams` and `set`s the view type.
- `ExamplesList` needed no change: it uses Next's `href` object, which already encodes and keeps arrays.

`parseQuery` is no longer exported from `^/lib/query`, so callers go through the validated `parseDiffOptions`.

## Judgment calls
- The limits above (10 / 256 / 64 / 0–100 / 64) are the ones suggested by the audit. Real-world `diffFiles` filters are far smaller.
- On the page, options are validated before the canonical redirect. A URL with invalid options shows the error right away and does not redirect first.
- A single version with no package (`/1.0.0`) now gives 404 on the page as well, because `versionsToSpecs` runs as part of validation. Before, the page tried to treat it as a catalog page for a package named `1.0.0`.

## Verification
- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run test-ci` (190 tests), `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build` all pass.
- New unit tests:
  - `parseDiffOptions`: the malicious brace pattern is rejected in under 500 ms; legitimate braces, the default glob and the boundary values for every limit are covered.
  - `parseParts`: malformed parts, bad percent-encoding, version-only input.
  - `searchParams`: encoding, arrays, round-trip.
  - `isRegistryNotFoundError`.
  - `canonicalSpec`: E404 and ETARGET both give `SpecNotFoundError`.
- Manual check against a production build on port 3201, before → after:
  - `/api/a...b...c`: 500 → **400**
  - `/api/1.0.0`: 500 → **400**
  - `/api/nope-xyz-123@latest...nope-xyz-123@1`: 500 → **404** (`Could not find "nope-xyz-123@1"`)
  - `/api/semver@^999...semver@7.6.3` (ETARGET): **404**
  - `/api/semver@7.6.0...semver@7.6.3?diffUnified=-5`: 200 with malformed hunks (`@@ -1,-5 +1,-3 @@`) → **400**
  - `?diffUnified=abc`: 200 → **400**
  - `?diffFiles={a,b}×7`: 200 → **400** in about 6 ms
  - `?diffFiles={classes,functions}/**`: still **200** with a diff
  - `/api/semver@7.6.0...semver@7.6.3`: still **200** with a diff
  - Page `/nope-xyz-123@latest...nope-xyz-123@1`: server-component error (redacted) → not-found page
  - Page `/a...b...c`: not-found page
  - Page `?diffUnified=-5`: renders "Invalid options: diffUnified must be an integer between 0 and 100."
  - Page `/semver@7.6.0...semver@^7.6.1?diffFiles=a%26b`: redirect target was `?diffFiles=a&b` → now `?diffFiles=a%26b`
  - Repeated `diffFiles`: both values are kept in the page and API redirects (the API redirect used to keep only `b`).
- Still open: `/%E0%A4%A` still returns a plain-text 500. Next's own server fails to decode the path before our code runs, and nothing is logged from the app. The `decodeParts` call in `parseParts` is now wrapped, so our code no longer throws, but this particular response comes from Next itself.

author: daiviksg
body:
Fixes #31746
While typing an album description, any upload that finishes into the album triggers a refresh of the album from the server. The description textarea was bound directly to `album.description`, so the refresh replaced the unsaved text with the saved (old) value.

`AlbumDescription` now edits a local `$derived` copy of the description, the same pattern `AlbumTitle` already uses. A refresh that returns the same saved description leaves the local edit untouched. On focus out, the change is saved only if it differs from the saved value, and the bound description is updated from the server response.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added a unit test to `AlbumDescription.spec.ts`: type into the textarea, re-render with the same saved description (simulating the refresh), and assert the typed text is kept. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- [x] Existing `AlbumDescription` tests pass.
- [x] `svelte-check` reports no errors in the changed files.
- [x] Manually reproduced the upload scenario in the running app.
Link to video of manual test is here

body:
## 问题

线上实测发现：在设置页或成员 API 里批准后，申请人的挂起消息没有被处理。

原因是 Next 路由 bundle 和长连接所在的 instrumentation bundle 不共享模块实例，重放处理器只在后者注册。结果 `decideMember` 在路由里领取了挂起消息，却没有处理器可以重放，消息就丢了，还给申请人回了一句「正在处理」。

## 修复

- 路由里（没有重放处理器）批准时，只改成员状态，挂起消息原样留在库里。
- manager 每 15 秒对账时，对 approval 模式的 bot 调用 `replayDeferredApprovals` 补做重放。
- 卡片、私聊命令、对账三条路径共用 `replayClaimedPending`，靠原子领取保证同一条消息只重放一次。

## 验证

- access 测试：25/25 通过，新增 2 个用例：
  - 没有重放处理器时批准，挂起消息保留；
  - 两路对账并发时只重放一次。
- 全量测试：561 pass / 5 fail，5 个失败均为存量问题，与本次改动无关。
- tsc：0 错误。

body:
## 무엇을 바꿨나

### 1. 내용 (커밋 8cd02d1)
- **"왜 Wearless인가요?" 자리를 새 섹션으로**: "의류 쇼핑몰에 최적화된 이유". 카드 세 장(옷은 실제와 가깝게, 색상은 한 번에, 문구는 확인한 정보로만)과 FaceMarket 안내 띠. 헤더 "주요 기능" 메뉴가 쓰는 `id="features"`는 그대로.
- **사용법**: 앱의 실제 네 단계(사진 올리고 확인하기, 컷 구성 고르기, 의류 재현도 높이기, 에디터로 수정하기)에 맞춘 문구와 앱 화면 조각. 근거 없던 "올리고 3분이면" 문구 삭제(생성만 실측 4~5분).
- **요금제**: 카드 아래 긴 안내 세 문단을 "해지 전까지 매월 자동으로 결제돼요." 한 줄과 환불 조건 링크로. 제공기간 부제(토스 PG 심사용)와 요금 카드는 그대로, 전문은 앱 `/pricing`과 환불 페이지에 있음.
- **폰트**: `globals.css`가 가리키던 `/fonts/PretendardVariable.woff2`가 저장소에 없어 실서버에서 404, 기본 글꼴(윈도우는 맑은 고딕)로 나오던 문제를 앱과 같은 파일(OFL)로 해결.
- 기존 가운데 영상(`real demo 2.mov`, HEVC 코덱이라 일부 브라우저에서 검은 상자)은 새 섹션에서 쓰지 않음. 파일 자체는 남겨 둠.

### 2. 모바일 가독성 (커밋 4178af0)
여러 폭(360, 390, 430) 캡처를 섹션별로 점검한 스펙 28건과 새 섹션 조정. **768px 이상은 바꾸지 않음.**
- 768px 미만 전역: 한글 단어 중간 줄바꿈 금지, 제목은 줄 길이를 고르게, 문단은 마지막 줄 한 단어 방지 (`globals.css`의 `@layer base` 안)
- 첫 화면: 제목을 "상세페이지에 / 시간 쓰지 마세요."로, 폭마다 13~15px로 줄던 부제를 15px 고정, 모바일에서 `min-h-screen` 해제
- 통계: 640px 미만에서 3열 대신 가로 행 목록(11px 글자 폐지)
- 섹션 제목 32px/1.3, 부제 16px/1.6, 섹션 세로 여백 `py-16 sm:py-24 md:py-32`
- 후기 인용 16px, 요금 카드 빈 공간 정리, 문의 카드와 FAQ 안쪽 여백 축소
- 메뉴 버튼, 로고, 푸터 링크, 이메일 링크 터치 영역 44px 이상
- 푸터 주소 번지와 호수(98-2, A-4호)가 하이픈에서 끊기지 않게

## 검증
- `npx tsc --noEmit` 오류 0, 바뀐 파일 `eslint` 오류 0, `pnpm build` 성공 (전체 `pnpm lint`의 기존 오류 8건은 `_mockup`, `ui/sidebar.tsx`, `wearless-survey-3-6.jsx`로 이번 변경과 무관)
- 헤드리스 크롬 360, 390, 430 폭: 가로 스크롤 0, 단어 중간 끊김 없음
- 데스크톱 768, 1024, 1440 폭: 기존 섹션 높이가 전후 동일(요금제만 안내 문단 축소로 짧아짐)
- 실제 아이폰 사파리는 아직 미확인. 이 PR의 Vercel 미리보기를 휴대폰으로 보고 머지 권장

## 확인이 필요한 것
- 데스크톱에도 단어 단위 줄바꿈을 걸지(1024 폭 후기 카드에 "다양 / 하게" 끊김 있음). 지금은 모바일만.
- 문의 섹션 "무료로 시작하기" 버튼 글자가 ghost 변형 스타일 때문에 회색으로 나옴(기존부터).
- 로컬에만 있는 `codex/wearless-black-brand` 브랜치가 `hero-section.tsx` 섹션 여백 줄과 `Header.tsx` 로고, 메뉴 버튼 줄을 같이 고쳐, 나중에 합치는 쪽에서 충돌 정리가 필요.

author: detail-app[bot]
body:
Closes #1503

## What this does

A `login_failed` audit row gets its org domain from the email passed with it. A row without one is excluded by the `email_domain IN (...)` filter that `/api/v1/org/audit-events` and `/admin/audit` apply, so org admins never see it.

- **Deactivated browser login.** `lookup_and_verify_authenticator` now returns `LookupError`. Its `Deactivated { email }` variant carries the credential owner's email: the asserted `user_handle` matched that owner, so the refusal row lands in the owner's org feed. `UserMismatch` and `NotFound` still record no email, because the assertion has not run and the handle is caller-supplied.
- **CLI `vouch login` refusals.** Browser login and the FIDO2 assertion grant both call `services::auth::record_lookup_failure`. The grant previously wrote no row for an unknown credential, an owner mismatch, or a deactivated owner. It now writes the same row as browser login, and the response is still a generic `invalid_grant`.
- **Key rename and removal.** `/v1/keys` and `/enroll/keys` take the audit email from the user loaded by `load_active_user` instead of the token's `email` claim. A token minted without the `email` scope has no such claim.
- **Revocation.** A revoked human token with no `email` claim takes the email from the user record for its `Logout` row. M2M tokens are unchanged.
- `TestSessionSpec` gains a `scope` field for minting tokens without the `email` scope.
- `docs/src/admin/organizations.md` lists `vouch login` among the audited deactivated-login refusals.

## Tests

- Browser login: a deactivated owner's row is found by a domain-scoped query; a mismatch row has no domain.
- FIDO2 grant: the same two cases through `/oauth/token`.
- One test drives all four key rename/delete endpoints with an `openid`-only token and finds every event through a domain-scoped query.
- RFC 7009: revoking an `openid`-only token records a domain-scoped `Logout` event.

Each production change was reverted on its own and its test failed. `make lint` is clean; `make test` passed 6,028 tests, 0 failures.

body: ## Summary A designed HTML email digest of repo activity, sent daily or on demand (**Repo Pulse → Send digest now**), with grouped sections, priority chips in the Kanban palette, 2-4 data-derived recommended actions, and an "all quiet" variant. Nothing about the sync interval or the Activity/Log tabs changes; this only adds capability alongside them. Closes #14 ## Changes - `src/lib/EmailDigestBuilder.js`: `buildDigestHtml(rows, recommendations, meta)` → `{ subject, htmlBody, plainTextBody }`; inline-styled nested tables, no images/CSS blocks/JS, 600px, `bgcolor` fallbacks for Outlook - `src/lib/DigestData.js`: the window (since the last *scheduled* digest, 24h default, 7-day cap), the Shipped / In motion / Needs attention selection, and data-derived recommended actions - `src/lib/GeminiClient.js`: `generateDigestInsights` returns the headline **and** 2-4 actions from **one** call (refactored onto a shared request path; `summarizeActivity` and its call site are unchanged); same retry and model fallback - `src/lib/DigestPrompt.js`, `DigestRecipients.js`; popup text in `SyncSummary.js` - `src/gas/EmailDigest.js`, `Menu.js` ("Send digest now"), `Triggers.js` (`installDigestTrigger()`, a daily trigger separate from the sync trigger), `Config.js`; a **DigestLog** tab records each send - Docs: `docs/features/email-digest.md`, ADR 0003, ARCHITECTURE component table and data model, README, the `html-email-digest` skill (corrected), and `PHASE5_INSTRUCTIONS.md` ## Deviations from the phase file (please review) - **`MailApp`, not `GmailApp`.** Google's reference says `GmailApp` needs `https://mail.google.com/` (full mailbox access); `MailApp` needs only send-as-you. body:
The live shop stayed on “Searching…”. Two causes:

1. A later successful action republished the previous once-Cap continuation. Boot then resubmitted a spent search Cap, and the page treated any once error as the buy button being spent.
2. The browser peer stored the timer continuation and never submitted it. The Cap was already minted. Submitting it is not a mint.

A success now publishes only the continuations that handling minted. `handle_event` still sees the earlier row. The peer arms `timer.fired` and submits the pre-minted Cap.

Live check after the fix: search for gadget shows 1 hit, add and buy-once work, checkout places the order and clears the cart. Layer check, continuation tests, phase 2, and hardening passed.

author: yasen-posthog
body:
## Problem

- People who read the audit log cannot tell which changes a scout or another sandbox agent made, unless they open each row.
- Layer 1 (#105745) records the request IP for those changes. The IP locates the sandbox, not a person, so showing it like a person's IP misleads.

This is layer 2 of 3, on top of #105745.

## Changes

- The User column tags a sandbox change "via sandbox", beside the client tag. A scout run already shows "via scout <name>" there, so it gets no second tag.
- The IP address column shows a dash with an info icon for sandbox and scout changes. The tooltip says the change used a token that PostHog issued for a sandbox task, and gives the request IP.
- The copy names the token binding, not the request origin. A sandbox token can leave the sandbox, so the row cannot prove where the request came from.
- Rows without a sandbox task look the same as before.
- A row counts as a sandbox change only when it carries a task id, which only the server's token binding writes. An agent intent without a task binding does not count.
- The handbook and internal docs describe the new display.

author: clauszy
body:
## Overview

Add support for the laya multilingual decision model.

Laya is a non-autoregressive "System 1" decision model (mmBERT/ModernBERT encoder + a typed decision head) that answers typed questions (`choice` / `score` / `noul`) over arbitrary state in a single forward pass, with no text generation. This PR:

- adds a model converter (`conversion/laya.py`) for the laya-multilingual checkpoint, the gguf-py LAYA arch definitions (tensor names, KV keys, tensor mapping and writer extensions), and registers `LLM_ARCH_LAYA` with the modern-bert model class reuse so `llama-quantize` can recognize and quantize the model;
- adds a self-contained inference runtime under `tools/laya/` (following the `tools/mtmd` layout) that loads the GGUF directly and builds the encoder + decision-head graph with ggml, plus a `llama-laya-cli` that answers `choice` / `score` / `noul` questions from a `state` + `questions` JSON input;
- adds verification under `tests/laya/`: golden fixtures (zh/en, no brand or entity names), GGUF tensor checks, quantization precision-protection checks, inference precision regression (F16 and Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M/Q8_0 vs the PyTorch reference), performance/stability benchmarks and an end-to-end script.

## Additional information

- Laya is non-autoregressive: there is no text generation, so it is not reachable through the `llama-cli` generation path; `llama-laya-cli` is the entry point.
- `tools/laya` is self-contained: it links `ggml`/`llama`, loads the vocabulary and merge rules from the GGUF tokenizer data, and ports the mmBERT Metaspace pre-tokenizer + byte-level BPE (llama.cpp's GPT-2 pre-tokenizer cannot reproduce this vocabulary). It does not modify core inference files or `include/llama.h`.
- Quantization keeps `token_embd`, all LayerNorms, `type_emb`, `scorer` and `act_head` tensors in F16/F32.
- Verification results: F16 scorer-logit deviation <= 0.13 vs the PyTorch reference; `choice`/argmax agrees with the PyTorch reference for F16 and all quantization tiers on every test case.

body:
## Summary

`skills/kizuna/SKILL.md` had 697 lines and repeated most of its references. It now works as a short router of 144 lines, and the details live in the references. Closes kizuna-onc and completes the epic kizuna-5da.8.

## What SKILL.md keeps

- the unchanged frontmatter with the activation description
- the core workflow with one example: register, build, resolve, scope, dispose
- a table for choosing a registration, a table of lifetimes, and a link to the ownership table in `lifecycle-guide.md`
- the rules that the old "Common Mistakes" section taught, one line each
- a routing table from each task to its reference

## Where the rest went

| Former SKILL.md section | Now in |
| --- | --- |
| Interface, factory, and multi-registration patterns | `registration-patterns.md` (already there) |
| Borrowing, including the interface-token example and the domain-boundary note | `registration-patterns.md` |
| Request scoping | `scoping-and-middleware.md` (already there) |

No information was removed. The package ships the new reference file (`npm pack --dry-run`).

- The Express snippet in `SKILL.md` called `scope.dispose()` in `res.on('finish')`. The scoping reference uses `disposeAsync()` with a rejection handler. The snippet is gone, and the rules route to the reference.
- `scoping-and-middleware.md` said sync disposal of async cleanup "does not await". Sync disposal also reports a `TypeError` in its `DisposalError`, so the sentence now says so.

- A `register*()`/`add*()` conflict throws `RegistrationConflictError` at the second registration. The moved example said "at build time".

author: timappbusiness-lgtm
body:
Signing up gets fast without giving up verification. The paperwork moves to the moment it pays off: sending an offer, publishing a route or seeing a contact. Every required document stays, and every upload now survives interruptions. **No database rule, verification requirement, mask, quota or guard changed.** The one migration adds an optional column (`vehicles.platform_slots`, 1–15).

## Done

**Part 0: ANAF autofill**
- The CUI is looked up as soon as its control digit is right. Filled fields are marked „Date preluate de la ANAF" and stay editable.
- Every failure is shown in the form: a typo, not found, or ANAF unavailable. Manual entry always works.
- Inactive and struck-off firms get a warning.
- `verify-cui-anaf` changes:
  - `map.ts` holds the mapping, with Deno tests. Struck-off is read the way ANAF actually writes it.
  - A `reason` on every answer that is not a company.
  - A `keep_details` mode, so the ANAF snapshot is saved when a firm is created. The inactive-firm guard in `submit_company_for_review` now has data to check.
- `scripts/ci/check-anaf.sh` runs as a report-only job.
- Finding: the function answers in production. `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is not set, but that does not cause a failure, because the app calls the function from the server.

**Part 1: carrier journey**
- Sign-up asks for name, e-mail, phone and password, then lands on the board. A banner there says what is next.
- `carrier-journey.ts` mirrors `company_can_act()`.
- `ActionGate` sits on offers, routes and contact reveals. It takes the person through the firm, vehicles and documents with `?pentru=&next=`, then back to where they were.
- The firm form uses ANAF. Vehicles need only plate, type and car slots.

**Part 2: one documents screen**
- `/cont/firma/documente` covers every requirement for the firm and each vehicle (`?vehicul=` narrows it to one vehicle).
- Each requirement has a drawn example, a one-line reason and the camera first. The carrier sees a thumbnail with progress and confirms the date the model read.
- A gallery upload can take several files at once. The model recognises each one and the carrier confirms it.
- Progress reads „X din Y încărcate". `submit_company_for_review` is unchanged.
- Staff get a 15-minute signed link to the file, and see the declared date next to the date the model read.

**Part 3: files survive interruptions**
- `useUploadQueue` covers every upload: documents, logo, request photos, driver photos, message images.
  - Files are kept in IndexedDB until the server confirms them. Limits: 15 MB per file, 80 MB in total, 7 days.
  - `UploadLine` shows each file's state.
  - A retry goes under an id chosen on the device, so nothing is stored twice.
- `/api/incarcare/[tip]` handles the re-encoded photos, with upload progress. It is idempotent and checks the Origin header.
- A message's text goes out under a kept id, and its images follow one by one.
- `docs/16-continuitate.md`: the limitation is closed. CLAUDE.md continuity rule 7 is updated.

**Part 4: client path**
- Signed out: the last step no longer asks for the name, phone and e-mail that the account form asks for anyway.
- Signed in: the phone comes from the account.
- Optional fields sit in boxes that say what they hold.
- Visible fields: 29 → 19. Nothing is typed twice.

**Part 5: `docs/17-viteza-inscriere.md`**
- Screens, fields, taps and minutes, before and after.
- The signed-out parts were walked in a browser on both builds. The signed-in screens were counted from code.
- Minutes are computed with the keystroke-level model (KLM).
- Also covers where people stop, and proposes rule changes without implementing them.

## Bugs found and fixed, each with a regression test
- A message sent again after a lost answer hit the repeated-message guard, and its images never went. Fixed with a client-kept message id.
- The upload started a few ms before the file was in IndexedDB, so a tab closed in between lost the file. The full browser suite caught this under load. Covered by a unit test plus `incarcari.spec.ts`, 96/96 at 8 repeats.
- The documents picker let through any `image/*`, which registration then refused after the upload. Fixed with `documentFileProblem()`.
- Registration counted any primary-key clash as its own earlier attempt. It now checks that the row belongs to this firm.
- Client and request form fixes:
  - The client typed name and phone twice.
  - The account phone was never prefilled.
  - The ANAF snapshot was never saved.
  - „RADIERE" was never matched as struck-off.

## Tests
- **Unit:** 1916 passing.
- **Deno:** 144 passing.
- **Database:** `db:test` passes, with all RLS checks and the 9 security guards.
- **Playwright, full suite locally:** 1307 passed, 0 failed. The 713 skipped need Supabase.
- **CI:** green on `7abdb3a`, including e2e with `/proba/incarcari`. That page exists only with `E2E_HARNESS=1`, which only `playwright.config.ts` sets.
- **Written but not run here:** `inscriere-rapida-supabase.spec.ts`, which needs a database.

## Remains
- Run the `-supabase` specs against a database.
- A person with a stopwatch: the 10-minute script in the report.
- Optional hygiene: set `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` on `verify-cui-anaf` to the production origin.

author: sitnas
body:
## Contesto
Revisione di sicurezza sulla gestione dei dati personali. Ho provato attacchi reali contro il backend: isolamento tra clienti, IDOR, ruoli, CSRF, injection e enumerazione dal tablet.

## Esito
Tutto in regola tranne un punto:
- **Isolamento tra clienti:** solido. Sessione, token del tablet e codice di associazione di un cliente vengono respinti su un altro (verificato con header Host reali in modalità subdomain).
- **Autorizzazioni / IDOR:** un receptionist non vede né liste, né dettagli, né file, né cancellazioni di sedi non sue (403). Accesso senza login: 401.
- **CSRF:** le richieste che modificano dati senza l'header dedicato vengono respinte.
- **Injection:** ricerca con `%`, `_`, `\` e payload SQL: nessun errore né sovra-corrispondenza (query parametrizzate + blind index).
- **VULNERABILITÀ TROVATA — enumerazione dei presenti:** in "Sto uscendo", cercando prefissi di cognome di 2 lettere e iterando l'alfabeto, un tablet (o chi ne rubasse il token) poteva ricostruire l'intero elenco delle persone in sede ("Cognome I."). Corretta in questa PR.

## Correzione
- `api/src/kiosk/kiosk.service.ts` (`findOpen`): un prefisso di cognome che corrisponde a più di 5 presenti non restituisce **nulla**. Così un prefisso generico non rivela nessuno; il visitatore digita più lettere o usa il codice del badge (percorso principale, invariato).
- `api/src/kiosk/kiosk.dto.ts` e `web/src/kiosk/CheckOut.tsx`: lunghezza minima della ricerca per cognome da 2 a 3 caratteri.
- `api/src/kiosk/kiosk.controller.ts`: limite su `/kiosk/visits/open` da 30 a 15 richieste al minuto.
- `docs/SICUREZZA-PRIVACY.md`: descrizione aggiornata.

## Verifica
- Prima: uno sweep di prefissi rivelava 4 nomi su 6 presenti. Dopo: **0 nomi rivelati**.
- Ricerca di 2 lettere: respinta (400). Cognome intero ("gialli") o prefisso specifico ("gia", poche corrispondenze): trova la persona. Percorso col codice: invariato.
- Typecheck e build di API e web senza errori.

author: komediruzecki
body:
## What this does

Two fixes with one cause. UI state changed inside a view transition's update callback, and the browser runs that callback only once it has rendered a frame.

1. **The export dialog closes when answered** (`Modal.tsx`). While an export ran, the answered export dialog stayed modal over the export tracker, and its Close did nothing. Close was a second answer, and `respond` ignores a second answer while the first is still waiting for its frame. `respond` now resolves and takes the dialog down at once, and the tracker shows the export. Found during the glass-panels work (#126, `docs/plans/glass-panels.md` section 8).
2. **The toggles change state at the input.** These each set state inside a transition:
   - F and the sidebar button;
   - Ctrl+D;
   - the timeline toggle;
   - the draw mode, colour init and point init selects.

   Each now sets its state in its handler.

What goes is the 250 ms root cross-fade on these changes and on a dialog closing. The dialog's fade-in on open stays.

## Measured

Headed Chromium 148, AMD RDNA 4 over Vulkan, on the hidden agent workspace, where rAF runs at about 1 Hz, so frames count and milliseconds do not. Each site was measured idle and during two 4K ultra offscreen image exports:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| input to state change | 1 frame (1.1 to 4.0 s here) | the input's own frame |
| a click during the transition, 3 to 6 frames | received by `<html>`, lost | reaches its target |
| timeline toggle clicked twice, 150 ms apart | toggled once | toggled twice |
| `drawMode` right after the change event | the old value | the picked value |

Adding `pointer-events: none !important` to `::view-transition` and all its pseudo-elements changed none of this. Keeping the fade with that rule was therefore not an option.

## Relation to lib/viewTransition and #131

- Main routes every transition through `lib/viewTransition` (a37f4b88, 14545b77). After this PR, nothing calls its `startViewTransition`. `viewTransitionCallers.test.ts` still stops a direct call from coming back.
- This leaves two things with nothing to act on: the render driver's present after a transition, and #131's Apple WebKit branch. This PR does not delete them, because #131 edits the same files. That is a follow-up decision.
- #131 also edits the same lines in `Modal.tsx`, `docs/audit/project-conventions.md` and the EARS spec. Whichever of the two lands second needs a rebase.
- `viewTransitionPresent.test.tsx` still passes. Its dialog no longer starts a transition, so its two cases now check the same thing.

## Tests

- `ExportPngDialog.close.test.tsx` (new):
  - Export Image closes the dialog at once, and the tracker shows the job.
  - Close, Cancel and Escape each close the dialog while an export renders.
- `Modal.back.test.tsx`: the dialog and its back entry go at the answer.
- `useWorkspaceShortcuts.test.ts`, `FloatingActions.test.tsx` and `RenderSettingsSection.modes.test.tsx` (new): each toggle changes state at the input.
- Every one of these stubs `document.startViewTransition` with a stub that never runs its callback, which models a renderer that has not drawn a frame yet. jsdom has no `startViewTransition`, so the earlier tests all ran the fallback branch. That is how this went unnoticed (`docs/agent/MISTAKES.md`).
- Each new test failed before its fix. `pnpm check` is clean, and the app suite passes: 345 files, 3861 tests, 4 skipped.

`MainWorkspace.tsx` lost an import, so its line ratchet is lowered to 4542.
