author: ruyteer
body:
## Depende do #58

Este PR foi rebaseado sobre `fix/pagamentos-confirmacao` (#58) — por isso o
diff inclui os commits dele até o #58 ser mergeado em `prd`. **A parte de
comissão SyncPay que estava aqui antes foi descartada**: o #58 já resolve
isso corretamente via `split_snapshot.feeCents`, calculado uma única vez na
criação do PIX (`gateway-clients.ts`, percentual enviado de fato ao gateway) e
reusado na confirmação — recalcular um percentual novo no webhook (como a
versão anterior deste PR fazia) usaria uma base que nunca foi enviada ao
gateway. Esse ajuste de comissão de indicação (valor retido vs. taxa nominal)
é uma decisão separada do dono do produto, fora deste PR.

## O que ficou: timeout nas chamadas aos gateways de pagamento

Os `fetch` para SyncPay/BuckPay/NexusPag/WiinPay não tinham timeout algum. Na
prática isso não travava "pra sempre" — o `fetch` nativo do Node (undici)
desiste sozinho de uma conexão parada depois de ~300s —, mas era tempo demais:
este fluxo roda dentro do handler de uma assinatura pubsub **at-least-once**
(`runner-process-update`, ver `services/runner/runner.ts`), e estourar o
prazo de ack faz o Encore reentregar o evento e reprocessar a compra inteira
do zero.

`services/payments/application/gateway-clients.ts`:

- **Orçamento por OPERAÇÃO, não por chamada HTTP** (`GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS =
  20_000`): a SyncPay encadeia até 3 chamadas numa única operação de cash-in
  (token, ensureWebhook, cash-in); um timeout por chamada isolada somaria bem
  mais que o orçamento pretendido. `runWithGatewayTimeout` cria um único
  `AbortController` compartilhado por operação e só limpa o timer no fim —
  inclusive depois de ler o corpo da resposta (`res.json()`/`res.text()`),
  não só depois dos headers (senão uma leitura de corpo lenta ficava sem
  proteção nenhuma).
- **`ensureSyncpayWebhook` não bloqueia mais o cash-in**: o cadastro do
  webhook só precisa existir antes da confirmação chegar (quando o PIX for
  pago), não antes do PIX ser gerado. Agora roda em paralelo, com seu próprio
  timeout independente, e nunca lança (trata os próprios erros).
- **`fetchChargeCreation`** loga quando a chamada que CRIA a cobrança falha —
  se foi por timeout, o gateway PODE já ter criado a cobrança do lado dele
  sem a gente ter recebido a resposta (não tem como recuperar esse PIX órfão
  daqui; é só pra diagnóstico se aparecer uma cobrança "fantasma").

`services/payments/application/create-pix-with-fallback.ts`:

- **Teto pra cadeia de fallback inteira** (`GATEWAY_CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS =
  24_000`, abaixo do prazo de ack do pubsub at-least-once acima): cada
  gateway tentado usa o que sobrar desse teto (até `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS`), e a
  cadeia para de tentar mais gateways se o teto já estourou — sem isso, uma
  cadeia de 2 gateways que os dois travassem gastaria até 2x
  `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS` somados (40s).

## Testes

`services/payments/payments.test.ts` (`pnpm exec vitest run
services/payments/payments.test.ts` — 73 testes, todos passando):

- Um teste por provider (syncpay/buckpay/nexuspag/wiinpay) provando que um
  gateway sem resposta rejeita com erro claro em vez de travar o handler
  (fake timers restritos a `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` — não fingem
  `Date.now()`, usado pelo cálculo do teto da cadeia — com
  `vi.waitFor(timer agendado)` antes de avançar o relógio).
- `createPixWithFallback`: gateway travado cai pro próximo da cadeia.
- Ajustei o teste de registro automático do webhook da SyncPay pra dar um
  tick vazio depois do `createPix` (já que `ensureSyncpayWebhook` roda em
  paralelo agora, sem `await`).

Confirmei a regressão manualmente: revertendo o timeout, o teste trava de
verdade e o worker do vitest precisa ser morto (não termina sozinho).

`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`: sem erros (fora os `Cannot find module
'~encore/...'` esperados do ambiente). Suíte completa: 596/597 passando — a 1
falha (`simplified-funnel.test.ts` dedup de PIX) é pré-existente e não
relacionada (funil simplificado, não toca nos clientes de gateway).

## Riscos

- `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS`/`GATEWAY_CHAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` são escolhas de compromisso
  (20s/24s); se algum gateway legitimamente responder mais devagar que isso
  no cash-in, passa a cair pro próximo da cadeia (ou falhar, se for o
  último) antes do que fazia antes (nunca) — comportamento pretendido, vale
  observar no Railway após o deploy.
- `ensureSyncpayWebhook` rodando em paralelo (sem `await`) significa que, numa
  janela bem estreita, o cash-in pode retornar antes do cadastro do webhook
  terminar — não deveria importar na prática (o webhook só precisa existir
  quando o PIX for de fato pago, alguns segundos/minutos depois), mas é uma
  mudança de timing a observar.

author: hjryoo-ai
body:
## 요약
`OutboxLeaderLockIT.리더의_세션이_죽으면_서버가_락을_푼다` 의 경합을 닫는다.

- **증상**: 2026-09-24 #60 의 CI(`libs/messaging` 과 무관한 변경)에서 `expected: LEADER but was: FOLLOWER` 로 한 번 실패했다.
- **원인**: 타임아웃 없는 `pg_terminate_backend(pid)` 는 신호를 **보냈다**는 것만 말하고 곧바로 true 를 돌려준다. PostgreSQL 문서: "returns true whether the process actually terminates or not". 그래서 바로 다음 `lead()` 가 아직 살아 있는 백엔드의 advisory lock 과 경합한다.
- **수정**: `pg_terminate_backend(pid, 5000)`(PG 14+)로 바꾸고, true 인 행만 센다. 프로세스가 실제로 사라졌을 때만 true 다. 사라지지 않으면 기존 전제 어설션(`죽인 백엔드 = 1`)이 이유와 함께 실패한다.
- **검사하는 것은 그대로다**: 「TTL 을 기다리지 않고 바로 이어받는다」. 기다리는 것은 백엔드의 죽음이지 락의 TTL 이 아니다.

## 검증
- 수정 전 main 에서 로컬 12회 반복: 0회 실패. **재현 시도했으나 실패**했고, 근거는 CI 1회 관측과 문서의 의미다.
- 수정 뒤 클래스 전체 로컬 5회 반복: 통과.
- `:libs:messaging:check` 통과.

author: arihantk15
body:
> **Stacked on #797** (which is stacked on #795 and #793). Merge in that order; retarget to `master` as each lands.

## What
The Flash review summary comment gets a collapsible **Blast radius** block: which other files import what this PR changes, direct and indirect, plus a one-line "nothing else imports the changed file(s)" when that is true. Computed from the import graph in the scan evidence with the engine's existing `find_blast_radius`. **No model is involved and nothing is guessed.**

```
Blast radius: 13 other file(s) depend on what this PR changes (12 directly, 1 indirectly)
- `adapters/base.py` is imported by `adapters/anthropic_native.py`, `adapters/claude_code.py`, ... (+7 more)
- `query.py` is imported by `cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`
Indirectly affected: `dashboard.py`
```
(rendered from Aletheore's own scan evidence)

## Design decisions
- **Exact-commit evidence only.** It reads the scan recorded for the PR's own `head_sha` and never the "latest evidence for the repo" fallback the review prompt path allows, because that can describe another branch and a wrong import graph would be a confident wrong answer. `run_pr_scan_job` and the review job run independently, so if the exact scan has not landed yet the section is omitted and appears on the next review of that PR.
- **Works for Flash.** `run_pr_scan_job` runs for every non-free plan on each PR event (Flash included): it clones the base and head into a temp dir, scans, stores the derived evidence keyed by `head_sha`, and deletes the clone. The blast radius reads that stored evidence, so it needs no extra clone and no AIR subscription.
- Files already in the PR are not counted as affected; lists are capped; imports only (dynamic imports, reflection and non-code references are not seen, and the comment says so). A changed file the scan does not know (docs, config) produces no claim at all.
- Cost: no LLM call, one small DB read. Failure-proof: any exception returns "" and never affects the review.
- On by default; `FLASH_REVIEW_BLAST_RADIUS=off` is the kill switch.

## Not in this PR
- Symbol-level "confirmed callers" (needs file contents at review time), and a graph or layered view like CodeRabbit's Change Stack. This is the small first version.
- Privacy note for anyone extending this: the GitHub App does send source code to our servers (privacy.html says so); PR clones are temporary, a working copy is kept between scans for repeatedly-scanned repos, and derived evidence is stored long-term.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_blast_radius_summary.py`: 12 passed (direct/indirect, files already in the PR excluded, nothing-imports-it line, caps, unknown files, malformed evidence never raises, exact-head-sha only and the latest-evidence fallback is never consulted, kill switch, missing evidence, DB failure)
- [x] `test_jobs` + `test_flash_review`: 592 passed
- [x] Rendered against Aletheore's own real scan evidence (output above)
- [ ] Not tested: a real PR through the hosted app end to end

author: martiangreed
body:
## Root cause

Tab titles were coming out as the first four words of the message, not from a model. The Haiku one-shot (`claude -p --model haiku`) was timing out on every call and the heuristic fallback named the tab, silently.

On this machine the login shell (Nushell) exports a `claude setup-token` OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat…`) as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The CLI takes that variable ahead of every other auth source and sends it as an API key; the API answers 401 `API key is invalid`, and the CLI retries eleven times with backoff, far past the helper's 15 s timeout. Traced with `--debug`: `API error (attempt N/11): 401`. The same token in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, the variable Clave's own token accounts already use in `buildSpawnEnv`, answers in 6–7 s.

A second gap sat behind it: the one-shot always ran a bare `claude` off the login PATH on the machine login, whatever agent the session actually ran. A tab on a custom Claude launch profile (a wrapper, a specific binary) or a token account was named by a different Claude than the one holding its conversation.

## Change

- **`src/main/claude-one-shot.ts`** (new, pure)
  - `oneShotEnv(base, account)`: the environment for a Clave-owned `claude -p`. Strips `CLAUDECODE`, puts the session's account (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) on first, then moves an OAuth token found in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` into `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` unless one is already set (the misplaced one is always dropped). A real `sk-ant-api…` key is left alone.
  - `buildOneShotLaunch({ profile, args, loginEnv, account, userShell })`: how a one-shot starts, the way a session does. The launch profile's command tokens lead, then the one-shot's args; the profile's `additionalArgs` stay out (they describe an interactive session). A command the login PATH places starts directly (`findExecutable`); otherwise it goes through the login-shell wrapper the sessions use (`resolvePosixShellLaunch`, diverted from Nushell/Fish), every token quoted.
- **`launch-profile-manager.ts`**: `resolveClaudeCli(workspaceId, profileId)`. The session's own profile when it starts the Claude CLI (built-in, custom, or the chat variant of either), else the workspace's default Claude, else the built-in `claude`. Never the echo fixture, a plugin's agent, or another family's chat: found when the chat e2e's echo default was handed the one-shot and printed its arguments back as the tab's name. A profile that no longer resolves falls through instead of losing the title.
- **`title-generator.ts`**: carries a `TitleLaunchContext` (workspace, profile, account, config dir) per session, from both spawn sites (`pty-handlers.ts` for terminal Claude, `pty-manager.ts` for chat), and spawns through the two above. Timeout 15 s → 30 s (cold boot measured at 5–9 s; the queue is serialised).
- **`shell-launch.ts`**: `shellSingleQuote` moves here from `pty-backend.ts` (re-exported there) so the pure launch builder can quote without importing node-pty.
- **`git-manager.ts`**: the commit-message and group-summary one-shots had the same hand-rolled env; they use `oneShotEnv`. Routing them through a profile is a follow-up: they have no session context, and importing the profile manager there would drag Electron into two git test suites.

Model stays `--model haiku`, which the CLI resolves to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, the cheapest Claude. The heuristic remains only as the fallback for a genuine outage.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh Claude tab or chat tab whose first message is a real request is named by Haiku, on a login whose profile puts an OAuth token in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- The title runs the agent the tab runs: its launch profile's command, on its account (token and config dir). A tab on another agent (Codex chat, a plugin, the echo fixture) is named by the workspace's Claude, never by that agent's command.
- A real API key in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not touched; a Clave account token is never overridden by a login token.

## Verification

- Unit: `claude-one-shot.test.ts` (13: env shaping, direct vs wrapper launch, quoting, family refusal), `launch-profile-manager.test.ts` (+4 on `resolveClaudeCli`), `title-generator.test.ts` (asserts the file, args, env and timeout the CLI is actually spawned with, and the profile/account the resolver is asked for), `pty-manager-chat-records.test.ts` (both spawn contexts). Every new assertion was red before the matching change. Full `vitest run`: 92 files, 1229 tests. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint --quiet` on touched files clean.
- E2E against the built app: `chat-first-message-title` 8/8 (this one caught the echo-default gap mid-way), `chat-launch-profiles` 4/4, `agent-launch-profiles` 13/15 — the 2 failures are pre-existing on dev: the spec expects Codex argv without the `-c tui.terminal_title=…` flag that `buildAgentArgv` has appended since 5c1c537 (2026-09-06), and this PR touches neither.
- Live: the real CLI started through `buildOneShotLaunch` with the Nushell login env and the built-in profile found `~/.local/bin/claude` on PATH, started it directly, and returned `sidebar tab sync` in 4.8 s; the same env untouched hangs past 90 s.

author: alexrbrowne
body:
"Should the steward not be completely opaque to the user? Maybe a on off toggle in triage."

## What changes

- **`t` on the triage table switches the steward on or off**, in the background, with no terminal takeover.
  - The headline says `steward on` while it runs, `steward starting` in the gap before a restart, and nothing when it's off.
  - The footer names the key by what it will do: `t start steward` / `t stop steward`.
- **"On" is recorded intent, and the cockpit keeps it true.** The switch is a file, `steward/enabled`, in the state directory. `steward.Ensure` runs at startup and on every poll:
  - it restarts a switched-on steward whose session has gone (reboot, WSL shutdown);
  - it replaces one whose claude has exited;
  - it leaves one alone when it can't tell whether the steward is still working.
- **Stop clears the switch before killing the session**, so a poll landing in between can't bring it straight back.
- **You don't need to look at its session.** What it does shows on your rows (`steward · yours: …`, `answered · …`). `: steward` still opens its session if you want to read its account of the fleet.
- **From a shell,** `claude-dispatcher steward` / `steward stop` flip the same switch.

## Verified live

On a scratch fleet, against the built binary and real tmux:

- `t` switched the steward on in the background: the headline showed `steward on` and the footer flipped to `t stop steward`.
- After I killed its session, the next poll brought it back 47 s later.
- `t` switched it off, and it stayed off through a full poll.

Full record: `docs/adr/0020-the-steward-is-a-switch.md`.

author: hervenivon
body:
## What and why

Rebased onto `main` after #144 merged. This diff contains only the upload-origin guard change. Refs #65.

Upload commands currently check active account scope but omit the coordinator's captured-origin guard. A queued upload can therefore stage or claim a mutation after its scene revision changes. Apply the existing thread-safe origin guard before staging, while saving intent, and through each initialization/part/finalization claim. Recheck after file/metadata preflight so invalidation cannot slip between the check and the durable claim.

Source and network I/O stay outside the revision lock. Already-claimed requests can save their receipts to the original scope/origin; inspection and explicit status refresh remain available after origin invalidation. No claim is reset or mutation retried. A completed private snapshot may remain after post-staging rejection, matching existing retention behavior; no intent is saved, and the user's source is preserved. The current staging API has no ownership-safe discard operation.

This is a prerequisite for separate JobSession upload forwarding. No UI/MCP path is activated, no identity is inferred, and a coordinator without an `origin_guard` still depends on its caller's origin policy. Existing SDK methods remain `uploads.with_raw_response.create`, `retrieve` and `trigger_action(action="complete")`; the adapter and dependency pin are unchanged, and there is no raw fallback.

## Validation

Validated rebased head `58c462f` on main commit `866c1dd`, using pinned uv 0.9.26 and locked dependencies.

- [x] Full offline unit suite: `uv run --locked --no-env-file python -m pytest -o addopts='' -q -rx` passes locally on Python 3.11.13: **1,567 passed, 1 known SDK authentication xfail**. [CI unit tests on Python 3.11 and 3.13 pass](https://github.com/scenario-labs/blender-plugin/actions/runs/36021923728).
- [x] Focused regressions: `uv run --locked --no-env-file python -m pytest -o addopts='' -q tests/unit/test_upload_commands.py tests/unit/test_upload_inspection.py tests/unit/test_job_origins.py`: **82 passed**. Coverage includes the 17 origin-guard cases for queued/stale origins, preflight invalidation, guarded claims, unlocked network work, late receipts and explicit refresh, using the actual `OriginRevisions` guard.
- [x] Changed-file `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass for `scenario/core/jobs/coordinator.py`, `scenario/core/jobs/uploads.py` and `tests/unit/test_upload_commands.py`.
- [x] `tools/check_knowledge.py --base origin/main --json`: **0 errors, 58 retained freshness warnings**. All 23 checker regressions pass in the full suite and [knowledge CI](https://github.com/scenario-labs/blender-plugin/actions/runs/36021923927). `git diff --check` and commitlint pass.
- [x] Installed native baseline: [all six Linux/Windows jobs pass for Blender 5.0.1, 5.1.2 and 5.2.1, including the aggregate gate](https://github.com/scenario-labs/blender-plugin/actions/runs/36021924048). Each job builds and tests its exact packaged ZIP in a fresh isolated profile. Linux jobs also complete the offline sidebar/composer capture steps; no manual native interaction acceptance is claimed.
- [x] Live/paid status: no live service or paid calls were performed; SDK tests use synthetic MockTransport responses.
- Packaging-change validation is not applicable: no packaging or dependency changes.
- UI-change validation is not applicable: no UI or Blender glue changes.

The sole rebase conflict was in `docs/knowledge.json`; resolution preserves merged session-result evidence and upload-origin evidence and records the current main base. The upload implementation and tests are unchanged. All CI checks on this head passed. Independent agent review recorded before the rebase found no issues; human review remains pending.

## Public content

- [x] No private account, customer, workspace, project or infrastructure records.
- [x] No real credentials, bearer tokens, signed URLs or private job/asset IDs; fixtures are synthetic.
- [x] No personal paths, agent session IDs, private exports or spend anecdotes.

## Coding rules

- [x] Existing first-party SPDX/GPL notices preserved.
- [x] Scenario service operations continue through the shared SDK adapter; no dependency or endpoint changes.
- [x] Core remains `bpy`-free; origin checks use pure synchronized state.
- [x] No em dashes or unrelated version/changelog edits; docs state the implemented boundaries and orphan-retention limit.

## Authorship and licensing

- [ ] Human review of the complete diff recorded before merge. Pending.
- [x] Original work; existing licenses and attribution preserved.
- [x] GPL-3.0-or-later inbound=outbound.

Codex assisted this change; preserve the fallback co-author trailer when squashing.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes durable upload claim ordering and rejection paths in shared job infrastructure, though behavior is constrained by tests and mirrors existing submission guards.
> 
> **Overview**
> Upload commands now enforce the same **captured-origin revision guard** as job submission, so a queued upload cannot stage sources or commit durable SQLite claims after its Blender scene revision changes.
> 
> `JobCoordinator._upload_guard` accepts an optional `origin` and runs the thread-safe `origin_guard` through intent creation and each initialization/part/finalization claim. `UploadCommands` requires a real `JobOrigin` before staging, rechecks before preflight, and keeps file I/O and HTTP outside the lock. Stale origins fail without saving intent (staging orphans may remain); work already claimed can finish under the original scope, and **inspect** / **refresh_upload** stay available without rebinding.
> 
> Docs and `knowledge.json` record the behavior and offline regressions; **17 new unit tests** cover races, preflight invalidation, and guard scope.

body:
The README opening described the `MCPServer` / `MCPAccessGrant` / `MCPAgentSession` CRDs and what the operator generates. This PR rewrites it around what users actually do:

1. Describe the server in `.mcp/servers.yaml` (`server init`, `--from-server`), then `server build` → `server push` → `server deploy`.
2. Grant a person, agent, or team specific tools, with a trust ceiling and allowed side effects (`access grant init`).
3. Time-box that access for one agent with a revocable session (`access session init`).

The gateway check and the underlying resources follow as a closing paragraph.

I checked the command names against `./bin/mcp-runtime server|access --help`, and the grant/session fields against `api/v1alpha1/access_types.go` (`subject`, `maxTrust`, `allowedSideEffects`, `expiresAt`, `revoked`).

## Resumo

- Corrige `ValorServicos` extraído errado (R$ 500,00) no layout Camaçari/BA escaneado (`camacari_ba_scan_v3`) quando a grade OCR discrimina múltiplos itens de mesmo CNAE/LC116 na mesma nota — achado real 2026-09-23, nota nº 1359, pág. 3 do lote `STAUMMAQ - NFSe TERCEIROS.pdf` (GRAFICA E EDITORA ITACIMIRIM LTDA → STAUMMAQ SERVICOS TECNICOS). Valor correto: R$ 2.700,00 (soma de 4 itens: 500,00 + 500,00 + 750,00 + 950,00).
- **Causa-raiz**: a regra que prioriza a linha `<qtd>,0000 <unitário> <total>` da discriminação sobre a célula da grade (criada para a nota nº 148) usava `re.search`, que só acha a PRIMEIRA linha que casa por inteiro. Aqui a 1ª e a 4ª linha quebram por ruído de OCR no unitário, e o total da 2ª linha (500,00) era usado como se fosse o total da nota inteira. A célula "Valor dos Serviços (R$)" da grade já vinha correta (2.700,00).
- **Fix**: quando há MAIS DE UMA linha de item com total totalmente legível (vírgula + 2 casas, valor > 0) na grade, o override por linha de item é desligado e o valor volta para a célula da grade — regra generalizável a qualquer quantidade de itens. Zero regressão: as outras 3 notas do mesmo lote (págs. 1, 2 e 4) saem byte-a-byte idênticas ao XML gerado antes da correção.

author: aqm857886159
body:
Windows 专属问题第三批：Agent 的 bash 工具在 Windows 上，读密钥文件的命令**没有被直接拒**。

## 用户会遇到什么

Windows 上没有 OS 沙箱，Agent 跑的每条命令都要用户点头（这一点不变）。但「读密钥」这类命令本该**直接拒绝、连卡都不弹**：

- `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` → 直接拒 ✅
- `cat "C:\Users\<名>\.ssh\id_ed25519"`、`type %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\id_rsa`、`cat ~/.s'sh'/id_rsa`、读 `%APPDATA%\nomi`（Nomi 自己的设置与密钥目录）→ **落到一张普通确认卡上** ❌

Windows 上每条命令都要点，用户最容易顺手点「允许」——点了，密钥内容就进了对话、发给模型供应商。macOS 上同样的命令有 OS 沙箱的 denyRead 再挡一道；Windows 上这张清单是唯一直接拒的一层。

> 分诊时一度以为是「记住 `cat *` 之后自动放行」，核实后不是：生产里没有沙箱时根本不提供「记住」（`laneNativeApproval.ts:31`），每条都问。实际风险是「本该拒的变成了问」。

## 根因

`codingCommandPolicy.ts` 的密钥清单只按 POSIX 的一种拼法写（`/.ssh`），拿原串字面匹配；Windows 与 Linux 的 Nomi 设置目录不在清单里。同一个文件里 `isSystemReadOnly` 用宿主 `path.resolve` 比 POSIX 前缀表，Windows 上 `/usr` 被补成 `C:\usr`，一条都对不上——和 #863 里对话身份被补盘符是同一类错。

## 修法（唯一判定点 `classifyCommand`）

- 硬清单同时比原串和一份归一视图 `hardListView`（去引号、反斜杠换 `/`）。**只用来比对，不改写要执行的命令**；只会多拦，不会少拦。
- 密钥清单补上 Nomi 设置目录的 Windows（`$APPDATA` / `%APPDATA%` / `AppData/Roaming`）与 Linux（`~/.config`）写法。
- `isSystemReadOnly` 的 POSIX 前缀表按 POSIX 语义比对。

## 验证

- 新增 13 种拼法 × 沙箱开/关：旧代码 12 条红，新代码全绿（`model-catalog.json` 那条旧代码按文件名本来就认得）。
- 归一不误伤：项目内 `cat src\main.ts` 仍落原档。
- `electron/shared/agentCapabilities` + `electron/agentLane/laneNativeApproval` 22 文件 218 条在 Windows 全绿（`cat /usr/share/dict/words` 那条样本原来在 Windows 上恒红，现在绿）。
- 本机 Windows `pnpm run gates`：104 项里红的 16 项 = 干净 main 在 Windows 上同样红的 15 项 + 本 PR 的评审收据；lint / typecheck / build 通过。完整 unit 与走查以 CI 为准。

## 根因合同与评审

- `docs/fixes/2026-09-24-hard-list-windows-path-spellings.root-cause.json`（recurring，门表 2 扇：唯一定义 + 唯一调用方）
- `docs/audit/2026-09-24-electron-shared-structure-review.md`：`electron/shared` 7 天 35 份合同触发症状聚类；本份属平台假设类，与另外 34 份（重述 / 第二个家 / 生命周期混用）不同根。

## 已知、不在本 PR

- 通配符与运行期变量拼法（`~/.ss?/id*`、`$(echo ~)/.ssh`）不归一；Windows 上它们仍落到**显示完整命令**的确认卡上，不会自动放行。
- 同一次分诊查出的另外三件：Windows 上后台脚本超时/停止后杀不干净（上游 pi 的 `taskkill /T` 找不到 Git Bash exec 出来的子进程）、命令沙箱在 Windows 上从来起不来却写「这次没能启动」、bash 依赖 Git for Windows 却完全没提示——涉及用户可见文案，先出样张再修。
- 与 #863 同批：`docs/lessons/mac-only-testing-ships-windows-blind.md` 在 #863 里。

## Ponytail

评审范围 `161c243b2..e24663b7c`，**最终一轮 PASS**（收据树 = 推送树）。前面三次没拿到有效评审（两次输出无结果标记、一次 600 秒超时），曾按规程 `--defer` 留痕；第四次出了结果，两条都改了：

- **已改**：`isSystemReadOnly` 的前缀表本来就全是 POSIX 路径，直接 `path.posix.resolve`，去掉按宿主分支。
- **已改**：Windows / Linux 的 Nomi 设置目录拼法并进 `SECRET_PATH_FRAGMENTS` 字面量清单，去掉单独的正则分支。

改完 22 文件 218 条在 Windows 仍全绿；在这棵树上重跑评审 PASS。

author: flaviusburca
body:
## Why

Rune's throughput did not grow with concurrency. On one RTX 5090 it served about 26 short decisions/s whether 4 or 64 clients sent them. A public benchmark measured a 680 ms median where one request takes 50–110 ms. This is SUROGATE-CHANGES #14.

## Cause

- **`Engine::submit_batch` paused execution** to hand a decision's rows over whole, and every decision is submitted through it. A busy worker retakes the execution lock at once, so each decision reached the executor only when the engine had gone idle. Decisions were served one at a time.
- **Admission counted a deferred first chunk as GPU work.** The executor therefore staged one waiting prompt per loop.
- **With no lane decoding, staged prompts were prefilled one per step.** The only exception was the rows of a single multi-question decision.
- **Under overload, a four-question decision prefilled its shared prefix, then had its questions refused** because the queue was full. The GPU time was wasted: served throughput fell from 8 to 3.5 req/s at 64 clients.

## What changed

- **`submit_batch`:** rows now go into a submission group and join the queue together when the group closes. Nothing waits on the worker.
- **Admission:** every waiting prompt that has a free lane is staged at once.
- **Packing:** with no lane decoding, the first staged prompt and the staged prompts of the same kind run as one mixed round, up to `--max-num-batched-tokens`. "Same kind" means plain prompts together, or GPU-prefix readouts together.
  - A first prompt that is at its end takes its first-token step first.
  - A lone prompt keeps the single-lane path and its prefill graphs.
  - Speculative (MTP, DFlash) and pipelined engines keep the old path: one prompt staged per pass, no zero-decode packing.
- **Decisions:** a decision takes the queue places its questions need before any of it runs, `min(questions, --max-num-seqs, 64)` of them (`Engine::reserve_submissions`). A chat request with `parallel_decoding` does the same for its readouts.
  - It waits for them in arrival order, within `--pending-timeout-ms` (then 503).
  - While it waits, those places are held back from single requests, which can therefore get 429 before the queue is full.
  - Each finished question hands its place to the next.
  - The reservation keeps the engine alive while the caller holds it. Requests hold only the executor's places, so no request keeps its own engine alive.
- **`/metrics`:** gains `packed_prefill_rounds_total` and `packed_prefill_prompts_total`. `SUROGATE_SERVE_PACK_TRACE=1` traces the packing decisions.

## Measured (RTX 5090, capacity loadgen, 15 s per level, before → after, final build)

Per-request latency, median / p95 ms:

| Model and shape | 1 client | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JD-Q4_K_M, short, 1 question (196 tokens) | 43/44 → 43/44 | 153/155 → 110/113 | 154/1,501 → 183/188 | 619/930 → 336/424 |
| JD-Q4_K_M, 1,000 tokens, 1 question | 121/134 → 122/135 | 443/468 → 395/525 | 457/3,653 → 822/828 | 1,793/2,982 → 1,651/1,662 |
| JD-Q6_K, short, 1 question | 59/60 → 59/60 | 223/225 → 162/165 | 225/1,748 → 255/260 | 904/1,248 → 472/568 |
| JD-Q6_K, 1,000 tokens, 1 question | 163/181 → 164/182 | 631/642 → 536/705 | 632/4,985 → 1,111/1,120 | 2,536/3,771 → 2,223/2,229 |

Throughput, req/s:

| Model and shape | 1 client | 4 | 8 | 16 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| JD-Q4_K_M short | 23.4 → 23.3 | 26.1 → 36.4 | 25.9 → 43.5 | 25.8 → 48.6 | |
| JD-Q4_K_M 1,000 tokens | 8.2 → 8.1 | 8.9 → 10.0 | 8.8 → 9.9 | 8.8 → 9.8 | |
| JD-Q4_K_M 4 questions (660 tokens) | 7.2 → 8.1 | | | 8.0 → 11.8 | 3.6 (2,353 × 429) → 13.0 (none) |
| JD-Q6_K short | 17.1 → 16.9 | 17.9 → 24.7 | 17.8 → 31.4 | 17.7 → 36.1 | |
| JD-Q6_K 1,000 tokens | 6.0 → 6.0 | 6.4 → 7.3 | 6.4 → 7.3 | 6.3 → 7.3 | |
| JD-Q6_K 4 questions | 5.7 → 6.3 | | | 6.1 → 9.6 | 2.7 (2,533 × 429) → 10.0 (none) |

**Reading the "before" medians at 8 clients.** Before this change, the engine served one decision at a time, and unfairly: some requests got through while others starved. That is why the "before" p95 is 8–10 times the median. In a closed loop, mean latency is clients / throughput. For short decisions on Q4_K_M at 8 clients, the mean went from 309 to 184 ms.

**A smaller round window is not better.** `--max-num-batched-tokens 1024` was slower than 2048 at every level: 43.1 vs 43.5 req/s for short decisions at 8 clients, and 9.1 vs 9.9 for 1,000-token ones.

## Exactness (Rune, GGUF)

- The decisions v1 golden set answers the same alone and under 8 concurrent clients: every choice and every probability is equal.
- The golden set reproduces its recording at tolerance 0.
- Chat first-token logprobs are identical whether prompts are prefilled alone or packed.
- Recurrent models: a prompt that shares a round is chunked by the remaining window, as in the existing rounds with decode rows. Its last bits may therefore differ.

## Tests (GPU 7, final build)

- **New:** `tests/serve/test_batch_prefill.py`, 5 passed on JD-Q4_K_M and on JD-Q6_K. It covers:
  - one-question decisions packed, with answers equal to alone;
  - multi-question decisions: rows of several decisions share rounds, and the answers under concurrency equal alone;
  - chat first-token logprobs equal packed or alone, including a 3,700-token prompt ahead of others with a 256-token window;
  - a decision that waits for its places without prefilling, with `surogate_requests{state="reserving"}`;
  - a decision ahead of it that hangs up while waiting: it leaves the line, and every place comes back.
- **Regression:** `test_cached_tokens.py`, `test_request_id.py` and `test_engine_oom.py` (29 passed), `test_decisions_v1_golden.py` at tolerance 0 against a recording from main, and `test_parallel_decoding.py`.
- **Chat TTFT beside decoding requests:** unchanged, 77.8 ms before and 78.1 ms after (median of 30).

## Reviews

Three independent reviews ran.

**The first review** found two bugs, both fixed:
- an extra decode round before newly staged prompts when others were decoding;
- one-prompt "packed" rounds when prompts of two kinds were staged.

Its six risks were also addressed:
- a submission group per thread replaces the global admission hold;
- reservations are first come, first served;
- reservations are taken after media, LoRA and CPU preparation;
- the exactness claim is narrowed to what was tested;
- speculative and pipelined engines keep the old path;
- the first prompt in line runs first.

**The second review** found two bugs, both fixed:
- a reference cycle through the reservation, which could make the worker join itself at teardown;
- extra accounting on pipelined engines.

It also raised four risks, all fixed:
- a submission group now fails its rows on a sleeping engine;
- parallel decoding reserves its places too;
- the docs describe the 429s;
- a test covers a long first prompt.

**The third review** found no bug. Its remaining notes are fixed:
- a foreign reservation is dropped;
- member order;
- the reserving gauge;
- stronger tests.

## What's left for latency

An nsys profile at 8 clients shows the GPU 92% busy. Gaps between rounds are under 3%, so host overhead does not limit throughput. GPU time splits as follows:

| Kernels | Share |
|---|---|
| Dense GGUF int8 GEMMs | 36% |
| MoE experts | 31% |
| Attention | 12% |
| First-token LM head and sampling | 4% |

A packed round runs at about 62 TFLOPS, under 10% of the int8 tensor-core peak. Getting under 105 ms at 8 clients needs about 1.75× more prefill throughput on the 5090 (about 1.6× on the PRO 6000). Follow-ups:

- wider token tiles in the K-quant prefill GEMM: +5–6%, bit-identical, next PR;
- a candidate-only first token for decisions;
- FP8 prefill planes for the dense weights, which changes the numbers and needs a decision first;
- MoE kernel tuning.

author: the-ult
body:
Field names that contain whitespace or match a prototype key no longer break ARIA ids or reach inherited properties.

- **Path lookups.** `injectFieldControl` walks a dotted field name with an own-property check (`Object.hasOwn`), as every other toolkit lookup already does. Keys such as `constructor`, `__proto__` and `toString` now give the normal "not found" error. Before this change, the walk reached `Function` and `Object` and called `Reflect.apply` on them. A primitive or `null` middle segment on a real `FieldTree` also gives "not found" now, not a `TypeError` from the proxy's descriptor trap.
- **Generated ids.** `normalizeFieldName` replaces inner whitespace with `-` and logs one dev-mode warning per process. The wrapper's `resolvedFieldName` and `createFieldNameResolver` now use it too. Before this change, a name such as `x other-id` produced ids like `x other-id-hint`. That split into two `aria-describedby` tokens, so a screen reader read the unrelated element `other-id-hint`.

Names that differ only in whitespace versus a hyphen (`a b` and `a-b`) now give the same id. The JSDoc says so. The three demo reference wrappers get the same normalisation through `createFieldNameResolver`.

Follow-up, not in this PR: the headless error-state id builders still use the raw name.

Closes #505

Adds Supercov to `data/curated.json` under `agents`, with the regenerated outputs. It was already in the catalog as community-indexed. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and `python3 scripts/build.py --check` pass.

Supercov is a CLI that coding agents run to find out what to fix and what to test. It asks Jev twelve named `Noul` questions about each source file for code quality (`god_class`, `long_method`, `deep_nesting` and nine more) and twelve for security (`secret_in_source`, `injection_sink` and ten more), and the CLI itself composes the score and orders the files. author: deibygs
body:
## What does this PR do?
`setup-agent` now injects a compact core instructions block (`applyr/templates/AGENT_CORE.md`, 81 lines) into an agent's context instead of the full 565-line `AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. A new `applyr guide [step] [--json]` command prints one section of the full instructions on demand — pulled live from the installed package — or lists the 20 available sections when no step is given.

## Motivation
The full instructions document cost roughly 5k tokens in every agent session and went stale on every release that touched it — this project has already shipped three fixes for that class of bug (v0.8.3, v1.5.0, and the `setup-agent --force` staleness detection). Now that `applyr next` (ADR-015) owns the pipeline step order, an agent only needs the compact core plus the detail for the specific step it is currently on, fetched on demand via `applyr guide <step>`.

## Changes

| File | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `CHANGELOG.md` | ✏️ modified | Documents the switch from the full instructions injection to the compact core under "Changed" |
| `README.md` | ✏️ modified | Updated references to reflect the new compact core + `applyr guide` command |
| `applyr/agent_instructions.py` | ✏️ modified | Adds `GUIDE_SLUGS` fixed slug→heading map, `guide_section` slicing logic (heading to next heading of same/higher level, skips `#` inside fenced code blocks), and keeps `_get_full_instructions` as a fallback when the core template is missing |
| `applyr/cli.py` | ✏️ modified | Wires up the `guide` subcommand; exempts `guide` from the init/DB guard since it only reads the packaged template |
| `applyr/commands/__init__.py` | ✏️ modified | Exports the new `guide` command handler |
| `applyr/commands/core.py` | ✏️ modified | Implements `cmd_guide` — prints a section (or lists all slugs), returns `invalid_value`/`not_found` errors as appropriate |
| `applyr/commands/workflow.py` | ✏️ modified | Updates the legacy-block foreign-heading warning (#144) to also recognize the core's headings |
| `applyr/templates/AGENT_CORE.md` | ✨ added | New 81-line compact core instructions block injected by `setup-agent` |
| `docs/cli-reference.md` | ✏️ modified | Documents the new `applyr guide` command |
| `specs/compact-agent-instructions/tasks.md` | ✏️ modified | Task tracking for this spec |
| `tests/test_agent_instructions.py` | ✏️ modified | Tests for `guide_section` slicing and `GUIDE_SLUGS` |
| `tests/test_guide.py` | ✨ added | Parametrized test that fails if any `GUIDE_SLUGS` entry points at a heading that no longer exists |

author: pyro1121
body:
Fedora's cold `omg daemon-status` can spend more than five seconds loading DNF package status. The QEMU lifecycle probe killed that CLI process and retried, leaving valid daemon requests without clients. Their eventual replies hit `EPIPE`, incremented `requests_failed`, and made the later zero-failure assertion fail. Main run 36021279823 captured two broken pipes and three active connections in the initial foreground status snapshot.

Readiness now checks the cheap Metrics IPC endpoint. Each daemon mode then runs one full status query with a budget longer than the daemon's 30-second request limit, and requires both the package-cache section and zero failed requests. The post-query status uses the same budget and reports a specific assertion if its metrics are invalid. The real failed-request gate remains strict.

The offline audit refusal rows now set `OMG_DISABLE_DAEMON=1`. This makes their intended direct path explicit: `security_audit_result()` otherwise prefers a reachable daemon, and a Unix socket can cross a network-namespace boundary. A focused Fedora WSL reproduction started a warm `omgd` outside the namespace. The isolated CLI returned 58 Fedora findings with daemon use enabled, but exited 1 with the expected unavailable-source error when daemon use was disabled. The safeguard prevents that real cross-namespace bypass of the offline test oracle.

Fixes #561
Fixes #563

Validation: Fedora WSL ran the full changed lifecycle probe against the exact native Fedora release artifact from main SHA `2506349`, including all four daemon modes, strict zero-failure metrics, singleton and shutdown checks, direct-query parity, and the DNF fault-injection refusal. It produced `daemon-lifecycle.json` with all fields true and `backend_faults: ["dnf-reason-refusal"]`. A temporary, command-scoped passwordless `sudo` entry allowed that one mount-namespace probe and was removed afterward. Fedora WSL also passed all 20 `test_qemu_daemon_contract` and `test_qemu_acceleration` tests; Bash syntax and `git diff --check` passed. The hosted QEMU matrix remains the merge gate.

Evidence correction: the first two local Fedora KVM inventories each reported 183 PASS, 4 FAIL, 0 skipped because my invocation omitted the workflow's `--inventory-isolate-hermetic` flag. Those audit rows were unconfined and could validly obtain Fedora advisories; the failures do not prove daemon contamination. The focused cross-namespace reproduction above establishes the separate risk. The corrected full Fedora KVM run used the main `2506349` native artifact, this PR's scripts, and `--inventory-isolate-hermetic`; it completed with lifecycle PASS and **187 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 skipped**. All four offline audit rows exited 1 with `network_scope: offline` and passed their refusal oracles. The hosted matrix on the rebased PR head remains the merge gate.

author: jjackdeng
body:
## 问题

#46 之前，Payload 的开发模式推送一直直接改生产库，所以生产库跟着集合配置在变，而迁移文件落在了后面。从零跑迁移得到的库，和生产库有 **26 处**不同。后果是：新环境（本地、CI、灾备恢复）按迁移建出来的库和生产不一样；以后写新迁移，也会以错误的状态为基线。

## 先确定以谁为准

生产库的结构来自 4、5 月当时的代码，不能直接假设它就是对的。所以我建了三个库两两比对：

| 对比 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 只跑迁移的一次性库 vs **当前代码** schema 推进空库的一次性库 | 26 处不同 |
| 当前代码 vs **生产** | **完全一致**（列 177、约束 49、索引 96 连名字都一致、枚举 10） |

结论：**生产库是对的，落后的只是迁移链**。

补充一点：Payload 自动生成的 schema 快照（`.json`）只到 04-10，之后的 9 条迁移都是手写的，没有快照。所以没有用 `payload migrate:create`，它会拿 4 月的快照当基线来算差异。

## 26 处差异

- 4 个 select 字段在迁移里是 `varchar`，代码里是 Postgres 枚举：`tools.tool_type` / `.embed_type` / `.last_run_status`、`tool_runs.status`（另有 4 个枚举类型迁移里没有）
- `tool_runs.detail`：迁移是 `text`，代码是 `varchar`
- `tool_runs.run_at`：迁移多了 `now()` 默认值
- `blogs.status`：迁移是可空，代码是 `NOT NULL`
- 索引：`categories_locales` 的唯一索引列顺序和名字不同；`tool_runs_tool_id_idx` 要改名为 `tool_runs_tool_idx`；缺 `created_at`、`updated_at`、`cover_image` 三个索引；多一个 `run_at DESC` 索引

## 改法

新增迁移 `20260924_000001_align_schema_with_code`。**每一步都先检查、再动手**：只有当前还是 varchar 才转枚举，枚举类型已存在就跳过，索引用 `IF [NOT] EXISTS`，改名前先检查新旧两个名字。所以它**在生产上什么都不改**，在从零建的库上会补齐全部 26 处。

`down()` 会完整还原到这条迁移之前迁移链的状态。注释里写明了：生产库本来就是目标状态，不要在生产上单独回滚这一条。

## 彩排（全部在一次性 Postgres 上）

| 步骤 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 迁移链库里先写入覆盖各种取值的测试数据（`automation`、`builtin`、`script`、`error`、NULL、长文本），然后执行 **up** | 和代码 schema **完全一致**；数据原样保留，列类型变成了枚举 |
| **down** | 和迁移前的快照**完全一致**；数据原样保留，列类型回到 varchar/text |
| 再 **up** | 和代码 schema **完全一致**，行数不变 |
| 在和生产同构的库上**连续跑两次** `up()` | **零变化** |

`typecheck`、`npm test`、`i18n:check` 全绿。一次性容器都已删除。

## 合并后要做的：在生产上登记这条迁移

Vercel 的构建不会自动跑迁移（`build` 只是 `next build`），所以需要手动对生产执行一次 `payload migrate`。它会执行这条迁移（结构不会变），并在 `payload_migrations` 表里写一行记录。**这一步会写生产库，我会先问你。**

## 顺带想到的

这次偏差持续了 5 个月都没人发现，因为 CI 从来没有比对过「迁移建出来的库」和「代码期望的 schema」。可以在 CI 里加一个 job：起 Postgres service，跑迁移，再把代码 schema 推进另一个空库，两边做 diff。这个 job 不需要任何 secret，以后改了集合却忘了写迁移，会直接报红。这次没做，可以另开 PR。

author: yulceleiro
body:
## Description of the change

**Security fix: AI chat aggregations can no longer bypass the account restriction.**

The OpenSearch tool always adds the account's security filter to the query (for example `origin = BestRx` for a SUBMITTER account). But it forwarded the model's `aggregations` to OpenSearch unchecked, and some aggregation types ignore the query. A `global` aggregation returns totals for the whole index, including **other accounts' data**. This was reproduced on Dev with a restricted SUBMITTER account: its normal query returned only BestRx, while the `global` aggregation returned all 503 documents and other tenants' counts.

Now the tool only accepts aggregation types that are computed over the security-scoped query results:
- **Allowed:** terms, multi_terms, rare_terms, date_histogram, auto_date_histogram, histogram, range, date_range, filter, filters, missing, composite, nested, avg/sum/min/max/stats/extended_stats/value_count/cardinality/percentiles/percentile_ranks/median_absolute_deviation/weighted_avg, top_hits, and bucket pipelines.
- **Rejected before OpenSearch is called:** `global`, `significant_terms`, `significant_text`, `sampler`, `diversified_sampler`, `scripted_metric`, and any unknown type. The error tells the model which type was refused and not to work around the security scope.
- The whole tree is checked, including nested `aggs`/`aggregations`. An object sent as a JSON string is decoded first. OpenSearch receives the **re-serialized validated tree**, never the model's raw bytes, so tricks such as duplicate keys cannot differ between what was checked and what runs.
- The tool's input schema now lists the allowed types and says the security scope must never be widened.

## Validation
- New unit tests: allowed shapes taken from real Production queries; every escape type, including nested and stringified forms, is rejected; a rejected request never reaches OpenSearch; duplicate-key and trailing-JSON cases. The full `go test ./...` suite passes (and with `-race` for this package).
- Replay of 90 days of Production AI-chat queries (1,017 queries, 860 with aggregations) through the validator: the only valid query now rejected is the single `global` aggregation, from an unrestricted SWITCH account on 2026-07-26. The 3 other rejections were malformed JSON that OpenSearch could not run anyway.

Release as **v1.7.2** (patch).

Nota contabilă: 4111 = 704 (service pe pagină) sau 706 (chirie) + 4427. Fișa acoperă și data facturii la prestările cu decontări succesive (art. 281 alin. 7, art. 319 alin. 16 din Codul fiscal) și e-Factura.

## Defecte găsite

Toate sunt confirmate în `odoo shell` și documentate ca limitări; codul nu e modificat în acest PR.

- 🔴 **Citirea de la instalare e facturată față de *Valoarea inițială*:** cu valoarea inițială 0, prima factură ia tot indexul.

Auditul `verificator-fisa`, tura 1, a găsit 🔴 contabile și de flux. Toate sunt corectate:

body:
## The question, asked once

`0012` F-1, `0009` §7 row 11 and the research document's §7 widening all route to one question: **what may this index assert about a surface it does not author?** Taken separately they amend `0007` §5–§6 twice, each amendment moving `tools/spec.py`'s pin with it — two windows in which the one stable normative text is in flux, for one decision. F-1 says so itself: *"They are one stage, and it needs `architect` before `@Plan`."*

## The decision

**The profile is not a `Surface`**, and `0009` §7 row 11 closes in its literal form — answered in substance by one narrow instrument.

The ground is a re-measurement rather than a preference. `0012` F-6 required it: §14's figures were taken 2026-09-08 and are dated across an edit to their own subject. Re-reading found **a second edit F-6 could not have seen** — `c75b2b8`, `#5` of 2026-09-18 — which replaced the very figures §14.3 convicts.

What that re-take found is the decision's ground: **the rule row 11 asks for is already being followed and nothing checks it.** Ten of the eleven committed surfaces are quoted on the profile byte-exact against their own page's headline as `render.parse` reads it. So row 11's second half is a carrier to build, not a clause to write.

Against that, registering the surface reddens gated clauses on markup this portfolio does not author — **three of them, or two**, depending on the `repo` field it is registered under, which is itself an argument against the option.

## What the acceptance commit must do

This document names its edits rather than asserting them, because a decision recorded only in an ADR is `ST-1` waiting to happen and **nothing in `tools/`, `tests/` or `.github/` reads `docs/adr/`**:

1. `0009` §7 row 11's own cell.
2. **Two** rows in `0010` §4 — the account fields, and the instrument — because §4.4's own rule is that a residual the queue cannot read is one the next session will not meet. *An earlier draft of this document broke that rule one subsection after stating it.*
3. The collision count, asserted at **four places in three files**. At two of them the **attribution** moves too: they say `ADR-0009` §0 *"refuses a fourth"*, and what §0 refuses is skipping to a free number.

The §4 row's shape is fixed by the parser, not by taste: ten columns; `—` in the `#` column, because a session number there would put 13b into `scanned()` and **silently drop `P0w3r223/P0w3r223` out of the queue's *what next***; and no `Index SHA` to invent, since `ancestry()` grades a dash-numbered row `none` and the SHA guard exempts it.

## Re-deriving the figures

§2.4 carries the commands. They are there because §2's readings are the decision's ground and **none is reproducible from this checkout** — `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule applied to this document rather than asserted by it.

The §2.3 recipe was wrong twice before it went in, and both times it looked right: blockquotes alone answer **three**, an extraction with no comparison answers **seven**, and the committed version is the one that was run — `10 of 11 quoted byte-exact; missing: ['car-price-ml/app']`.

## Review

Four `code-reviewer` passes, three blocking. Each found a class the previous could not have derived: prose misquoting other sections; the fourth number collision, with a test that stays green over the change its own name describes; and the document breaking its own §4.4 rule plus an unexecutable row shape. The fourth returned conditional, with nothing at the decision or executability level.

Instruments: `pytest` 671 · `citations` 0 unresolved · `pagespec --detail` byte-identical before and after · `queue` unmoved.

**Status is `proposed`.** No code exists for this and none should until it is accepted.

author: guryashzone
body:
## Summary
Stacked on #1 (auth schema). Implements the email/password half of `docs/11-backend-mvp1.md` §2:

- Argon2id password hashing behind a `PasswordHasher` port (`@node-rs/argon2`, pinned cost params, `needsRehash` for forward cost bumps).
- 15-min HS256 access JWTs + rotating opaque refresh tokens (`auth_sessions`), with reuse detection: a 60s grace window absorbs a lost response or double-refresh, anything outside it is treated as theft — revokes every session for the user and bumps `token_version`.
- A global default-deny `AuthGuard` (`APP_GUARD`) that re-checks session revocation, `token_version`, account status and role in one indexed query on every request — never trusting the JWT alone. `@Public()` added to the existing health/geo routes so they aren't locked out by the new global guard.
- `POST /v1/auth/{register,verify-email,resend-verification,login,refresh}` and `POST /v1/auth/logout` (`?all=true` for sign-out-everywhere).
- Login lockout (5/email/15min, 20/IP/hour) backed by `login_attempts`; `resend-verification` throttled 1/min + 5/day via `@nestjs/throttler`.
- Register/login/forgot all use the same generic response shape/errors regardless of whether the email exists (enumeration protection, docs/11 §2.3).

**Supporting infra added along the way** (needed by the above, not separate features):
- Minimal `UsersModule`/`UsersRepository` (just enough for auth to create/read users; `/v1/me` lands in a later PR in this same module).
- `AuditModule` + the `audit_logs` table (new migration `0005_audit_logs.sql`) — needed for the refresh-replay/theft audit trail docs/11 §2.1 calls for.
- `TransactionRunner` in `common/db` (docs/02 §4.3's `db.transaction` wrapper — wasn't built yet).
- `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` in `main.ts` so IP-hash-based lockout reads the real client IP behind nginx, not the proxy's.

**Deliberately deferred** (separate PRs, per docs/11 §4's endpoint table): `POST /v1/auth/google`, `password/forgot`, `password/reset`, `password/change`.

## A bug this caught
Manual end-to-end testing (see below) surfaced a real bug: the theft-detection branch originally revoked every session for the user *and then threw* an exception from inside the same database transaction. Since a thrown error rolls back everything written in that transaction, the revocation was silently undone before the response ever reached the client — so a detected "theft" replay returned 401 but left every other session (including the attacker's) still valid. Fixed by having `rotate()` return a `{kind: 'theft'}` result instead of throwing mid-transaction, letting the transaction commit, and only raising the error after the commit succeeds. Covered by the manual test transcript below.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `supertest/types` error)
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npm run test` / `npm run test:e2e` — existing health e2e still passes
- [x] **Full end-to-end run against a real local Postgres 16 + PostGIS.** Docker's daemon isn't available in this sandbox, so `docker-compose` couldn't be used — instead I installed `postgresql-16` + `postgresql-16-postgis-3` directly via apt and ran the actual Drizzle migrations (all 6, including this PR's `0005_audit_logs.sql`) against it, then drove the running API with real HTTP requests:
  - register → verify-email (wrong code rejected, correct code issues tokens) → DB shows unverified user, `password` identity, hashed 6-digit code
  - logout revokes the session; the same access token is rejected on the very next request (guard's live check, not just JWT expiry)
  - login (success + wrong-password rejection, generic error either way)
  - normal refresh rotation
  - replaying an already-rotated token **within** the grace window → succeeds, reissues tokens, original abandoned successor revoked (this caught and confirmed the fix for a lookup bug: the replay's "was the successor itself reused" check was querying by refresh-token-hash using a session id, so it always missed and forced the theft branch — fixed to look up by primary key)
  - replaying a token whose successor **was itself already rotated** → correctly detected as theft, revokes every session for the user (verified all rows revoked in the DB, not just the one presented), bumps `token_version`, writes the `audit_logs` row
  - login lockout after 5 failed attempts (6th returns 429)
  - `resend-verification` 1/min throttle (2nd call within a minute returns 429)

author: oliviertrudeau
body:
## Problem

Two related symptoms observed on staging:

- Clicking **Activate** for a channel (e.g. `all-test`) marked it **Active** in the Aurora connector UI, **but Aurora never joined the channel in Slack** — it wasn't a member, couldn't post there, and didn't appear in the bot's channel listing.

The activate path (`_activate_channels`) only flipped `metadata_status` / `is_dismissed` in the DB and enqueued a metadata task. It never called `conversations.join`, so "Active" in the UI didn't correspond to actual Slack membership.

## Fix

`_activate_channels` now best-effort **joins** each activated channel via `SlackClient.join_channel` (`conversations.join`) and sets `is_member = TRUE` on the rows that were successfully joined, so the UI reflects real membership.

- **Public channels**: joined automatically on activation.
- **Private channels**: cannot be self-joined (Slack requires a human invite), so the join fails silently and activation still proceeds. When a human later invites Aurora, the existing `member_joined_channel` handler picks it up.
- Joining is fully best-effort and never blocks activation or the metadata enqueue.

## Not in scope

The separate symptom — *adding Aurora to a channel in Slack (e.g. `social`) didn't auto-switch it to Active* — is **not** a code bug in this repo. `_handle_member_joined` / `register_single_channel` already handle that correctly; on staging the `member_joined_channel` event simply isn't reaching the server (Slack app Event Subscriptions config / no Socket Mode listener deployed on the `1.5.0` staging cluster). That's an environment/config issue tracked separately.

## Testing

- `ast.parse` syntax check passes.
- Reuses the existing, already-tested `join_channel` client method and `set_rls_context` RLS pattern; single-file change.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

body:
Closes #716

## Approach

- `tools/render_command_sources.py` declares each brand once in `BRAND_TABLE` as three independent axes: layout (`command-file` or `skill-directory`, templated in `LAYOUTS`), frontmatter key allowlist, and sigil. `BRANDS`, `SIGILS`, and `BRAND_FRONTMATTER_KEYS` are derived from that table, so existing consumers keep working.
- `CommandSource`'s `claude_commands_dir`/`codex_skills_dir` pair is replaced by an `outputs` mapping from brand to directory. Its keys are the entry's brand set. `output_paths` and `render_entry` produce output for exactly those brands, and `render` refuses any brand outside the set. The eleven shipping entries share a read-only `BUNDLE_OUTPUTS` (claude + codex).
- `select_brand` now takes the entry's declared set. A brand block naming a brand the table knows but the entry doesn't render is refused with its line number (requirement 6). Unknown brands are still refused as before.
- `workflow_vocabulary` is unchanged: it still raises on a missing Claude or Codex bundle directory (requirement 7).
- The fixture adds a third brand, `grok`. It combines the skill-directory layout, the `/` sigil, and `name`/`description`/`argument-hint` keys, which is the combination verified in `grok-plugin/.../solve/SKILL.md`. Its output lands at `tools/command_render_fixture/grok/skills/fixture-command/SKILL.md`, outside every bundle. The only change to the fixture source is a `grok` variant inside the existing brand block, so the Claude and Codex fixture outputs are byte-identical.

author: alexklimaj
body:
Motors configured at 60–260 kV bypassed the RPM-dependent duty ceiling. This enables it for them and keeps only the stored 20 kV setting as the opt-out, porting [upstream AM32 commit 7ebdc129](https://github.com/am32-firmware/AM32/commit/7ebdc12927fd9c7ff85530d04a5f8e9fcb44e6ad). For a motor configured as 180 kV with 42 poles, the ceiling now rises from 20% to 100% across about 95–619 shaft RPM on targets without kV scaling.

Review of the first commit found that settings reloads were not idempotent and that the opt-out could be reached by accident. The second commit fixes both.

## Changes

**Low-kV limiter**
- Test the raw EEPROM byte for the 20 kV opt-out, so target-specific kV scaling cannot create extra opt-outs.
- Keep ARK32's pole-scaled envelope and the separate 300 effective-kV automatic-timing threshold.

**Settings reloads** (boot, DroneCAN reset to defaults, SITL EEPROM editor)
- `loadEEpromSettings()` now resets the limiter flag and envelope, low-RPM ceiling, dead-time override and current-limit enable to their power-on values before applying the EEPROM. Previously each reload added the running-brake dead time to the ceiling again (400 → 580 → 760 … at running brake level 5), `use_current_limit` could never clear, and a layout-version-0 reload kept the previous limiter state.
- The RC-car limiter override (limiter forced on, 1000/2000 low-speed ceiling) moved from `main.c` into the loader so reloads keep it. Boot behaviour is unchanged.

**Startup floor** (all motors)
- The low-speed ceiling is never below `min_startup_duty`. `setInput()` clamps the startup floor to `duty_cycle_maximum`, so a lower ceiling overrode the configured minimum duty and startup power. This only changes anything when minimum duty × 10 + startup power exceeds 400; for example, minimum duty 30 with startup power 150 now gives a 450/2000 ceiling.

**DroneCAN `MOTOR_KV`**
- Writes outside 20–10220 kV are ignored instead of wrapping into the byte (10260 kV used to store 0, the opt-out).
- 21–59 kV is stored as 60 kV, so only an explicit 20 kV selects the opt-out. Other values truncate as before.

**Docs**
- `doc/eeprom-settings.md`: the Motor KV entry now says 20 kV turns the low-rpm limit off, and that motors under 60 kV should be entered as 60. **The configurator's `guide.ts` needs the same text.**
- `doc/low-kv-protection.md`: stored-kV examples, the startup floor, reload behaviour and the hardware validation plan.

## Known limitation

`setPwmDeadTime()` only ORs bits into the timer's dead-time register, so a running brake level change still needs a restart to reach the hardware. This predates the PR; fixing it needs per-MCU register writes and hardware validation.

## Validation

- `Mcu/SITL/tests/test_low_kv_limit.py`: all 26 cases pass. They cover every affected kV bin at 14/42/128 poles, the stopped duty ceiling, opt-out reload transitions, repeated reloads at running brake level 5, the startup floor, current-limit disable, RC-car and version-0 reloads, and DroneCAN kV stores.
  - Against `main`, 19 fail. For example, the 180 kV/42-pole case sees the limiter off and the old unrestricted 2000 ceiling instead of 400.
  - Against the first commit, the 9 cases added in the second commit fail. For example, the ceiling goes 580 → 760 on the first reload.
- Full SITL pytest suite: 106 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- Upstream ESCSim behavioural suite at the pinned revision: all passed.
- `make size-check-ark` (F051, embedded bootloader) passes: HWCI_PERF 27,452 B flash / 6,576 B RAM; release 26,616 B / 6,056 B.
- `check-codegen-ark`, `make cppcheck`, `make eeprom-check`, the EEPROM schema unit tests and `make check_format` (clang-format 22.1.5) pass.

## Hardware validation (pending)

No physical hardware was exercised for this PR. Before release, compare `main` and this branch on the 160 kV/42-pole motor with the intended saved encoding (180 kV), load and supply. Check repeated starts, low-speed throttle steps and the sine-to-six-step handoff, recording RPM, duty, current, desyncs and failed starts, then repeat the normal-kV baseline. The SITL tests verify policy and runtime ceilings, not loaded starting torque.

author: pacificcode
body:
**dsv-gitlab can't currently release.** #60 (2025-03) moved the aqua pin from goreleaser v1.23.0 to **v2.7.0** without migrating the config. The last release, v1.0.6, predates that, so nothing has tried to release since and nobody noticed. The next attempt would fail immediately:
```
⨯ only version: 2 configuration files are supported, yours is version: 0
```
and mage also passes flags that v2 removed.

## Changes
| file | change |
|---|---|
| `.goreleaser.yaml` | `version: 2` (after the leading `---`, since before it goreleaser silently ignores the rest of the file) |
| `.goreleaser.yaml` | `changelog.skip` → `disable`; archives `format` → `formats`; `snapshot.name_template` → `version_template` (removed or deprecated in v2) |
| `.goreleaser.yaml` | `announce.slack.enabled: false`. The GitHub Slack app already posts every release to the channel. Same decision as terraform-provider-dsv #118, where this announce step failed a release run after publishing. |
| `magefiles/goreleaser.mage.go` | `--skip-validate` → `--skip=validate`, `--skip-publish` → `--skip=publish` |

Release config is otherwise **unchanged since v1.0.6** (verified with `git log v1.0.6..main`), so everything else is exactly what last shipped successfully.

## Testing
- `goreleaser check` (aqua-pinned v2.7.0): valid, no deprecation warnings.
- Full local snapshot, `goreleaser release --snapshot --skip=validate,publish,announce` with `DOCKER_ORG` set to a dummy registry: **succeeded**. It produced the binary, tarball, checksums and syft SBOM, and built both Docker images (`<DOCKER_ORG>/dsv-gitlab:{tag,latest}` and the local ones, about 9 MB distroless).
- `docker run` of the built image: the binary starts and reports version and commit.
- ⚠️ Not testable locally: the Docker Hub push and the GitHub release. Both need repo secrets and run for real on release.

## After merge
No CHANGELOG.md change, so no automatic release. The release PR (v1.0.7) comes next and carries #63's Go 1.26.8 toolchain (3 ArmorCode tickets) and #62's `x/sys`/`x/text`/`x/mod` security bumps.

author: aurelienfeignon
body:
## Ce que la PR livre

Trois choses, nées d'un signalement de la session qui instruisait la **récidive NVMe du
homeserver** : le conteneur de développement du portfolio fuyait dans le swap du SSD dont le
contrôleur a gelé deux fois.

1. **La fuite est bornée** — `mem_limit` **et** `memswap_limit` sur le service `web`.
2. **Le prompt de reprise est à jour** après un mois de pause, et deux commandes qu'il documentait
   étaient fausses.
3. **La cadence réelle de la sonde externe est mesurée**, là où le dépôt avait réservé sa place.

## ⭐⭐ `mem_limit` seul n'aurait pas réglé le dommage rapporté

Sans `memswap_limit`, Docker autorise la mémoire virtuelle totale à monter jusqu'à **deux fois**
`mem_limit` — et le surplus part précisément dans le swap qu'on cherche à ne plus toucher. Les deux
valeurs égales veulent dire « aucun swap ».

Vérifié **dans le cgroup, depuis l'intérieur du conteneur**, plutôt que dans la configuration
Docker :

```
memory.max      = 4294967296
memory.swap.max = 0
```

⚠️ **Et la portée de l'affirmation s'arrête à cette machine** : sur un hôte sans comptabilité du
swap (cgroup v1, certaines configurations WSL2), Docker **ignore `memswap_limit` avec un simple
avertissement** — la borne de RAM tient, la coupure du swap non, et rien d'autre ne le dit. Le
contrôle à rejouer sur une machine neuve est écrit à côté de la valeur.

## ⭐ Le plafond est mesuré, pas choisi

| | |
|---|---|
| 858 Mio | serveur de dev au démarrage |
| 959 Mio | après compilation de six routes, accueil 3D comprise |
| **1 526 Mio** | **pic d'un `make bundle` complet** (`next build` + gates) |

4 Gio laisse ~2,6× de marge sur le geste le plus lourd du dépôt, et reste treize fois sous ce que la
fuite avait atteint. **Les portes de `make ci` qui passent par le service `web` ont été rejouées
sous la borne** — `lint`, `typecheck`, `coverage`, `bundle` — avant de conclure : une borne qui
casse une porte serait pire que pas de borne.

⚠️ **Ce que la borne ne fait pas** : corriger la fuite. La cause n'est pas instruite. Elle la rend
**datée et bruyante** — à 1,7 Go/jour depuis ~1 Gio, 4 Gio sont atteints en ~2 jours de marche
continue. ⛔ Or un `OOMKilled` se lit comme « Next a planté » : les deux commandes qui tranchent
(durable *et* jetable) sont écrites dans le compose, et aucune politique `restart:` n'est ajoutée —
elle transformerait ce signal en boucle silencieuse.

## ⛔⛔ Deux commandes documentées répondaient à une autre question

```bash
gh run list --branch main --limit 1     # annoncé : « ce que la CI a conclu »
```

Sans `--workflow ci.yml`, elle rend le run le plus récent **tous workflows confondus** — donc
toujours la *Sonde externe*, qui tire plusieurs fois par jour, et **jamais** la CI. On lisait un
déploiement d'après un tir de sonde.

Elle figurait **quatre fois** : deux dans le prompt, deux dans `deploy/README.md` — dont la ligne de
la checklist de mise en ligne *« les cinq jobs du run de `main` ont conclu »*, qui se cochait donc
sur une sonde verte. ⭐ Le fichier employait déjà l'idiome `--workflow` deux lignes plus bas, pour la
sonde elle-même.

Trouvée en l'**exécutant**, pas en la relisant.

## ⛔⛔ La sonde ne tire pas toutes les 10 minutes — facteur 21

100 tirs planifiés sur 14,6 jours : **médiane 3 h 27**, moyenne 3 h 32, min 1 h 39, **max 6 h 58**,
contre `cron: '*/10 * * * *'`. Ce n'est pas une dérive passagère — première moitié 3 h 26, seconde
3 h 37, indiscernables.

Le délai honnête de détection d'une panne est donc **~7 h**. La garantie visée par R-15 — *une panne
ne dure pas des jours* — tient toujours, et c'est elle qu'il faut citer, jamais la ligne `cron`.

⭐ **La mesure va dans `deploy/README.md` §7.4 ter et non dans le prompt**, parce que c'est
l'emplacement que `uptime.yml` désigne lui-même : *« le retard réellement observé est relevé dans
deploy/README.md plutôt que supposé »*. Le prompt n'en porte qu'un renvoi.

## ⛔⛔ Un nombre qui fondait une décision, jamais remesuré

`uptime.yml` justifie l'épinglage du **majeur** de Node par « ~50 Mo à chacune des **144 exécutions
quotidiennes** ». 144 est le compte théorique de la ligne `cron` ; la mesure donne **~7**. Le gain
réel est de 350 Mo/jour, pas 7 Go.

Le choix tient quand même — le majeur est dérivé de la même source, il ne coûte rien à maintenir —
mais il tient désormais sur son argument de correction, pas sur un chiffre inventé.

⭐⭐ **La copie de `phase-4-log.md` est AMENDÉE, pas corrigée** : c'est un journal, et la leçon est la
péremption elle-même. *Un nombre qui fonde une décision doit être remesuré avec elle*, et celui-ci
avait l'air d'une mesure sans jamais en être une.

## ⛔⛔⛔ Une échéance qui s'auto-invalidait à la fusion

« GitHub désactive un workflow planifié après 60 jours sans activité » est un vrai risque : passé ce
délai la sonde ne rend plus ni vert ni rouge — elle ne tourne plus, et *rien ne le dit*.

Mais la première rédaction gravait « échéance au 2026-10-25 », dérivée du dernier commit sur `main`
— donc **fausse dès la poussée suivante, celle qui l'écrit comprise**, et le texte le disait
lui-même deux lignes plus bas. Remplacée par la règle et la commande qui la calcule, aux trois
endroits.

## État du projet

**P6-03 est fusionnée et déployée** (26/08, cinq jobs verts). **Phase 6 à 2 tâches sur 10**, la
suite est **P6-02**. Le site est debout — sonde verte sans interruption sur toute la fenêtre.

## Ce que la PR ne fait pas

- **Pourquoi `pnpm dev` fuit n'est pas instruit.** La borne contient la conséquence.
- **Ne pas faire tourner le conteneur en permanence** reste une habitude à prendre (`make up` à la
  demande, `make down` après), pas un correctif à écrire — l'étage `dev` porte `CMD ["pnpm", "dev"]`.
- Aucun lien de causalité n'est affirmé entre la fuite et les gels du contrôleur NVMe. Elle ajoute
  une charge d'écriture continue et inutile ; c'est tout ce qui est démontré.

## ⭐⭐⭐ Et ce que les deux passes de revue ont appris sur la manière de corriger

`/code-review` a rendu neuf constats, que j'ai traités **en ajoutant des rectificatifs à côté du
texte fautif**. `/simplify` en a rendu dix, dont le premier était la conséquence directe : une
contradiction ouverte à **trois lignes d'écart**, la version fausse en premier — plus courte, plus
affirmative, et celle où le lecteur s'arrête.

*Une correction qui n'efface pas ce qu'elle corrige est un ajout.* Et chaque rectificatif ajouté
avait dupliqué son chiffre, dans un dépôt dont la règle affichée est « une seule copie de chaque
chiffre ».

La seconde passe a donc **réécrit** au lieu d'annoter, et donné un domicile unique à chaque fait :

| fait | domicile |
|---|---|
| le piège `--workflow ci.yml` | `deploy/README.md` §4.2 |
| la borne mémoire — chiffres, raisonnement, contrôles | `docker-compose.yml` |
| la cadence de la sonde | `deploy/README.md` §7.4 ter |
| la règle des 60 jours et le calcul de l'échéance | `deploy/README.md` §7.5 |
| « 144 était théorique » | `phase-4-log.md` §21.7 bis *(journal : amendé, pas effacé)* |

Vérifié fichier par fichier après coup : `1 526`, `858`, `959`, `2,6×`, `1,7 Go`, `53 Go`,
`memory.swap.max`, `OOMKilled`, `3 h 27`, `6 h 58`, `7 tirs` n'ont plus qu'un seul domicile chacun.

⛔ Trois copies existaient là où j'en voyais deux : `uptime.yml` énonçait **toujours** « 10 minutes
plus un retard non garanti », trois lignes au-dessus de la mesure qui la réfute — la formulation même
que le commit précédent se félicitait d'avoir retirée d'ailleurs.

⛔ Et j'ai écrit dans ce lot un renvoi `§21.6 bis` là où la section est `§21.7 bis`. Trouvé en
cherchant la section qui contient réellement le texte, pas en la comptant de tête : *un `§x.y`
recopié dans une chaîne n'a aucun garde*, et ce dépôt l'avait déjà payé en P4-14.

author: ironpinguin
body:
Closes #117

**What.** When the last piece snaps in: about 3.5 s of fireworks (`canvas-confetti`, ISC, loaded on demand) plus about 3 s of applause. The *Solved!* banner stays.

**Only on an actual solve.** Besides the restore case the issue names, there was a second one: `PuzzleBoard` called `onSolved` on *every* drop while a single group was left, so each time the finished picture was moved it would have celebrated again. It now fires only when that drop actually merged (`changed` from `resolveConnections`). The solver hangs the celebration off `onSolved`, not off `solved`, so a restored finished puzzle shows the banner and nothing else.

**Sound.** On by default, as the issue proposes. There is a toggle **🔊/🔇 Applause** (`aria-pressed`) in the toolbar, stored as `celebration:sound` in localStorage and read after mount (cf. #7). The key is deliberately outside the `solve:` prefix, which `storedSolves` treats as solve states.

**Recording.** `public/sounds/applause.mp3` is a 6.3 s CC0 field recording of an audience in De Doelen, Rotterdam (Sandermotions, [Freesound #277021](https://freesound.org/people/Sandermotions/sounds/277021/), via Wikimedia Commons), converted to 96 kbit/s MP3 with a 1 s fade-out and loudness normalisation, 76 KB. The source is credited in `NOTICE`. `next start` serves `public/` from disk, so an installation can replace the file without a rebuild, either by overwriting it or with a volume mount. The README has a new *Applaus austauschen* section with a compose example. Played with `HTMLAudioElement` inside the drop's gesture. A refused `play()` or a missing file stays silent. (An earlier revision of this PR synthesised the applause with Web Audio. It did not sound like applause and is gone.)

**Reduced motion.** With `prefers-reduced-motion` there are no fireworks (checked in `celebrate`, and `disableForReducedMotion` as a backstop). Applause still plays, since it is not motion, and can be muted.

**Pointer events.** The confetti canvas is `pointer-events: none`, so the board stays usable while it plays. *Start over* and unmounting stop a running celebration, and so does the next click, tap or key press anywhere (bare modifier keys aside). That press is listened for in the capture phase and not prevented, so it still picks up a piece or presses a button.

**Tests.** `PuzzleSolver`: celebrates on `onSolved` with sound on by default, not on a restored solved state (banner shown, no celebration), the mute choice survives a remount and reaches `celebrate`, and *Start over* stops it. `celebrate`: plays `APPLAUSE_URL` and fires fireworks, stays silent when muted, leaves out the fireworks under reduced motion, swallows a refused `play()`, ends on a click or a key press but not on a bare modifier, and stopping pauses the audio and clears the confetti. The one-line `changed &&` in `PuzzleBoard` has no test, because that component has none (canvas).

Checked that the production server serves `/sounds/applause.mp3` (`200 audio/mpeg`). Not tried in a real browser in this session (no DevTools MCP). Worth a manual solve of a 12-piece puzzle to judge how it looks and sounds.

author: renfordn
body:
## Summary

- `hooks/path_resolution.py`'s `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` fallback silently guessed a bare, non-suffixed `~/.claude/plugins/data/agent-isdd/` path whenever the env var wasn't set — with no warning. Root cause of a false `commit_audit_gate.py` denial: Claude Code can load `agent-isdd` under more than one identity at once (e.g. this monorepo's checkout as `agent-isdd@inline` alongside a marketplace install as `agent-isdd@<marketplace>`), each getting its own `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` injected into its own registered hook subprocesses — but never into a manual/direct `python3 hooks/*.py` invocation, which silently diverged instead. Confirmed in practice via a duplicated `DOC-AUDIT-STATE.md`/`DOC-AUDIT-HISTORY.md` and an entirely invisible SDD feature folder.
- Every `agent-isdd` hook that discovers its own state via `memory_dir()`/`active_state_file()`/`find_state_files()` (none receive an explicit spec-folder path in their own hook payload) inherits this exposure. Worst case: `hooks/design_spec_gate.py` treats "no state found" as "no SDD workflow active" and falls through with no decision — a resolution mismatch there means a silent **allow** of an unapproved `agent-tdd:agent-TDD` Design Spec spawn, not just a stale read.
- Fix: the fallback now prints a clear, one-line warning to stderr (never stdout, reserved for a hook's JSON decision) whenever `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is unset. Kept in sync across the per-plugin copy (`agent-isdd/hooks/path_resolution.py`) and `shared/path_resolution.py`. Deliberately a detection/visibility fix, not a resolution-unification one — normalizing to one path would fight Claude Code's own per-identity data isolation. Documented the actual discipline instead (never invoke `hooks/*.py` directly outside the real hook chain) in every affected hook's docstring and a new `README.md` section.
- Reconciled this project's already-split SDD memory data: copied/merged the fuller non-`-inline` records into the `-inline` location (canonical, since real hooks resolve there), left the non-`-inline` originals in place with superseded-pointer notes — nothing deleted.
- Scoped to `agent-isdd` only; most sibling plugins carry the same per-plugin `path_resolution.py` fallback pattern and likely share this exposure — noted as a follow-up, not fixed here to avoid scope creep.

## Test plan

- [x] `agent-isdd/tests/test_path_resolution.py` (new) and matching cases in `shared/test_path_resolution.py` cover: warning present on stderr, absent on stdout, absent when the env var is set, fallback still returns a usable path.
- [x] Full suite green: `python -m pytest agent-isdd/tests/ shared/test_path_resolution.py -q` → 355 passed.
- [x] `agent-isdd` version bumped 0.1.53 → 0.1.54 with a full `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

body:
## Problemas detectados

1. **Crear producto podía congelar toda la pestaña** después del PR #61. El optimizador global de imágenes observaba mutaciones del DOM y su propio `textContent` generaba otra mutación, entrando en un ciclo continuo cuando aparecía `#product-image`.
2. **Envíos quedaba mostrando solo el encabezado**. El frontend es zoneless y `ShippingSettingsPage` asignaba la respuesta HTTP a una propiedad normal (`settings`) sin notificar a Angular para volver a renderizar.
3. El mismo patrón zoneless estaba presente en **Andreani** y en el **panel de seguimiento del pedido**, por lo que podían quedar visualmente vacíos o desactualizados después de cargas HTTP.

## Cambios

- El optimizador de imágenes solo modifica el texto de ayuda cuando realmente cambió, cortando el loop del `MutationObserver` sin perder la optimización automática de fotos grandes.
- `ShippingSettingsPage` fuerza el refresh de vista después de la carga/guardado asíncrono y muestra un estado de carga explícito.
- `CarrierSettingsPage` refresca la vista al cargar/guardar configuración de Andreani.
- `ShipmentPanel` refresca la vista cuando llega el shipment, incluso si el estado inicial sigue siendo `PENDING`.

## Alcance

No cambia contratos backend, base de datos, pagos, stock ni reglas de cotización. Es un hotfix de runtime/renderizado del Admin.
