## Backlog item

`record-astrology-consultations`, the first `status: todo` item in
`docs/marketing/seo-backlog.yml`. Set to `shipped` in this branch. The `pr:` field
says `TBD` because there is no PR number to write yet.

**Why it is on the list** (verbatim from the file):

> This is our hero claim and we do not rank for it at all. On 2026-09-17
> astrologerapp.org held both #1 and #2 on Bing/DDG for "astrology software that
> records client sessions", one of them a dedicated /sessions-scheduling page.
> /astrologer-workspace buries the recording story under "More than charts and a
> client list" and is 548 words. This is the highest-value page on the list.

## Are the queries still worth the page? Yes

Searched 2026-09-24. Steliara does not appear anywhere in the top results for any
of the four target queries, so the "already top 3, drop the item" branch of the
brief does not apply.

| Query | Who ranks today (top 5) |
| --- | --- |
| astrology software that records client sessions | 1 appscrip.com/astrologer-consultation-software, 2 **astrologerapp.org**, 3 phpcrm.com/astrologer-appointment-booking-software, 4 techjockey.com Q&A page, 5 **sacredsystems.io/for/astrologers** |
| record astrology consultation | 1 kennethsorensen.dk, 2 astrodaiva.com, 3 etsy.com, 4 astrology.org.uk, 5 foodforthesoul.net |
| transcribe astrology reading | 1 en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychic_reading, 2 Wikipedia disambiguation, 3 alicebell.substack.com, 4 astro-charts.com, 5 astrologyreadings.online |
| astrology session notes software | 1 en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrology_software, 2 TimePassages App Store listing, 3 **astrolium.com**, 4 astroapp.com, 5 alabe.com |

Two honest notes on that table:

- **"record astrology consultation" is not a software query.** Every result is an
  astrologer selling a reading, and the page will not win it and should not try.
  The page is aimed at the first and fourth rows, where the intent is a tool.
- **A new name appeared in row one: `sacredsystems.io`.** Search snippets describe a
  "Sacred Scribe" that records the astrologer's spoken interpretation as a voice memo
  and turns it into a client report. That is adjacent to our differentiator but not
  the same thing (their own interpretation dictated alone, not the two-way
  consultation). I could not verify it: the site renders client side and every fetch
  returned only the page title, so nothing about it is claimed on the page. **Worth a
  human look before the Astrolium alternative page is written.**

## The page

`/record-astrology-consultations`, 1548 words of static English HTML in the served
document, no `data-i18n`, three JSON-LD blocks (Organization, SoftwareApplication,
FAQPage). Routed on `/record-astrology-consultations` and `.html`, sitemap priority
0.9 (a peer of the other conquest landings, not above the home page), `lastmod`
bumped to 2026-09-24, added to `llms.txt` and to the Solo-hostname fence.

Inbound links from all three pages the item names: `/astrology-practice-management`
(nav plus an in-body link), `/astrologer-workspace` (nav plus an in-body link), and
the home footer. The home footer link needed a new catalog key
(`page.index.nav.recordedConsultations`) in all four locales, so `/de/`, `/ru/` and
`/uk/` carry it too, pointing at the English page exactly as the existing conquest
links do. No RU/UK/DE mirror of the page itself, per the backlog rule.

### Claims about Steliara, and where each comes from

Two claims on this page are sharper than anything on the sibling pages, and both
come from the shipped product rather than from `product-marketing.md`:

- **Only audio is recorded, never video.** `app/frontend/locales/en.json`, the
  in-call consent notice: "Only audio will be recorded - no video." The existing
  conquest pages say "records the video consultation", which is loose. This page
  says the call is video and the recording is audio.
- **Recording does not start until both sides agree.** Same file: "Both sides must
  agree before recording begins", plus the "Recording consent" modal shown to the
  other participant.

Everything else traces to `.agents/product-marketing.md` (the HERO, the three
pillars, the AI trust line, the "record on a dictaphone, you will only remember
20-30%" customer-language row) or to live site copy:

- Plan names, prices and **which plan includes recording** come from
  `page.pricing.plans` in the catalog and from `/pricing.md`. Recording,
  transcription and summaries are Studio only, so the price block says that rather
  than letting a reader assume it is included at $24. `product-marketing.md` still
  calls the tiers Standard/Pro at $19/$29 annual; the live site says
  Practitioner/Studio at $20/$32. I followed the live site. **That doc is stale and
  should be corrected.**
- The privacy section quotes `/terms.html`: you retain ownership of your content
  including recordings; personal data is not sold; content is kept while the account
  is active and deleted or anonymized within a reasonable period after closure; the

author: mhalinge
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the GitHub Actions workflow failure where the app E2E test comment could not be posted on fork PRs due to token permission restrictions. The solution uses the `workflow_run` event to post comments on the base branch where the token has full permissions.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Docs / tests only

## How it works

**Problem:** The `app-e2e.yml` workflow tried to post a PR comment directly, but fork PRs get a read-only token in `pull_request` events—GitHub denies `pull-requests: write` permissions to `pull_request` events from forks as a security measure.

**Solution:** Separated comment posting into a new workflow (`post-app-e2e-comment.yml`) triggered by `workflow_run`:
1. The app-e2e workflow generates the comment and uploads it as an artifact
2. The new post-app-e2e-comment workflow is triggered when app-e2e completes
3. It runs on the base branch (where the token has full permissions)
4. It downloads the comment artifact and posts it to the PR

This is the standard GitHub Actions pattern for commenting on fork PRs and is used by many projects.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run lint` passes (YAML formatting verified)
- [x] Solution tested against the failing workflow
- [x] Follows GitHub Actions best practices for fork PR permissions

## Related issues

Fixes the workflow failure reported in the GitHub Actions run https://github.com/omniship-labs/eyeread.in/actions/runs/36028983328/job/107778456873

author: poyrazk
body:
## Milestone

Ops / release pipeline: rollout speed and runner isolation. No ADR; this changes CI infrastructure, not platform architecture.

## Why

The only `faas-fleet` runner lived on the control plane (`faas-fsn-1`). That caused two problems.

1. **Security.** The repo is public, and fork-PR workflows need approval only for first-time contributors. A PR whose workflow targets `runs-on: [self-hosted, faas-fleet]` therefore ran on the host that holds Postgres and the internal CA, under a persistent runner with the default compute service account.
2. **Speed.** It was a single process, so the "parallel" compute prepare jobs queued on it. In the last rollout, fsn-2's prepare waited 10.5 min for fsn-3's.

## What

- **`fleet_runner.yml`** installs `faas_runner_instances` runner processes per host. Instance 1 keeps the historical names; instance N adds a `-N` suffix to the runner name, install root and systemd unit.
- **`github_actions_runner` role** pins `faas_runner_private_hosts` in a managed `/etc/hosts` block, validated as IPv4 plus hostnames. `cd-compute` fails closed on public or ambiguous answers. A dedicated host lacks the control plane's manifest-managed aliases: `fsn-3.gregale.dev` resolves publicly to a Cloudflare address.
- **`pki-renew`** no longer assumes it runs on the issuer:
  - it renders the fleet inventory on the control plane over SSH (`CP_HOST` + `CP_SSH_KEY`, pinned with `ssh-keyscan` like the CD workflows);
  - it rejects unsafe archive paths in the rendered inventory;
  - it reaches the CA through that address instead of loopback.

  The contract test now forbids loopback, and it fails when a pinned string is removed.
- **Docs:** the `deploy/ansible/README.md` runner section now describes the dedicated-host layout.

## Already provisioned (outside this diff)

`faas-fleet-runner` VM:
- e2-medium, Ubuntu 24.04, europe-west3-a;
- **no public IP** (egress through the existing `gregale-egress-ew3` Cloud NAT), **no service account**, Shielded VM;
- reachability through the existing `default-allow-internal` rule: SSH to all nodes and to `pg_hba`'s 10.156.0.0/20;
- runners `faas-fleet-runner` and `faas-fleet-runner-2` registered with `faas-fleet`, private endpoints pinned.

The control-plane runner `faas-fsn-1` is **stopped but still registered**, as a fallback until the first rollout succeeds on the new runners. It is removed after that.

## Validation

- `pki-renew` dispatched from this branch ran on `faas-fleet-runner-2`. It rendered the inventory on the control plane over SSH and ran the renewal play against the control plane over the network.
- It then stopped at `faas_pki_registry_nodes == faas_pki_inventory_nodes`: the registry still lists the retired `fsn-4.faas`. That is the **same assertion main's nightly run has failed on since 2026-09-21**, so this is parity with main, not a regression. It is tracked separately.
- `actionlint` is clean, `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` passes, and the contract test is updated and passes.

body:
The packed-version guard added in #4975 blocked the first release run after it ([run 36041732468](https://github.com/vchelaru/Gum/actions/runs/36041732468/job/107775278123)) on a false positive:

```
FNA.2026.9.24.2-preview.2  lib/net8.0/FNA.dll  expected 2026.9.24.2  actual 25.3.0.0
```

`FNA.dll` is built from the vendored submodule and carries upstream's own `AssemblyVersion` (`fna/src/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:42`). That version is unrelated to the one we stamp on the package, so comparing them says nothing about a clobbered build. Skipped by package id, with the reason inline.

Also skipped `*.symbols.nupkg`, which `--include-symbols` fills with the same lib assemblies, so every finding was reported twice.

Nothing else in that wave mismatched, so the #4974 fix itself held.

## Verification

Synthetic waves, one case each:

| case | expected exit | got |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package with id `FNA` present | 0 | 0 |
| `.symbols.nupkg` present | 0 | 0 |
| real GumCommon 2026.4.10.1 vs 2026.9.24.1 | 1 | 1 |

## Not fixed here

The workflow packs and tries to publish an `FNA` package built from the submodule. Worth a look at whether that should be packed at all, but it predates this guard.

author: hurricane1026
body:
## Problem (found by the op-sequence fuzzer, `test/pagestore-op-fuzz`)
Under clean/SIGKILL restart cycles, the daemon started refusing to open its store every 1–3 minutes per worker, with `storage open: Invalid or incomplete multibyte or wide character` and no diagnostic line.

Root cause: background maintenance compacts the retention log once it holds ≥64 records. The steps are `begin_pending` → write+fsync `.tmp` → rename over `retention.meta` → `write_state` → `clear_pending`. `retention.pending` was a zero-byte guard, and `ps_retention_open()` failed closed whenever it existed (`errno = EILSEQ`, no log line). A process crash anywhere in that window left the store permanently unopenable. Deleting the marker is not enough either: a crash after the rename but before `write_state` leaves meta holding the new record count and state holding the old one. This breaks the MVP's process-crash recovery promise (RELEASE_VALIDATION.md; MVP_STATUS "compacted off the request path"). The fuzzer did not violate any contract: the SIGKILL landed while the client was idle and background maintenance was running.

## Fix
- **Intent record:** `retention.pending` now holds `{magic, version, op=APPEND|COMPACT, old_n, old_hash, new_n, new_hash, crc}`, fsynced before any log byte changes.
- **Recovery at open:** `retention_recover_pending()` removes `.tmp`, then classifies meta against old and new:
  - COMPACT: roll forward when the whole file equals the new state (count + hash); otherwise roll back when it equals the old state.
  - APPEND: always roll back (tolerating one torn or complete trailing record), because an append is not acknowledged before its pending marker is cleared.
  - Then it writes the state and clears pending. Anything else fails closed. Recovery recomputes from the bytes on disk each time, so a crash during recovery is idempotent.
- **Live-process failures:** when a running process cannot prove a mutation committed (a failed rollback, or a post-rename step failing), it installs a durable `retention.failed` marker, which hard-refuses open. This keeps "failed while live" separate from "interrupted by a crash".
- Compaction and the v1→v2 migration now share `retention_republish()`, so both get the fix.
- **Diagnostics:** every fail-closed branch in `ps_retention_open()` prints a line (e.g. `state nrecords 65 != log 4`). Every failure in `ps_core_open_impl()` goes through `OPEN_STEP`, which prints `pagestore_core: open step <name> failed: <strerror>` and ensures errno is set, so the daemon's `perror` is never stale.
- No change to steady-state persisted formats (`retention.meta`/`retention.state` bytes unchanged; fixture identity tests pass).

## Tests
- 6 new crash-only fault points: `retention_compact.after_{pending,tmp_sync,rename,after_state}` and `retention_append.after_{pending,write}`.
- New `pagestore_retention_crash` test, 7 cases / 83 checks. Each case asserts the child dies at the fault point, the first reopen recovers the expected pin set, and a second restart is idempotent. A literal kill during recovery is not tested.
- **Fail-before evidence:** the crash test itself cannot show it, because the fault points do not exist in the old code. The real fail-before is a gdb-driven SIGKILL at the compaction lines 1536/1577/1584 on the **unfixed** daemon: all three leave a store that refuses to open, and 1584 still refuses after deleting the marker. The fixed daemon recovers from all four crash points and reopens cleanly on a second restart.
- Local cassert: pagestore meson suite 78/78 (`pagestore_wal_reclaim_core` needed a 2× timeout under concurrent fuzz load).

## Not covered
The v1→v2 migration path under fault injection (no legacy-v1 fixture) and a literal kill during recovery.

body:
## Summary

The complete V5.1 rich workload took 1266 seconds in exact-master CI 36002482606. Prepare one immutable source backup, run three whole-cell shards (published controls, automatic healthy, automatic concurrent), and independently replay all five cells in the required aggregate. Preserve all 1080 frozen-window seconds and calls, per-cell limits, physical/history/read oracles and ten evidence negatives.

Shards return only PARTIAL. Full acceptance requires the complete source/build/seed-bound set, combined storage limits and a shared decoded-trace budget. Retain the serial entry point and all portable aggregate inputs; all new jobs remain required, with docs-only skips preserved.

Make negative replay portable: after download, validate the inventory and inspect retained authority bytes against their recorded original paths, using the same location handling as the physical validator. Validate the unmodified history before any mutation so an unrelated original failure cannot count as ten successful rejections. Check negative results after packing/unpacking in the producing shard, retain aggregate diagnostics before comparison, and keep exact case/status/reason equality.

## Validation

- PR CI 36043850713 passed all three shards and all five physical cells. Its aggregate failed because negative replay omitted the location mapping: all ten mutations stopped early at `copied/stale seal path`. Reproduced that failure using its unchanged retained artifact.
- Repaired complete aggregate replay of that unchanged CI artifact: all five cells, 1080 calls, ten exact negative results and combined evidence budgets passed in 154.751 seconds. Original source/build checks ran against the exact detached CI merge checkout and pinned Java; no workload was rerun. Receipt: `target/v51-rich-negative-replay/repaired-aggregate/receipt.json`.
- Three new regression tests fail against the original negative driver and pass with the correction: relocated authority, invalid original evidence, and missing/altered inventories. All 446 V5.1 Python tests pass.
- Earlier clean reactor: 899 tests, four existing skips, zero failures/errors; 31 CI/toolchain tests passed. This correction changes Python validation and documentation only.
- YAML, 127 shell blocks, 68 expanded artifact names, Required/docs-only outcomes and unchanged unrelated jobs were checked for the topology migration. Documentation contract, changed local links and whitespace checks pass.

Corrected-source protected CI remains required. Prior local timing failures remain retained and documented; the successful hosted workload establishes this run's execution result, not a timing root-cause fix. No runtime Java, POM, workload parameters, measurement retries or paid-cloud changes.

Closes #263. Supersedes #265 by porting only its documentation work onto current main, without the old runtime stack.

- Add a shared 15-entry feature map and all eight numbered RFCs to `/spec`, `/api.md` and `/llms-full.txt`; link it from the homepage and participation guide.
- Reflect published experimental peer-stream 0.1.0 and the recorded live read-only browser MCP rollout. Distinguish endpoint compatibility from account UI/directory acceptance.
- Represent merged room budgets and unmounted HTTP/client integration without presenting private rooms, standing streams, blobs or C2C adapters as released.
- Correct stale wake-hook, identity, encryption, complete-history and adapter-parity claims. Keep welcoming self-service participation copy and unchanged competitor review dates.
- Add visible-content/generated-document checks and no-JavaScript mobile/desktop browser coverage; fix specification overflow.

- Frozen lockfile install (same dependency tree; no package/lockfile changes)

Documentation, static UI and regression checks only. No runtime API, schema, deployment configuration, listener, npm version or publication change. author: hsb3
body:
Codex sessions in an unarmed project are now told atelier is not activated (kata fynq).

**Cause.** `codex_lifecycle.prepare` returns `None` when `codex_workers.active()` is false, and the surfacer returned straight away, before the not-activated check. The fix is in the surfacer, not in `prepare()`, which other Codex hooks share: changing it there would turn every Codex hook on in unarmed projects.

**Change**
- `session-handoff-surfacer/hook.py`: when `prepare` says inactive, print `UNARMED_MESSAGE` under the Claude Code gates (source `startup`/`clear`, main session only: no `agent_id` and an empty or `main` `agent_type`, inside a git worktree, no activation file, `ATELIER_ACTIVATION_NUDGE` not `off`). Nothing else prints. **Decision:** no handoff surfacing in an unarmed Codex project, because Codex hooks are off there by design. Docstring and hook README now say so.
- `tests/test_session_handoff_surfacer.py`: `test_codex_stays_silent_on_an_inactive_project` is replaced by `test_codex_says_not_activated_and_nothing_else` (a HANDOFF.md is present and must not be surfaced; this test fails on dev) and `test_codex_not_activated_line_keeps_the_claude_gates` (opt-out, `resume`, worker `agent_id`).
- atelier 0.37.9 → 0.37.10 (both manifests and marketplace.json), plus one line in the bundle README.

**Proof**
- RED on dev: the new-behavior test errors. GREEN: 37/37 in the module, `make ci` 2649 tests OK, `check_version_bump.py` and `check_labels.py` both exit 0.
- Mutation: removing each gate (source check, `agent_id` check, the print) turns the codex tests red.

**Parity.** Claude Code and Codex now match. Nothing here is one-sided, so `docs/atelier-parity.md` has no row to change. I have not checked whether the opencode port has a not-activated line at all.

**Not covered by the gate.** No live Codex session was run. The tests drive the hook with `ATELIER_HARNESS=codex` and a synthetic payload, so they assume a real Codex SessionStart payload has no `agent_id` for a main session.

## Summary

Add a stationary monochrome region pattern behind the Locations tab, layered over faint full-view rosette rings. Alternate rows shift by half a cell. A 54-point preferred cell pitch keeps the repeat compact, with compensated artwork extent to preserve the region size. The print uses flat, faint strokes without shadows; slender regions receive a bounded size adjustment to balance the marks.

The pattern includes every visited region in the selected year, including manual entries and Elsewhere. It uses catalog order so ranking changes do not rearrange it. Repeated cells extend beyond all four edges, and every region retains a fully visible copy.

## Why

Extend the personalized print on the region cards into a quieter screen background while preserving a continuous staggered repeat.

## Review focus

- Appearance lives in dedicated stylesheet tokens. Region paths come from the existing injected cache; full-view rosettes use the existing shared renderer.
- Layout keeps square cells with a half-cell horizontal offset on alternating rows and overscan at every edge.
- Obsolete artwork is hidden when membership changes. Empty, initial-loading, and failed states retain only full-view rosettes. Reduce Transparency hides all decorative ink.
- Screen snapshots allow one second for native glass and artwork settling. The loaded fixture warms its outline cache before capture, including accessibility preparation.
- No persistence, public API, or dependency changes.

## Testing

- Focused layout and stylesheet tests passed, covering half-cell row offsets, overscan, full region coverage, and empty history.
- 36 reviewed captures across LocationsBackground, LocationsView, and RootView, including light/dark, iPad, accessibility sizes, and Reduce Transparency.

author: jyothri
body:
Fixes items 4.3–4.6 ("UI / UX") and 5.2–5.3 ("Code health") from `docs/codebase-review.md`, plus the follow-ups raised in review after #13. One commit per item or issue, then a commit that updates the doc. One commit changes the backend (the scan-time fix below); everything else is UI and CI.

## Review items

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| 4.3 | Elapsed time and history durations are shown as m:ss (h:mm:ss from an hour up). An unfinished scan reads "Not finished" instead of `-1`. The always-0 ETA column is replaced by a Progress column: an indeterminate `<progress>` while messages are being fetched, which switches to a percentage once `completion_pct` is non-zero (7.6). Start times are formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. |
| 4.3 (backend) | **Found along the way:** the history API sent Pacific wall-clock time labelled as UTC (`AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'`), so a scan started at 16:52 UTC came back as `09:52Z`. `GetScanRequestsFromDb` and `GetScansFromDb` now use `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` and return the real instant. |
| 4.4 | Request history shows "Loading scans…", "No scans for this account." and "Couldn't load scans: <message>". The accounts error now includes its message. |
| 4.5 | Progress headers are `<th scope="col">`, and the "Elapsted" typo is fixed. New shared `Table`/`Tr`/`Td` and `Input` components replace the duplicated class strings. Dark mode now covers the page body and form: body colours, `color-scheme: light dark`, and dark border variants. |
| 4.6 | A drive icon (`public/favicon.svg`) replaces `vite.svg`, and the package is renamed `bhandaar-ui` in `package.json` and the lockfile. |
| 5.2 | The last `console.log` calls are removed. |
| 5.3 | New `typecheck` script. A new `check` job in the UI workflow runs `npm ci`, lint and typecheck (Node from `ui/.nvmrc`), and the image job `needs` it. |

## Review follow-ups (recorded in the doc as 1.11–1.14, 3.9, 5.5)

| Issue | Change |
|---|---|
| Cancelled consent showed the state-mismatch message | `validateSearch` reads `error`. `access_denied` shows "Linking was cancelled."; any other error is named. |
| Back returned to the spent callback | The redirect uses `throw redirect({ href, replace: true })`. |
| Stream errors hidden before the first update | `ScanProgress` shows the error line with or without data. |
| History never picked up a finished scan | `scanRequests` drops `staleTime: Infinity` and opts back in to `refetchOnWindowFocus` (off globally in `App.tsx`). It also polls every 10 s while any listed scan has no end time. |
| Reversed dates not caught | `submitRequest` rejects an end date before the start date. |
| Trailing space in the filter | `buildGmailFilter` joins an array of terms. |

## Worth knowing
- **Stream errors:** the error line shows only once the `EventSource` is `CLOSED` (from 1.7), e.g. on an HTTP error response. While the browser keeps retrying an unreachable server, nothing is shown.
- **Polling:** a scan that never gets an end time (e.g. one that crashed, see 7.10) keeps the history page polling every 10 s while it's open.
- **Error delay:** a failing scan-requests call shows its error after TanStack Query's default 3 retries, about 7 seconds.

## Testing
- `go test ./...` passes (no `-race` locally: no C compiler on this box; CI runs it with `-race`). `npm run lint` is clean, and `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.
- `actionlint` reports no issues in the new `check` job. The only findings are pre-existing SC2086 info notes on the `REPO=` lines in both workflows.
- Browser check: headless Chrome over CDP, against Vite and the **real backend on the local Postgres**. SSE, the `/api/glink` hop and the empty/error accounts were faked, and no real scan was submitted.
  - **Start times:** the API returns `16:52:01Z` for scan 10, and the history shows "Sep 24, 2026, 9:52 AM" in a Pacific-time browser.
  - **Durations:** shown as m:ss; scan 6 reads "Not finished", and the list polls while it's shown.
  - **Empty and error states:** both appear.
  - **Progress:** a faked event shows "1:05" elapsed and an indeterminate bar.
  - **Stream error:** with SSE returning a 500, "Scan progress unavailable: …" shows before any data.
  - **Reversed dates:** rejected, and no POST is sent. The filter is `label:inbox after:2026/09/10 before:2026/09/02`, with no trailing space.
  - **Cancelled consent:** `?error=access_denied` shows "Linking was cancelled."
  - **Link and Back:** linking adds one history entry instead of two, and Back lands on `/request`.
  - **Favicon:** served as `image/svg+xml`.
  - **Themes:** light and dark screenshots of both pages look right.
- Not tested: a real Google login, and a real scan end to end.

body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable team of [subharness](https://github.com/vercel-labs/subharness) specialists for vgpu development and the lead workflow that coordinates them, so research, API design, planning, implementation, docs, and review run with purpose-built agents.

- `.subharness/agents/` — 8 specialists:
  - `api-researcher` / `graphics-researcher` (fx `gemini-3.8-flash` → Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`): raw, cited findings only.
  - `api-designer` (`gpt-6-astra` xhigh → `claude-opus-5.5`): API alternatives with illustrative snippets, judged for AI-agent ergonomics.
  - `planner` (`gpt-6-astra` high → Opus): plan folder with index, per-task specs, parallel lanes, progress log, and a PR record.
  - `implementer` (`gpt-5.6-sol` high → Opus): one task test-first; runs `writer` and `reviewer` as children; commits on its lane.
  - `writer` (Opus → `gpt-5.6-sol`): docs in the concept-guide house style (embedded in `tools/docs-style.ts`).
  - `reviewer` (Opus, read-only → `gpt-6-astra`), `builder` (`gpt-5.6-sol` → Opus) for integration polish.
- `.subharness/tools/shared.ts` — shared instructions that route every agent through AGENTS.md and `.github/guides/` (workflow selection, independent adoption, changeset/migration format, bundle budgets, CI-only snapshots, compat-safe shaders).
- `.claude/skills/vgpu-agent-flow/SKILL.md` — lead workflow: select workflow → research → design → human-validated `decisions.md` → plan → parallel lanes in worktrees → integration review → polish → PR.
- `.gitignore` ignores `/.context/` (pipeline scratch, lane worktrees); `AGENTS.md` gains a short pointer section.
- Root devDependencies: `subharness@0.0.2`, `zod`.

## Workflow and origin

maintainer-original — internal maintainer request (@matiasngf) to set up subharness agents for vgpu development.

## Triage and plan

Triage: vgpu work repeatedly needs the same stages (state-of-the-art research, API alternatives, plan, implementation with docs and review), and there was no shared, versioned agent setup across contributors.

Plan: commit specialist definitions and the lead skill so any maintainer gets the same flow; keep per-task artifacts (research, decisions, plans, progress, worktrees) in the ignored `.context/work/<topic>/`; keep personal access (`.subharness/agents.local.json`, Vercel OIDC) out of the repo. fx research uses the `vercel-labs/vgpu` project OIDC token, documented in the skill.

Known limitation: harness fallback only applies when the first harness is unavailable before submission; xAI models are blocked by the team's AI Gateway provider allowlist.

## PR type

development

## Release impact

none — Adds repository-only agent definitions, a contributor skill, a gitignore entry, and root devDependencies; no published package, bundled doc, or runtime behavior changes.

## Validation

author: rizukirr
body:
droid-nvim now covers Kotlin, Gradle and Android tooling only.

## What changed

- `lua/droid/lsp/java/init.lua` (the jdtls launcher) is deleted.
- Java is removed from LSP start, stop, restart, clean workspace, commands, diagnostics, the decompiler and config.
- `lsp.java` and `lsp.kotlin.attach_to_java` are gone. kotlin_ls attaches to `kotlin` buffers only. Old keys in a user config are ignored without a warning.
- The README no longer describes Java support.

## Breaking change

droid no longer starts jdtls or attaches any server to Java buffers. Users who need Java can configure jdtls separately.

## Checks

- A headless Neovim script loads every droid module, runs `setup({})`, and asserts that `lsp.java` and `attach_to_java` are gone and that kotlin_ls filetypes are `{ "kotlin" }`. It passes.
- `grep -rn jdtls lua/` and a README grep for `jdtls`, `attach_to_java` and `JDTLS_DIR` find nothing.
- `stylua --check` passes on the touched files. `diagnostics.lua` already failed stylua before this change and was left as is.

Not tested against a running kotlin-lsp: go to definition into a library class (decompiler) and `:DroidImports`.

## Small leftovers

These don't change behaviour and were left alone:
- `M._filetypes` now ignores its argument.
- `M._decompile` still takes an `lsp_name` it no longer uses.

## Cleanup (5 more commits)

- fix(logcat): `:DroidLogcatFilter` re-filters the running session. `apply_filters` checked `M.job_id`, which nothing assigned, so it always listed devices again.
- One `android.pick_running_device` replaces three copies of the device picker (quick actions, `:DroidMirror`, logcat).
- Logcat merges filters with `vim.tbl_extend`, and the never-toggled `auto_scroll` flag is gone.
- One `run_install` helper for both gradle install jobs.
- Removed code nothing called: `android.wait_for_device_id`, `android.clear_application_id_cache`, `client.run_command`, the `workspace_cache_dir` wrapper, `jre.get_version`, `jre.bundled_jre_dirs`, `kotlin._filetypes`, the `android.device_wait_timeout_ms` key, and `config.migrate_old_config` (the flat `lsp` config shape replaced in February).

Visible changes: the logcat picker shows `name (id)` like the others, and a failed plain install says "Install failed". A pre-February flat `lsp = { inlay_hints = ... }` config is now ignored without a warning.

Checks: headless tests for module loading, the logcat filter fast path (failed before the fix) and the device picker all pass. Not run on a real device.


## Bug fixes from a review (6 more commits)

- Security: `.droid-lsp.lua` was run with `dofile` as soon as a Kotlin buffer opened, so a cloned repo could run any Lua. It now goes through `vim.secure.read`, the trust prompt Neovim uses for 'exrc'.
- A stopped job's `on_exit` cleared the job that replaced it, so restarting logcat left an adb that `:DroidLogcatStop` could not stop. `buffer.release_job` clears a job only if it is still the current one.
- Logcat joins lines split across output chunks and no longer inserts blank lines.
- After starting an AVD, droid waits for that emulator. It used to take the first device adb listed, which could be a connected phone.
- `:DroidTask` passes its extra arguments to gradlew separately.
- Logcat refuses to start while a Gradle task runs in the shared panel instead of killing it, and `:DroidLogcatStop` no longer releases the guard of a running `:DroidRun`.

Each fix has a headless test with fake `adb` and `gradlew` that failed before the fix and passes after. Not yet run on a real device.

author: huydepzai121
body:
## Summary

Adds the OpenSpec change `openspec/changes/add-task-memory` and implements it.

When a run completes cleanly, the host records how it was done: a bounded, secret-screened list of the steps it actually dispatched on that site. When a later request of the same kind arrives on the same host, the model receives those steps as advice, so it can skip exploration it no longer needs. Nothing is replayed, and the memory grants no permission.

### Host (`host/agent/memory/`)
- **`derive.js`**: only a clean `run_done` produces a memory.
  - Any `run_error` in the window disqualifies the run. `finishRun()` also appends `run_done` after an error, so `run_done` alone is not enough.
  - `run_stopped`, a Jev end that is not `done`, and a drift outcome also produce nothing.
  - Reuses the workflow materialization's trail reader and secret screen.
  - Typed values and script source are dropped, and the step is marked as having had one. Credential-shaped control names are not kept.
  - Tool results and assistant text never enter the record.
- **`store.js`**:
  - One JSON file per memory under `<agent root>/memory/<host-hash>/`, written atomically.
  - Guards reject instead of truncating: 64 KiB, 40 steps, 200-character intent.
  - Authority-shaped keys are rejected.
  - A repeat of the same task (intent and step sequence each ≥ 80 %) replaces the stored entry instead of adding a copy.
  - Eviction keeps 20 per site and 400 in total, stale entries first.
  - Supports forgetting per site, per conversation, or everything.
- **`recall.js` / `intent.js`**: exact-host, deterministic recall of at most 3 memories, using token overlap on the intent. Repeat cues such as "làm lại như lần trước" are honoured. Stale memories are never offered.
- **`guidance.js`**:
  - An additive `## What worked on this site before` system-prompt section. When nothing is recalled, the system prompt is byte-identical to before.
  - Bounded `prior_path_advice` on Jev's plan request. Jev's selection logic is unchanged.
- **`task_memory` tool**: read-only (`recall`, `list`), pinned to the run's own site.
- **`companion.js`**:
  - Recall at run start and one durable `memory_recalled` event.
  - After the terminal event: reinforce and derive on success, or mark stale on a failure that contradicts the memory.
  - Deleting a conversation forgets its memories. If that fails, the delete is reported as failed.
  - Settings-relay ops for the switch, list and forget.
  - START accepts the panel's history `privacy` field. When "Không lưu nội dung câu hỏi" is on, no new memory is written.

### Extension
- Panel: a line "Đã tham khảo cách làm lần trước · <site> · <khi nào>" inside the run's timeline card. It is never counted as an operation, and it is restored from the durable event on reconnect. Also a tool label, and the privacy policy is sent with every send.
- Settings: a new "Bộ nhớ cách làm việc" page with the switch (default on), a per-site list, "Quên trang này" / "Quên tất cả" with a second-click confirmation, and an empty state. The ops are allowlisted in `background.js`.

## Testing
- New host suites, 76/76 passing:
  - `task-memory-store` 19
  - `-derive` 18
  - `-recall` 13
  - `-guidance` 8
  - `-tool` 8
  - `-wiring` 10 (through the real `CompanionCore`)
- New panel suites: `settings-memory-controller`, `sidepanel-memory-recall`. The drift guard in `background-agent-settings-relay` now also reads `memory-client.js`.
- The full host and root test directories were run. The only failures (`agent-settings-relay`, `settings-all`, `settings-capability-test`, `skills-scope-verification`, `settings-ui-real-companion`) fail identically on the base commit: the container runs as root, and the Claude CLI refuses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` there.
- `openspec validate add-task-memory --strict` passes, and `design-tokens-contrast` passes.
- The memory page was rendered in headless Chromium at 320, 400 and 480 px, light and dark: no page errors and no horizontal overflow.
- **Not done:** live QA (task 8.2). It needs the extension loaded in a real browser with a real provider.

author: umer-bytefinch
body:
Fixes #56

## The problem

An agent caller could destroy or replace a stored value with no human in the loop. There were three routes:

1. `secretveil rm -y <ref>` removed a value.
2. `secretveil set <ref>` replaced a value that already existed.
3. A second `secretveil init` on a new file, for example `.env.local`, wrote the new value over a stored value with the same name. The probe on main changed `db_pass` from `fake-first` to `fake-second`, as an agent.

The product rule is that a command that can put a value where a file can hold it needs a human caller. The same rule must apply to a command that removes or replaces a value, because a lost value cannot come back.

## The change

- `rm` needs a human caller. An agent or CI caller is refused, and the refusal goes into the audit log as a `delete` record.
- `set` of a reference that already has a value needs a human caller. An agent can still add a new reference.
- The new `agefile.Store.Create` adds a value only when the reference has no value. The check and the write run under the same write lock, so two agent calls cannot both see "no value" and then both write. `set` from an agent uses `Create`, and `store.ErrExists` becomes the same refusal.
- `init` now reads the values that the store already holds before it writes.
  - If the same name holds the same value, it keeps the name.
  - If the name holds a different value, the new value gets a new name, for example `db_pass -> env_local_db_pass`.
  - `Apply` never replaces a stored value. As a last check, it stops with an error when a stored value differs.
- `set` and `rm` now write `write` and `delete` audit records. These events existed but no command used them. The logger for `set` is made after the write, so the first `set` of a new project, which makes `.secretveil`, is not lost.

## Tests

- `TestCase5bAnAgentMayNotRemoveOrReplaceAValue`: an agent `rm` and an agent replace are refused, and the value stays.
- `TestAHumanMayRemoveAndReplace`: a human keeps both powers.
- `TestTheFirstSetIsInTheAuditLog`: the first write of a new project has its record, and the record holds no value.
- `TestCreateNeverReplacesAValue` in agefile.
- `TestASecondInitNeverReplacesAStoredValue` and `TestASecondInitKeepsTheNameOfTheSameValue` in migrate.
- `go test -count=1 ./...` passes, with the four suites adversarial, leak, nonetwork and hygiene.

## Probe

The probe used a temp project under the job directory. As an agent, `rm` and a replace were refused, and a new reference was added. As a human, add, replace, reveal and remove all worked. The audit log had `added`, `replaced`, `reveal` and `delete` records and no value.

## Docs

`docs/commands.md` (init, set, rm), the README command table, and `docs/threat-model.md`.

## 무엇을 바꿨나

계획의 결함 D1~D14를 결함마다 재현 테스트를 먼저 쓰고(수정 전 의도한 이유로 실패하는 것을 확인), 고쳐서 통과시켰다. 결함 하나가 커밋 하나다(D1·D9는 같은 병합 경로라 한 커밋).

| # | 결함 | 재현 테스트 | 수정 전 실패 | 수정 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 재개 런의 `status`·`show`가 이전 턴 전체를 읽음 | `test_every_view_of_a_resumed_run_covers_its_own_turn_only`, `test_a_resumed_run_does_not_count_the_earlier_turns_children` | status 사용량 2000 대 result 0, 실행 중 status 자식 3 | 새 `_evidence.py`(런 범위 증거 뷰: 턴 경계·자식·답·출처·사용량)를 result·status·show·log가 공용 |
| D2 | 재개 턴 마커가 아직 안 보이면 이전 턴의 답을 확정 | `test_a_turn_that_has_not_appeared_yet_is_waited_for_not_replaced_by_the_last_one`, `test_a_turn_that_never_appears_is_not_reported_from_the_turn_before` (S2) | 이전 턴 답 `Python 3.14.7 …`을 이 런의 답으로 보고 | `turn_start_index`가 미관측이면 `None`. 감독자는 기다리고, 끝내 안 보이면 stdout 답으로 `completed_unstructured` + 사유 |
| D3 | 도구 호출로 멈춘 턴의 텍스트를 답으로 채택 | `test_only_a_finished_turn_supplies_the_answer` (S2, 빈 종료 턴·도구 호출 중 종료) | 답이 `잠시 확인하겠습니다` | 종료된 assistant 턴의 텍스트만, 마지막 종료 턴이 비면 `""` |
| D4 | 재-crawl이 `000-*.md`를 덮어씀 | `test_a_crawl_never_writes_into_a_folder_that_already_has_files`(manifest 있음/없음), `test_crawls_without_out_each_get_their_own_folder` | 종료 0으로 기존 파일 교체, 기본 경로 공유 | 비어 있지 않은 `--out`은 작업 전 `bad_arguments`, 기본 경로는 `crawls/<host>/<타임스탬프>/` 예약, 번호 붙은 이름을 저장 시점에 결정(나중 rename 제거) |
| D5 | run·세션·자식 id가 레지스트리 밖 경로를 가리킬 수 있음 | `test_a_run_id_that_names_a_path_outside_the_registry_is_refused`(status·log·result·show·stop), `test_resume_does_not_continue_a_session_named_by_a_path`, `test_a_child_id_that_is_not_an_id_is_not_followed` | 바깥 meta를 읽고 `stop`이 바깥 meta에 씀, 바깥 세션을 재개, `../escaped`를 자식으로 추적 | `_errors.is_safe_id` 한 판정을 run id 해석·세션 확인·자식 id 추출이 공용 |
| D6 | 레지스트리 런(abandoned) 재개가 실시간 세션 검사를 건너뜀 | `test_an_abandoned_run_whose_session_is_still_working_is_not_resumed` | 살아 있는 턴에 붙는 재개가 수락됨(종료 0) | 어떤 경로로 고른 세션이든 `_resumable_session` 검사 |
| D7 | `map`이 탐색 실패를 숨김 | `test_map_reports_what_it_could_not_read`, `test_map_that_read_nothing_exits_empty`, `test_map_says_when_a_budget_or_the_cap_cut_discovery_short`, `test_map_from_a_sitemap_says_so` | 커버리지 없음, 아무것도 못 읽어도 root 하나로 종료 0 | `coverage`(sitemap 여부·읽은 페이지 수·놓친 페이지·예산 초과·상한 도달)를 map·crawl 응답에 포함, 아무것도 못 읽으면 종료 5 |
| D8 | HTML을 저장했는데 종료 4 / 빈 본문인데 `ok` | `test_a_file_that_was_written_counts_as_success`, `test_an_empty_body_is_not_a_page_that_was_read`(markdown·plain) | 저장했는데 종료 4, 빈 본문이 `ok` | 파일을 쓴 항목은 성공으로 셈(상태는 그대로 페이지 판정), 빈 텍스트 본문은 `shell` + `the response body is empty` |
| D9 | 자식 출처 병합이 `opened`·id를 잃음 | `test_what_a_child_read_is_evidence_of_the_run` | 자식이 연 URL이 `opened: false`, 자식 id 인용 미해석, `show --source <자식 id>` 실패 | URL 병합 시 `opened`는 OR, `ids`에 모든 id 보존, 인용·`show --source`가 모든 id로 해석 |
| D10 | 잘못된 커서·manifest 모양·저장 OSError가 트레이스백 | `test_a_cursor_that_is_not_one_is_refused_rather_than_replayed`(5종), `test_a_manifest_of_the_wrong_shape_is_refused`(3종), `test_an_unwritable_destination_is_reported_in_json`, `test_an_unwritable_registry_is_reported_in_json` | `ValueError`·`AttributeError`·`OSError`·`PermissionError` 트레이스백, 쓰레기 커서는 조용히 처음부터 재생 | 커서 엄격 해석(`bad_arguments`), manifest 모양 검사(`bad_arguments`), `main`에서 OSError를 `run_failed` JSON으로 |
| D11 | 동일 출처 판정이 netloc만 비교 | `test_same_site_means_same_scheme_host_and_port_over_http` | `ftp://site.test/…`가 sitemap 결과에 포함 | `_crawl.origin`(scheme·host·port, http(s)만)을 sitemap 필터·링크 순회·`resolve_links`가 공용 |
| D12 | `stop`이 대기 중 정상 완료된 런을 abandoned로 덮어씀 | `test_stop_never_overwrites_a_run_that_finished_while_it_waited` (S2) | 최종 상태 `abandoned` | 어떤 종료 상태든 도달하면 대기 종료, 종료 상태는 덮어쓰지 않음 |
| D13 | heartbeat의 children이 전체 자식 수 | `test_heartbeat_counts_only_the_children_still_working` | `children=2`(하나는 끝남) | 이 턴의 비종료 자식만 셈 |
| D14 | doctor REPL 왕복이 `{ok:true}`·종료 코드를 안 봄, 고정 `.write-probe` | `test_a_repl_that_answers_without_running_the_probe_fails_doctor`, `test_the_writability_probe_cannot_collide_with_what_is_already_there` | 거부 응답에도 통과, 같은 이름 디렉터리가 있으면 쓰기 가능한 폴더를 불가로 판정 | 정확히 `{"ok": true}`와 종료 0을 확인, 쓰기 검사는 `mkstemp` 고유 이름 |

리뷰에서 추가로 고친 것(모두 재현 테스트 먼저):

| 발견 | 재현 테스트 | 수정 |
|---|---|---|
| `--max-urls` 도달 뒤 같은 라운드의 실패 기록을 버림 | `test_a_miss_after_the_cap_is_reached_is_still_reported` | 상한 뒤에도 라운드의 기록을 끝까지 읽음 |
| REPL 120초 강제 종료가 커버리지에서 사라짐 | `test_a_discovery_snippet_cut_off_by_the_repl_limit_is_reported`(links·sitemap) | 부분 출력에 `hit_budget: true` 종료 레코드를 덧붙임 |
| sitemap 스니펫이 자체 예산으로 멈춰도 알리지 않음 | node 하네스(가짜 fetch)로 완료 `false`·중단 `true` 확인 | `sitemap.js`가 `hit_budget`을 실음 |
| 재사용 자식의 이전 턴 답을 현재 답으로 붙임 | `test_a_reused_childs_earlier_answer_is_not_its_answer_now` (S2) | 답은 마지막 user 뒤에서만 찾음 |
| 재개 부모가 이전 자식에게 새 과제를 줄 때 이전 과제의 사용량·출처·로그가 섞임 | `test_a_child_reused_by_a_resumed_run_counts_only_its_new_task` | 자식 전사를 이 턴 시작 이후의 첫 프롬프트부터 읽음(result·status·show·log 공용) |
| 빈 webfetch가 검색 발췌를 가림(이 PR의 회귀) | `test_an_empty_read_does_not_hide_what_a_search_already_showed` | 빈 본문이면 발췌로 대체 |
| href 하나의 잘못된 IPv6 괄호로 map 전체가 트레이스백 | `test_one_malformed_link_does_not_lose_the_rest_of_the_page` | 그 링크만 건너뜀 |
| href의 `&` 등 문자 참조 미해석 | `test_an_escaped_ampersand_in_a_link_is_the_url_the_page_meant` | 브라우저의 속성값 규칙대로 해석(`_repl._decode_attribute`) |
| 빈 텍스트로 변환되는 문서(빈 CSV)가 `ok` | `test_a_document_that_converts_to_nothing_is_not_a_page_that_was_read` | `unsupported` |
| manifest `root` 타입, 비ASCII 숫자 커서(`²`), 명시적 포트 0 | 기존 파라미터 테스트에 입력 추가 | 각각 거부·거부·기본 포트와 구분 |

가짜 Aside 추가: `FAKE_ASIDE_RESUME_LATE`(재개 턴 전체가 프로세스 종료 뒤 도착), `FAKE_ASIDE_REPL_PROBE=fail`(샌드박스가 왕복을 거부), links 경로의 `__hit_budget__`, sitemap·links 경로의 `__timeout__`(120초 강제 종료).

## 왜

재구성 계획의 감사에서 확인된 결함들이다. 대부분이 "조사 결과로 보고되는 것이 실제로 이 런이 확보한 것인가"(D1·D2·D3·D9·D13)와 "저장된 것을 잃거나 잘못 쓰지 않는가"(D4·D5·D8·D10·D12)에 걸린다. 증거 범위를 명령마다 따로 계산하던 것이 D1·D9의 뿌리라서, 한 뷰(`_evidence.Turn`)로 모았다.

## 영향

- 응답 필드 추가: `result`·`search` 출처의 `ids`, `show`의 `source.ids`, `map`·`crawl`의 `coverage`.
- 빈 텍스트로 변환되는 문서는 `unsupported`, 탐색 스니펫이 끊기면 `coverage.budget_exhausted`.
- 동작 변화: 재개 턴이 관측되지 않으면 `completed_unstructured`, 빈 텍스트 응답은 `shell`(auto면 탭 승격 대상), `--format html`로 파일을 쓰면 종료 0, 비어 있지 않은 `--out`으로 crawl 거부, 기본 crawl 경로가 타임스탬프 하위 폴더, 커서가 아닌 `--since` 거부.

## 검증

- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → `234 passed, 14 skipped in 309.82s` (PR① 머지 시점 `182 passed, 14 skipped`)
- 결함마다 재현 테스트를 먼저 돌려 의도한 이유로 실패하는 것을 확인한 뒤 고쳤다(위 표의 "수정 전 실패" 열이 그때의 실제 출력).
- codex(gpt-6-astra high, 읽기 전용) 리뷰 5회, 같은 스레드를 이어 가며 앞 회차 수정의 확인과 회귀만 묻는 식으로 범위를 좁혔다.
  1. 13개 커밋 전체: 일상 사용에서 도달 가능한 CONFIRMED 5건, 기타 3건, PLAUSIBLE 1건(빈 문서 변환 — 실물 변환기에서 빈 CSV가 종료 0·빈 출력임을 확인해 재현). 9건 모두 반영.
  2. 9건 수정 확인. 이 PR 이전부터 있던 도달 가능 결함 3건(sitemap 자체 예산, 재사용 자식의 이전 과제, `&`) 추가 발견 → 반영.
  3. 2건 수정 확인. 재사용 자식 규칙의 빈틈 1건과 `html.unescape`가 `&copy=2`를 바꾸는 회귀 1건 → 반영.
  4. 2건 수정 확인. 내가 넣은 "새 프롬프트 전까지 재사용 자식을 비우는" 규칙이 재개로 늦은 자식 결과를 수거하는 흐름을 깨뜨린 회귀, 세미콜론 없는 숫자 참조 → 규칙을 되돌리고(남는 짧은 창은 `_evidence._from`에 `성진:` 주석으로 기록) 속성 규칙대로 해석.
  5. 2건 수정 확인, 새 회귀 없음. 해석기 경계 2건(`¬ebook;=2`, `&copy한글`) → 반영하고, 이후는 리뷰를 더 돌리는 대신 독립 판정자로 검증했다: 설치된 HTML 파서 linkedom이 해석한 속성값과 16개 입력에서 16개 일치.
- 수용한 한계: 재개 부모가 이전 자식에게 새 과제를 준 직후, 그 새 프롬프트가 전사에 보이기 전의 짧은 창에서는 자식의 이전 과제가 이 런의 것으로 보인다(`_evidence._from`의 `성진:` 주석).

body:
Fixes https://github.com/tenstorrent/ttnn-visualizer/issues/2044.

This pull request refactors the toast notification exit animation to fix a bug where toasts were not properly unmounted due to the use of `display: none`, which prevented the `animationend` event from firing. The transition logic is now encapsulated in a new module, and related styles and tests have been updated to ensure correct behavior.

**Toast notification exit animation fix and refactor:**

* Moved the toast transition configuration to a new `toastTransition.ts` module, replacing the previous inline definition in `Layout.tsx`. The new config uses an exit class (`toast-exit-immediate`) with a 1ms animation duration to ensure `animationend` fires and toasts are unmounted correctly. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c57554feeb357eca471f5ce867860a89ee4adec38783c27fb8b165b7f3a566d2R1-R16)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d72ac54801a218d7cfd27d169a7724d8c041bba5f6ba18e501670faab655a4L8-R13)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d72ac54801a218d7cfd27d169a7724d8c041bba5f6ba18e501670faab655a4L24-L31)`)
* Removed the `.no-toast-animation` class and its usage, which previously hid toasts with `display: none` but caused unmounting issues. (`[src/scss/_common.scssL22-L27](diffhunk://#diff-3088c098c5b26094adbafed7ffd65bc0bb10ed0c15a361b11e09688d9db9dcfdL22-L27)`)
* Updated the SCSS to add the `.toast-exit-immediate` class with a 1ms animation duration, ensuring compatibility across browsers and proper event firing. (`[src/scss/components/ToastOverrides.scssR16-R20](diffhunk://#diff-a08d4e5fa3f07008dc20cf604f452f6d0f1660f73b54cd6f1d1cf7ecc7e73c07R16-R20)`)

**Testing improvements:**

* Added and updated tests in `Layout.spec.tsx` to verify the new toast exit transition logic and confirm that toasts are properly unmounted after the exit animation. (`[tests/Layout.spec.tsxR185-R239](diffhunk://#diff-4324337fb65b1c366ca800a2bef540bfb3d1af491cd1170ac70507078ffa7d61R185-R239)`)
* Added a new test file `toastTransitionStyles.spec.ts` to assert that the exit styles do not use `display: none` and that the `.toast-exit-immediate` class has the correct animation duration. (`[tests/toastTransitionStyles.spec.tsR1-R28](diffhunk://#diff-50a2373a0472a544dcbd066116e79ee6ce29aa98b5ae266edc3ae12634ccb309R1-R28)`)

author: alexander-bain
body:
Refs #8427 (issue stays open until the after-check on production).

**Reader-visible:** on Alex's TestFlight build 20, typing `superbowl` or `nfl superbowl winner` shows **No Results**, while `super bowl` finds **NFL Super Bowl Winner** (86832). Reproduced today with HTTP 200 and empty futures on both `/api/events/search` and `/api/events/typeahead`. After this change, the joined spelling finds the market on full search and in suggestions.

**Change:** one entry in `_SEARCH_TERM_SYNONYMS`: `"superbowl": "super bowl"`, one-way. Both routes already apply this table as an ORed ILIKE plus rank expansion, the same mechanism as `champion`↔`winner` and `fired`→`head coach`. There is no fuzzy matching or global widening; only that one token gains a second spelling. It goes in the token table rather than `_QUERY_PHRASE_ALIASES`, because that table requires multi-word aliases.

**Gates:**
- `tests/integration/test_search_superbowl_joined_pg_8427.py` runs through the real route on real Postgres (CI job `search-recall`; run locally with the PG14 shim, **10 passed**, not skipped). It covers the spaced control, the 4 joined variants (`superbowl`, `nfl superbowl winner`, `superbowl winner`, `Superbowl`) on both routes, and unrelated words (`superbowlx`, `stanley cup`) that must stay empty. **Strawman:** with the entry removed, 8 fail and 2 pass (the control and the unrelated-word case).
- `tests/test_search_superbowl_synonym_8427.py` is a no-database pin that runs on the ordinary shards: 2 passed; with the entry removed, 1 fails.
- Search/typeahead band + startup: **3184 passed**, 1 skipped, exit 0. The only red during the run was my own new test's wrong assumption (`super` already folds to `süper` for Süper Lig), which I fixed in the test.

Class: search recall vocabulary, no data writes, no migration, not a heavy task.



**Update (ded2fa99):** `tests/test_pg_gated_tests_are_named_in_ci.py` correctly refused the new Postgres gate as unwired, so I added a `search-recall` step beside #6977 with the same skip detector. CI on the exact sha is `completed/success`; the new step ran **10 passed**, not skipped. CodeQL flags one note, `py/import-and-import-from` (no security severity), on the test's model-registration import, the same pattern as the template.

author: itzmuff1n
body:
## What this does

Rewrites `docs/TOPICS.md` §2/§3 and adds `docs/templates/child-brief.md`.

**T2 of the Pipeline v2 plan — #69.**

## The change

§2 used to say *"The Lead does not write product code."* It now says the Lead
writes it, in pieces of ≤200 lines, building after each, with the tests in the
same commit.

§3 stops describing **builder children** and describes **report-producing
children** instead: a blind attack (§4) or recon, briefed from
`docs/templates/child-brief.md`, each carrying an `output_schema`.

## Why — the evidence, from this repo

Topic #38, 19 Sep 2026, measured from `session_model_usage`:

| child | tokens | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `20260919_162616_375b76` | 3.07M | `agent_close` after `max_iterations` |
| `20260919_164104_bd6edb` | 2.75M | `agent_close` after `max_iterations` |
| **together** | **5.82M** | for **one commit** |

One of the two reported killing a process that did not exist. The Lead finished
the task alone.

The lesson kept in the file is not "children are bad" — it is that **a child
which cannot bank partial progress does not get more done with a bigger budget,
it fails for longer.** That reasoning is not overturned. What is overturned is
the conclusion drawn from it: that the remedy was more child machinery.

## Removed, and why it is not replaced

The **"delegation upgrades"** this routine used to assume — a worktree per child,
commit-after-each-green-step — are gone. They existed for one reason: to make a
*builder child* survivable across an iteration cap. With no builder child there
is nothing for them to protect. The plan issue #65 and milestone #2 "Delegation
upgrades" that specified them were closed as superseded for the same reason.

`delegation.max_iterations` stays **50**. The old precondition ("may not be
raised until worktree-per-child and commit-after-each-step exist") was written
against the builder-child split and does not survive it; the cap is now simply
the cap, and raising it is a separate decision.

## Also in this commit

- **§4**: "never alongside a builder" → "never alongside another child", since
  there is no builder for a blind attack to run alongside.
- **§6**: parking now names the **`parked`** label (created 24 Sep 2026, colour
  `#d4c5f9`). The goal gate that T4 adds reads it, so the label has to be the
  mechanism, not the word "parked" in prose.

## Honest limits recorded in the file, not just here

The `output_schema` **does not** protect against the wrong-summary trap. It is
applied to a child's *final* answer, so a child that ran out of room still
returns a well-formed summary of unfinished work — the schema gives that summary
a shape. The template says so explicitly: the transcript is the evidence.

## Checks

- `scripts/check.sh` — **passes locally** on this commit (ran in full: fmt,
  build, test, clippy, deny; `=== all checks passed ===`).
- CI on this commit: see the checks below.

Refs #69

author: dhyabi2
body:
## What was wrong

The install block in `## Using it` is the only instruction a reader has. Its first two commands both fail.

**1. The clone URL answers 403.**

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -L https://github.com/PANDeveloper001/agent-runtime
403
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -L https://github.com/dhyabi2/agent-runtime
200
```

A reader who copies line one never gets a checkout, and has nothing to debug with.

**2. `pip install -q ''   # stdlib only` is not true of the tree it installs.**

`hub.py:32` opens with `from websockets.asyncio.server import serve`. `websockets` is not in the
standard library and is not anywhere in this repository:

```
$ python3 -c "import hub"
  File "hub.py", line 32, in <module>
    from websockets.asyncio.server import serve
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'websockets'
```

So the README's venv cannot run the live feed, and the failure arrives much later — at the one
command that starts it — rather than at the install step that caused it.

The claim is right about everything else: the agent, modeld, the guard, the journal and the secret
scan really are stdlib only. The README now says exactly that and installs the one dependency that
exists.

## The laws, shown failing then passing

Both are derived from the tree rather than restated from it, so they stay true after the next
dependency or the next rename. `test_every_dependency_the_code_has_is_one_the_readme_installs` walks
every `.py` file with `ast`, subtracts `sys.stdlib_module_names` and this checkout's own modules, and
requires the README to name whatever is left.

Against the **old** README:

```
FAIL: test_the_clone_url_names_the_repository_this_is
AssertionError: 'PANDeveloper001/agent-runtime' != 'dhyabi2/agent-runtime'

FAIL: test_every_dependency_the_code_has_is_one_the_readme_installs
AssertionError: Lists differ: ['websockets'] != []

Ran 2 tests ... FAILED (failures=2)
```

Against the **new** README: `Ran 2 tests ... OK`.

## Whole suite

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` -> **Ran 59 tests, OK**.

## Deliberately not fixed here

The rest of the install block also disagrees with the units it ships, and fixing it changes how a
deployed agent starts, so it is left for someone who knows the live boxes:

| README says | `systemd/` ships |
|---|---|
| `systemctl enable --now agent-modeld.service agent@a01.timer` | `swarm-modeld.service`, `swarm-agent@.timer` — the names in the README do not exist |
| `git clone ... /opt/agent` | `ExecStart=/opt/swarm/venv/bin/python /opt/swarm/swarm/agent.py` |
| `install -d /srv/agents/a01` | `WorkingDirectory=/srv/swarm/%i`, `SWARM_AGENT_HOME=/srv/swarm/%i` |

The unit's `ExecStart` also names a directory this repository does not ship: the runtime is published
as `runtime/`, and the unit looks for `swarm/`.

Recorded in `audits/agent-runtime-2026-09-24.md`.

author: threeebs
claude[bot]
body:
## What does this change?

Before: the no-install download was a zip holding a folder of files. Starting Webcam Bridge opened a terminal window with the TUI plus a browser tab for the dashboard. At 1080p with background blur and face touch-up on, one frame took ~70 ms (~14 fps).

After: releases ship `WebcamBridge-<version>-portable.exe`, one file you double-click. adb and the Android app are inside it. The app, installed or portable, opens the dashboard in its own window with no terminal, and closing that window quits it. The same 1080p frame now takes ~36 ms (~28 fps).

How:
- `packaging/pyinstaller/webcam-bridge.spec` builds the installer's folder and the single-file exe from one analysis, and both are windowed. The single file unpacks to a temp folder each time it starts, so adb gets copied to the data folder before its daemon starts (`adb.unpack_bundled`). The APK is read from the bundle.
- `ui.py` opens the window with pywebview (WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS). If no window can open it falls back to the browser, and on Linux it always uses the browser. `--browser` keeps the old behaviour.
- CLI commands (`doctor`, `camera`, `fetch`, `--version`) print to the terminal they were started from. When there isn't one, such as the Start-menu troubleshoot shortcut, they open a console and wait for Enter. The windowed app writes its output to `webcam-bridge.log`, and startup errors show a message box.
- Starting the app while it is already running opens the running dashboard instead of failing on the port.
- The FFmpeg subprocesses use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, so they don't flash console windows from the windowed app.
- The dependency is now `opencv-contrib-python`, the OpenCV build MediaPipe itself requires. Before, both OpenCV builds got installed into the same `cv2` folder.
- Frame processor: the background blur/replace and touch-up blends use `cv2.blendLinear` on 2-D weights precomputed in the segmenter thread, replacing NumPy float math on 3-channel masks. BGR→RGB uses `cv2.cvtColor` instead of a strided copy, and touch-up writes its face crop in place instead of copying the frame. Profiling showed these as the slowest steps; FFmpeg decoding itself is ~5 ms per 1080p frame.

## How was it tested?

- `pytest` (66 passed) and `ruff check .`. New tests cover CLI detection, the running-instance check, unpacking bundled adb and finding the bundled APK.
- Built both variants locally with PyInstaller on Linux. `packaging/smoke_test.py` passes on both (version, doctor, model fetch, MediaPipe background blur and touch-up in the frame processor). The portable build unpacked its bundled adb, found its bundled APK, and a second launch detected the running instance.
- Frame processor, before and after, run on a real face image with blur and touch-up on, on one 2.1 GHz Xeon core: 1080p went from 70 ms to 36 ms per frame and 720p from 26 ms to 16 ms. The new blend's output differs from the old one by at most 1 level per channel (rounding vs truncation).
- Not yet verified: the Windows window itself. CI now runs `webcam-bridge _window-test` (a hidden WebView2 window) on both the installer build and the portable exe.

## Checklist

- [x] `pytest` and `ruff check .` pass (desktop changes)
- [ ] The Android app builds (Android changes): no Android changes
- [x] Docs / README updated if behaviour changed
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated under **Unreleased**
- [ ] Any new assets are my own work or MIT-compatible and listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: no new assets

author: waelhe
body:
Root cause (measured, not inferred): main's own CI run failed on the same commit `b9432d9` that had been green ten hours earlier (02:47 UTC), with `AuthorizationServerLoginGateIntegrationTest` reporting 3 failures (last-admin gate 200 instead of 409, two consent-page mismatches). The only measured difference between the green and red runs is test-class execution order — Maven pins no `runOrder` in the root pom, so the class ran at position 264 in one run and 266 in the other, preceded by a different class. (`event_publication does not exist` is a red herring: 5 occurrences in the green log, 0 in the red one.)

Those classes run against the workflow's shared PostgreSQL service, so they read and write the auth tables (`auth_users`, `auth_authorities`, `oauth2_registered_client`, `oauth2_authorization_consent`) left behind by whichever class ran before them. A leftover admin row from `PublicPkceClientGateIntegrationTest` is exactly what turns the last-admin guard off.

**Corrected measurement (this PR's second edition — supersedes the first edition's "66 already use the pattern / 6 violators" claim, which the review finding exposed as wrong):** the measured split is **54 owners / 18 silent borrowers**. The 18 carried `@Testcontainers` as text with no `@Container` field at all and were still on the workflow's shared PostgreSQL through the test profile's `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432` default:
- 6 classes with neither annotation text (the measured incident path — fixed in the first edition)
- 17 `@ApplicationModuleTest` module slices (admin, availability, booking, catalog, disputes, identity, ledger, media x3, messaging, notifications, payments, pricing, provider, reviews, search)
- `ReviewsTwoWayIntegrationTest`, a full `@SpringBootTest` that writes users/reviews/provider_profiles through the real AFTER_COMMIT event flow

## What the four commits do

1. **`901a844`** — the six measured violators get the container pair (`@Container @ServiceConnection` on `postgis/postgis:18-3.6-alpine` + `redis:8-alpine`), the pattern the 54 established owners already use.
2. **`8f54aae`** — the review finding adopted root-cause: **all 18 hidden borrowers get the same container pair**, and **the gate goes structural** — ArchUnit imports the *compiled* test classes and requires, per `*IntegrationTest` class, a class-level `@Testcontainers` AND an actual `@Container` field annotated `@ServiceConnection` whose raw type is assignable to `PostgreSQLContainer`. Annotation text can no longer satisfy the gate: neither a lone `@Testcontainers`, nor a commented-out `@Container`, nor a redis-only container. `@ApplicationModuleTest` receives `@ServiceConnection` through the same TestContext machinery as `@SpringBootTest` — the Modulith reference ("Testing") documents the annotation as "a replacement for `@SpringBootTest`… sliced by application module", and the Spring Boot reference ("Testing: Testcontainers") defines the field-level `@ServiceConnection` contract (the container contributes the `ConnectionDetails` consumed by auto-configuration). TDD: the strengthened gate reports exactly those 18 classes on the pre-fix tree and zero after (72/72; CI compiles and runs it as the authority).
4. **`0f9b527`** — the structural guard's first CI catch (measured, deterministic in both jobs): exactly six classes still failed the assignability check — `ai×3`, `geo`, `reviews×2`. Their source text is identical to the 66 passing classes; the difference is the import: the deprecated location `org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer` vs the canonical `org.testcontainers.postgresql.PostgreSQLContainer` (Testcontainers 2.0.5's module-package layout — the same relocation that produced the "uses or override a deprecated API" compile note pinned to AiDeepSeekProviderSelectionIntegrationTest.java). The migration to the canonical import is what the deprecation already prescribes — no behavior change, and one import location for all 72 classes.

3. **`b18a104`** (cherry-picked from `docs/yelp-level-plan`) — the container-scan CVE gate fails **any** fresh build right now on `libexpat CVE-2026-93990` (HIGH, fixed 2.8.4-r0 → 2.8.5-r0); the Dockerfile's own documented prescription for a fixable finding is the date-token bump (`os-pkgs-refresh 2026-09-09` → `2026-09-24`), which re-runs `apk upgrade` against the fresh index. An `.trivyignore.yaml` entry would be wrong here — the policy file reserves entries for findings with NO fix published.

AGENTS.md (Testing) already requires `@Testcontainers`/`@Container` on every integration test; with this PR **every `*IntegrationTest` class owns its PostgreSQL**, so the suite's result no longer depends on class execution order at all — the property the 2026-09-24 incident demanded. Spring Boot 4.1.1 reference, Testcontainers: "A single test container instance can, and often is, retained across execution of tests from multiple test classes" — isolation therefore comes from per-class ownership, not from ordering.

Deliberately NOT done:
- pinning `<runOrder>` — it would make CI reproducible while leaving the shared state in place (hide the defect, not remove it)
- removing the workflow's shared postgres/redis services — they are now unreferenced by the suite, but their removal is a CI-infra change with its own measurement (the test-profile datasource defaults remain a valid local-dev fallback)

Zero production code, zero schema, zero config (beyond the Dockerfile CVE token), zero dependency changes. The two `marketplace-edge` `*IT` classes keep their in-place documented exception (zero containers by design, WireMock in-process).

Merge by user word only.

body:
Follow-up to dxos/dxos#13412. The merge queue merged it seconds after CodeRabbit's review posted, before these fixes landed. All four come from that review.

- **The caption banner survived a `cut`.** It is page DOM, so it stayed in every later frame even though its timeline entry was dropped. `cut` now removes it and waits for a repaint, then waits for that frame to reach the recorder, and only then cuts. The frame the recorder keeps as the new first frame is therefore clean.
- **The first `goto` waited for nothing on the 1x fallback.** Without a full ffmpeg the recorder can't drop frames, yet `goto` still waited up to 3 minutes for the ready selector. It now returns `boot: {cut: false, reason}` immediately.
- **A frame painted before a cut could land after it.** Frames are now dated by the browser's presentation `timestamp` rather than delivery time, and any frame older than the current start is dropped.
- **`--ready` docs** now state that the selector's first match is the element waited on.

body:
Closes arch-review **D3**. A user asked for more ribbon icons. This takes the chance to rebuild the ribbon editor and bar properly, and gives each button its own icon, colours and shape.

## What users get
- **Icons.** A searchable picker covering about 110 emoji plus every Fluent UI System Icon in both faces, regular and filled (5,700+ in all). The icons come from Microsoft's single MIT-licensed "Resizable" font. An icon is saved by its set and name, never by code point, because upstream renumbers code points between releases.
- **Colours.** Each button has three colour slots: icon and text, background, and border (with an outline weight).
  - Every slot can be the theme default, a `Swatch.*` token that keeps following the theme, or any custom colour.
  - The shared `ColorPicker` offers a saturation/value square with hue and alpha strips, hex and R/G/B/A entry, a screen eyedropper, and the colours already used on the ribbon.
  - The editor shows a WCAG readability check.
  - Theme-default text on a custom background switches to whichever of the theme's text or page colour reads better on it.
- **Shapes.** Standard, Rounded, Pill and Leaf frame the whole button. Circle, Squircle and Hexagon draw a badge behind the icon.
- **Quick edit.** Right-click → Recolour (icon and text / background / border), Change icon and Shape all use the same shared pickers.

## Structure
- **Editor.** `RibbonEditorViewModel` works on a deep-cloned draft, and Done commits it with a single save. The view is `InitializeComponent` plus a width. Cards are `ListBoxItem`s, so journeys can select them, and three ids leave the journey ratchet.
- **One button visual.** `RibbonItemButton` is the only button the bar, the editor strip and the shape gallery draw. Frame geometry is rebuilt only when the button's size changes; badge geometry is frozen and shared.
- **New shared controls.** `Visuals.Common` gains `SearchBox`, `ColorPicker`, `ScreenEyedropper`, `DragReorder` and `ColorSpec`. The new `Nexaflow.Visuals.Icons` project holds the font, `IconCatalog`, `IconGlyph` and `IconPicker`.
- **Saved layout.** `ribbon.json` now has the shape `{ "Version": 2, "Items": [...] }`, and a v1 bare array still reads, with its `AccentColor` becoming the Foreground. This is one-way: a build older than this one falls back to the default ribbon when it meets a v2 file.

## Performance
The ribbon is in every window and edited rarely, so drawing it is what was optimised:
- Each item's button is built once and re-parented between layout passes, not rebuilt. The widths of the preferred and all-compact layouts are cached, so a window resize costs a comparison.
- Buttons use only `TemplateBinding`s; there are no per-button bindings or converters.
- The context menu and overflow entries are built only when they open.
- The Fluent name map is streamed into a glyph lookup only if a Fluent icon is actually on the ribbon. The sorted list a picker searches is built only when a picker first opens.
- The editor view, and the pickers inside it, exist only while the editor is open.

## Also
- `ThirdPartyNotices.md` gains rows for Fluent UI System Icons (MIT) and Bravura (OFL-1.1), which was already bundled but missing.
- The product tree is updated (new nodes, snaplinks re-pointed, `i18n` for the ribbon editor marked done). The pending snaplinks are in `docs/product/pending/`.
- Updated docs: `arch_review_2026-07.md` (D3 closed), `Architecture.md`, `theming.md` (`ColorSpec`, `Ribbon.HoverOverlay`) and `localization.md`.

## Tests
- `dotnet build Nexaflow.slnx`: clean.
- `Tests.Core` Unit: 376 pass. New tests cover v1→v2 migration and round-trip, the editor draft rules, shape geometry, and the shipped defaults.
- `Tests.Visuals`: 50 pass. New tests cover `ColorSpec`, HSV and contrast maths, the icon catalog (every Fluent glyph is present in the font) and the picker view-model.
- `Tests.Features.Architecture`: 45 pass, including journey coverage and the modal ratchet.
- `ShellChromeJourneyTests` passes. It now selects cards, moves and deletes them, searches for and picks a Fluent icon, sets swatch and outline colours, picks a shape, and resets the look.
- Driven by hand in the app against an isolated config folder: styled several buttons, pressed Done, checked the live ribbon and the saved v2 `ribbon.json`, and used right-click → Recolour.

author: amirmfth
body:
## Summary
Adds persisted, streaming German conversation practice and secret-objective vocabulary missions on one shared learning engine. Also fixes all four automated review findings from merged PR #45.

### Fixes from PR #45 review
- Vocabulary Universe topic-pack nodes are now scoped to the current user.
- Comparison structured output now requires exactly one production prompt for each side.
- ConfusionPair counters update atomically inside a transaction.
- Mistake semantic refresh now reports per-item rebuild failures instead of incorrectly saying the index is current.

### Shared conversation engine
New persisted models:
- ConversationSession
- ConversationMessage
- ConversationTarget

Session state stores:
- practice vs mission
- CEFR/target level
- scenario
- AI role
- optional mission objective
- target visibility
- full persisted message history
- target usage counts / successful usage counts
- structured final evaluation
- completion state

### Target selection
Conversation targets are selected deterministically from:
1. explicitly selected topic-pack/collection
2. active Focus Session targets
3. weakest production/context vocabulary

Targets remain canonical Lexeme IDs.

### Compact AI context selector
The tutor receives only:
- session goal/scenario/role/objective
- target lexical units + lexical patterns
- related known lexical units
- recent unresolved target-related mistakes
- learner level
- translation preference
- recent conversation turns

It does not receive the whole vocabulary database.

### Conversation practice
New routes:
- `/conversation`
- `/conversation/[id]`

Features:
- optional topic/situation
- optional collection targeting
- 3 / 5 / 7 target lexical units
- AI-generated level-aware scenario and opening
- streaming Responses API chat UX
- persisted learner + assistant messages
- target usage progress shown live
- natural target elicitation instead of explicitly demanding vocabulary
- brief relevant corrections without derailing the conversation
- resumable conversation history

### Per-turn evaluation
Each learner turn receives a separate structured target-usage evaluation:
- whether each target was actually used
- correctness
- lexical score
- actionable target-specific feedback
- article/case/preposition/reflexive/collocation/word-choice/form/spelling mistakes
- optional concise correction for the tutor response

Used targets create real Attempt rows.

Correct/incorrect usage updates:
- production
- contextual usage
- ConversationTarget usage counters

Mistakes feed into the existing Mistake Memory model.
Semantic mistake embedding is deferred to the explicit refresh flow so chat latency is not inflated by extra embedding calls.

### Streaming tutor
`POST /api/conversation/[id]/message`

- Node runtime
- persists learner message first
- turn evaluation fails gracefully instead of destroying chat
- streams `response.output_text.delta` text to the UI
- persists completed assistant response
- records OpenAI usage after stream completion
- records errors in usage telemetry
- 4,000-character per-message guardrail

### Secret-objective missions
New route:
- `/missions`

Mission generation includes:
- scenario
- AI role
- concrete conversational objective
- German opening
- selected target lexical units

Mission options:
- show target words explicitly
- hide target words for secret-objective mode

The tutor stays in role and does not declare success prematurely.

### End-of-session evaluation
Conversation and mission completion produces structured evaluation:
- task/mission success
- overall score
- grammar
- naturalness
- vocabulary
- strengths
- improvement areas
- target-by-target:
  - used/missed
  - correct/needs work
  - naturalness
  - note

Final target results are normalized against persisted target IDs so model output cannot invent or omit canonical targets.

Completion also persists contextual Encounter records for the session's target vocabulary.

### Replay / new session
Completed sessions support:
- replay with the same role/scenario/targets
- start a fresh conversation
- start a fresh mission

### UI
- Conversation and Missions added to desktop Explore navigation
- both surfaced from Home on mobile
- existing four-tab mobile bottom navigation remains unchanged
- mobile-first streamed message layout
- sticky composer
- explicit streaming state
- start/evaluate/replay pending states
- failure states
- mission objective card
- live target progress
- structured completion dashboard

### Migration
`20260925021500_conversation_missions`

Adds:
- ConversationKind
- ConversationStatus
- ConversationRole
- ConversationSession
- ConversationMessage
- ConversationTarget

### Issues
Completes #16 and #17.
Further progresses #30 and #31.

### Verification
Repository-level static/type-oriented review was performed through the GitHub connector. A full local dependency install/lint/build was not available in the current execution environment.

O editor rola dentro do seu próprio contêiner (.mosaico-app, overflow-y:auto + scroll-snap-type próprio), não a página inteira - isso quebrava o cálculo de posição do react-joyride de duas formas: o scroll-snap nativo brigava com a rolagem programática do tour (desligado só em modo edição via CSS, não afeta a leitura pública), e o próprio cálculo de "rolar até o alvo" do react-joyride pra esse tipo de contêiner ("custom scroll parent") é bem menos confiável que o de página normal. Erro de hidratação (console) nos campos contentEditable (nome, frase, endereço) do editor - causa comum e documentada desse padrão (o conteúdo pode ser alterado fora do React, por extensão de navegador etc). author: janicduplessis
body:
## Description

Windows CI intermittently fails `gc.test.ts` > "EAS orphan session sweep" >
"dry run does not wait behind an active remote session creation lock",
which asserts the dry run returns in under 500 ms. It failed on `main` in
run 36041519085 (job 107774581842) with an observed 1028 ms.

Across roughly 111 Windows runs, `gc.test.ts` shows one random 0.3-2.0 s
scheduling stall per run on `windows-latest`, landing on a different
EAS-sweep test each time; tests that normally take 20-80 ms stall to
1.6-2.0 s. This assertion had failed only this once in 500 runs since
2026-09-11, consistent with runner noise rather than a product regression:
the timed code path cannot itself wait, since the dry run sets
`EAS_LOCK_WAIT_MS = 0` and fails fast on a held claim instead of waiting.

## Solution

Loosen the bound from 500 ms to 5,000 ms. That is still tight enough to
catch a real regression, where the dry run waits for
`withRemoteSessionLock`'s 4-minute default instead of failing fast, while
clearing the 2.0 s worst-case stall observed on Windows CI.

## Test plan

- `pnpm test packages/stim-cli/src/__tests__/gc.test.ts`: 151 passed.
- `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run knip`: all pass.

Closes #1040
