author: tas50
body:
Makes `auditd.rules` read the ruleset the way the audit service loads it and parse the rule syntax auditctl accepts. It also adds the fields hardening checks have been rebuilding by hand in MQL.

**Nothing here is breaking.** A missing ruleset still returns empty lists, and the new `exists` field lets content tell "no ruleset" apart from "ruleset without this rule". Returning an error for a missing ruleset instead would be a breaking change and is left for the next major version.

## Rule loading

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Default source | `/etc/audit/rules.d` only | `rules.d` when it holds `*.rules` files, else `/etc/audit/audit.rules` |
| Files read | Recursive, every `*.rules` below `rules.d` | Top-level `*.rules` only, which is what augenrules reads |
| Order | Byte order: `10-b.rules` before `9-a.rules` | Natural order: `9-a.rules` before `10-b.rules` |
| No rules found | Empty lists | Empty lists, and `exists == false` |

augenrules (`init.d/augenrules.in`) globs `"${SourceRulesDir}"/*.rules`, sorts with `sort -zV`, and leaves an existing `audit.rules` alone when that produces nothing. Order matters because augenrules keeps only the last `-e`, `-D`, `-b` and `-f`.

## Parser fixes

Each fix below was checked against audit-userspace `src/auditctl.c`:

- **`-F key=` now sets `keyname`,** like `-k` (`auditctl.c:1035` routes `key=` through the same `process_key_option`). `auditctl -l` prints this form, so rules copied from it reported `keyname == ""`.
- **`-A` (prepend) is parsed as a syscall rule.** Before, the whole rule became a `{flag: "-A"}` control (`auditctl.c:846`, `opt_prepend`).
- **`-a exit,always` reads as action `always`, list `exit`.** auditctl tries both orders (`audit_rule_setup`, "Try opt both ways").
- **Tokens are split on byte offsets.** `parseKeyVal` indexed runes but sliced bytes, so a multibyte character corrupted the path and the tokens after it: `-w /srv/données` became `/srv/donn\xc3`.

## New fields

| Field | What it gives content |
|---|---|
| `auditd.rules.exists` | `auditd.rules.exists && …` on the same line fails, rather than passing vacuously, when no ruleset exists |
| `auditd.rules.watches` | `-w` rules plus their syscall form `-a always,exit -F path=\|dir= -F perm=`, which several hardening guides prescribe (for example `-F path=/usr/bin/kmod -F perm=x`) and `-files` never saw. Trailing `/` removed; permissions are an ordered set, so `-p aw` == `-p wa`; a `-w` without `-p` watches `r w x a`, as in `audit_setup_watch_name` (`libaudit.c:827`). |
| `auditd.rules.immutable` | Directory: the last `-e` is `2` (augenrules keeps the last one). Single file: any `-e 2`, because the kernel rejects changes after it. `controls.any(flag == "-e" && value == "2")` passes when a later file sets `-e 1`. |
| `auditd.config.maxLogFile`, `numLogs`, `maxLogFileAction`, `spaceLeftAction`, `adminSpaceLeftAction`, `diskFullAction`, `diskErrorAction`, `actionMailAcct` | Typed values. An absent key reports **auditd's built-in default** from `clear_config()` in `src/auditd-config.c`: `0`, `0`, `ignore` ×4, `syslog`, `root`. These are the same in v2.8.5, v3.0.7, v3.1.2 and v4.2.1. They differ from the values in the `auditd.conf` distributions ship (`8`, `rotate`, `suspend`…), which are what a host with that file gets. A missing `auditd.conf` is an error, as `params` already is, so "not configured" can't read as "configured at the defaults". |
| `auditd.status` | The loaded kernel state from `auditctl -s`: `enabled` (2 = immutable), `failure`, `pid`, `rateLimit`, `backlogLimit`, `lost`, `backlog`. Parses both the numeric and the `-i` word forms (format unchanged since v2.8.5). It errors when auditctl can't run (images, unprivileged scans) rather than reporting zeros. |

## Testing

- **Unit tests** for each fix and field, including source resolution, ordering, fallback, immutable in both modes, both watch syntaxes, `auditctl -s` parsing, and the unprivileged error.
- **Mutation check:** reverting each fix individually fails its test (natural sort, `audit.rules` fallback, `-A`, reversed order, `-F key=`, byte offsets, last-`-e`-wins, the `-w` default permissions). The one gap is `rules.d` entries that are directories named `*.rules`: the mock serves a directory as empty content where a real filesystem errors.
- **`go test ./providers/os/resources/...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`:** clean.
- **End to end** with the provider built from this branch, against an `ubuntu:24.04` image with `auditd` installed. The image keeps the package's `rules.d/audit.rules` and adds `9-early.rules` (`-e 2`), `10-cis.rules` (a `-w`, a `-F path=` watch, and an `-A exit,always` rule), `99-zz-late.rules` (`-e 1`) and `nested/x.rules`:
  - `controls` load in the order 9-early, 10-cis, 99-zz-late, audit.rules; `nested/` is not read.
  - `watches` returns `/etc/shadow [w a] identity watch` and `/usr/bin/kmod [x] modules path`.
  - `immutable` is `false` because the last `-e` is `1`.
  - `auditd.config` returns `maxLogFile 8`, `maxLogFileAction "rotate"` and so on, from the shipped file.
  - `auditd.status` errors with `auditd.status runs auditctl, which this connection cannot do`.
  - A plain `ubuntu:24.04` image returns `exists: false, files: []`.
- **Live hosts over SSH**, with the provider built from this branch. Each EC2 instance ran auditd with the same augenrules layout: a `-w` watch, a `-F path= -F perm=` watch, an `-A exit,always` rule, a `-F key=` rule, and `99-finalize.rules` holding `-e 2`.

  | Host | auditd | `watches` | syscall rules / keys | `immutable` | `auditd.status.enabled` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | RHEL 7.9 | 2.8.5 | 2, both syntaxes | 3 / `modules`, `modules`, `time-change` | true | 2 |
  | RHEL 8.10 | 3.1.2 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | RHEL 9.8 | 3.1.5 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | RHEL 10.2 | 4.0.3 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | Ubuntu 18.04 | 2.8.2 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | Ubuntu 20.04 | 2.8.5 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | Ubuntu 22.04 | 3.0.7 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | Ubuntu 24.04 | 3.1.2 | same | same | true | 2 |
  | Debian 13 (existing host, own rules) | 4.0.2 | `/etc/localtime wa time-change watch` | 10 | false | 1 |

  Every value matches the host's `auditctl -s` and `auditctl -l`. On the Debian host, every `auditd.status` field and every typed `auditd.config` field was compared with `auditctl -s` and `auditd.conf` directly.

  The released provider (14.0.1), on the RHEL 7 and Ubuntu 24.04 instances, reports the `-A exit,always` rule as a control, finds 2 syscall rules instead of 3, and returns an empty `keyname` for both `-F key=` rules.

  Scanning without `--sudo`, where `/etc/audit/rules.d` is root-only, `exists` and `files` return `permission denied` rather than empty lists, and `auditd.status` returns auditctl's error.

## Content follow-ups (cnspec, after release)

- 17 `mondoo-linux-security` auditd checks can add `auditd.rules.exists &&` and move to `watches` / `keyname`.
- The MAC check's `+ auditd.rules(path: "/etc/audit/audit.rules").files` union becomes unnecessary.
- The proxmox check's hand-rolled `files.find` over both locations becomes unnecessary.
- The three `file("/etc/audit/auditd.conf").exists &&` guards become typed fields.
- The immutable check becomes `auditd.rules.immutable`.

## Not in this PR

Each item below is tracked in its own issue: #11061, #11062, #11063.

- Erroring on a missing ruleset, which is breaking (#11061).
- Per-architecture syscall coverage: aarch64 has no `open`/`chmod`/`chown` (#11062).
- Applying `-d`/`-W` deletions, which are still reported as controls (#11063).

author: captainpaws
body:
### Motivation
- Fix incorrect title resolution, unreadable detail UX, incomplete reservation flow and missing discussion integration without rewriting the addon from scratch. 
- Bring AdvancedWanted visuals and behavior in line with existing KB/ATF patterns (cards, chips, wiki-style detail, modal flow) and add durable reservation and discussion primitives required by the product acceptance criteria.

### Description
- Make the title field explicit by adding a per-field `is_title` setting, an ACP checkbox that enforces a single semantic title, and a one-time migration that locates the existing "Имя и фамилия [en]" field and marks its `field_key` as the title so cards, detail, modal and discussion chips show the real name rather than a fallback technical label. 
- Revamp frontend layout and styles to match ATF wiki patterns: a single toolbar (tabs left / Create right), compact unified filter row, two-column responsive create/edit grid, cards with 200×200 cropped images (`object-fit: cover; object-position: center;`), chips set to `font-size: 8px` + `text-transform: uppercase` and inline wrap, and a detail page with an opaque high-contrast ATF-style surface, serif title, accent lines and a readable infobox (no nested `.pun`).
- Implement Origin → Variant dependency robustly by reusing the KB resolver (`af_kb_get_origin_variants()`), emitting a small dependency payload for the client that hides the variant control when no variants exist and clears stale values on origin change, and adding server-side validation that rejects unknown or incompatible Origin+Variant combinations.
- Extend reservation model and admin settings: add DB columns `reserved_guest_name` and `reserved_until`, persist a concrete `reserved_until` at booking time, add independent reservation permissions and guest-reservation toggle plus `Срок reservation, дней` and `af_wanted_discussion_tid` settings, ensure release/archive clears `reserved_by_uid`, `reserved_guest_name`, `reserved_at` and `reserved_until`, and repair settings registration so existing setting rows are updated into the live `af_wanted` group without overwriting stored `value` fields.
- Add discussion workflow and safe message markers by introducing a configured discussion `tid` and a short-lived HMAC-signed cookie-intent for prefill; `wanted.php?action=discuss&id=...` prepares an intent and redirects to `newreply.php?tid=...` where `newreply_start` consumes the cookie and pre-fills the editor with a mentions-compatible `[mention=uid]Username[/mention]` and a compact `[wanted=id]` marker (not raw HTML).
- Reuse existing KB chips/modal runtime by extending `knowledgebase_chips.js` with a `fetchChipEntry()` path that resolves `data-wanted-id` via `wanted.php?action=modal&ajax=1&id=...` and passes the same JSON payload into the KB modal renderer, and add a server-side `modal` AJAX handler that returns a compact Wanted payload for the modal.

### Testing
- Ran the full PHP regression suite: `for f in tests/*.php; do php "$f"; done` (41 regression scripts) and all PHP regressions passed in this branch. 
- Performed syntax and tooling checks: `php -l` on modified PHP files and `node --check` on modified JS assets, all checks passed. 
- Ran focused regression/contract scripts covering title migration, KB dynamic resolver, origin/variant, reservation lifecycle, ACP field builder, discussion prefill and KB chip/modal reuse; these scripts passed and confirm server-side validation, reservation deadline persistence, guest-name handling, settings repair and the editor prefill flow. 
- Note: visual verification (browser screenshots) was not performed because the working checkout does not include a running MyBB instance or seeded DB, so visual QA should be done on a staging instance with the current theme to confirm contrast and responsive behavior.

author: 0x7067
body:
## Problem

The eval corpora carried only the typed request, so no rerun could see the v0.20.0 answers feature: `extract` stored the typed prompt, `run` fed it to `judge_edit` directly, and the composed request never existed on the eval path. Verification probes compounded it by stubbing `jev.ask`, which proves wiring, not behavior.

## Change

- `scripts/rules.py`: request composition factored into `request_with_answers(task, answers)` — the single place that knows the request format; `last_user_prompt` returns `(uuid, request, n_answers)` on every path, including unreadable transcripts; decision-log rows carry `user_answers` so live outcomes can split by whether the user answered questions. Hook request bytes are unchanged (probe-verified identical).
- `eval/rules_eval.py`: `extract` records each edit's answers since its request, collecting unconditionally like the hook (an AskUserQuestion's result line normally carries no tool name, so a substring gate would have missed 135 of 140); `judge` composes through the shared `request_with_answers`; `report` gains an `answers: N/M` line. Records without answers compose to the old request text, so their cache entries still hit.
- `scripts/check_no_stubs.py` (new) + AGENTS.md invariant: `.ask =` assignments are banned everywhere except the sanctioned `cached_ask` wiring shapes in `cmd_run` — including inside `rules_eval.py` itself. A probe cannot fake the client and present the result as verification; cost is bounded by shrinking the sample, never by faking the ask.

## Verification (live calls only — no stubs anywhere)

- Lint catches the real failure both outside and inside the sanctioned file: injected `jev.ask = lambda …` → exit 1 naming the line; sanctioned wiring and clean tree pass.
- Gate: `compileall`, `check_no_comments` (18 files), `check_no_stubs`, router stdin smoke exit 0, Stop hook fails open with no key.
- Hook request bytes identical to pre-refactor on the four-case synthetic probe; caps, sidechain skip, and malformed input unchanged.
- Live probe through the real client (`cached_ask` wiring exactly as `cmd_run` sets it): `a313bcf9#932` judged with real calls, its re-judgment hitting at 0.0s the cache key only its answers-carrying state could produce; none acted. A synthetic result line with no tool name composes into the request exactly as the hook does (`Q: Which fix? A: Docker (run inside container)`).
- Full `run --sample 250 --seed 0` on the pre-gate-fix corpus: 301/303 judged, 0 errors — identical numbers to the pre-change run (2/248 real-edit blocks at 0.81 and 0.83, 19/29 violations blocked, 0/24 compliant).
- Corpus: 1,569 real edits, **140 carrying answers** (5 under the old gate) — a normal 250-sample now measures the feature (~22 records expected).

- Confirmed 849 referenced first-party genre images exist in public Supabase storage; 12 Re-Master songs lack a full YouTube URL but have audio files.
- No production uploads or video publishing were initiated by this PR. Run TypeScript/CI and a single manually approved Short smoke test before production merge.

author: rjpower
body:
Build a separate tcc-shellsim.wasm artifact while retaining the ordinary WASI compiler. Initialize the compiler working directory from PWD so relative inputs resolve inside the caller process. Mark linked executables through shellsim.path_chmod, and compile the MIT-licensed shellsim_libc.c bridge into generated programs so C chmod resolves relative paths against the guest current directory and changes only virtual filesystem permissions.

Package the bridge source and license with the shellsim-targeted compiler. The standard tcc.wasm remains free of the shellsim import.

author: lobbystack
body:
## What broke

A PostHog alert fired today at 13:02 ET: `ProviderFailureError — voice-gateway openai_realtime_server_error failed`. PostHog carries no provider code, but the Railway logs for that call do:

```
17:02:42 Received OpenAI Realtime event type="error"
17:02:42 openai provider failure (unknown: conversation_already_has_active_response)
         callSid="CA1c89ef5c09eb2f32ac73e076673d11e9"
```

Two seconds earlier the model emitted two function calls in the same turn, 30ms apart. Each spawns its own `handleToolCall`, and each posted its own `response.create` after submitting tool output. OpenAI Realtime allows one active response per conversation, so the first won and the second was rejected.

The call itself was fine — it transferred and completed 439s later. One occurrence, one business.

## Why fix it

Two separate problems.

The rejection is a symptom: when the second create is refused, the slower tool's output can go unanswered for the rest of the turn. Parallel tool calls are normal Realtime behavior, so this recurs.

The alert is noise. A client/server race over conversation state is not a provider failure and should not page anyone.

## Changes

**Serialize response creation.** New `apps/voice-gateway/src/realtime/responseGate.ts`. Every assistant turn now goes through one `postAssistantResponse` helper instead of five scattered `response.create` posts. The first request is posted; the rest coalesce into a single deferred request, re-issued on `response.done`.

The deferred request fires only when it still has something to answer: the gate compares when the tool output landed against when the active response was created. Output the model already saw is dropped rather than producing a redundant turn. The gate also tracks `response.created`, so responses that server-side turn detection starts on its own close it too.

Two guards, both of which would be worse than the original bug if missing:

- Terminal paths (`requestAssistantFinalMessageBeforeHangup`) force through and reset the gate, so a deferred follow-up cannot outlive the call. The flush also refuses to post while the call is finalizing, transferring, or hanging up.
- The gate marks in-flight optimistically at request time. If a create were rejected outright, no `response.done` would arrive and every later turn would be deferred forever. `releaseUnconfirmedRealtimeResponse` frees the gate when an error arrives with no confirmed response, and deliberately does not fire for `conversation_already_has_active_response`, where a real response is running and will emit its own `response.done`.

**Stop paging on it.** The `error` case checks `isBenignRealtimeClientError` before `captureProviderFailureException`. `conversation_already_has_active_response` and `response_cancel_not_active` now emit `ops.voice.openai_realtime_state_conflict` at warn level. It gets its own event rather than reusing `ops.voice.openai_realtime_error`, which backs the provider-failure signal and should not absorb client-state races.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck` clean across all workspaces
- `pnpm test` — 20 suites pass (voice-gateway 29 files, admin 135, domain 37)
- `pnpm build` clean

12 unit tests in `responseGate.test.ts` cover coalescing, the already-answered drop, the unconfirmed release, and the reset. Two telemetry tests drive the real `handleOpenAiMessage` path and assert the benign error emits the conflict event and no `ProviderFailureError`, while `server_error` still pages.

Note: `packages/jobs` fails on a first `pnpm test` in a fresh worktree because `@lobbystack/contracts` has no `dist` yet. It passes after `pnpm build`. Pre-existing build-order dependency, unrelated to this change.

## Follow-up

The existing PostHog issue can be marked resolved once this deploys.

## What this fixes

ForensiScope was publicly described, but CHUM only generated pain doors for `sell_now` offers. Because ForensiScope is currently `verification_required`, generic media-overflow queries could resolve through the intent router yet still lack a generated pain page.

## Changes
- generate CHUM pain doors for all public catalog entries, independent of sellability
- keep machine checkout URLs null unless `commercial_state === sell_now`
- expand ForensiScope brand-blind intent language around long video, transcription, deduplication, and chatbot file limits

- cross-link the media-overflow contract and sitemap
- sharpen Official MCP Registry metadata and bump ForensiScope to 1.1.2

## Safety / commerce boundary
Discovery becomes wider. Payment authority does not. Verification-gated ForensiScope is explicitly tested to expose no machine checkout URL.

## Implementato

- `scripts/ci/report-vitest-failure.mjs`: quando `publishComment()` fallisce (fork/403, `TRUSTED_GH_BIN` mancante, PATCH/`pr comment` con errore), il main stampa `::warning title=Vitest failure report::` su stdout con PR, repository e causa (exit code/stderr catturati da `gh()`/`ghOutput()` tramite `describeExecError()`), mantenendo exit 0 e `continue-on-error` invariati.
- Stesso percorso: se `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` esiste, il `body` gia' prodotto da `buildComment()` viene appeso al file con `writeStepSummary()`, così il dettaglio dei test falliti resta consultabile anche quando il commento sticky non è stato pubblicato.
- `gh()`/`ghOutput()` ora propagano la causa dell'errore al chiamante invece di inghiottirla silenziosamente in `false`/`''`; `publishComment()` restituisce `{ posted, cause }`.
- `tests/report-vitest-failure.test.ts`: due nuovi casi che eseguono lo script come processo figlio con `TRUSTED_GH_BIN` puntato a un finto `gh` (exit 1 simula 403, exit 0 simula successo), `PR_NUMBER`, `GH_REPO`, `VITEST_REPORT_FILES` con un report fixture fallito e `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` su file temporaneo. Verificano `::warning` su stdout + marker `<!-- vitest-failure-report -->` nel summary sul fallimento, e l'assenza di entrambi sul successo.

## Non implementato (ancora)

- Gemello nel corpus `scripts/ci/report-node-test-failure.mjs`: PR concatenata #1787 (nanakokyobashi-rgb/frontaliere-articles), lavorata in una sessione separata sullo stesso cluster di issue applica la stessa fix di osservabilità al publisher del corpus.

Motivo: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` è marcato `adapted` nel manifest di sincronizzazione ed è di competenza del corpus, e la scheda ratificata #9739 vieta esplicitamente di toccare il workflow, `permissions:`, `GH_TOKEN` o `TRUSTED_GH_BIN` in questa PR. author: anghulam
body:
## الملخص

### الموقع التسويقي الخارجي (متعدد الصفحات)
- صفحات: الرئيسية، المزايا، الأسعار، من نحن، تواصل معنا (بنموذج فعلي يحفظ الرسائل في قاعدة البيانات)
- هيكل مستقل (`site/inc/`) لا يعتمد على `includes/bootstrap.php`، حتى يبقى الموقع قابلاً للعرض بغض النظر عن حالة تثبيت النظام أو الاتصال بقاعدة البيانات
- `index.php` الجذر يعرض الموقع التسويقي للزوار، ويحوّل المستخدمين المسجّلين مباشرة للوحة التحكم

### إعدادات السوبر أدمن (`superadmin/settings.php`)
- رفع شعار النظام — يظهر في الشريط الجانبي للتطبيق والموقع التسويقي (نافبار + فوتر) بدلاً من شارة "ب" الثابتة، مع الإبقاء عليها كقيمة افتراضية عند عدم رفع شعار
- ضبط بيانات اعتماد Google OAuth (Client ID / Client Secret) اللازمة لتفعيل ربط Google Drive، مع عرض رابط إعادة التوجيه (redirect URI) المطلوب تسجيله في Google Cloud Console
- صفحة عرض رسائل "تواصل معنا" (`superadmin/messages.php`)

### ربط Google Drive لكل شركة على حدة
- كل شركة تربط حساب Google Drive الخاص بها بشكل مستقل عبر OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code flow)، بتنفيذ مباشر عبر cURL دون أي SDK خارجي (`includes/google_drive.php`)
- تبادل/تحديث التوكنات تلقائياً، وإنشاء مجلد مخصص لكل شركة عند الرفع
- صفحات الربط/الفصل (`modules/settings/google_connect.php`, `google_callback.php`, `google_disconnect.php`) بحماية CSRF وصلاحيات (مالك/مدير الشركة فقط)

### اللترهيد وهوامش الطباعة لكل شركة
- كل شركة ترفع صورة اللترهيد الخاصة بها (ترويسة/تذييل بتصميمها) وتضبط الهوامش الأربعة (مم) من صفحة إعدادات الشركة
- تطبيق فعلي على طباعة الفاتورة (`modules/invoices/view.php`): خلفية اللترهيد بملء الصفحة عند الطباعة + هوامش المحتوى المضبوطة كـ padding داخل `@page`
- إصلاح جانبي: الشريط الجانبي كان يظهر فوق محتوى الصفحة عند الطباعة (لا يوجد له قاعدة إخفاء)، ما كان يُفسد أي طباعة سابقاً — تمت إضافة `display:none` له ضمن `@media print`

### قاعدة البيانات
- أعمدة جديدة في `companies`: `letterhead`, `letterhead_margin_top/right/bottom/left`
- جداول جديدة: `system_settings` (شعار النظام + بيانات Google OAuth)، `company_google_drive` (ربط كل شركة بحساب Google Drive الخاص بها)

## إصلاح تم اكتشافه أثناء الاختبار
نموذجا "شعار النظام" و"إعدادات Google" في `superadmin/settings.php` كانا يُرسَلان كنموذجين منفصلين لكن يُعالَجان بمعالج POST واحد بلا تمييز بينهما — فكان حفظ أحدهما (مثلاً رفع الشعار فقط) يمسح بيانات الآخر (Client ID/Secret) بقيم فارغة لأنها غير موجودة في ذلك النموذج. تم فصلهما بحقل `form` مخفي (نفس النمط المستخدم في إعدادات الشركة)، والتحقق من ذلك فعلياً بتجربة حفظ كل نموذج على حدة والتأكد من بقاء بيانات الآخر سليمة في قاعدة البيانات.

## خطة الاختبار
- [x] `php -l` على كل الملفات المتأثرة + فحص شامل للمشروع بالكامل (بدون أخطاء صياغة)
- [x] أداة تدقيق آلية للتأكد من تطابق عدد `?` مع نوع/عدد المعاملات في كل استدعاءات `bind_param` بالمشروع بالكامل (لا مشاكل)
- [x] اختبار حي (خادم PHP + MariaDB): تسجيل دخول كمالك شركة، رفع لترهيد وتعديل الهوامش الأربعة، التأكد من حفظها في قاعدة البيانات وظهورها في النموذج
- [x] اختبار حي: تسجيل دخول كسوبر أدمن، رفع شعار النظام وحفظ بيانات Google OAuth كنموذجين منفصلين، والتأكد أن حفظ أحدهما لا يمسح الآخر (هنا تم اكتشاف الخلل أعلاه وإصلاحه والتحقق مجدداً)
- [x] التأكد من ظهور الشعار المرفوع في الشريط الجانبي للتطبيق وفي نافبار/فوتر الموقع التسويقي، مع رجوعه لشارة "ب" الافتراضية عند عدم وجود شعار
- [x] معاينة طباعة فاتورة تجريبية (Playwright، `emulateMedia: print`): التأكد من ظهور خلفية اللترهيد، وتطبيق الهوامش الأربعة كـ padding فعلي على منطقة الطباعة، وإخفاء الشريط الجانبي
- [ ] **لم يتم اختباره بالكامل (يتطلب بيانات اعتماد Google حقيقية لا يمكن توليدها هنا):** إتمام تدفق OAuth الكامل حتى شاشة موافقة Google الفعلية وتبادل الكود بتوكن حقيقي. تم التحقق فقط من: صحة بناء رابط التفويض (authorization URL)، وأن الزر لا يظهر إلا بعد إعداد بيانات Google من قبل السوبر أدمن، وأن صفحة الاستدعاء الراجع (`google_callback.php`) تتحقق من `state` بشكل آمن (`hash_equals`) وتتعامل مع الفشل بلطف

author: onlinovosk-bit
body:
Zatvára dieru, ktorú našiel mutation gate v #29: `validate_evidence_structure` má dve ramená a routované bolo len jedno.

## Dôkaz — rovnaká mutácia, pred a po

Vypnutá slučka povinných polí:

| | zlyhaní | ktoré |
|---|---|---|
| **pred** | `2 failed, 397 passed` | len PS-R1 bookkeeping o `prompt_stack` |
| **po** | `24 failed, 417 passed` | + `test_every_route_denies`, `test_every_route_denies_for_its_own_reason`, `test_neutering_the_named_guards_opens_the_route` (3× každý) a 13 field testov |

Predtým sa dalo vypnúť všetkých štrnásť povinných polí a ani jeden route dôkaz to nezbadal. Desať trás, ktoré menujú `validate_evidence_structure`, sú všetko prompt-stack trasy a každá je o binding ramene.

## Čo pribudlo

**Tri trasy** pod novým `NON_PRINCIPLE_GUARDS` záznamom `EVIDENCE-STRUCTURE` — `ES-R1` (`commit_sha`), `ES-R2` (`agent_claim`), `ES-R3` (`branch`).

**Jedna asertácia na každé povinné pole** (13 parametrov).

Rozdelenie je zámerné: trasy dokazujú, že rameno **zamieta**, parametrizovaný test dokazuje, **za čo**. Trinásť trás by povedalo to isté trinásťkrát.

## Ktoré polia — merané, nie vybrané

`commit_sha`, `agent_claim` a `branch` drží toto rameno **samo**: po vyradení guardu sa každá z tých trás otvorí na PASS, takže zamieta z vlastného dôvodu a nič ju nekryje.

`probes` a `results` som **zámerne nerouteoval**. Merané: ich absenciu chytá aj fabrication detektor (`evidence_forgery_detected: PASS claim with empty probes`) a claim gate (`agent PASS rejected: no results.findings`). Trasa na nich by menovala tento guard, kým prácu robí iný mechanizmus — presne tá chyba, ktorú `test_every_route_denies_for_its_own_reason` existuje chytať.

**Korekcia k #29:** text šiesteho mutačného prípadu tam hovorí, že required-field list je „jediná vec medzi bránou a evidence bez `commit_sha`, bez `probes` a bez `agent_claim`". Pre `probes` to podľa tohto merania neplatí. Opravím to v #29 samostatným commitom.

## Jedna zmena existujúceho testu

`test_routes_for_partitions_the_registry` mal skupiny natvrdo (`("P8", "P10", "APS-001")`) a nová skupina ho rozbila. **Neprilepil som štvrtú** — odvodil som zoznam z `enforced_principles() | NON_PRINCIPLE_GUARDS`.

Nedeklarovaná skupina tak stále rozbije súčet (trasa v žiadnej deklarovanej skupine sa jednoducho nezapočíta), ale test už nepotrebuje úpravu pri každej novej skupine. Úprava testu kvôli tomu, aby prešiel, je presne ten druh, po ktorom test prestane niečo tvrdiť.

## Overenie

```
python -m pytest                            441 passed
python -m runner.cli mutation-gate          exit 0  (3 prípady z #26 na tomto base)
python -m runner.cli enforcement-evidence   exit 0, ok: true, problems: []
                                            routes_reaching_pass: []
                                            routes_denied_for_another_reason: []
git status                                  čistý strom
```

## Vzťah k #29

Nezávislé, oba sa dajú mergnúť v ľubovoľnom poradí — nestackujem ich zámerne, aby jedno neblokovalo druhé. Po mergnutí oboch stojí za to pritvrdiť sentinely šiesteho prípadu v `mutation_gate.py`, aby menovali aj tieto route dôkazy namiesto len PS-R1 bookkeepingu. author: copilot
body:
The watch listed only the doses due within six hours, which is too short a horizon to answer "what am I taking today?", and a dose led nowhere — three lines of text with no way to see the medicine behind it.

## The agenda

- `DayAgenda` replaces `UpcomingWindowFilter`: every pending dose whose local date is today or tomorrow, grouped by the minute it is due, in the watch's own zone. It stays free of Android imports, so the rule that decides what the user sees is a plain unit test.
- The screen renders *Today*, its time headings and doses, then *Tomorrow*, in one vertically scrolling `TransformingLazyColumn` (touch and rotary). The time moves off the card into its heading; doses due at the same minute share it.
- Overdue unanswered doses need no special case — they are the earliest times of today and sort to the top by themselves. Taken, skipped and missed stay hidden, as before.
- The empty state is reworded to "No medicines scheduled for today or tomorrow".

## Read-only dose details

- Tapping a dose opens `DoseDetailsScreen`: this dose's amount and time, the medicine's default dose, its schedule, and its stock where the medicine records stock. A medicine with no batches gets no stock line — not tracking stock is not the same as having run out.
- Navigation is one remembered dose id plus `BackHandler`, which is also what the watch's swipe-to-dismiss triggers. Adding `wear-compose-navigation` for a single destination would be a dependency and a graph for one boolean. The selection resolves against live state, so a dose answered on the phone returns the user to the agenda instead of stranding them on a dose that no longer exists.
- Nothing on either screen writes: no field, button, menu or gesture. A tap opens details and does nothing else.

## Sync contract

`SyncedDose` gains an optional `details`; `CURRENT_VERSION` is unchanged, so an older watch reads a newer phone's payload and a newer watch shows an older phone's dose with the details absent.

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class SyncedMedicineDetails(
    val defaultDoseText: String,
    val scheduleLines: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val stockText: String? = null,
)
```

The phone formats all three with the same formatters its own screens use, so the watch reads word for word as the phone does; a watch that formatted schedules itself would need the whole schedule model and every plural resource, and the two sides would drift. `DoseSyncPublisher` resolves each medicine once per publish; a dose whose medicine is gone is still published, without details.

## Rest

- New strings in all six languages; `README.md` and `PRIVACY.md` updated for what the watch shows and what is sent to it.
- OpenSpec change `wear-day-overview` carries the proposal, design and the `wearable-app` / `wearable-sync` deltas.
- No new dependency, no network access, no schema change, nothing touched in reminders or in how a dose is answered.

## Note for reviewers

Gradle could not run in this environment (`dl.google.com` unreachable, so AGP cannot resolve), so CI is the first compile of the Android modules. `DayAgenda` was executed and verified standalone; the Wear Material3 typography roles on the new screens and the `BackHandler`/swipe-to-dismiss behaviour on device are the two things I could only reason about.

Venus chooses

## 目的（P-0148）
「ClaudeとChatGPTを交互に使う（複数推論モデルリレー）と、単発では出る見落としを拾えて品質が上がるのか」を**実測**で判定する。AIニュース提案 P-0148 の検証。

## 追加したもの

  - stage1: lane A が単発回答 / stage2: lane B が **要件の見落としだけ** を JSON で指摘（required 一覧は渡さない）/ stage3: lane A が指摘を織り込んで統合回答
  - 決定的採点（`gradeRequired` は required のキーワード一致）で `recall1 / recall2 / lift` と、検出の `precision / recall`（誤検出＝充足済みなのに指摘した項目）を算出
  - `--live`（実測）/ `--write`（doc生成）/ `--check`（drift検出）/ `--json`
- `tools/model-relay-catalog.json` — オージャスト実務に即した6タスク（一次返信 / 要点抽出 / 議事録 / 見積前提）。各タスクに4〜6要件

- `docs/model-relay.md` + `tools/model-relay.results.json` — 実測結果（生成物）

## 実測結果（2026-09-25・6タスク・repeat=1）
レーン: lane A = `genspark:claude-sonnet-5`（Claude側）/ lane B = `genspark:gpt-5.6-luna`（ChatGPT側）

| 指標 | 値 |
|---|---|
| 単発 recall 平均 | 96.7% |
| 統合 recall 平均 | 100.0% |
| **lift 平均** | **+3.3pt** |
| 見落とし検出 precision / recall | 100% / 100% |
| コスト倍率 | **未計測**（proxy が usage を返さない） |
| errors | 0 / 6 |

**読み方**: 6件中5件は単発ですでに全要件を満たし、リレーの上乗せは1件（学会協賛の空き枠確認・80%→100%）のみ。検出側は誤検出ゼロで、実際の見落としを正しく1件指摘した。**「リレーは有効」と断言できるほどの lift ではない**（n=6・repeat=1・lift は1件由来）。コストは未計測のため、コスト倍率を含む判定条件は未確認。

- `node tools/model-relay.mjs --write` → `--check` exit 0（drift なし）
- `--live` 実走 → 6/6 status=ok

- 2モデル・6タスク・repeat=1 に限定。一般化には反復とタスク追加が必要

author: thesherwood
body:
## What

**1. Direction: DURABILITY §4, "The cut and its boundary"** (owner, 2026-09-24). Everything inside the cut is data. Only the cut's boundary is an interface, and a boundary edge is recorded and re-bound, never refused. Every `DeclineCause` / `NonDurableKind` is a gap against this rule (#1703).

**2. Re-issuable host calls (#1672).** A host call is a *reload* suspend point: on thaw it re-delivers the result it got before the cut. A pipe read/write or reap bench that would park while a freeze is landing has no result yet. Parking held the freeze until the park woke on its own, or until the deadlock check's `ThreadFault`.
- **temen-ir:** a per-context re-issue word (`REISSUE_IN_REGION_OFF`), in the spare 4 bytes of the region header after the thaw word. No layout change.
- **temen-durable:** `Leaf` now carries its host call.
  - The unwind moves the re-issue word into the frame and clears it.
  - The thaw arm re-issues the call with its reloaded operands when the flag is set, and reloads the result otherwise.
  - This generalizes the `atomic.wait` `WAIT_FROZEN` rule, and the two share one `reissue_branch` helper.
- **temen-interp:**
  - `decide` returns `Abandon` for a would-be pipe or reap park on a durable domain under `UNWINDING`, covering all four call forms. The caller sets the word and continues.
  - `admit_parks_for_freeze` now re-admits pipe- and reap-parked vCPUs.
- **Fix:** a vCPU that unwinds for a freeze no longer releases its domain's pipe ends as if it had exited. Before, that caused a false EOF/`EPIPE` elsewhere in the tree mid-freeze.
- Only the oracle abandons. The JIT and bytecode engines never set the word, so their host calls reload exactly as before.

**3. Pipes inside the cut ride the artifact (#1680 slice 1).**
- `DurableBinding::PipeEnd { pipe, write }` is keyed by the pipe's live global id.
  - A pipe the domain tree minted is durable, and a drain keeps it.
  - An embedder-fed pipe is the boundary and still refuses.
- A nested child's pipes ride the subtree sink beside its `FrozenChildState`. Their bytes are read at capture, once the tree has quiesced.
- **Snapshot v32:**
  - `B_PIPE_END` carries an artifact number, assigned by first appearance, so a thawed tree re-freezes byte-identically.
  - Section 9 carries each pipe's bytes.
  - A pipe with an end outside the cut fails the freeze with `PipeCrossesCut`. The boundary edge is slice 2.
  - Restore rebuilds each pipe with the cut's end counts and rejects dangling or unnamed pipes.
- **FRONTIER:** `PipeEnd` durability is now 🔶 (conditional) instead of ⛔.

## Tests
- `temen-durable/tests/quiesce_parks.rs::a_pipe_parked_root_is_abandoned_and_its_read_reissued_on_thaw`
  - Mutation-checked: without the abandon, the freeze hangs.
  - Without the unwind fix, the thaw returns the false-EOF answer (`7` instead of `1127`).
- `temen/tests/durable_pipes.rs`: a parent and its live nested child piped together are frozen through the codec, re-frozen byte-identically, and thawed to the uninterrupted result.
- Codec unit tests: pipe numbering, and the boundary refusal.
- `c_posix.rs`: the freeze-witness test is updated. The personality's `HostProc` still refuses; a minted pipe no longer does.
- Local gate (`scripts/ci/local-gate.sh`) passes on CI's toolchain. Ran the `temen-durable`, `temen-interp`, `temen-snapshot`, `temen-jit` and `temen-parity` tests plus the `temen` durable, pipe and posix suites.

## Not in this PR
- #1680 slice 2: boundary pipes as re-bindable edges.
- The JIT and bytecode setting the re-issue word.
- `stopped`, `cap`/`ticket`/`completion` parks (#1678).
- Folding `SvcServe` into the re-issuable `Leaf`.

body:
Overlay settings changes currently have no undo/redo, and placement history is lost when its screen closes. This adds separate settings and placement histories that survive editor close/reopen for the lifetime of the Minecraft client.

- Undo and redo info box/custom bar creation and deletion, names, content, templates, and settings. Placement history also covers render ordering.
- Keep up to 100 entries per history, grouping text editing and dragging into individual steps. Add textured Undo/Redo buttons to the settings sidebar, tooltips listing up to five available actions in execution order, and keyboard shortcuts. Focused settings text fields restrict undo/redo to edits involving that field.
- Save preserves history and records a checkpoint. Close without saving restores that checkpoint. History survives disconnecting, reconnecting, character changes, and server transfers. Restarting Minecraft, external configuration reloads, and profile changes clear history.
- Record changed configuration values at interaction boundaries, with no periodic history processing. Create, delete, and restore individual overlays in memory instead of rebuilding their entire group and reloading configuration. Batch render-order updates and release removed overlays' persisted metadata.
- Preserve overlay identity after unregistering so reopening a cached editor screen after a configuration reload resolves the replacement overlay safely.

Depends on #4337. This branch includes its rename commit until that PR merges.

body:
## Scope

Issue #1106 follow-up stacked on Draft #1241. A direct `CostRoutingCoordinator.submit_batch` call could submit synthetic review text work to a batch backend while review allocation evidence was unavailable. The existing non-ZDR resolution returns requests unchanged, and the library API had no review preflight. The HTTP `/api/v1/batch_routing_jobs` route shares that submission path.

The change checks every batch item with the existing review allocation guard before target resolution or backend submission. The guard is outside the RuntimeError-to-BatchModelSelectionError conversion so its typed 400/503 response survives. Non-review coordinators retain the previous behavior.

## RED and GREEN

- RED at parent #1241 `c2c72b6d`: synthetic explicit-model direct batch reached mocked backend `submit` and failed the no-send assertion.
- GREEN at `10133087`: direct and HTTP batch requests return nonretryable 400 `review_model_not_allowed` for an explicit member or nonretryable 503 `allocation_evidence_unavailable` for `orchestrator/free`; zero backend submissions.
- Local bounded suite: 168 passed with one pytest config warning. The separate expanded test collection mismatch identified in #1241 remains unresolved and is not claimed clean here.

Ingress inventory before commit: HTTP media/rerank routes share `proxy_capability` (#1240); sync/batch embedding HTTP uses `_require_pool_model`, and direct embedding batches use `submit_embeddings_batch` (#1241); text batch HTTP and direct library callers use `submit_batch` (this PR); synchronous Chat/Responses routes enter `complete`/`proxy_completion` admission (#1235). Retrieval/poll routes act on previously owned job handles and do not submit new work.

Draft/HOLD. No real data, secrets, provider egress, merge, or deployment. Required hosted checks, independent approval, calibrated allocation release, and consumer migration remain open.

author: toddmedema
body:
## Problem
`blackoutStartMinute` and `blackoutUnservedWh` lived in module-level variables in `src/reducers/Game.tsx`, and `resume` reset them to "started now, nothing missed yet". A save taken mid-blackout therefore logged a shorter, cheaper "Blackout ended after Xh. The grid could not supply Y…" message than the uninterrupted run.

## Fix
- `GameType` gains an optional `blackout?: { startMinute; unservedWh }`, present only while a blackout is underway. It travels with the saved slice, so no envelope change is needed.
- The tick edge-detects against `state.blackout`, which also replaces the module-level `previouslyInBlackout` (one source of truth; a resumed save keeps the blackout it was taken during).
- `initGame` clears it; `resume` no longer touches blackout state.
- `parseSave` rejects a `blackout` that isn't an object with an integer `startMinute` in `[0, date.minute]` and a finite, non-negative `unservedWh`.

## Behavior change
The old code accumulated the first blackout tick's shortfall and then reset the total to 0 on the edge, so that tick never counted. It now counts, so reported unserved energy is slightly higher.

## Tests
- `Resume.test.tsx`: saves scenario 102 (seed 8675309) at minute 9600, mid-way through a 9465–9795 blackout, runs both games to minute 10000, and compares `eventLog`s. Fails on the old reducer (2.7 GWh vs 2.4 GWh), passes now.
- Rejection cases for malformed `blackout` values in `parseSave`.
- `npm run compatibility:generate`, then `npm run check`: all steps pass.

No UI changes, so no screenshots.

author: aehlke
body:
## Summary

Dictionary term serialization calls `_quoteJsonStringCached` for rules, definition tags, and term tags. Cache hits currently perform `Map.delete` + `Map.set` solely to maintain LRU-like ordering even while the cache is below its 8,192-entry capacity and cannot evict anything.

Skip those two mutations until the cache is full. Once eviction is possible, the existing promotion behavior remains in place.

## Benchmark

Standalone Node benchmark using the production cache logic:

| workload | baseline median | candidate median | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1M serialized rows, repeated rule/tag pools | 179.7 ms | 64.8 ms | -64.0% |
| 64 recurring strings | 31.9 ms | 7.2 ms | -77.5% |
| 4,096 recurring strings | 79.6 ms | 11.3 ms | -85.9% |
| >8K high-churn hot/streaming mix | 162.0 ms | 165.7 ms | +2.3% |

The high-churn result is effectively the existing behavior after capacity is reached; the common sub-capacity workloads avoid two Map mutations per cache hit.

No persisted data or cache values change.

author: janacm
body:
## Why

The site's API ran on a MacBook behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. When that Mac was off, every API call from https://random-address-retriever.netlify.app failed with Cloudflare error 1033, which was the state on 2026-09-24 before this change. The data was already on Neon (the 3M-row sample from #13). This moves the API next to it, so no local machine is in the request path.

```text
Browser -> Netlify (apps/web) -> edge proxy /api/* -> Neon Function addressapi -> Neon Postgres (production)
```

## What changed

- **Neon Function entry** (`server/src/function.ts`, declared in `neon.ts` as slug `addressapi`). It runs the same `buildApp()` as local dev, forces production mode so a missing `ADDRESS_API_TOKEN` fails startup instead of falling back to `local-dev-token`, caps the `pg` pool at 5 per isolate, and calls `attachDatabasePool`.
- **Fastify to `fetch` bridge** (`server/src/fetch-adapter.ts`). It dispatches through `app.inject()`, the same approach `@fastify/aws-lambda` uses, so the hooks, validation, and error envelopes are unchanged.
- **`DATABASE_URL` support** in `config.ts`/`db.ts`. When set, it replaces the `PG*` fields.
- **`/api/healthz`**: Neon answers an exact `/healthz` at the platform with a plain-text `ok`, so the request never reaches the app. The DB-backed check is also served at `/api/healthz`, and the web app calls that path. `/healthz` stays for the local API and `scripts/healthcheck.sh`.
- **Edge proxy**: sets `x-forwarded-for` from Netlify's `context.ip` (tested: Neon passes the first hop through, so the in-memory limiter now keys on the visitor), uses `redirect: "manual"` so the token never follows a redirect, and drops the unused Cloudflare Access headers. The `/healthz` edge route is removed.
- **About page copy**: the health card and source panel no longer claim a local API or local Postgres in production builds.
- **Docs**: new `docs/DEPLOY.md` (deploy, token rotation, rate limiting, logs, limits, rollback). The tunnel docs are marked retired, and README, REQUIREMENTS, TODO, HOSTED-SAMPLE, and server/README are updated.

## Already live (done outside this PR)

- The Function is deployed on the `production` branch (deployment 3).
- Netlify's `ADDRESS_API_URL` points at the Function, and `ADDRESS_API_TOKEN` was rotated in all three contexts. The old value was unreadable (a masked Netlify secret, and `.env.local` is off-limits to the agent). `main` was rebuilt with the new env vars and the site works. Until this merges, only About > "Check API" is broken, because `main` still calls `/healthz`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter random-address-api run test:coverage` with `RUN_DB_TESTS=1` against local Postgres: 79 tests, 87.9% lines
- [x] `pnpm --filter @random-address/web run test:coverage`: 104 tests, 99.3% lines
- [x] Both typechecks, both builds, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- [x] `neon dev` locally against the production branch: every route, plus 401 and 404
- [x] Deployed Function: every route with the token, 401 without or with the dev token, and `/api/healthz` reports `neondb`
- [x] New `api-proxy.ts` run under Node against the live Function: all routes pass, and a browser-supplied `Authorization` header is ignored
- [x] Live site after the env var change: provinces, random address, cities, `/api/healthz`
- [x] About page in dev: "Check API" calls `/api/healthz` and reports healthy
- [ ] Netlify deploy preview for this PR: About > "Check API" shows the Neon Function label and `neondb`

## Follow-ups

- The hero, header badge, About paragraph, and city-picker counts still describe all 17,169,294 addresses, while the hosted API serves a 3,000,009-row sample. The wording needs a decision first.
- Delete the `random-address-api` Cloudflare Tunnel, its `address-api.janac.me` DNS record, and the connector LaunchDaemon on the Mac that ran it.

author: mgoldey
body:
## Summary
Step **W0** of the validation campaign (design spec: `wiki/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-validation-campaign-design.md`). It builds the infrastructure every Narrow/Smoke row will use, and proves it end to end on one row, UHF/ROHF.

### Validation tier
- **Test files.** Validation tests live in `crates/*/tests/validation_*.rs`, and each test is marked `#[ignore = "validation: <row>"]`, so the per-commit shards never run them.
- **CI job.** A new `validation` job runs `cargo nextest run --run-ignored only -E 'binary(/^validation_/)'` with a new `[profile.validation]`.
  - It runs on a **weekly** schedule and on `workflow_dispatch` only.
  - The nightly cron is split into two entries. The nightly jobs match both, so they still run once a day; `validation` matches only the Sunday entry.
- **Tier guard** (`ci_validation_tier_guard.rs`, regular tier). It derives the validation files from disk and checks that:
  - the job selects every one of them;
  - every test in them carries a `validation:` ignore;
  - no such ignore lives outside them;
  - the job is weekly and manual only;
  - no other job runs ignored tests.
- **pytest:** a registered `validation` marker, excluded by default.

### Proof links (user request: "make the validation docs link out to the proof file")
- **The page.** In `site/src/reference/validation.md`, the Anchors column "Pinned by" becomes **Proof**, with GitHub links to the test file that asserts each row and, where one exists, its reference generator.
  - A new UHF/ROHF row is added.
  - The stale "COSX has no gradient" note is corrected, since #164 merged.
- **Link-rot guard** (`proof_links_are_live.rs`). Every `blob/main` link on that page must resolve in the tree, with no `#L` line anchors. Every `validation_*.rs` file must be linked from the page. Either a renamed test or a deleted link fails CI.

### Harness
- **`scripts/validation/common.py`:**
  - rebuilds ferric's bundled basis JSON for PySCF (and ORCA `NewGTO`), and writes geometry in ferric's Bohr;
  - records a provenance block with each reference;
  - generates stability-checked open-shell references, and refuses to write an unstable state;
  - has a `--self-check`: all 8 system/basis pairs have unit overlap diagonals to 1e-15.
- **`scripts/validation/run_slot.sh`:** a single `flock`-guarded whole-CPU slot, printing the sentinel `SLOT_DONE rc=N`. `--light` runs at RAYON 2 outside the slot.

### Row: UHF / ROHF
- **References:** PySCF 2.13.1 `UHF` and `ROHF` plus `stability()`, for HO2, NO2, CH2 (triplet) and allyl, each at 6-31G and def2-SVP. The generator is `gen_uhf_rohf.py`.
- **ferric's setup:** it runs with the stability check and descent on. NO2 needs the descent in both bases: ferric's first state sits 2.3e-3 / 1.3e-4 Ha above PySCF's minimum, and the descent reaches it.
- **Measured over all 16 references:**

  | Quantity | Max \|d\| | Bar |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | Energy | 4.04e-12 Ha | 1e-10 |
  | ⟨S²⟩ | 3.13e-7 | 1e-6 |
  | HOMO/LUMO | 2.44e-8 | 2e-7 |
  | λ_min | 6.73e-8 | 5e-7 |
  | E_nuc | 4.3e-14 | 1e-9 |

- **Controls:** UHF must miss the ROHF reference and vice versa, and each basis must miss the other basis's reference.
- **Mutations:** turning the descent off fails NO2 UHF, and swapping the two HO2 reference files fails both HO2 cases.

### F3 (part)
`tests/uhf.rs` no longer silently skips a missing reference JSON; it panics with the path. All three references it reads exist.

## Test plan
- [x] Tier guard 5/5, proof-link guard 3/3, `uhf.rs` 5/5.
- [x] 8/8 validation tests pass; both mutations fail as expected.
- [x] Re-run at the tightened bars (energy 1e-10, orbital energies 2e-7, λ_min 5e-7): 8/8 pass; proof-link guard 3/3.
- [ ] CI. The validation job itself only runs on the schedule or dispatch, so after merge I'll trigger it once with `workflow_dispatch`.

**Merge order:** #167 (TDDFT) adds `validation_tddft.rs` and links it on the same page. Whichever of the two merges second needs a small rebase of the Anchors table.

author: yaniv-golan
body:
## What & why

### Stale premise

Since Desktop 2.7032.0, the host-loop sub-agent manifest tells the sub-agent to **pass absolute paths** to its file tools (`src/prompt/subagent-manifest.ts`). It no longer says where a relative path resolves. `subagent-manifest-probe` still graded the retired claim with a `subagent_file_write` (unanchored suffix) + `file_exists` pair. A live re-run passed that pair with **no relative write at all**: every sub-agent `Write` used an absolute path. The pair passed only because the attached folder was read-only and the sub-agent fell back to the outputs folder.

### Re-aimed assertions

The probe now asserts what the manifest says. Both keys already exist, so there is no schema change:

- `subagent_file_write: { path_suffix: "/outputs/manifest-probe-check.md" }`: a sub-agent write reached the outputs folder and got a non-error result. The leading `/` matters: without it, a bare relative filename satisfies the suffix.
- `no_vm_path_file_op: true`: no file tool was sent a `/sessions/` path.
- `file_exists: outputs/manifest-probe-check.md` is kept, because the suffix alone can't name this run's per-session outputs folder.

`subagent_dispatch_healthy` was considered and rejected: with no `type`, it requires *every* dispatch to deliver, so a legitimate one-sub-agent-per-method split would fail spuriously. The prompt now asks for "the outputs folder" by name. `docs/subagents.md`, the `DESIGN.md` scope note and the CHANGELOG are updated to match.

### Shown to fail, at $0

I graded the new and old assertions with `evaluate()` over a **real persisted** hostloop `result.json`, then altered the sub-agent's delivered write:

| Case | New assertions | Old pair |
|---|---|---|
| unaltered real run | green | green |
| bare relative write | **red** | green |
| write into the attached folder | **red** | green |
| VM path sent to a file tool | **red** | green |
| extra VM-path write alongside an intact delivery | **red** | green |
| same run graded as the container tier | **red** (hostloop-only) | n/a |

### Live re-run

`desktop-2.7032.0`, agent 2.1.280, hostloop: **9/9 assertions**, 1 sub-agent, 31s, $0.26. From the on-disk transcript: the sub-agent `Read` the ledger on its host path, summed it again with `awk` in `mcp__workspace__bash` on its `/sessions/…/mnt/` path, and made one `Write` to the outputs folder's host path. The note contains the correct total.

### Honest limit

The parent sees its own copy of these paths and **may spell the outputs path out** in its dispatch prompt. It did in the live re-run above. A green then shows the sub-agent *used* the host path, not that it *learned* it from the manifest. An earlier, pre-re-aim run is the evidence for that part: the parent named only the attached folder, which was read-only, and the sub-agent fell back to the outputs folder's host path, which only the manifest listed. The scenario header and `DESIGN.md` both state this limit.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run ci` passes (typecheck · test · build): 380 files, 6670 tests
- [x] `npm run format:check` passes
- [ ] Added/updated unit tests for new schema fields, `Decider` rules, or egress logic: n/a, no new schema fields or logic; existing assertion keys only
- [x] Shipped examples still validate (`test/examples.test.ts`); the CI lint step (`--strict --min-severity WARN`) is clean on 18 scenarios
- [ ] If I touched the sandbox: n/a
- [ ] If release-specific: n/a, no baseline change
- [ ] Unverified-against-live-agent code is marked `// UNVERIFIED`: n/a, no source change; the scenario was run live
- [x] Updated docs / CHANGELOG as needed: `docs/subagents.md`, `DESIGN.md` scope note, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`

## Fidelity / boundary impact

None to what the harness reproduces: no source or baseline change. This fixes live coverage. The probe now grades the manifest's current absolute-path claim instead of the retired relative-cwd one. The gap it leaves (a green can't show *where* the sub-agent learned the path) is stated above and in the scenario header.

author: tada5hi
body:
## Problem

A fast reload of a hosted auth page under `authup dev` flashed a white, unstyled page. The server-rendered markup was correct (login form or account chooser), but the dev render emitted no stylesheet: `tailwind.css` is imported from `app.ts`, and the styles only arrived once vite's client modules ran. A production build links its css through the manifest and is not affected.

## Fix

`createViteRender` walks the SSR module graph from `/src/server.ts`, loads each stylesheet it reaches through `?inline`, and emits it as `<style type="text/css" data-vite-dev-id="<id>">`. The attribute is what vite's client looks a sheet up by, so on load and on hot updates it reuses these tags rather than appending a second copy. `</style` inside the css is escaped.

## Verification

- New case in `apps/authup/test/unit/dev-console-auth.spec.ts`; the `apps/authup` suite, `check:types` and lint pass.
- Against a real vite server, the SSR graph holds `src/tailwind.css` and `?inline` yields the compiled sheet.
- Confirmed in the browser: fast reloads of `/console/auth/authorize` now paint styled.

## Default console favicon

None of the three consoles named an icon, so browsers asked `/favicon.ico`, which nothing serves.

- Each console bundle ships `src/favicon.svg` (the logo mark from the auth card) linked from its `index.html`; vite emits it as a hashed asset under the bundle's base (`/console/<name>/assets/favicon-*.svg`).
- A theme `theme.json` with `favicon` **replaces** it: `applyTheme` strips the shell's `rel="icon"` links (`removeFaviconLinks`) before injecting the theme head, instead of relying on the browser picking the last one.
- Specs in `packages/server-console-kit/test/unit/theme.spec.ts`; the kit and the three console service suites pass, and the icon is served in `authup dev` and in a build.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Account, admin, and authentication consoles now display an SVG favicon.
  * When a theme provides its own favicon, it replaces the console’s existing icon.
  * In development, server-rendered pages include their referenced stylesheets inline, allowing Vite hot updates to refresh them.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated theming and development guidance to describe favicon replacement and stylesheet hot updates.

body:
## Summary
Codifies the proven token-saving working method in `policies/default/AGENTS.md` (fixes #201):
1. **MergeSequencer lane:** Serializes backend/ops merges with ≥10-minute spacing for deploy attestation and feed warmup; feature lanes send `ready to merge` rather than merging directly.
2. **Frontend-only small PR self-merge:** Small frontend PRs (<250 lines) self-merge directly once local gates pass and CI shows no failed checks.
3. **CI wait cap & local gates:** Never wait >5 minutes on CI; proceed on local gates, but any FAILED check strictly blocks.
4. **Review economy & single-pass:** Review only high-risk areas or diffs >250 lines; never review twice for identical content; delta review only after content changes.
5. **Main frugality:** Long job polls (120–240s), one batched multi-lane dispatch per turn, and zero inline investigations.
6. **CI hygiene:** Concurrency `cancel-in-progress` groups mandatory on all PR workflows.
7. **Nested sub-agents:** Default to cheap lanes (Flash `task`, or `spark` for small reviews); Opus/`reviewer` restricted to high-risk reviews.

- Diff stat: 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-) (well under the 40 lines limit).
- Verified working method in active production fleet on 2026-09-24.

Closes #201.

author: jshorwitz
body:
Prep for submitting this repo at cursor.com/marketplace/publish. It follows the Cursor plugin submission checklist (https://cursor.com/docs/reference/plugins#submission-checklist).

## Changes
- **Logo path:** `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` and `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` now use `"logo": "assets/logo.png"` instead of the absolute `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/...` URL. Cursor resolves relative paths to a raw URL pinned to the commit SHA, and the checklist asks for a committed logo referenced by relative path. The file is the existing 1024×1024 transparent mark.
- **No "free" wording:**
  - `SYNTER_API_KEY` variable description: "…Leave blank to run /synter:quickstart and the GA4 and onboarding tools first; paid actions need Solo ($20/mo) or credits."
  - README L55: "GA4 and onboarding tools work before you add a key; paid actions need Solo ($20/mo) or credits."
  - README L213: "Reads are always free to run." is now "Reads (lists, reports, pulls) never need spend approval."
- **Root `plugin.json`:** it was a 26-byte symlink to `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. It resolved locally, but Cursor treats a root `plugin.json` as an **Agent Plugins 1.0.0** manifest, and the symlinked Claude manifest **fails that schema**: `$schema` must be the agent-plugins const, and `displayName` isn't allowed because `additionalProperties: false`. Symlinks also turn into plain text files on checkouts without symlink support, and some crawlers don't follow them. This PR replaces it with a real, schema-valid Agent Plugins manifest with the same name, version, description, author, and keywords as the Claude manifest. Nothing in the repo referenced the root file, and the Claude zip build and `claude plugin validate` use `.claude-plugin/`.
- **`scripts/validate-manifests.js`** now checks that:
  - root `plugin.json` is a regular file, uses the Agent Plugins `$schema`, has only allowed keys, and its name and version match the Claude manifest
  - Cursor `logo` values are relative and the file exists
  - Cursor listing manifests contain no "free" wording

  Run against `main`, it reports 6 errors. On this branch it passes.
- README structure section and CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` updated.

## Verified locally
- `node scripts/validate-manifests.js` passes.
- `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.263 plugin validate . --strict` passes.

## Consider (not implemented)
- **OAuth for Cursor instead of the API-key header.** Cursor's `mcp.json` sends `X-Synter-Key: ${SYNTER_API_KEY}`, while the Claude `.mcp.json` uses browser OAuth. The hosted server already supports OAuth with DCR and PKCE, so Cursor could probably use a header-less `url` entry and the standard MCP OAuth flow. Reviewers may ask why a key is required. Not changed here: it's not trivial because it changes the install and variables UX and needs testing in Cursor.
- If you'd rather not ship two manifest formats, delete root `plugin.json` entirely. `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` is the full-featured manifest.
- Before submitting, test locally: symlink the repo into `~/.cursor/plugins/local/synter`, reload, and confirm the logo renders from the relative path.

author: krisbuytaert
body:
## Summary

`mattx_hooks_exit()` unregisters every other kretprobe registered in `mattx_hooks_init()` — including `shmat`'s DSM siblings (`shmget`, `shmctl`, `shmdt`, `force_sig_fault`) — but not `shmat_kprobe` itself. One-line omission, fixed here.

## Root cause

Left registered in the kernel's kprobe table after `rmmod`, `shmat_kprobe` collides with the next `insmod`'s `register_kretprobe()` call for the same symbol, which fails with `-EINVAL` (`register_kretprobe failed for shmat, returned -22`, per the kernel strace on #16). That failure isn't checked, and execution continues into code that assumes the probe registered successfully, causing a NULL pointer dereference shortly after (in `__get_valid_kprobe()`, via `mattx_resolve_hidden_symbols()` → `mattx_migr_init_handlers()`).

This matches the crash described in #16/#17: a node's very first `systemctl restart mattx` after boot crashes, because that's the first time the module is unloaded and reloaded — the shmat_kprobe leak only happens on that first `rmmod`, so only the first reload hits the collision. Matches Matt's own observation on #16 that it's reproducible, kernel-version-independent, and specific to the first restart after boot.

Root-caused from the kernel strace Matt captured and posted on #16 — thank you for that, it made this a five-minute fix once we knew where to look.

## Testing

Verified the module builds cleanly (kernel 6.12.0-211.56.1.el10_2, AlmaLinux 10) with this change. Haven't yet re-run the full crash reproduction against this specific commit to confirm it resolves #16/#17 end-to-end (our test cluster's own reliability has been the bulk of the battle this week — see the test suite's CHANGELOG for the full story) — happy to do that if useful before merge, just say the word.

Related: #16, #17

author: alienwalker1995
body:
## What changes for a user

A local-only user gets from the one-line installer to a UI with no Tailscale or Google account. Remote access becomes a later, reversible command.

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Local-only questions (installer + `ordo init`) | 14 | 3 |
| Accounts needed for a local UI | Tailscale + Google | none |
| Remote access | wizard step 4 (6 prompts) | `ordo remote enable` (5 prompts, or `--yes` + flags) |

### 1. Local access without the edge
- Open WebUI and the dashboard declare `local_port: {host, container}` in their manifests.
- Edge off: the render publishes them on loopback only (`127.0.0.1:8443` chat, `127.0.0.1:8444` dashboard). A manifest names a port, never an address, so nothing can publish off-loopback this way.
- Edge on: those ports are not published, so Caddy stays the one front door.

### 2. `ordo remote enable` / `ordo remote disable`
- Collects the tailnet hostname (domain derived), the Caddy bind, the Google OAuth client id/secret and the allowlist. Interactive by default, or `--yes` with flags. The id and secret can also come from `OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID` / `OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET`.
- Reuses the wizard's validators (`hostname_error`, `parse_emails`, `invalid_emails`) and prompt helpers.
- Edits `site:` and an explicit `plugins:` list in place (new `edit_site_keys` beside `edit_plugins_list`). It updates `secrets.env` line by line and generates the edge's cookie secret and gateway key. Then it writes the allowlist and re-renders.
- It checks every input before writing any file, so invalid input leaves everything untouched. `disable` reverses the change: source bytes are identical afterwards, the OAuth pair is removed, and the allowlist placeholder is restored.
- The `tailscale cert` command it prints or runs writes `auth/caddy/certs/tailnet.{crt,key}`, the file names Caddy loads (audit F11).

### 3. `ordo init`: three questions
- 1/3 model (auto best fit), 2/3 features (chat only / chat + tools / everything, default everything), 3/3 start now.
- "Start now" does render, then host preflight, then `ordo up --all` (which builds images), then prints the loopback URLs.
- The front-door and token prompts are gone. The closing message points to `ordo remote enable`.
- It prints the chosen model, plugins and tool servers, also under `--yes`.
- The installers no longer ask for an install directory (`ORDO_DIR` still overrides it).

### 4. Host preflight
Runs in `ordo preflight` and automatically in `ordo up` (`--no-preflight` skips it). Each failure prints one line saying what to do:
- Docker daemon reachable
- Compose v2 present
- NVIDIA runtime present, only checked when the render reserves an NVIDIA device
- Free disk for the model
- Host ports the render publishes are free (ports this project's own containers hold are ignored, so re-running `up` works)
- No blank required secrets. Plugins declare the secrets they can run without in a new `optional_secrets:` field (HF_TOKEN, GitHub PAT). A blank optional secret is a note, not a blocker.

### Opt-in by default
`obsidian-livesync-funnel` and `tailnet-names` need a tagged Tailscale auth key. `plugins: auto` enabled them anyway, so a fresh install had a blank required `TS_AUTHKEY` and crash-looping sidecars. They are now `default: false`. The live source lists both explicitly, so the live render does not change.

## Validation
- `ruff check .`: clean.
- `pytest tests`: 1899 passed, 7 skipped.
- New tests: `test_local_access.py`, `test_preflight_host.py`, `test_remote_access.py`, and additions to the wizard, source-edit and fresh-install tests. The interactive init is driven with scripted input and asserts exactly 3 prompts.
- Live operator render (edge on): `docker-compose.yml` rendered from the operator source with this branch is byte-identical to the running `out/docker-compose.yml`, and identical to a render from `main`.

## Summary

Adds a source-bound `--compare-baseline` mode to the dependency-license inventory. It reports added, unchanged, and removed findings and package changes, while preserving the strict global gate: unresolved inventory debt remains exit 2. Malformed or stale baselines fail with exit 1 before the current report is written. Candidate-bound inventories are excluded until their artifact provenance has its own comparison contract.

- Closes #9681

- Blocking: none

- Base dependency: none.

- Safe to review independently: yes.

- Validate the baseline's exact report and summary schemas, value types, digest, failures, repository-input rows, package records, dispositions, and profile records; require the same recorded interpreter environment.
- Bind comparison to the current generator, canonical profile-manifest and license-policy hashes, and reported policy, project, target, profile, and selected-surface semantics. Require baseline/current input path sets to match while allowing dependency-input content changes. Reject candidate provenance in package rows and output paths that alias the baseline.
- Reconcile derivable summary counts and maps against retained package, profile, disposition, and failure rows before writing output. Counters whose source multiplicity or profile-component membership is not retained remain type-checked. Lock and dependency changes remain available as comparison signals, including reviewed development-only exclusions.
- Document the reproducible comparison command in `docs/context/dependency_license_inventory.md`.

## Why It Matters

Maintainers can review dependency changes against a reproducible prior inventory without manually assembling JSON deltas. The comparison remains diagnostic and cannot approve a dependency or clear the strict license gate.

Not applicable — support/tooling change; no research claim. Synthetic fixtures verify comparison behavior and do not establish license approval.

- `scripts/dev/run_worktree_shared_venv.sh -- uv run pytest tests/tools/test_check_dependency_license_inventory.py -q` — 99 passed.

Baselines that omit required source or report-shape fields now fail closed and must be regenerated. author: lialan
body:
## Motivation

CDNA5 host simulation still had two expensive matrix paths:

- `v_wmma_bf16f32_16x16x32_bf16` performed scalar work across every output and K step.
- The five 16-bit K64 SWMMAC forms repeatedly gathered packed inputs and sparse metadata for every output element.

This change adds dedicated AVX-512 execution for both families while retaining `RJ_FORCE_SCALAR=1` as the bit-exact oracle.

## Technical Details

### BF16F32 WMMA

- Snapshot mixed-width A, B, and C operands before packed D writes so supported operand overlaps remain safe.
- Bulk-convert BF16 inputs, accumulate with AVX-512 FMA, and pack BF16 outputs.
- Keep scalar accumulation fused and define deterministic RocJITsu NaN payload priority: current A, current B, then the running accumulator. Invalid operations use a fixed canonical NaN.

### K64 SWMMAC

- Cover all five gfx1250 forms:
  - `v_swmmac_f32_16x16x64_f16`
  - `v_swmmac_f32_16x16x64_bf16`
  - `v_swmmac_f16_16x16x64_f16`
  - `v_swmmac_bf16_16x16x64_bf16`
  - `v_swmmac_bf16f32_16x16x64_bf16`
- Snapshot A, B, C, and sparse metadata before acquiring D, then bulk-widen packed F16/BF16 inputs and resolve sparse K selections once.
- Process all 16 output columns with direct ZMM `vfmadd231ps` operations while preserving compressed-K accumulation order.
- Implement BF16F32's asymmetric contract: read eight F32 C VGPRs, write four packed-BF16 D VGPRs, and preserve the upper four C registers.
- Keep the cheap eligibility gate outside the scratch-heavy fast-path body so forced-scalar and non-K64 instructions do not pay its stack allocation cost.

The change leaves CMake feature selection and AVX-512 runtime-dispatch policy unchanged.

## Issue Tracking

Related implementation: #12151

## Test Plan

- Build the combined AVX-512 and portable RocJITsu configurations through the final `rocjitsu_tests` link.
- Compare AVX-512 results bit-for-bit with `RJ_FORCE_SCALAR=1` across directed edge cases and randomized inputs.
- Cover finite values, signed zero, cancellation, NaN/Inf, denormals, maximum finite values, BF16 RNE ties, sparse metadata patterns, packed tails, and destination aliasing with A, B, C, and metadata.
- Run decoded execution, generator routing, existing WMMA/SWMMAC regressions, and fresh-state instruction microbenchmarks.

## Test Results

- AVX-512 build and final test-executable link passed.
- `SwmmacK64SimdExact.*`: 4/4 passed.
- `WmmaSimdExact.*`: 16/16 passed.
- BF16F32-focused tests: 12/12 passed across six suites.
- Non-benchmark SWMMAC tests: 11/11 passed across five suites.
- Portable build and final link passed; relevant tests: 7 passed and 4 native-AVX-512 tests skipped as expected.
- Generator routing tests: 80/80 passed.
- Project formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent correctness and generated-instruction reviews found no introduced blocker. Disassembly confirms direct spill-free ZMM FMA on the accepted K64 path and early rejection before the heavy body for scalar/non-K64 paths.

## Performance

Release GCC 13, matching AVX-512 flags, CPU 31 pinned, and seven fresh processes. K64 measurements reset C outside each timed interval so every sample measures one decoded instruction from identical state.

### BF16F32 WMMA

| Path | Pre-change scalar | AVX-512 SIMD | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct helper | 111,981.5 ns/op | 1,376.2 ns/op | 81.37x |
| Decoded execute | 51,127.4 ns/op | 1,191.3 ns/op | 42.92x |

### K64 SWMMAC

| Form | `origin/develop` | AVX-512 SIMD | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| F32/F16 | 133,445.3 ns/op | 1,528.6 ns/op | 87.30x |
| F32/BF16 | 123,440.1 ns/op | 1,525.5 ns/op | 80.92x |
| F16/F16 | 135,210.0 ns/op | 1,902.3 ns/op | 71.08x |
| BF16/BF16 | 125,622.8 ns/op | 1,397.1 ns/op | 89.92x |

The pre-change BF16F32 SWMMAC path wrote eight F32 registers instead of the architectural four packed-BF16 registers, so it is not an apples-to-apples baseline. On the corrected branch, its scalar path measures 237,575.0 ns/op and AVX-512 measures 1,382.1 ns/op, a 171.89x speedup.

These are single-instruction RocJITsu host-simulator microbenchmarks, not GPU or whole-workload measurements.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md.

author: arigsela
body:
## Summary
Sets `smartShutdownTimeout: 30` on `postgresql/postgresql-cluster`. The CNPG 1.30.1 upgrade (#580) caused a **~3m15s** database outage instead of ~30–60s, and this cuts future restarts to about 30 s. It matters for the 1.36 upgrade, whose `k3s-worker-01` step restarts this instance.

## Changes
- `base-apps/postgresql/cnpg-cluster.yaml`: adds `smartShutdownTimeout: 30`, down from CNPG's default of 180, with a comment explaining why.

## Context
In the #580 timeline, `Stopping container postgres` came at 18:28:18, but the old pod only went away at about 18:31:20. PostgreSQL's *smart* shutdown waits for every client to disconnect, and donetick's connection pool never disconnects on its own. So the instance waited the full 180 s before CNPG fell back to a *fast* shutdown, which disconnects clients, rolls back open transactions and takes a clean checkpoint. With 30 s, clients get a short grace period and then the fast path runs.

**This change doesn't restart the database.** I checked CNPG v1.30.1's source:
- The instance manager reads `smartShutdownTimeout` from the Cluster object **at shutdown time** (`pkg/management/postgres/instance.go:643`, `internal/cmd/manager/instance/run/lifecycle/lifecycle.go:144`).
- It isn't in the pod spec. The only shutdown input there is `maxStopDelay`, which becomes `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (`pkg/specs/pods.go:536`).

Since the pod template doesn't change, there's no rollout. (Contrast §B.5, where changing affinity *did* restart the primary.) The value must stay below `maxStopDelay` (default 1800 s), or CNPG ignores it (`instance.go:645`).

## Verification
- `kubectl diff --server-side` against the live Cluster changes **exactly one field**: `smartShutdownTimeout: 180 → 30`.
- A server-side dry-run apply passes CNPG's admission webhook. The only output is the expected barman deprecation warning, which SPEC §T.79 tracks.
- yamllint and kubeconform are clean, and the OKF, TechDocs, agent-docs, catalog and k3s-upgrade checks pass.

After merge, check:
```bash
kubectl get cluster postgresql-cluster -n postgresql -o jsonpath='{.spec.smartShutdownTimeout}'   # 30
kubectl get pod postgresql-cluster-2 -n postgresql   # AGE unchanged, i.e. no restart
```

body:
## Resumen

El 24-sep medimos en producción, campo por campo, el formulario de traslados y el de pedidos de venta. La medición se corrió como un usuario de la planta (id 187, `su=False`), no como administrador:

| Registro | Campo | Consultas | Tiempo |
|---|---|---|---|
| TL/OUT/14115, TL/B/07249, LIB4657 | `sgi_coa_attachment_ids` | 411 | 12.2–13.1 s |
| PV16849 | `sgi_coa_attachment_count` | 413 | 12.1 s |
| (el resto de los campos) | — | < 40 | < 1 s |

Como administrador el mismo campo cuesta 0 s, por eso no apareció en pruebas.

**Por qué pasa:** `Many2many.read` llama primero a `comodel._search(domain)` y solo después cruza con la tabla de relación. En `ir.attachment`, cuando el usuario no es superusuario y el dominio no restringe `res_model`, `_search` carga **todos** los adjuntos y revisa el acceso de cada uno (`_filtered_access`). Esto pasa en cada apertura de traslado y de pedido de venta, aunque no tengan COA. Explica la mayor parte de las ~4 h de servidor que se fueron hoy en `stock.picking/web_read` y `onchange`, y de la lentitud que empezó el 23-sep, cuando se desplegó el COA (19.0.32).

**Qué cambia:** `bypass_search_access=True` en `stock.picking.sgi_coa_attachment_ids` y en `sgi.coa.attach.wizard.attachment_ids`. Con eso `_search` no filtra acceso sobre todos los adjuntos: el cruce se hace en SQL con la tabla de relación. Los adjuntos ligados son los COA de esa salida (`res_model = stock.picking`, `res_id` = la salida), y quien puede leer la salida puede verlos. Abrir o descargar el archivo sigue revisando el acceso del adjunto.

## Validación

- [x] `flake8 addons/` sin hallazgos.

- [x] `python3 tools/check_addons.py --base-ref origin/main` → 0 errores, 0 advertencias.

author: dennyhle
body:
I noticed my Unraid syslog was almost nothing but this one line, repeated eight times every few seconds:

php: [StorageMountService] Mounting Home Stack for root

It came to about 119,000 lines a day,  My server uses Unraid 7.3's new Internal Boot (/boot on a ZFS pool on an NVMe drive), and the plugin correctly picks the passthrough storage backend for that.

The cause: on passthrough, storagectl.sh's _pt_mount bind-mounts the persist directory at the home mount point instead of creating an OverlayFS. But isHomeMountHealthy() only looked for an overlay line in /proc/mounts, so on this backend it could never return true. That made the fast path in ensureHomeMounted unreachable, so every 5-second supervisor tick logged "Mounting Home Stack" and re-ran storagectl.sh mount for each open session. Nothing was actually remounted (_pt_mount exits early if already mounted), so no data was at risk; it was just log noise and wasted work.

The fix: isHomeMountHealthy() now also accepts the home mount when it and the passthrough directory (<persist>/passthrough/homes/<user>, the same path _pt_dir uses) are the same directory, i.e. the same (dev, ino) pair, which is what a live bind mount of the right source looks like. It's a plain stat() with no subprocess, since this runs on every tick. The existing overlay check is unchanged, so USB-boot systems behave exactly as before.

Tested on my server: the log went from 329 of these lines in the 3 minutes before the patch to 0 after, with the home still mounted and writable.
