author: 0thernet
body:
Second pass on `kb/plans/valhalla-private-rooms-native-only.md` after the owner asked for Linux and Windows, what Tailcat costs, how same-Wi-Fi and public-Internet participation work, and for the mechanics to be decided with simplicity, footprint and universality as the goals.

Decisions recorded:

- Three connection tiers behind one outbound-only client: loopback on the same machine; direct pinned-TLS to a LAN or public address (a server or VPS the participant already runs) with no extra software; Tailcat only when the room host sits behind NAT. Participants in sandboxes or containers need no inbound port, daemon or root. No Hraness infrastructure in any tier.
- `private-host` may leave loopback, with the hardening a hostile network requires (pinned TLS and token before any work, connection and handshake caps per window and per source, deadlines, slow-client refusal, loopback default kept).
- Idle footprint budgets (host at most 16 MB and no measurable CPU; client at most 12 MB and at most one relay request per minute idle; sub-second arrival while active) and a bounded wait on the relay page operation to replace 1 to 5 second polling. Measured now on the owner's Mac after 37 hours: host 11 MB RSS at 0.0 percent CPU, gateway 19 MB, Tailcat server 32 MB at 0.0 percent CPU.
- One-file invite (`vhalla private invite` / `vhalla private join`) that changes packaging, not admission or authority semantics.

author: crustyrustacean
body:
Part of #62 — **PR 2 of 3**. PR 1 (#64) persisted resolution changes; this migrates the reads onto a session-owned overlay. PR 3 removes `Entry.resolution` itself.

## Why

`Entry.resolution` is mutable state sitting on a supposedly append-only node. That is what forces the session to stay linear: two branches sharing an ancestor also share each other's downgrade decisions, and the field has to be threaded through every reader by hand.

Moving resolution to a sparse `HashMap` on `Session` separates the two concerns — the entry is data, resolution is a view over it. It is the same shape #65's per-cursor `Cursor` needs, since a per-cursor `resolution` map is the whole point of the log/view split.

## What

- **`EntryResolution::default_for(&EntryPayload)`** encodes the default-resolution table from `entry.rs`'s module docs as code. Table-driven test with one row per payload variant *and* an asserted row count, so a new variant fails until its default is chosen.
- **`Session.resolution`** — sparse overlay. Absent entry ⇒ `default_for(payload)`.
- **`Session::resolution_of(&EntryId)`** / **`resolution_overlay_is_empty()`** — the read side.
- **`PathEntry<'a> { entry, resolution }`** — `path_to_root` now returns these, and a new `path_entries()` (chronological) is what every reader consumes. Readers no longer touch `Entry::resolution`.
- **`open_session` builds the overlay**: `Resolution` lines in file order (last-write-wins, unknown ids warn-and-skip), plus a v1 file's embedded resolution when it differs from the default. Both paths stay sparse.

`Entry.resolution` is **still mirrored** by `set_resolution` and asserted to agree with the overlay, so this PR is behaviour-preserving. PR 3 drops the field.

## Readers migrated

`fit_path` (trait + `SlidingWindow` impl) · `context_stats` · the compaction range walk incl. the `Pinned` barrier · the eviction planner (`plan_downgrades`, `estimate_entry_token_cost`, `group_entries_into_turns`) · one `path_to_root` consumer in `rho/src` (`handle_clear`).

Verified scope: `LlmCompactionStrategy` does *not* read the field (the caller pre-filters), so it needed no change.

## Behaviour notes

- **Global overlay, deliberately.** Two branches sharing an ancestor still share downgrade decisions, exactly as they do with the field today. That is what makes this cutover behaviour-preserving; the per-cursor split is #65.
- `Session::new_internal` (now-unused thin wrapper) removed — `new_internal_with_overlay` is a strict superset and its only remaining caller was a test.

## TDD

Tests written first and confirmed red (10 compile errors naming the missing API) before implementation. The cutover then exposed **three existing tests that mutated `Entry.resolution` directly**, invisible to the overlay — `pinned_entry_survives_compaction` and `path_messages_filters_compacted_entries` now go through `set_resolution` / `pin_entry`. One also relied on an `Outlined → Pinned` transition the validator correctly rejects; reordered to pin before outlining. Net: 8 new tests.

Three pedantic lints fixed rather than suppressed: `map_unwrap_or` (restructured with `let-else`), `if_not_else` (inverted), `too_many_lines` ×2 (extracted `build_resolution_overlay` and an `empty_summary` test helper).

## Gates

`cargo xtask ci` → **0**: fmt ✅ · lint ✅ · audit ✅ · build ✅ · test ✅ (1605 passed, 1 skipped).

body:
## Summary of Changes
- **Agent/Model Used:** Claude Code — Opus 5.5 orchestrating, Sonnet builder subagents per plan unit
- **Task/Ticket:** Entrega A — Núcleo. Spec `docs/specs/wolven-harness-a-core.md` and plan `docs/specs/wolven-harness-a-core-plan.md` in One-Man-Team (rafiti052/One-Man-Team#30)
- **Overview:** First release candidate of `@wolventech/wolven-harness`: `wolven-harness init` scaffolds the harness into a repo without overwriting anything, and `wolven-harness validate` enforces the writing profile, the skill/rule spine, and a fail-closed ADR claim gate with a legacy mode.

## What
A TypeScript CLI (Node ≥22, runtime dep `yaml` only) with two commands.
- `init` asks for the git host (`gh`/`bit`) and runtimes (`claude`/`codex`/`cursor`), or takes them as flags. It creates only missing paths: `WOLVEN.md`, `docs/` profile dirs with ADR-000, `.agents/` with the `qmd` and `pragmatic-guard` skills and two rules, a `.claude/skills` symlink plus `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code, and a `harness:validate` script.
- `validate` resolves the git top-level and checks four things: the profile rules on `docs/{adrs,specs,notes,deferrals}`, the skill frontmatter and cited rules, the pending "harness-init step 0", and every ADR reference in tracked files.

## Why
Wolven code repos outside One-Man-Team copy the agent harness by hand or go without it, and nothing stops an ADR reference from pointing at a decision that doesn't exist or isn't settled. This package makes the harness installable and the ADR canon fail-closed. `agentic-mkt` is its first consumer (spec C).

## How
- **`init`** is create-only. It never edits an existing `AGENTS.md`; integrating `WOLVEN.md` is step 0 of the `harness-init` wizard (spec B).
- **Runtimes read `.agents/` directly.** Codex and Cursor discover `.agents/skills` natively; only Claude Code gets a symlink.
- **Claims** are `ADR-NNN` or `adr-NNN-<slug>` tokens.
  - A claim passes only against exactly one `stable` profile ADR under `docs/adrs/`.
  - Missing, duplicate, invalid, `draft`, `deprecated`, and slug-mismatch claims fail with file:line.
  - Legacy ADRs (ADR-like files outside `docs/adrs/`) turn claims against them into warnings, with one `legacy ADR-NNN (<path>): … — migrate via harness-init` line each. A claim that matches no ADR always fails.
- **`ignore`** in `.wolven-harness.json` accepts only `<dir>/**` and never `docs/` or `.agents/`. This repo ignores its own `templates/` and `test/`, and records the policy as ADR-001.

## Changes Made
- [x] `src/cli.ts`, `src/init/*`: the `init` command (options/config, template apply, runtime wiring, package script, `WOLVEN.md` render)
- [x] `src/validate/*`: the orchestrator (git root, ignore guard, report), profile, spine, claims, and legacy detection
- [x] `templates/`: `WOLVEN.md`, `docs/WRITING-PROFILE.md`, ADR-000, `.qmd/index.yml`, `.agents/{skills,rules,hooks}`
- [x] `docs/adrs/adr-001-claim-path.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `.wolven-harness.json`
- [x] 114 `node:test` tests (`test/*.test.ts`), with in-process fixtures via `makeRepo`/`run`

## Verification & Testing
- **Tests Run:** `rm -rf dist && pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm validate`, re-run fresh for this PR
- **Test Coverage:** Yes — 114 tests, 0 fail. Every one of the spec's 21 proofs maps to named tests (test-name prefix = proof id, counts recorded in the plan's unit 07 and unit 13 gates)
- **How Verified:**
  - `tsc` build is clean.
  - `pnpm test` → `tests 114 / pass 114 / fail 0`.
  - `pnpm validate` → `claims: 2 ok, 0 legacy-warn, 0 fail`, `ignored: templates/**, test/** (25 files)`, `validate: ok`.
  - The residue grep for One-Man-Team-only terms over `src templates` is empty.
  - No `LICENSE` (internal distribution, Q22).

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass locally (`pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm validate`)
- [x] Documentation updated (`README.md` runtimes section, `AGENTS.md`, ADR-001, templates)
- [x] No unrelated changes included (Entrega A scope only)

## Pre-merge closure (Code initiatives)

The initiative's closure (archiving the spec, plan and PRD) happens in One-Man-Team and is owned by spec C. This repo carries no initiative specs.

- [ ] Implementation specs/plans moved to `docs/specs/archived/` with `status: archived` — n/a here; in One-Man-Team under spec C
- [ ] Initiative PRDs moved to `docs/prds/archived/` with `status: archived` — n/a here; in One-Man-Team under spec C

- [ ] `pnpm docs:index && pnpm validate` PASS after archive moves — pending in One-Man-Team

## Risk & Reviewer Notes
- **Risk Level:** Medium — first code in the repo; `init` writes into consumer repos
- **Sensitive Areas Touched:**
  - `init` file creation and the symlink (macOS/Linux only; a symlink failure exits 1)
  - the claim gate's fail-closed rules

  - `src/validate/claims.ts` resolution order.

body:
Interface-constraint capture scanned every recursive slot and forced-dynamic root for each captured node, so unrelated graph state made capture quadratic (#11677).

Store both producer-authored membership bits directly on union-find classes. Marking resolves the current representative, unions preserve both bits, and summary replay restores them on fresh cells. Capture, shareability, interface identity, minted joins, and iterator finalization now read the exact class metadata. This preserves representation decisions while removing both graph-wide inventories.

Regression coverage varies captured roots and unrelated marked classes independently and requires identical capture work as unrelated state grows, with a linear union-find-resolution bound. Correctness tests cover independent flags, repeated marks, marking redirected nodes, both union directions, path compression, settled-leaf sharing, summary replay, and graph reset.

Validation: `zig build minici` passed all 77 stages (0 failed, crashed, or skipped), including the complete postcheck suite, evaluator tests, SIMD differential tests, CLI integration, and snapshots.

Both compilers use Zig 0.16.0, `ReleaseSafe`, and retained debug symbols. Baseline is main at `60994d3f64`; the fixed compiler adds this change. ```

| Type inference | 7.802 s | 8.119 s |
| Shared lambda-set solving | 3.463 s | 3.489 s |
| Peak RSS | 10,739,800 KiB | 10,554,036 KiB |

Both builds completed with zero errors and warnings. Shared Monotype lowering is about 39% faster in this comparison. A separate successful `perf` run collected 6,382 user-cycle samples: `compiler_rt.memset` accounts for 26.56% self overhead, `InterfaceConstraints.Capture.node` 11.02%, `memcpyFast` 8.00%, and `InstGraph.find` 1.48%. These are whole-build samples, not directly comparable to the issue's macOS lowering-only profile.

This fixes the confirmed quadratic membership scans. It does not claim the broader sub-second target: allocation/copying and other lowering work, inference, and lambda-set solving remain substantial. The detailed shared Monotype counters printed as zero were not used as measurements.

body:
## Summary

Adds a German **Impressum** (`/impressum`) and **Datenschutzerklärung** (`/datenschutz`), both public (no login), and links them from every page.

> **Draft legal text - the operator must check it.** These texts are a starting point derived from the code, not legal advice, and make no claim to legal completeness. Please have them reviewed before relying on them. Points that need the operator's own judgement are listed below.

## What changed

- **Operator details only from the environment.** New server-only variables in `.env.schema` and `.env.example` (placeholder values only): `LEGAL_OPERATOR_NAME`, `LEGAL_OPERATOR_STREET`, `LEGAL_OPERATOR_CITY`, `LEGAL_CONTACT_EMAIL`, plus optional `LEGAL_CONTACT_PHONE` and `LEGAL_HOSTING_PROVIDER`. Nothing personal is hard-coded. The pages read them at request time (`connection()`), so a self-hosted deploy needs no rebuild.
- **Behavior when unset:** the pages still render and show an "Angaben unvollständig" notice. Outside production the notice names the unset variables; in production it only says the details are being completed.
- **Footer links everywhere:** a site-wide `SiteFooter` in the root `AppShell` (landing, login, signup, all coach pages, the legal pages). The share links (team, player, collection) already have their own `ShareShell` footer, which now carries the same two links; the site footer stands aside there. The login-free share surface still links nowhere else. The immersive watch/tagging HUD fills the viewport and has no footer; coaches reach the links from any other page.
- The middleware allowlists `/impressum` and `/datenschutz`.
- The landing page and the auth layout use `flex-1` instead of `min-h-screen`, so the footer sits at the bottom of the viewport instead of below the fold.
- Coach guide: a short section on where the pages are and which env vars to set.

## What the privacy policy covers (derived from the code)

Coach accounts (name, email, scrypt hash, invite-code signup), sessions and the `hva_session` cookie (HttpOnly, 30 days), the in-memory login rate limiter (IP + email, 15 min), the `hva-theme` localStorage entry, roster names and jersey numbers, game recordings, tags and clips, share tokens (noindex, rotatable, single clips only on the own link), comments (free-text name + text), server logs on a generic self-hosted server (optional hoster name via env), originals on Google Drive, and Google Fonts.

## Findings to act on (not changed in this PR)

- **Google Fonts is loaded from Google's CDN** (`src/styles/tokens/fonts.css` `@import` of `fonts.googleapis.com`). Every visitor, including share-link viewers, sends their IP address to Google. The policy discloses this honestly, but German courts have treated this as a violation (LG München I, 3 O 17493/20). **Recommendation:** self-host the fonts (e.g. `next/font`), then drop the "Google Fonts" section. That is a separate change, so it is not part of this PR.
- **No cookie banner needed:** the only cookie is the technically necessary session cookie, and the only local storage entry is the theme preference. There is no analytics, no tracking and no third-party CDN apart from Google Fonts.

## For the operator to check

- Legal basis for game recordings and player data, especially for **minors** and whether consent from players or guardians is needed or already on file.
- Whether a data processing agreement (Art. 28) exists with the hoster; the text says so. For Google Drive the text does **not** claim a DPA (consumer accounts usually have none).
- Log retention: the text says "only as long as necessary"; a concrete period would be better.
- Whether an Impressum is required at all for this non-public, non-commercial tool; it does no harm either way.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/legal/operator.test.ts` - env reading, missing list, trimming
- `tests/unit/legal/legal-pages.test.tsx` - Impressum and Datenschutz rendering, the unset notice in dev and prod, the generic vs named hoster
- `tests/unit/legal/legal-links.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/shell/site-footer.test.tsx` - footer links on public and coach routes, footer hidden on share and watch routes
- `tests/unit/legal/middleware.test.ts` - legal pages reachable without a session
- `share-shell.test.tsx` updated: the only links on share pages are the two legal pages

Quality gate passes locally (`check-env`, lint, typecheck, 846 tests, build). I checked it in a browser with a logged-out visitor on `/impressum`, `/datenschutz`, `/`, `/login` and a share link.

author: biafra23
body:
## Summary

`cargo clippy -p myotis-net --lib` fails on `main` with a deny-level lint that CI never sees:

```
error: this loop never actually loops
   --> myotis-net/src/el/eth/session.rs:148:31
    = note: `#[deny(clippy::never_loop)]` on by default
```

This PR:
1. Fixes that lint without changing behaviour.
2. Adds unit tests for the eth handshake's Status stage.
3. **Proposes** a workspace-wide clippy lane that fails only on deny-level lints. The lane lives in its own commits, which touch only `.github/workflows/rust-clippy.yml`, so it can be dropped on its own; whether it stays is your call.

## 1. The `never_loop` in the eth handshake (`a36244d1`, `a64a3413`)

The Status read was a `loop` whose three arms all exit:
- `break` on Status
- `return Err` on Disconnect
- `return Err("expected Status, got code …")` on anything else

So the loop could never run a second time. Its comment said it looped to answer Pings in between, but Ping answering has always happened inside `recv_answering_ping`, which has its own loop.

**Should it read once and fail, or skip the unexpected frame and read again?** Read once and fail, for these reasons:
- **History:** the loop has never repeated. It was written this way in the first commit of this code (`2f23c23b`, EL-A5). The two later edits (`64d643c5`, `527a97e0`) touched only the Disconnect arm. The `other =>` arm, with its own formatted error, has been unchanged from the start. It is a deliberate choice, not a `continue` that got lost.
- **Consistency with the Hello stage:** the stage directly above is strict in the same way. The first frame must be Hello or Disconnect, otherwise `expected Hello, got code …`.
- **The reference client does the same:** geth's `readStatusMsg` ("reads the first message on the connection") returns `errNoStatusMsg` if the first eth message isn't Status. It doesn't retry.
- **Compliant peers are unaffected:** a compliant peer sends Status before any other eth message, and TCP keeps that order. The only frames that can come first are a p2p Ping (answered) and a Disconnect (handled).
- **The Java twin is the exception, and this PR leaves it alone:** `EthHandler` waits past an unexpected frame until its 30 s timeout, at both stages (at the Status stage it logs `Unexpected msg during Status` first). Because Rust is strict at both stages, this is a consistent design difference, not a porting mistake in one arm. If you want Java's behaviour (skip and keep reading), that is a behaviour change for its own PR. The test `status_stage_rejects_any_other_first_frame` is the one it would flip.

The fix is the equivalent straight-line code: read one frame, `match` it, with the same three outcomes and the same error strings. A new comment explains why the stage is strict and how it differs from Java.

### Tests

Before this PR, this code path was covered only by `#[ignore]`d live tests. There are now four unit tests. Each runs `EthSession::handshake` against a scripted peer over `tokio::io::duplex`, and together they cover every exit of the Status stage:
- `status_stage_answers_a_ping_then_accepts_the_status`: the peer sends a Ping, gets a Pong back, and its Status is accepted (eth/69, snap, the peer's latest block).
- `status_stage_rejects_any_other_first_frame`: Transactions, NewPooledTransactionHashes, an eth/69 BlockRangeUpdate or a stray Pong where the Status should be each give `expected Status, got code 0x…`, and we send nothing back.
- `status_stage_disconnect_classifies_as_busy`: a Disconnect with reason TooManyPeers lands in the pool's busy class. The test calls the pool's real `is_busy_disconnect`, now `pub(crate)` just as its producers already are.
- `status_stage_undecodable_or_foreign_status_is_incompatible`: an undecodable Status and a foreign-network Status fail with the `peer Status decode` and `incompatible peer` prefixes the pool's dial arm blacklists on.

Helpers, all test-only:
- `RlpxConnection::from_secrets` builds a connection from ready-made secrets, skipping ECIES.
- `SessionSecrets::test_pair()` holds the mirrored fixed secrets that `frame.rs`'s private `pair()` used to build. Both test suites now share it, and `frame.rs`'s tests keep exactly the same inputs.

Mutation checks, run locally:
- All session tests pass against the original `loop` code put back in, so the rewrite is equivalent.
- A variant that skips unexpected frames, Java-style, fails `status_stage_rejects_any_other_first_frame` in under half a second. `start_paused` makes the 30 s handshake timeout fire immediately, so the failure is a clear assertion diff rather than a hang.
- A variant that never answers Pings fails the Ping test.

## 2. Workspace clippy: current state

With this PR, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports **0 deny-level errors**, both on stable **1.98.1** (what `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` installs today) and on 1.94.1. Warn-level findings on 1.98.1, counted as unique sites (lib and lib-test targets report each site twice):

| clippy group | sites | lints |
|---|---|---|
| suspicious | 1 | `empty_line_after_doc_comments` |
| perf | 3 | `cloned_ref_to_slice_refs` ×2, `double_ended_iterator_last` |
| complexity | 41 | `manual_is_multiple_of` ×20, `type_complexity` ×10, `unnecessary_sort_by` ×5, `too_many_arguments` ×4, `int_plus_one`, `useless_conversion` |
| style | 28 | `missing_safety_doc` ×6, `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` ×5, `manual_saturating_arithmetic` ×4, `unnecessary_map_or` ×3, `mixed_case_hex_literals` ×2, `manual_range_contains` ×2, `single_match` ×2, `field_reassign_with_default` ×2, `doc_lazy_continuation`, `items_after_test_module` |
| **total** | **73** | per crate: myotis-net 46, myotis-engine 9, myotis-consensus 7, myotis-evm 5, myotis-core 4, myotis-bls 2 |

On 1.94.1 the total is 66: 1.98 adds `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` and `unnecessary_sort_by` and drops three sites. Every one of these is a mechanical fix.

## 3. Proposed: a deny-level workspace clippy lane (`f82c2d8a`, `b7834e32`), your call

**Why:** CI never lints the engine workspace:
- `roost.yml` is the only clippy lane, and `--manifest-path rust/roost/Cargo.toml` lints roost alone, not the `myotis-*` crates it depends on by path.
- Gradle's `check` in `ci.yml` does run `cargo test --workspace` (with the runner's preinstalled toolchain), but never clippy.

That is how this `never_loop` stayed on `main` since EL-A5.

**What:** `.github/workflows/rust-clippy.yml` runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` from `rust/`, **without `-D warnings`**:
- **What fails it:** only deny-by-default lints, i.e. clippy's `correctness` group ("outright wrong or useless" code). Warnings are printed, not enforced.
- **Setup, like the other Rust lanes:** `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `components: clippy` set explicitly, plus `Swatinem/rust-cache`.
- **Triggers:** push to `main`, `pull_request`, and a weekly run on `main` every Friday. Rust stable releases ship on Thursdays, so a new release's deny-level lint shows up on `main` within a day, not on whichever PR next touches `rust/`. `workflow_dispatch` is there for manual runs.
- **`--keep-going`:** a red run lists every independent target's deny-level hits at once.
- **Paths:** `rust/**`, minus `roost` and `tor-poc`, which are excluded from the workspace.
- **Features:** default only, so the `tor` feature never pulls Arti into CI.

**It isn't red on arrival:**
- 0 deny-level errors on 1.98.1 and on 1.94.1.
- actionlint is clean.
- This PR's own run of the lane checks it for real.

**It catches this bug class:** on the pre-fix tree, the same command on 1.98.1 exits 101 with exactly the `never_loop` error above.

**Why not `-D warnings`:** with 73 warnings, a warnings gate would be red from day one. Suggested ratchet (follow-ups, not in this PR):
1. Clear the 1 `suspicious` and 3 `perf` findings, then add `-D clippy::suspicious -D clippy::perf`.
2. Clear the rest, then `-D warnings`, the way `roost.yml` does it.

**Alternative considered:** a Gradle `cargoClippy` t

author: qingyunqian
body:
`composedkraus` preserves the density-matrix map but can return **incorrectly normalized Monte Carlo trajectories** when composing three or more random-unitary channels. The superoperator/Choi round trip changes the Kraus representation, yet the result inherits `is_unitary=True` from its inputs.

`NoiseConf` uses that flag to select `Circuit.unitary_kraus`, which assumes every returned operator satisfies `K†K = p I`. The eigenvectors of the composed Choi matrix need not have this property. A channel can admit a random-unitary representation without every equivalent Kraus representation consisting of scaled unitaries.

For example, compose three completely depolarizing single-qubit channels (`depolarizingchannel(0.25, 0.25, 0.25)`). Sampling the reconstructed operators with the unitary shortcut can give zero or norm-squared-two states from `|0>`. With an unequal superposition, trajectories can instead have norm squared 0.6 or 1.4. The density-matrix result remains correct, which is why tests of channel equivalence alone miss the issue.

### Changes

- Set `is_unitary=False` on the Choi-reconstructed, three-or-more-channel path. `NoiseConf` then uses state-dependent Kraus probabilities and normalizes each sampled trajectory.
- Preserve the two-channel direct-product path and its existing unitary metadata: products of scaled unitaries remain scaled unitaries.
- Document the representation-dependent flag and update the changelog. The returned Kraus operators, composition order, and bounded operator count are unchanged.

### Regression coverage

Cover NumPy, JAX, TensorFlow and PyTorch, two/three/six-channel compositions, a basis state and an unequal complex superposition, eager and backend-JIT execution. Choose deterministic points within the nonzero Kraus probability intervals to check every supported outcome. Verify each trajectory's normalization, the probability-weighted trajectory ensemble, and the DMCircuit result against sequential density-matrix evolution.

- Original implementation with the 24 new cases: **16 failed, 8 passed**; the two-channel controls pass.
- Fixed `tests/test_channels.py` and `tests/test_noisemodel.py`: **61 passed**.
- Targeted Black and mypy passed; Pylint **10.00/10**.
- Repository-wide Black and mypy passed; all three Pylint invocations scored **10.00/10**.
- Both English and Chinese Sphinx builds exited **0**. English: **816** reported diagnostics (649 WARNING-level, 167 ERROR-level); Chinese: **893** (726 WARNING-level, 167 ERROR-level). The builds succeeded but were not diagnostic-free.

author: dkijania
body:
Fixes #7, fixes #8, fixes #9.

## #7: default `--work-dir` and a missing work dir
- `extract` checks each entry name with `filepath.IsLocal`. The old prefix test rejected every entry when `--work-dir` was `.` or `./`.
- `archive` creates `--work-dir` before the download.

## #8: SQL errors are ignored
- Every psql call runs with `-X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d <uri>`. A failing restore or tuning statement now fails the command.
- The tuning statements run in sorted order, so a failure is reported the same way every time.
- There is no `--single-transaction`, because `CREATE DATABASE` cannot run inside a transaction.
- **Behavior change:** `import` onto a server that already has the dump's database now stops at `CREATE DATABASE` and changes nothing. Before, it reported success and appended rows. The README said that an import "replaces whatever the target database holds". That was not true, and the text is now correct.

## #9: `--if-present` looked at the wrong database and treated errors as "empty"
- The provider schema has a new field, `archive_dump.database`. It is set to `archive` for `o1labs` mainnet and devnet, because the published dumps are made with `pg_dump --create`.
- `DetectArchive(ctx, uri, db) (Presence, error)` first checks `pg_database` through a maintenance connection, then checks the `blocks` table of `db`. "Empty" needs positive evidence. Any psql failure is an error. The probe retries for up to 60 s while psql exits 2 (the server cannot be reached).
- Before the load, the dump header (`CREATE DATABASE` / `\connect`) must name the configured database. If it does not, the dump is refused and nothing is loaded.
- A dump that creates its own database is loaded through a maintenance database, so `--pg-uri …/archive` also works on a new server. A `--pg-uri` that names an unrelated database gets a warning.
- `TestDetectArchiveOnAnUnreachableServer` now expects an error.

## Found during the work: `\restrict` and older psql
The published dumps (pg_dump 17.11) contain `\restrict` and `\unrestrict`. A psql from before the 2025 security releases (17.6, 16.10, 15.14, 14.19, 13.22), and every psql 12, rejects these commands. With `ON_ERROR_STOP`, such a psql would stop at line 5 with "invalid command \restrict". `archive` therefore reads the header and the psql version first, and stops with a message that names the minimum version. The container image has psql 15.19, which qualifies. This affects `.deb` installs on older hosts, for example Ubuntu 20.04 with psql 12.

## Other things to know
- `--pg-uri` must now be a `postgres://` or `postgresql://` URI whenever psql is used. A libpq `key=value` string is refused, because the tool must read and change the database name. The flag help already asked for a URI.
- A custom provider that mirrors the published dumps must add `database: archive`, because a user artifact replaces the built-in one completely. Without it, the dump is refused, and the message names the setting to add. The README and `docs/providers.md` examples include the field.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./...` (unit tests), including tests that fail on the old code for `.` and `./`.
- [x] `go test -tags integration ./cmd ./internal/pg` in `golang:1.21.13-bookworm` (psql 15.19) against `postgres:17`:
  - the first run loads into the database the dump creates;
  - a second run with `skip` or `fail` does not download, when `--pg-uri` names `postgres`, the dump's database or an unrelated database;
  - `import` over an existing archive fails, and the row count does not change;
  - an unreachable server with `skip` or `fail` fails and does not download;
  - a dump for another database is refused before the load;
  - a syntax error stops the load;
  - a second load of a `CREATE DATABASE` dump fails and does not append rows;
  - tuning as a non-superuser fails 10 times out of 10;
  - a role that cannot read `blocks` gets an error, not "empty".
- [x] Header scanner tested with the first 60 lines of the real `mainnet-archive-dump-2026-09-24_0000.sql`.
- [x] Manual run of the binary with the local psql 12.22 on the real header: it stops with the version message and creates no database.
- [ ] CI

author: devikaverma
body:
This change adds an additional safety layer to OpenWorker.
Adds a sandbox, built on NVIDIA OpenShell, that confines the commands an AI agent runs to the files and network addresses the user has approved, so a compromised or misled agent cannot reach the user's keys, documents or other systems.

When the AI agent runs commands or edits files, it can now do so inside a "sandbox": a sealed-off workspace, built on NVIDIA's OpenShell technology, that contains only the folders the user chose to share for that task and nothing else on the machine. The part of the system that makes decisions, and the credentials that give it access to the user's accounts, stay outside. The practical effect is that if the agent is tricked by malicious content - for example, hidden instructions in a web page or a file - the damage is contained: the command runs in a space that holds nothing worth stealing and cannot reach anywhere it should not.

One Linux container per agent with the session's folders bind-mounted at the same paths.
Read-only where the session has them read-only.

author: grauzone-git
body:
## Summary

Adds sandbox-owned Azure CLI browser sign-in, driven by one foreground host command on Linux and native Windows, for AzureCloud and AzureChinaCloud. Also fixes native Azure DevOps PAT storage in the image.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Host as ./sandbox tools NAME setup azure --interactive
    participant SSH as managed SSH
    participant Sandbox as az login (in sandbox)
    participant Browser as host browser
    Host->>SSH: start login in sandbox
    Sandbox-->>Host: callback port + cloud
    Host->>SSH: temporary loopback forward, verify it
    Host->>Browser: open authorization URL
    Browser->>Sandbox: callback through forward
    Sandbox-->>Host: done → close forward (also on failure / Ctrl+C / timeout)
```

- The sandbox owns the session. No host Azure login and no mounted credentials. The active context is replaced only after a successful sign-in; failure or cancellation keeps the previous session (exit 130).
- `--cloud AzureCloud|AzureChinaCloud` is remembered; default device-code setup stays available.
- `tests/live-azure-auth.py`: a human-run lifecycle runner that writes sanitized JSON evidence.

Native DevOps fix (`542da81`):

```diff
 az extension add --name azure-devops --system
+pip install --no-deps --target <extension dir> keyring~=17.1.1 entrypoints==0.4
```
```diff
 setup azdo (native)
-  az devops login
+  (umask 077; az devops login)
+  chmod 600 ~/.azure/azuredevops/personalAccessTokens
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** `setup azdo` failed on both hosts with "Pip failed with status code 2 for package keyring~=17.1.1". The extension tried to pip-install keyring into its root-owned `--system` directory before its own file-store fallback could run. Reproduced locally as uid 1000 with Azure CLI 2.90.0.
  **After:** full runner runs on image `542da81`, source `dbdaf98`, passed every check in all four combinations, native DevOps included, with PAT file mode `600`:

  | Host | Cloud | Report |
  |---|---|---|
  | Linux | AzureCloud | [#25](https://github.com/grauzone-git/sandboxed-ai-agents/issues/25#issuecomment-5822999605) |
  | Native Windows | AzureCloud | [#26](https://github.com/grauzone-git/sandboxed-ai-agents/issues/26#issuecomment-5823379142) |
  | Linux | AzureChinaCloud | [#27](https://github.com/grauzone-git/sandboxed-ai-agents/issues/27#issuecomment-5823262476) |
  | Native Windows | AzureChinaCloud | [#27](https://github.com/grauzone-git/sandboxed-ai-agents/issues/27#issuecomment-5823418532) |

  Each run covered: browser login → access after the tunnel closes → restart → recreation → renewal after expiry with no new login → Ctrl+C cancellation → remembered-cloud sign-in → logout → DevOps checks (native and saved PAT) before and after Azure replacement and logout.
- `./tests/run` passes. The new regression test in `test-azdo-setup.cjs` checks the umask, the `0600` mode, and the Containerfile install step, and fails if either fix is reverted.

Not verified live: device-code login (tenants allow browser sign-in only; accepted on offline coverage), WSL-shell controller with a Windows browser, and policy-triggered recovery.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New opt-in commands and additive image changes; reverting the merge restores the previous behaviour. Existing sandboxes need `update` with a rebuilt image to get the keyring fix.

**Blast Radius:** image

Every rebuilt image gets keyring 17.1.1 in the azure-devops extension directory, installed without dependencies so it can't shadow Azure CLI's `cryptography`. Native DevOps setup now stores the PAT in plaintext at `0600` in the home volume, and all agents in the sandbox can read it (documented). Plain `up`/`start` still don't touch `~/.ssh`.

Closes #25
Closes #26
Closes #27

author: kpenfound
body:
Closes #210

## Summary

Adds a `type: slack` connector (`internal/connector/slack`). It holds a Socket Mode stream owned by the runtime (ADR-0015) and ingests the public channels a source names.

- **Ingest:** messages, thread replies, edits (as new revisions), deletions (as tombstones) and reactions. Artifact ids are `<channel>/<ts>`, because a Slack `ts` is unique only within its channel. A reply's `thread` and `parent` are both the message it answers. Identity hints are Slack user or bot ids, and the ACL is `public`.
- **Channel classes:** construction refuses `D…` (direct message), `G…` (private channel or group DM) and `*`. Private channels created since 2021 also have `C…` ids, so every connection first reads each channel with `conversations.info`. A private, DM or Slack Connect channel then stops the source with `ErrStreamPermanent` and failed health. A channel the app has not been invited to shows as degraded. Events from another workspace, with a `channel_type` other than `channel`, or flagged `is_ext_shared_channel` are acknowledged and dropped.
- **Stream:**
  - Every envelope is acknowledged only after its events are through the gate. A failed emit leaves the envelope unacknowledged, so Slack delivers it again.
  - When Slack sends `disconnect` to refresh the link, the connector opens a new connection itself. It does not return to the runtime's backoff.
  - A connection that breaks is retried by the runtime.
  - `link_disabled` and auth failures are permanent.
  - `/readyz` shows `connecting`, `connected`, `reconnecting`, or failed with the reason.
- **Secrets:** `app_token` (`xapp-…`) and `bot_token` (`xoxb-…`) are named environment variables. The package comment covers scopes, events, Socket Mode setup and a paste-ready manifest.
- **`read_only`:** the connector never writes to Slack, declares no `command` kind and answers no slash command. The assertion worker reads gestures only from Discord sources. So `read_only` changes nothing today, and the tests run both ways to check that.
- **Wiring:** registered in `connectorRegistry`. Documented in `docs/config.md` (Slack source) and `docs/connector-contract.md` (Slack example).

### A generic gap this fixes outside the connector

The contract says a reply's `thread` is the root of its conversation. On a two-level chat source, that root is the message the reply answers. The distiller only built `chat_thread` documents from a `thread` event. The pump enqueued a Slack reply for `l1:<src>:<root message>`, and `Distill` then skipped it, so Slack threads would never have been distilled.

The fix is generic:
- `l1.ChatRoot` / `l1.BuildChatReplies`: a channel message that replies name as their `thread` heads a `chat_thread` keyed by its own artifact, with bursts over the message and its replies.
- `Distill` and `provenanceNow` use it. When the replies are all gone, the document is removed.
- The pump also enqueues that document when the root message is edited or deleted (`threadHeadOf`).

Discord is unchanged: its replies outside a native thread name their message only as `parent`, and only events whose `thread` names the message count as replies.

## Choices I made (please rule on them)

1. **Generic distiller fix in this PR** rather than a follow-up issue. Without it, the "chat_thread/chat_burst" part of the acceptance criteria is not met. It touches `internal/l1` and `internal/service/distiller`, which the issue allows for a generic contract gap. I can split it out if you'd rather.
2. **The root message stays in its channel's 30-minute window too.** Window membership then doesn't change when a reply arrives. The thread document repeats the root's text, which it needs as the question.
3. **Content token is a hash, not `edited.ts`.** Slack re-sends a thread root on every reply (with `reply_count`), and apps can `chat.update` without an `edited` mark. A token of the edit timestamp alone would hit `l0.ErrRewrite` on changed content under the same id, and that loops the stream on an unacknowledged envelope. The token is `<16 hex of sha256(author, text, thread, edited ts)>+perm:public`, and `edited.ts` goes in `revision.edited_at`.
4. **`perm:public` in every token** leaves room for #211 to re-emit a channel that goes private as a new revision.
5. **The payload is deterministic by construction:** no channel name in `container`, no display names (Slack events carry none), no raw `native` for messages. A re-observation with the same token must be byte-identical, or `Append` returns `ErrRewrite`.
6. **An unsupported channel class stops the whole source** (permanent), because it's a configuration error, as the issue asks. A channel without the app in it is only degraded, and it heals on the next connection.
7. **Permalinks** are `https://slack.com/archives/<channel>/p<ts>` (plus `thread_ts`/`cid` for replies). They avoid a workspace domain, which can change and would make the payload differ between observations. I haven't confirmed against live Slack that `slack.com/archives/…` redirects a signed-in reader to their workspace.
8. **`team` setting is required.** Events from other workspaces are dropped, like Discord's `guild`.
9. **Slash commands and interactive envelopes are not acknowledged.** That's #212/#215.
10. **Files outside the list in the issue, beyond the generic fix:** `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, the `internal/config` "type is required" message, `deploy/compose/env.example` and the env table in `docs/deploy.md`. These list the shipped connectors or the variables a service reads, and CLAUDE.md requires new env vars in both places. `hearsay init` does not write Slack yet (#214), so env.example says where the names come from.

## Not in this PR

- History backfill and visibility re-sync: #211.
- Gestures and commands: #212.
- `hearsay init`: #214.

## How I tested it

Recorded Socket Mode and Web API fixtures only (`internal/connector/slack/testdata`, plus an httptest fake of `apps.connections.open`, `conversations.info` and the socket):

- `TestStreamThroughRuntimeGate`, run with `read_only` false and true, through the real runtime and gate. It checks:
  - the conversion of every event kind, ids, revisions, ACL, identity hints, mentions and URLs;
  - the dropped classes;
  - that re-sent roots and redelivered replies reuse their ids;
  - that the Slack refresh does not count as a stream failure while a broken socket does;
  - `/readyz` state while reconnecting and after reconnecting, and the allowlist drop count.
- `TestStreamRefusesUnsupportedChannels`: private, legacy group, DM, group DM, Slack Connect and pending Slack Connect channels, `channel_not_found` and a revoked token are all permanent; a 503 and `ratelimited` are not.
- `TestStreamReportsAChannelWithoutTheApp`: a channel without the app is degraded, and `link_disabled` is permanent.
- `TestStreamLeavesAFailedEventUnacknowledged` and `TestCloseStopsStream`.
- `TestNewValidatesSource`: config validation.
- `TestConnectorRegistry`: registry construction.
- `l1.TestBuildChatReplies`, `distiller.TestChatRepliesDistilUnderTheMessageTheyAnswer` (message edit, reply deletion) and `TestChatPumpEnqueuesTheConversationAMessageHeads` (Postgres integration tests).

author: richardcmckinney
body:
Part of venturi-systems/landing-page#2309
Tracks venturi-systems/feedback#256 (issues are disabled on this repository). That issue carries items 4 and 5 of venturi-systems/feedback#253.

## Problem

An independent check of quackback main `69026970b` found two gaps left after #131:

- **DEF-06 (residual):** the sign-in gate picks its first-step lead from the portal's visibility, but the email step and both two-factor steps (`two-factor-enroll`, `two-factor-challenge`) show `headerForStep`'s description instead. On the gate that description always read "This portal is private. Sign in or create an account to continue." (or "... Create an account to continue."), even when the visibility is `authenticated`, where anyone who signs in can read. `portal-access-gate.tsx` treats only `credentials` as the first step, and `HeaderOptions` in `auth-step-header.tsx` carried no visibility. These steps are not reachable under the live Google and GitHub sign-in configuration, but the copy was wrong wherever they appear.
- **REQ-07:** `roadmap-tabs.tsx:43` puts `whitespace-nowrap` on roadmap tab labels, which admins write. Suite v6.6.0 prohibits nowrap as a typography remedy, and the label was not marked as user text for the design text checker.

## Solution

- **DEF-06:** `headerForStep` takes the portal's visibility through `HeaderOptions`, and the gate passes it. On an `authenticated` portal the email and two-factor steps say "Anyone who signs in can read and take part.", the open lead's own sentence, followed by the existing "Sign in or create an account to continue." or "Create an account to continue.". Private portals, and a gate with no visibility, keep the private copy. The code, forgot and reset steps and the public sign-in dialog are unchanged.
  - The source change and `auth-step-header.test.tsx` are byte-identical (same git blobs) to commit `79fb6a5c4` on `richard/2309-merged-verify-fixes`, an earlier lane's branch with no pull request. Either branch can merge after the other without a conflict.
- **REQ-07:** the tab drops `whitespace-nowrap`, keeps `shrink-0` and gains `max-w-full`; the label sits in `<span className="min-w-0 break-words" data-text-origin="user">`. Removing nowrap alone would change nothing, because a `shrink-0` flex item is as wide as its whole label: a label longer than the tab row would still stay on one line and run past it. With `max-w-full` such a label wraps inside the row; shorter labels stay on one line and the row scrolls as before.

## Changes

- `apps/web/src/components/auth/auth-step-header.tsx`: `HeaderOptions.visibility`; the open copy (`portal.auth.open.loginTagline`, `portal.auth.open.signupTagline`) for the base-falling steps.
- `apps/web/src/components/portal/portal-access-gate.tsx`: passes `visibility` to `headerForStep`.
- `apps/web/src/components/public/roadmap-tabs.tsx`: the tab class and the user-text label span.
- Tests:
  - new `apps/web/src/components/auth/__tests__/auth-step-header.test.tsx`: each of `credentials`, `email`, `two-factor-enroll` and `two-factor-challenge`, in login and sign-up modes, with `authenticated`, `private` and no visibility; the `code` and `forgot` copy is unchanged;
  - extended `apps/web/src/components/portal/__tests__/portal-access-gate.test.tsx`: the rendered gate moved to each later step, in both modes, on an open portal (open copy, no "private", no first-step lead) and on a private portal (private copy);
  - new `apps/web/src/components/public/__tests__/roadmap-tabs.test.tsx`: no `whitespace-nowrap`, `shrink-0` and `max-w-full` kept, each label whole and marked `data-text-origin="user"`, the tablist name, `aria-selected` and `onSelect` unchanged.

## Validation

On the devbox (the standing rule allows only per-file syntax checks there; every suite runs in this PR's cloud CI):

- `bun <scratchpad>/tsx-syntax.ts <6 touched files>` (Bun.Transpiler, loader `tsx`, parse only): 6 files, all `ok`.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`: clean.
- For each of the three shared files, `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` equals `git rev-parse 79fb6a5c4:<path>`: identical blobs.
- All three commits are signed (`git log --format=%G?` prints `G` for each).
- `bun run test`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build` and `bun run test:e2e`: NOT RUN locally (cloud-only rule); this PR's CI is the gate.

Cloud CI:

- Head `0769c9e70`, CI run 36068944358: failure. `Database migrations and tests` failed 6 of the new gate tests (the two-factor steps) with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')` at `portal-access-gate.tsx:114`: the gate's 2FA-abandon revoke calls `void signOut().catch(...)` on unmount, and the file's `signOut` mock returned undefined. `portability-gate` failed only because it requires that lane. Every other job passed.
- Fix `38b49badb`: the mock resolves, as the two-factor-abandon test's mock does. No source change.
- Head `38b49badb`, CI run 36071220998: success. `Static analysis` (`bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run --filter @quackback/web typecheck`, widget build and test) success; `Database migrations and tests` (`bun run test --run`): 586 files passed, 2 skipped; 7416 tests passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed, including `portal-access-gate.test.tsx` (20 tests), `auth-step-header.test.tsx` (17) and `roadmap-tabs.test.tsx` (3); `End-to-end tests` shards 1 to 8: job success, but the known-failures ratchet (`e2e/scripts/check-known-failures.ts`) tolerated 40 failing tests that `e2e/known-failures.json` lists (per shard 2, 1, 2, 3, 3, 0, 17, 12; 3 more were flaky). None is in `touch-targets.spec.ts`, the portal gate, `auth-step-header` or the roadmap tabs; 22 are in `post-list.spec.ts` and 5 in `post-list-filters.spec.ts`. `touch-targets.spec.ts` (it narrows the roadmap tab row to 180px and requires the scroll button) passed; `portability-gate` success; CodeQL success. `mergeStateStatus` CLEAN.
- Rendered design check (suite checker) and a keyboard walk of the roadmap tabs and gate steps: NOT RUN. No checker route exists for signed-in quackback surfaces yet; that is REQ-31 (#148, open).

Production does not change until a later feedback release (REQ-11); feedback.venturi.systems serves fork `8ed10c3`.

Verifier findings resolved (independent verification of this PR after merge, head `38b49badb`):

- The E2E line above under-reported the ratchet: corrected here. The counts were re-measured from the eight shard logs of run 36071220998 (`E2E ratchet: OK.` in each; 40 failed, 3 flaky).
- The long-label reflow path of the roadmap tabs had no rendered check. #163 adds an E2E test with a label wider than the 320px row. Rendering it showed two defects in this PR's `max-w-full` approach: a tab as wide as the row stays under the scroll-arrow overlays, and a capsule radius cuts into a tab of three or more lines. #163 fixes both.
- Admin-written names were still truncated in the post sidebar and the help-center navigation (outside this PR's diff): fixed in #163, together with the same pattern on the notifications page, the support list and the similar ideas card.
- The stale worktree of `richard/2309-merged-verify-fixes` (local branch behind its remote, with uncommitted edits including a `roadmap-tabs.tsx` without the reflow) is another lane's work. It was left untouched for the orchestrator to decide; if it is continued, its `roadmap-tabs.tsx`, `auth-step-header.tsx` and `portal-access-gate.tsx` must come from `main`.

## Risk and rollback

- **Risk: gate copy.** Only the `private-portal` surface with `visibility === 'authenticated'` gets new text; every other path renders what it rendered before. The new message ids have default messages and no catalog entries, as the other gate messages do.
- **Risk: roadmap tabs.** A label longer than the tab row now wraps onto a second line inside a rounded tab instead of running past the row. Labels that fit are unchanged.
- **Risk: overlap with `richard/2309-merged-verify-fixes`.** The DEF-06 files are identical to that branch's

author: tafreeman
body:
Stacked on #339 (base `cancel_fix`). Fourth and last ADR-060 per-defect fix.

## Summary

- **Defect:** `on_update` is an observer (UI, WebSocket, step scoring, the checkpoint wrapper), but its exceptions changed the run. Probe evidence from before the fix: on `step_end` the exception escaped `execute()` and orphaned the running step. On `step_start` both steps were recorded **FAILED without their work running**. On `workflow_start` and `workflow_end` it escaped, and on `workflow_end` the finished result was lost.
- **Fix:** every event goes through `_notify`, which logs the failure with its traceback and counts it in `metadata["observer_errors"]`. Cancellation still propagates. Side effect: a `TimeoutError` raised by an observer can no longer be mistaken for the workflow timeout.
- **Replay test hardening:** the replay asserted its safety checks *inside* `on_update`, and `_notify` would now swallow those assertions. It now records violations and asserts on them after the run. Verified by letting the scheduler exceed its limit by one: the replay reports `step_start N: concurrency exceeded`.
- **Model:** observers are omitted from the Lean model, and the README now says why that is sound.

## Test plan

- [x] Fail-first: all 4 parametrized observer tests fail on the previous commit; 46 pass with the fix
- [x] Mutation: a limit+1 scheduler is caught by the replay's violation list
- [x] Full unit suite (CI form): 4104 passed, 57 skipped, 2 xfailed (pre-existing, unrelated)
- [x] `ruff check`, strict mypy (CI flags), `pre-commit run --files`, `generate_doc_stats.py`

body:
Depende de #169 (se apila sobre ella): la rama nace de `infra-219-p1-role-catalog` y usa `kc_rbac.py`, `ROLES.yaml` y el job CI `keycloak-rbac-contract` de P1. Mergear #169 primero; esta PR queda con un solo commit propio.

## Qué
- `platform/keycloak-next/PRINCIPALS.md`: 19 principals del realm `edani` (9 usuarios + 10 SA, medidos 24-09) con dueño, fuente, propósito, `realm_roles` (espejo de los `grantees` de `ROLES.yaml`) y estado. Un único bloque json, leído con `kc_rbac.load_json_block`.
- `platform/keycloak-next/scripts/verify-principals.py`: usuarios + `users?username=service-account&exact=false`, paginados; solo lee `users` (sin clients ni role-mappings, apto para el auditor sin `view-clients` de P4). `OK` exit 0 / `DRIFT` exit 1 / `ERROR` exit 2.
- `tests/test_keycloak_rbac_principals_contract.py`: Keycloak falso en loopback; OK, principal sin entrada, entrada sin dueño, entrada sin principal vivo, roles distintos de ROLES.yaml, retirada sin motivo, paginado, 401.

No toca `kc_rbac.py`, `ROLES.yaml`, `ci.yml` ni `kustomization.yaml`. Solo lectura del realm; no se borra ningún principal.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_keycloak_rbac_*.py'` → 49 tests OK (15 nuevos).
